children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>

children.text: tatsadbrahmaṇe+namaḥ
children.translated_text: Salutation to that <s>Brahman</s> which is Being and Truth.

children.text: māṇḍūkyopaniṣad
children.translated_text: <s>Māṇḍūkyopaniṣad</s>

children.text: (MANDUKYA UPANISHAD)
children.translated_text: (MANDUKYA UPANISHAD)

children.text: śāntipāṭha
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntipāṭha</s> (Peace Invocation)

children.text: oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devā bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhiryajatrāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods; may we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O worshippers;

children.text: sthirairaṅgaistuṣṭuvā sastanūbhirvyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ
children.translated_text: With steady limbs, with bodies [fit for praise], may we enjoy the life allotted by the gods.

children.text: oṃ śāntiḥ !! śāntiḥ !! śāntiḥ !!!
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Peace! Peace! Peace!

children.text: svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ /
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> of great fame be auspicious to us; may <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, be auspicious to us;

children.text: svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu
children.translated_text: May <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa), of unimpaired protection, be auspicious to us; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us auspiciousness.

children.text: oṃ śāntiḥ !! śāntiḥ !! śāntiḥ!!!
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Peace! Peace! Peace!

children.text: Āgamaprakaraṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Āgamaprakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Scripture)

children.text: INVOCATION
children.translated_text: INVOCATION

children.text: prajñānāṃśupratānaiḥ sthiracaranikaravyāpibhir vyāpya lokān bhuktvā bhogānsthaviṣṭhānpunarapi dhiṣaṇodbhāsitānkāmajanyān /
children.translated_text: Having pervaded all the worlds with the rays of consciousness, extended and penetrating all assemblages of moving and non-moving beings, having enjoyed the grossest pleasures born of desire and illumined by intelligence,

children.text: pītvā sarvān viśeṣān svapiti madhurabhuṅ māyayā bhojayanno māyāsaṃkhyāturīyaṃ paramamṛtamajaṃ brahma yattannato 'smi //1//
children.translated_text: Having drunk in all particularities, the sweet-tasting one sleeps; and through <s>māyā</s> (illusion), causing [all beings] to experience, I bow to that <s>Brahman</s> which is the supreme, immortal, unborn <s>Turīya</s> (Fourth), beyond <s>māyā</s> and enumeration. ||1||

children.text: yo viśvātmā vidhijaviṣayān prāśya bhogān sthaviṣṭhān paścāc cānyān svamativibhavāñ jyotiṣā svena sūkṣmān /
children.translated_text: He who is the Self of all (<s>Viśvātman</s>), having consumed the gross objects of experience produced by <s>Brahmā</s>, and then again the subtle ones illumined by his own light of intelligence,

children.text: sarvān etān punar api śanaiḥ svātmani sthāpayitvā hitvā sarvānviśeṣānvigataguṇagaṇaḥ pātvasau nasturīyaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Having again gradually absorbed all these into his own Self, and having abandoned all particularities, free from all qualities — may that <s>Turīya</s> (Fourth) protect us. ||2||

children.text: START MandUp 1
children.translated_text: START MandUp 1

children.text:
omityetadakṣaramidaṃ sarvam /
  tasyopavyākhyānaṃ vedāntārthasārasaṃgrahabhūtamidaṃ prakaraṇacatṛṣṭayamomityetadakṣaramityādyārabhyate /
  ata eva na pṛthaksambandhābhidheyaprayojanāni vaktavyāni /
  yānyeva tu vedānte sambandhābhidheya prayojanāni tānyeveha bhavitumarhanti /
  tathāpi prakaraṇavyācikhyāsunā saṃkṣepato vaktavyāni /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> — this syllable is all this. Its exposition, which is a compendium of the essence of <s>Vedānta</s>, consisting of four chapters beginning with 'Oṃ — this syllable,' is now commenced. Therefore, the connection (<s>sambandha</s>), subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), and purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) need not be stated separately. Whatever are the connection, subject matter, and purpose in <s>Vedānta</s>, those very ones apply here as well. Nevertheless, for one who wishes to explain the treatise, they should be stated briefly.

children.text:
tatra prayojanavat sādhanābhivyañjakatvenābhidheyasambaddhaṃ śāstraṃ pāramparyeṇa viśiṣṭasaṃbandhābhidheyaprayojanavad bhavati /
  kiṃ punas tat prayojanam ity ucyate rogārtasyaiva roganivṛttau svasthatā /
  tathā duḥkhātmakasyātmano dvaitaprapañcopaśame svasthatā /
  advaitabhāvaḥ prayojanam /
children.translated_text: Among these, the scripture (<s>śāstra</s>), being connected with its subject matter through the indicative power of its purposeful means, is traditionally understood as possessing a specific connection, subject matter, and purpose. What then is that purpose? It is stated: just as for one afflicted by disease, the removal of disease results in health, so too for the Self whose nature is suffering, the subsidence of the phenomenal world of duality results in health — that is, the state of non-duality (<s>advaitabhāva</s>) is the purpose.

children.text: dvaitaprapañcasyāvidyākṛtatvād vidyayā tad upaśamaḥ syād iti brahmavidyāprakāśanāyāsya ārambhaḥ kriyate /
children.translated_text: Since the phenomenal world of duality is created by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), its subsidence should be achieved through knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) — thus this [work] is commenced for the purpose of illuminating the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavidyā</s>).

children.text: "yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati"(bṛ.u 2 / 4 / 14) "yatra vānyad iva syāt tatrānyo 'nyat paśyed anyo 'nyad vijānīyāt"(bṛ.u 4 / 3 / 31) "yatra vāsya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ paśyet kena kaṃ vijānīyāt"(bṛ.u 2 / 4 / 14) ity ādi śrutibhyo 'syārthasya siddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The establishment of this meaning is from <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'Where there is duality, as it were' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14), 'Where there seems to be another, there one sees another, one knows another' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.31), 'But where everything has become the Self alone, then by what and whom would one see, by what and whom would one know?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14), and so forth.

children.text:
tatra tāvad oṃkāranirṇayāya prathamaṃ prakaraṇam āgamapradhānām ātmatattvapratipatty upāyabhūtam /
  yasya dvaitaprapañcasyopaśame 'dvaitapratipattī rajjvām iva sarpādivikalpa upaśame rajjutattvapratipattis tasya dvaitasya hetuto vaitathyapratipādanāya dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam /
  tathādvaitasyāpi vaitathyaprasaṅgaprāptau yuktitas tathātvadarśanāya tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇam /
  advaitasya tathātvapratipattipakṣabhūtāni yāni vādāntarāṇyavaidikāni teṣām anyonyavirodhitvādatathārthatvena tadupapattibhir eva nirākaraṇāya caturthaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Among these, first, the first chapter, primarily based on scripture (<s>āgama</s>), serves as the means for the realization of the truth of the Self through the determination of <s>Oṃkāra</s>. The second chapter is for demonstrating, through reasoning, the unreality of that duality whose subsidence leads to the realization of non-duality — just as when the imagined snake and the like upon the rope subside, the truth of the rope is realized. The third chapter is for showing, through reasoning, the reality of non-duality when the objection arises that non-duality too might be unreal. The fourth chapter is for refuting, through their own logical arguments, the other non-Vedic doctrines that stand opposed to the realization of the truth of non-duality, since they are mutually contradictory and therefore not of true import.

children.text: kathaṃ puna oṃkāranirṇaya ātmatattvapratipatty upāyatvaṃ pratipadyata ity ucyate"oṃ ity etat"(ka.u 1 / 2 / 15) "etad ālambanam"(ka.u.1 / 2 / 17) "etad vai satyakāma"(pra.u.5 / 2) "oṃ ity ātmānaṃ yuñjīta"(maitryu.6 / 3) "oṃ iti brahma"(tai.u.1 / 8 / 1) "oṃkāra evedaṃ sarvam" (chā.u.2 / 23 / 3) ity ādi śrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: How then does the determination of <s>Oṃkāra</s> become the means for the realization of the truth of the Self? It is stated from <s>śruti</s> passages such as: '<s>Oṃ</s> — this is that' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.15), 'This is the support' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.17), 'This verily, O <s>Satyakāma</s>' (<s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s> 5.2), 'One should concentrate the Self with <s>Oṃ</s>' (<s>Maitrī Upaniṣad</s> 6.3), '<s>Oṃ</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 1.8.1), '<s>Oṃkāra</s> alone is all this' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 2.23.3), and so forth.

children.text:
rajjur ādir iva sarpādivikalpasyāspado 'dvaya ātmā paramārthaḥ sanprāṇādivikalpasyāspado yathā tathā sarvo 'pi vākprapañcaḥ prāṇādy ātmavikalpaviṣaya oṃkāra eva /
  sa cātmasvarūpam eva tadabhidhāyakatvāt /
  oṃkāravikāraśabdābhidheyaś ca sarvaḥ prāṇādir ātmavikalpo 'bhidhānavyatirekeṇa nāsti /
  "vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam"(chā.u.6 / 1 / 4) "tad asyedaṃ vācā tantyā nāmabhir dāmabhiḥ sarvaṃ sitam" "sarvaṃ hīdaṃ nāmāni"ity ādi śrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the non-dual Self, which is the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), is the substratum of the imaginary constructs of snake and the like upon the rope and the like, so too the entire verbal elaboration — the realm of imaginary constructs such as <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the like upon the Self — is nothing but <s>Oṃkāra</s>. And that [<s>Oṃkāra</s>] is the very nature of the Self, since it denotes the Self. And all the imaginary constructs upon the Self, such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, which are denoted by words that are modifications of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, do not exist apart from the name. [This is established] from <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'Modification is merely a name, a verbal handle' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.1.4), 'All this of his is bound by speech as by a thread, by names as by cords,' 'For all this is names,' and so forth.

children.text: ata āha
children.translated_text: Therefore he says —

children.text:
oṃ ity etad akṣaram idaṃ sarvaṃ tasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyad iti sarvam oṃkāra eva |
  yac cānyat trikālātītaṃ tad apy oṃkāra eva || MandUp_1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> — this syllable is all this. Its exposition: the past, the present, and the future — all this is indeed <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone. And whatever else there is beyond the three times — that too is <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 1 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_1
  oṃ ity etad akṣaram idaṃ sarvam iti /
  yad idam arthajātam abhidheyabhūtaṃ tasyābhidhānāvyatirekād abhidhānasya ca oṃkārāvyatirekād oṃkāra evedaṃ sarvam /
  paraṃ ca brahmābhidhānābhidheya upāyapūrvakam eva gamyata ity oṃkāra eva /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 1: '<s>Oṃ</s> — this syllable is all this' — whatever totality of objects constitutes the denotable, since there is no difference between the denotable and its denotation, and since the denotation is not different from <s>Oṃkāra</s>, therefore <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone is all this. And the supreme <s>Brahman</s> too is known only through the means of denotation and denotable — therefore it is <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone.

children.text: tasyaitasya parāpara brahmarūpasyākṣarasya oṃ ity etasyopavyākhyānam; brahmapratipatty upāyatvād brahmasamīpatayā vispaṣṭaṃ prakathanam upavyākhyānaṃ prastutaṃ veditavyam iti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of this syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, which has the form of the higher and lower <s>Brahman</s>, the exposition (<s>upavyākhyāna</s>) — since it serves as a means for the realization of <s>Brahman</s>, it should be understood as a clear elucidation, a detailed explanation by virtue of proximity to <s>Brahman</s>. The completion of the sentence is: 'is to be known.'

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavadbhaviṣyad iti kālatrayaparicchedyaṃ yat tad apy oṃkāra evoktanyāyataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The past, the present, and the future' — whatever is determinable by the three times, that too is <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone, for the reason already stated.

children.text: yac cānyat trikālātītaṃ kāryādhigamyaṃ kālāparicchedyamavyākṛtādi tad apy oṃkāra eva //1//
children.translated_text: 'And whatever else is beyond the three times' — that which is knowable through its effects but not determinable by time, such as the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>) and the like — that too is <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone. ||1||

children.text: START MandUp 2
children.translated_text: START MandUp 2

children.text:
abhidhānābhidheyayor ekatve 'py abhidhānāprādhānyena nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ /
  oṃ ity etad akṣaram idaṃ sarvam ity ādy abhidhānaprādhānyena nirdiṣṭasya puno 'bhidheyaprādhānyena nirdeśo 'bhidhānābhidheyayor ekatvapratipatty arthaḥ /
  itaro 'thā hy abhidhānatantrābhidheyapratipattir ity abhidheyasyābhidhānatvaṃ gauṇām ity āśaṅkā syāt /
  ekatvapratipatteś ca prayojanam abhidhānābhidheyayor ekenaiva prayatnena yugapatpravilāparyastadvilakṣaṇaṃ brahma pratipadyeta iti /
  tathā ca vakṣyati"pādā mātrā mātrāś ca pādāḥ" (mā.u.8) iti /
  tadāha
children.translated_text: Although the name and the named are one, the statement was made with prominence given to the name. What was stated with prominence to the name — 'Oṃ, this syllable is all this' and so on — is now restated with prominence to the named, for the purpose of realizing the identity of name and named. Otherwise, the understanding of the named would be dependent on the name, and one might suspect that the named being identical with the name is only secondary (figurative). The purpose of realizing this identity is that, through a single effort, both name and named may be simultaneously dissolved, and <s>Brahman</s>, which is different from both, may be realized. And so it will be stated: 'The quarters are the measures, and the measures are the quarters' (<s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 8). Therefore he says —

children.text: sarvaṃ hy etad brahmāyam ātmā brahma so 'yam ātmā catuṣpāt || MandUp_2 ||
children.translated_text: All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. This Self (<s>Ātman</s>) is <s>Brahman</s>. This Self has four quarters (<s>pādas</s>). || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 2 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_2
  sarvaṃ hy etad brahmeti /
  sarvaṃ yad uktam oṃkāramātram iti tadetad brahma /
  tac ca brahma parokṣābhihitaṃ pratyakṣato viśeṣeṇa nirdiśatyayamātmā brahmeti /
ayam iti catuṣpātvena pravibhajyamānaṃ pratyagātmatayābhinayena nirdiśati ayam ātmeti /
children.translated_text: 'This' — by the gesture of pointing to the innermost Self, which is being analyzed into four quarters, it is indicated as 'this Self.'

children.text: so 'yamātma oṃkārābhidheyaḥ parāparatvena vyavasthitaś catuṣpātkārṣāpaṇavan na gaur iveti /
children.translated_text: This Self, which is denoted by <s>Oṃkāra</s>, is established as having both higher and lower aspects, and has four quarters — like a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin), not like a cow [whose feet are not separable parts of it].

children.text: trayāṇāṃ viśvādīnāṃ pūrvapūrvapravilāpanena turīyasya pratapattir iti karaṇasādhanaḥ pādaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'quarter' (<s>pāda</s>) is derived in the instrumental sense of 'means,' because the realization of the <s>Turīya</s> (Fourth) is achieved through the progressive dissolution of the preceding [quarters] — <s>Viśva</s> and the rest — into each prior one.

children.text: turīyasya padyata iti karmasādhanaḥ pādaśabdaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: The word 'quarter' for the <s>Turīya</s> is derived in the objective sense of 'that which is reached' (<s>padyate</s>). ||2||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 2: 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' — all that was stated as being nothing but <s>Oṃkāra</s>, that very thing is <s>Brahman</s>. And that <s>Brahman</s>, having been referred to indirectly, is now indicated directly and specifically by saying 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: START MandUp 3
children.translated_text: START MandUp 3

children.text: kathaṃ catuṣpātvam ity āha
children.translated_text: How does it have four quarters? He says —

children.text: jāgaritasthāno bahiḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ sthūlabhug vaiśvānaraḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ || MandUp_3 ||
children.translated_text: The first quarter is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose sphere is the waking state, who is conscious of the external, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who is the experiencer of the gross. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 3 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_3
  jāgaritaṃ sthānam asyeti jāgaritasthānaḥ /
  bahiṣprajñaḥ svātmavyatirikte viṣaye prajñā sa bahiṣprajño bahir viṣaya eva prajñāvidyākṛtāv avabhāsata ity arthaḥ /
  tathā saptāṅgānyasya"tasya ha vaitasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāś cakṣurviśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā saṃdoho bahulo vastir eva rayiḥ pṛthivy eva pādau" (chā.u.5 / 18 / 2) ity agnihotrakalpanāśeṣatvenāhavanīyo 'gnir asya mukhatvenokta ity evaṃ saptāṅgāni yasya sa saptāṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 3: 'Whose sphere is the waking state' — the waking state is the sphere of this one, hence he is 'one whose sphere is the waking state.' He is 'conscious of the external' — consciousness directed toward objects other than the Self; the meaning is that consciousness shines as if in external objects, which are appearances created by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Likewise, 'seven-limbed' — his seven limbs are [described in]: 'Of that <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self, the head is the brilliant heaven, the eye is the sun of universal form, the breath is the air moving in different paths, the body is the vast ether, the lower part is the water, the feet are the earth' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.18.2) — and the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire is stated as his mouth, as a supplementary part of the fire-ritual meditation; thus the one who has these seven limbs is 'seven-limbed.'

children.text:
tathaikonaviṃśatir mukhāny asya buddhīndriyāṇi karmendriyāṇi ca daśa vāyavaś ca prāṇādayaḥpañca mano buddhirahaṅkāraccittam iti mukhānīva mukhāni tāny upalabdhidvārāṇityarthaḥ sa evaṃ viśiṣṭo vaiśvānaro yathoktair dvāraiḥ śabdādīn sthūlān viṣayān bhuṅkta iti sthūlabhuk /
  viśveṣāṃ narāṇām anekadhā nayanād vaiśvānaraḥ /
  yad vā viśvaś cāsau naraś ceti viśvānaraḥ /
  viśvānara eva vaiśvānaraḥ /
  sarvapiṇḍātmananyatvāt saḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ /
  etat pūrvakatvād uttarapādādhigamasya prāthamyamasya /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'nineteen mouths' — his mouths are: the five cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>), the five organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>), the five vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s> and the rest), and mind (<s>manas</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), and thought (<s>citta</s>) — these are mouths, as it were, being the doorways of experience. This one, thus characterized, is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, who through the aforesaid doorways consumes the gross objects such as sound and the rest — hence he is 'the experiencer of the gross.' He is called <s>Vaiśvānara</s> because he leads all human beings (<s>naras</s>) in diverse ways. Or, he is both universal (<s>viśva</s>) and human (<s>nara</s>), hence <s>Viśvānara</s>; and <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is derived from <s>Viśvānara</s>. He is the first quarter because the understanding of the subsequent quarters is preceded by this. It is 'first' because it comes first.

children.text:
katham ayamātmā brahmeti pratyagātmano 'sya catuṣpāttve prakṛte dyulokādīnāṃ mūrdhādyaṅgatvam iti /
  naiṣa doṣaḥ /
  sarvasyaprapañcasya sādhidaivikasyānena ātmanā catuṣpāttvasya vivakṣitatvāt /
  evaṃ ca sati sarvaprapañca upaśame 'dvaitasiddhiḥ /
  sarvabhūtasthaś cātmaiko dṛṣṭaḥ syāt sarvabhūtāni cātmani /
  "yas tu sarvāṇi bhūtāni"(ī.u.6) ity ādiśrutyarthopasaṃhṛtaś caivaṃ syāt /
  anyathā hi svadehaparicchinna eva pratyāgātmā sāṃkhyādibhir iva dṛṣṭaḥ syāt tathā ca satyadvaitam iti śrutikṛto viśeṣo na syāt sāṃkhyādidarśanenāviśeṣāt /
  iṣyate ca sarva upaniṣadāṃ sarvātmaikyapratipādakatvam /
  ato yuktam evāsyādhyātmikasya piṇḍātmano dyulokādy aṅgatvena virāḍātmanādhidaivikenaikatvam abhipretya saptāṅgatvavacanam /
  "mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat"(chā.u 5 / 12 / 2) ity ādi liṅgadarśanāc ca /
children.translated_text: If the context is that this inner Self has four quarters, as in 'this Self is <s>Brahman</s>,' how can the celestial world and the like be its limbs such as the head? This is no defect, because the intention is to express the fourfoldness of this Self as inclusive of the entire phenomenal world together with its presiding deities (<s>sādhidaivika</s>). When this is so, upon the subsidence of the entire phenomenal world, the reality of non-duality is established. And the one Self would be seen as dwelling in all beings, and all beings in the Self. This would be in agreement with the import of <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'He who sees all beings' (<s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> 6) and the like. Otherwise, the inner Self would be seen as confined to one's own body, as by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others, and then the distinction made by <s>śruti</s> — namely that 'it is non-dual' — would not hold, since there would be no difference from the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other views. And it is accepted that all <s>Upaniṣads</s> aim at establishing the oneness of the Self with all. Therefore it is quite proper that the statement of seven-limbedness is made with the intention of the identity of this individual self (<s>piṇḍātman</s>), which is related to the body, with the cosmic self (<s>virāj-ātman</s>), which is related to presiding deities, by attributing the celestial world and the like as its limbs. And this is also indicated by the <s>śruti</s> passage 'Your head would have fallen off' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.12.2) and the like.

children.text:
virāja ekatvam upalakṣaṇārthaṃ hiraṇyagarbhāvyākṛtātmanoḥ /
  uktaṃ caitan madhubrāhmaṇe"yaś cāyam asyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yac cāyam adhyātmam"(bṛ.u.2 / 5 / 1) ityādi /
suṣuptāvyākṛtayaḥ sa tv ekatvaṃ siddham eva nirviśeṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: In deep sleep and the unmanifest, the identity is already established, since they are without distinctions.

children.text: evaṃ ca satyetat siddhaṃ bhaviṣyati sarvadvaita upaśame cādvaitam iti //3//
children.translated_text: And when this is so, the following will be established: upon the subsidence of all duality, non-duality [alone remains]. ||3||

The identity with <s>Virāj</s> is mentioned to imply also [the identity with] <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and the Unmanifest Self. And this has been stated in the <s>Madhu Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'This luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this earth, and this one who is in the individual self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.1), and so forth.

children.text: START MandUp 4
children.translated_text: START MandUp 4

children.text: svaprasthāno 'ntaḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ praviviktabhuktaijaso dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ || MandUp_4 ||
children.translated_text: The second quarter is <s>Taijasa</s> (the luminous one), whose sphere is the dream state, who is conscious of the internal, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who is the experiencer of the subtle. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 4 ||

children.text:
__________
  MandUpC_4
  svapnaḥ sthānasya taijasasya svapnasthānaḥ /
  jāgratprajñānekasādhanā bahir viṣaya evāvabhāsamānā manaḥspandanamātrā satī tathābhūtaṃ saṃskāraṃ manasyādhatte /
  tan manas tathā saṃskṛtaṃ citrita iva paṭo bāhyasādhanān anapekṣam avidyākāmakarmabhiḥ preryamāṇaṃ jāgradvadavabhāsate /
  tathā coktam"asya lokasya sarvāvato mātrām apādāya"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 9) iti /
  tathā"pare deve manasy ekībhavati"(pra.u.4 / 2) iti prastutya"atraiṣa devaḥ svapne mahimānam anubhavati"(pra.u.4 / 5) ityātharvaṇe /
children.translated_text:
MandUpC_4
Dream is the state of <s>Taijasa</s>, the dream-state.
The cognition of the waking state, having a single means [of knowledge] directed outward toward objects, being merely a vibration of the mind, deposits a corresponding impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) in the mind.
That mind, thus imprinted — like a painted canvas — without depending on external means, being impelled by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s> (action), appears as if in the waking state.
As it has been said: 'Taking a measure of this entire world' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.9).
Likewise, in the <s>Ātharvana</s> [i.e., <s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s>], having introduced 'In the higher god, the mind becomes unified' (<s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s> 4.2), [it says] 'There this god experiences greatness in dream' (<s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s> 4.5).

children.text:
indriyāpekṣayāntaḥsthatvān manasas tad vāsanārūpā ca svapne prajñā yasyātyantaḥprajñaḥ /
  viṣayaśūnyānāṃ prajñāyāṃ kevalaprakāśasvarūpāyāṃ viṣayitvena bhavatīti taijasaḥ /
  viśvasya saviṣayatvena prajñāyāḥ sthūlāyā bhojyatvam /
children.translated_text:
Because the mind is internal relative to the senses, and because cognition in dream has the form of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — he whose [cognition] is extremely internal is 'the internally conscious one' (<s>antaḥprajña</s>).
He who, in [a state where] cognition is devoid of objects and is of the nature of pure illumination alone, becomes the subject [of experience] — he is <s>Taijasa</s> (the luminous one).
Because the cognition of <s>Viśva</s> (the universal) is gross and has objects, it is [called] the enjoyable (<s>bhojya</s>).

children.text: iha punaḥ kevalā vāsanāmātrā prajñā bhojyeti pravivikto bhoga iti /
children.translated_text: Here, however, the cognition that is merely latent impressions alone is the enjoyable — hence the enjoyment is said to be 'subtle' (<s>pravivikta</s>).

children.text: samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: The rest is the same [as before].

children.text: dvitīyaḥ pādas taijasaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: <s>Taijasa</s> is the second quarter. || 4 ||

children.text: START MandUp 5
children.translated_text: START MandUp 5

children.text:
darśanādarśanavṛttyas tatvāprabodhalakṣaṇasya svāpasya tulyatvāt suṣuptigrahaṇārthaṃ yatra supta ityādi viśeṣaṇam /
  atha vā triṣv api sthāneṣu tattvāpratibodhalakṣaṇaḥ svāpo 'viśiṣṭa iti pūrvābhyāṃ suṣuptaṃ vibhajate
children.translated_text:
Since the states of seeing and not-seeing are equal [in that both involve] sleep characterized by non-awakening to reality, in order to define deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), the qualifying phrase 'where the sleeping one...' etc. is used.
Alternatively, since sleep characterized by non-awakening to reality is undifferentiated across all three states, [the Upaniṣad] distinguishes deep sleep from the two previous [states].

children.text:
yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati tat suṣuptam |
  suṣuptasthāna ekībhūtaḥ prajñānaghana evāndamayo hy ānandabhukcetomukhaḥ prājñaḥ tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ || MandUp_5 ||
children.translated_text:
Where the sleeping one does not desire any desire, nor see any dream — that is deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>).
The one whose state is deep sleep, who has become unified, who is a mass of pure consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), who is full of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>), who is indeed the enjoyer of bliss (<s>ānandabhuk</s>), whose doorway is consciousness (<s>cetomukha</s>) — <s>Prājña</s> (the wise one) is the third quarter. || MandUp 5 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_5
  yatra yasmin sthāne kāle vā supto na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate /
  na hi suṣupte pūrvayor ivānyathāgrahaṇalakṣaṇaṃ svapnadarśanaṃ kāmo vā kaścana vidyane /
  tadetat suṣuptaṃ sthānam asyeti suṣuptasthānaḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpC_5
'Where' — in whichever state or at whichever time — the sleeping one does not see any dream, nor desire any desire.
For in deep sleep, unlike in the two previous [states], there is neither dream-perception, characterized by misapprehension, nor any desire whatsoever.
This state is deep sleep; one whose state this is, is called 'one whose state is deep sleep' (<s>suṣuptasthāna</s>).

children.text:
sthānadvayapravibhaktaṃ manaḥ spanditaṃ dvaitajātaṃ tathā rūpāparityāgenāvivekāpannaṃ naiśatamograstamivāhaḥ saprapañcamekībhūtam ity ucyate /
  ata eva svapnajāgran manaḥspandanāni prajñānāni ghanībhūtānīva seyamavasthāvivekarūpatvāt prajñānaghanocyate /
  yathā rātrau naiśena tamasā vibhajyamānaṃ sarvaṃ ghanam iva tadvat prajñānaghana eva /
  eva śabdān na jātyantaraṃ prajñānavyatirekeṇāstītārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The mind, which was differentiated in the two [previous] states, vibrating, producing the entire multiplicity of duality, and similarly, having not abandoned those forms [and thus being] in a state of non-discrimination, as if swallowed by the darkness of night — [this mind], together with its entire phenomenal elaboration, is said to have become 'unified' (<s>ekībhūta</s>).
Therefore, the cognitions that are the vibrations of the mind in dream and waking, having become as if condensed — this state, because of its nature as the absence of discrimination, is called 'a mass of consciousness' (<s>prajñānaghana</s>).
Just as at night, due to the darkness of night, everything appears as if a solid mass — so too is it 'a mass of consciousness' indeed.
The word 'eva' (indeed) means that nothing of a different kind exists apart from consciousness.

children.text:
manaso viṣayīviṣayyākāraspandanāyāsaduḥkhābhāvādānandamaya ānandaprāyo nānanda eva /
  yathā loke nirāyāsasthitaḥ sukhyānandabhugucyate 'tyantānāyāsarūpā hīyaṃ sthitiranenānubhūyata ity ānandabhuk"eṣo 'sya parama ānandaḥ"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 32) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text:
Because of the absence of the pain and fatigue of the mind's vibration in the form of subject and object, [this state is] <s>ānandamaya</s> — predominantly blissful, not bliss itself.
Just as in the world, one who is established in a state free from exertion is called 'happy' or 'a bliss-enjoyer' — for this state, which is of the nature of complete absence of exertion, is experienced by this [self] — hence he is 'the enjoyer of bliss' (<s>ānandabhuk</s>). As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'This is his supreme bliss' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.32).

children.text:
svapnādipratibodhicetaḥ prati dvārībhūtatvāc cetomukhaḥ /
  bodhalakṣaṇaṃ vā ceto dvāraṃ mukham asya svapnādy āgamanaṃ pratīti cetomukhaḥ /
bhūtabhaviṣyaj jñātṛtvaṃ sarvaviṣayajñātṛtvam asyaiti prājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of being the knower of past and future, and the knower of all objects — he is <s>Prājña</s> (the supremely wise).

children.text: suṣupto 'pi hi bhūtapūrvagatyā prājñocyate /
children.translated_text: Even in deep sleep, he is called <s>Prājña</s> by virtue of his prior [capacity for] knowing.

children.text: athavā prajñaptimātram asyaivāsādhāraṇaṃ rūpam iti prājña itarayor viśiṣṭam api vijñānam asti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, his unique essential nature is mere cognizance (<s>prajñaptimātra</s>) — hence he is <s>Prājña</s>; the other two [quarters] also have distinct cognition.

children.text: so 'yaṃ prājñas tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: This <s>Prājña</s> is the third quarter. || 5 ||

Because [consciousness in deep sleep] serves as a door for the consciousness that awakens into dream and the other [states], it is called <s>cetomukha</s> (consciousness-faced).
Alternatively, consciousness (<s>cetas</s>), characterized by awareness, is the door (<s>mukha</s>) through which the entry into dream and the other [states] occurs — hence <s>cetomukha</s>.

children.text: START MandUp 6
children.translated_text: START MandUp 6

children.text: eṣaḥ sarveśvara eṣa sarvajña eṣo 'ntaryāmy eṣa yoniḥ sarvasya prabhavāpyayau hi bhūtānām || MandUp_6 ||
children.translated_text: This is the lord of all (<s>sarveśvara</s>); this is the knower of all (<s>sarvajña</s>); this is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmī</s>); this is the source (<s>yoni</s>) of all — for [this is] the origin and dissolution of all beings. || MandUp 6 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_6
  eṣa hi svarūpāvasthaḥ sarveśvaraḥ sādhidaivikasya bhedajātasya sarvasyeśitā naitasmāj jātyantarabhūto 'nyeṣām iva /
  "prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya manaḥ"(chā.u.6 / 8 / 2) iti śruteḥ /
ayam eva hi sarvasya sarvabhedāvastho jñātetyeṣa sarvajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: This very one, in the state of all differentiations, is the knower of all — hence 'this is the omniscient' (<s>sarvajña</s>).

children.text: eṣo 'ntaryāmy antaranupraviśya sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ niyantāpy eṣa eva /
children.translated_text: This is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmī</s>) — having entered within, it is also the ruler of all beings.

children.text: ata eva yathoktaṃ sabhedaṃ jagatprasūyata ity eṣa yoniḥ sarvasya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the differentiated universe is born from this, as described — hence this is the source (<s>yoni</s>) of all.

children.text: yata evaṃ prabhavaś cāpi yaś ca prabhavāpyayau hi bhūtānām eṣa eva //6//
children.translated_text: Since this is so, the origin and also the dissolution — indeed the origin and dissolution of all beings are from this alone. || 6 ||

MandUpC_6
For this [self], when established in its own nature, is the lord of all — the ruler of the entire collection of differentiated [phenomena] together with the deities (<s>adhidaivika</s>); [this lord] is not of a different species from this [self], unlike in the case of other [lords].
As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'For the mind, O dear one, is bound to <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.2).

children.text: atha gauḍapādīyakārikāḥ
children.translated_text: Now the <s>Kārikās</s> of <s>Gauḍapāda</s>.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.1
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.1

children.text: atraitasmin yathokte 'rtha ete ślokā bhavanti
children.translated_text: On this [Upaniṣad], whose meaning has been stated thus, these verses are [composed]:

children.text: bahiḥprajño vibhuḥ viśvo hy antaḥprajñas tu taijasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The externally conscious (<s>bahiḥprajña</s>) [is] the all-pervading <s>Viśva</s>; the internally conscious (<s>antaḥprajña</s>) is <s>Taijasa</s>;

children.text: ghanaprajñaḥ tathā prājña eka eva tridhā smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: The densely conscious (<s>ghanaprajña</s>) is likewise <s>Prājña</s> — the one [Self] alone is remembered as threefold. || MandUpK 1.1 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.1
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_1.1

children.text: bahiḥprajña iti /
children.translated_text: 'The externally conscious' —

children.text: paryāyeṇa tristhānatvāt sa aham iti smṛtyā pratisandhānāc ca sthānatrayavyatiriktamekatvaṃ śuddhatvam asaṅgatvaṃ ca siddham ity abhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of being in three states in succession, and because of the continuity established through the memory 'I am the same [person],' the oneness, purity, and unattachedness [of the Self] that is distinct from the three states is established — this is the intended meaning.

children.text: mahāmatsyādidṛṣṭāntaśruteḥ //1//
children.translated_text: As [demonstrated] by the <s>śruti</s> examples of the great fish and the like. || 1 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.2
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.2

children.text: jāgaritāvasthāyām eva viśvādīnāṃ trayāṇām anubhavapradarśanārtho 'yaṃ ślokaḥ
children.translated_text: This verse is for the purpose of demonstrating the experience of the three — <s>Viśva</s> and the rest — even in the waking state alone:

children.text: dakṣiṇākṣimukhe viśvo manasy antas tu taijasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> [resides] in the right eye; <s>Taijasa</s> internally, in the mind;

children.text: ākāśe ca hṛdi prājñas tridhā dehe vyavasthitaḥ // MandUpK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Prājña</s> in the space of the heart — [thus the Self] is established in three ways within the body. || MandUpK 1.2 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.2
dakṣiṇam akṣyeva mukhaṃ tasminprādhānyena draṣṭā sthūlānāṃ viśvo 'nubhūyate"indho ha vai nāmaiṣa yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣaḥ" /
iti śruteḥ /
indho dīptiguṇo vaiśvānaraḥ /
ādityāntargato vairāja ātmā cakṣuṣi ca draṣṭaikaḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_1.2
The right eye is the principal opening; in it, as the primary seer of gross [objects], <s>Viśva</s> is experienced — 'Indeed, the person in the right eye is called <s>Indha</s> (the luminous one)'
as the <s>śruti</s> says.
<s>Indha</s>, having the quality of luminosity, is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
The cosmic Self (<s>Vairāja</s>) dwelling within <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) and the seer in the eye are one and the same.

children.text: nanv ayo hiraṇyagarbhaḥ kṣetrajño dakṣiṇo 'kṣi(kṣa)ṇyakṣṇorniyantā draṣṭā cānyo dehasvāmī /
children.translated_text: But is not <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the cosmic embryo), the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), the ruler and seer of the right eye, different [from the individual self], the owner of the body?

children.text:
na svato bhedānabhyupagamāt /
"eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ"(śve.u.6 / 11) iti śruteḥ /
"kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhiṃ sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata" /
(gītā 13 / 2) "āvibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam" /
(gītā 13 / 16) iti smṛteḥ /
"sarveṣu karaṇeṣv aviśeṣe 'pi dakṣiṇākṣaṇy upalabdhipāṭavadarśanāt tatra viśeṣeṇa nirdeśo viśvasya /
children.translated_text:
No, because no inherent difference is accepted.
As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'The one God, hidden in all beings' (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 6.11).
'And know Me as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> in all fields, O <s>Bhārata</s>' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 13.2); 'Undivided among beings, yet appearing as if divided' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 13.16) — so says the <s>smṛti</s>.
'Although there is no distinction among all the sense organs, because the keenness of perception is observed [especially] in the right eye, <s>Viśva</s> is specifically indicated there.'

children.text:
dakṣiṇākṣigato rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā nimīlitākṣas tadeva smaran manasyantaḥ svapna iva tadeva vāsanārūpābhivyaktaṃ paśyati /
yathātra tathā svapne /
ato manasyantas tu taijaso 'pi viśva eva /
children.translated_text:
Having seen a form through the right eye and then closing the eyes, one remembers that very [form] internally in the mind — in dream, as it were, one sees that very thing manifested in the form of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>).
As it is here, so it is in dream.
Therefore, <s>Taijasa</s> too, [residing] internally in the mind, is indeed <s>Viśva</s> [itself].

children.text:
ākāśe ca hṛdi smaraṇākhyavyāpāroparame prājña ekībhūto ghanaprajña eva bhavati manovyāpārābhāvāt /
darśanasmaraṇa eva hi manaḥspandite tadabhāve hṛdyevāviśeṣeṇa prāṇātmanāvasthānam /
"prāṇo hy evaitān sarvān saṃvṛṅkte"(chā.4 / 3 / 3) iti śruteḥ /
taijaso hiraṇyagarbho manaḥsthatvāt /
"liṅgaṃ manaḥ"(bṛ.u4.4.6) /
"manomayo 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ" (bṛ.u5 / 3 / 1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
And <s>Prājña</s> [resides] in the space of the heart — when the activity called remembering ceases, [one becomes] unified, a mass of pure consciousness, because of the absence of mental activity.
For mental vibration is indeed [the cause of] seeing and remembering; in their absence, one abides in the heart alone, without differentiation, as <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath).
As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'For <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed absorbs all these' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.3).
<s>Taijasa</s> is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, because of being situated in the mind.
[As the śrutis say:] 'The mark [of the subtle body] is the mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.6); 'This <s>Puruṣa</s> is made of mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.1), and so on.

children.text:
nanu vyākṛtaḥ prāṇaḥ suṣupte /
tadātmakāni karaṇāni bhavanti /
katham avyākṛtatā?
children.translated_text:
But surely, <s>Prāṇa</s> in deep sleep is differentiated (<s>vyākṛta</s>)?
The sense organs, being of its nature, [still] exist.
How then can there be undifferentiatedness?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣo 'vyākṛtasya deśakālaviśeṣābhāvāt /
yadyapi prāṇābhimāne sati vyākṛtataiva prāṇasya tathāpi piṇḍaparicchinnaviśeṣābhimānanirodhaḥ prāṇobhavatītyavyākṛta eva prāṇaḥ suṣupte paricchinnābhimānavatām /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault, because in the undifferentiated [state] there is no distinction of space and time.
Although <s>Prāṇa</s> is differentiated when there is identification with <s>Prāṇa</s>, nevertheless, when the identification with particular, body-limited [aspects] ceases, it becomes <s>Prāṇa</s> [in its universal form] — thus <s>Prāṇa</s> in deep sleep is indeed undifferentiated for those who had limited identifications.

children.text:
yathā prāṇalaye paricchinnābhimānināṃ prāṇo 'vyākṛtas tathā prāṇābhimānino 'py aviśeṣāpattāvavyākṛtatā samānā prasavabījātmakatvaṃ ca tadadhyakṣaś caiko 'vyākṛtāvasthaḥ /
paricchinnābhimāninām adhyakṣāṇāṃ ca tena ekatvam iti pūrvoktaṃ viśeṣaṇamekībhūta prajñānaghana ityādyupapantam /
tasminn uktahetutvāc ca /
children.translated_text:
Just as <s>Prāṇa</s> is undifferentiated for those with limited identifications when they merge into <s>Prāṇa</s>, so too, when even one who identifies with <s>Prāṇa</s> reaches the state of non-distinction, the undifferentiatedness is the same — [it has] the nature of the seed of [future] creation, and there is one presiding [consciousness] in the undifferentiated state.
The oneness of those with limited identifications and those who preside [over them] with that [undifferentiated state] — thus the previously stated qualification, 'unified, a mass of consciousness,' and so on, is justified.
And because [this state] is the cause, as stated.

children.text: kathaṃ prāṇaśabdatvam avyākṛtasya /
children.translated_text: How can the term '<s>Prāṇa</s>' [be applied] to the undifferentiated?

children.text: "prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya manaḥ"(chā.u6 / 8 / 2) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the mind, O dear one, is bound to <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.2) — so says the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: nanu tatra"sadeva somya"(chā.u6 / 2 / 1) iti prakṛtaṃ sadbrahma prāṇaśabdavācyam /
children.translated_text: But there, what is referred to by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is <s>Sat</s>-<s>Brahman</s>, introduced by 'Being alone, O dear one' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.1).

children.text:
naiṣa doṣo bījātmakatvābhyupagamātsataḥ /
yady api tadbrahma prāṇaśabdavācyaṃ tatra tathāpi jīvaprasavabījātmakatvam apiratyajya eva prāṇaśabdatvaṃ sataḥ sacchabdavācyatā ca /
yadi hi nirbījarūpaṃ vivakṣitaṃ brahmābhaviṣyat"neti neti"(bṛ.u.4.4.2.24.5.15)"yato vāco nivartante"(tai.u.2.9)"anyadeva tadviditād athāviditāt"(ke.u1.3) ityavakṣyata"na sattannāsaducyate"(gītā.13.12) iti smṛteḥ /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault, because <s>Sat</s> is accepted as having the nature of a seed.
Although that <s>Brahman</s> is denoted by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' there, nevertheless, <s>Sat</s> has the designation '<s>Prāṇa</s>' precisely without relinquishing its nature as the seed of the production of individual souls, and it also has the designation '<s>Sat</s>.'
For if the seedless form of <s>Brahman</s> were intended, it would have been expressed as 'Not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.22/4.5.15), 'From which words turn back' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.9), 'It is different from the known and also from the unknown' (<s>Kena Upaniṣad</s> 1.3).
As the <s>smṛti</s> says: 'It is said to be neither existent nor non-existent' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 13.12).

children.text:
nirbījatayaiva cet sati līnānāṃ suṣuptapralayayoḥ punarutthānānupapattiḥ syāt /
muktānāṃ ca punarutpattiprasaṅgo bījābhāvāviśeṣāt /
jñānadāhyabījābhāve ca jñānānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ /
tasmāt sa bījatvābhyupagamena eva sataḥ prāṇatvavyapadeśaḥ sarvaśrutiṣu ca kāraṇatvavyapadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text:
If [<s>Brahman</s>] were seedless alone, then for those who have merged [into it] during deep sleep and dissolution, re-emergence would be impossible.
And there would be the undesirable consequence that the liberated too would be reborn, since there would be no distinction in the absence of seeds.
And if the seeds that are to be burned by knowledge were absent, knowledge itself would become purposeless.
Therefore, it is only by accepting its seed-nature that <s>Sat</s> is designated as '<s>Prāṇa</s>,' and in all <s>śrutis</s> it is designated as the cause.

children.text:
ata eva"akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ"(mu.u2.1.2) /
"sabāhyābhyāntaro hy ajaḥ" (mu.u2.1.2) /
"yato vāco nivartante"(tai.u2.9) /
children.translated_text: 'From which words turn back' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.9);

children.text: "neti neti"(bṛ.u4.4.12) ityādinā bījavatvāpanayanena vyapadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.22) — by such [expressions], the designation [of <s>Brahman</s>] is [made] by removing its seed-nature.

children.text: tāṃ bījāvasthāṃ tasyaiva prājñaśabdavācyasya turīyatvena dehādisaṃbandhajāgradādirahitāṃ pāramārthikīṃ pṛthagvakṣyati /
children.translated_text: That very seed-state of that [<s>Brahman</s>] which is denoted by the word <s>Prājña</s> — its ultimate reality, as the fourth (<s>Turīya</s>), free from association with body and the like, and free from waking and the other [states] — will be separately stated [later].

children.text: bījāvasthāpi na kiñcidavediṣamityutthitasya pratyayadarśanāddehe 'nubhūyata eveti tridhā dehe vyavasthitety ucyate //2//
children.translated_text: Even the seed-state is experienced within the body, since upon waking one perceives the cognition 'I did not know anything' — therefore [the Self] is said to be 'established in three ways within the body.' || 2 ||

Therefore [it is said]: 'Higher than the <s>Akṣara</s> (the imperishable) is the Supreme' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2);
'Both external and internal, [it is] indeed unborn' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2).

children.text: START MandUpK 1.3-4
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.3-4

children.text: viśvaḥ hi sthūlabhuṅ nityaṃ taijasaḥ praviviktabhuk /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> is always the enjoyer of the gross; <s>Taijasa</s> is the enjoyer of the subtle;

children.text: ānandabhuk tathā prājñastridhā bhogaṃ nibodhata // MandUpK_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Prājña</s> is the enjoyer of bliss — know the enjoyment to be threefold. || MandUpK 1.3 ||

children.text: sthūlaṃ tarpayate viśvaṃ praviviktaṃ tu taijasam /
children.translated_text: The gross satisfies <s>Viśva</s>; the subtle [satisfies] <s>Taijasa</s>;

children.text: ānandaś ca tathā prājñaṃ tridhā tṛptiṃ nibodhata // MandUpK_1.4 //
children.translated_text: And likewise bliss [satisfies] <s>Prājña</s> — know the satisfaction to be threefold. || MandUpK 1.4 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.3-4
uktārthau ślokau //3-4 //
children.translated_text: These two verses state what has already been explained. || 3-4 ||
MandUpKC_1.3-4

children.text: START MandUpK 1.5
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.5

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yadbhojyaṃ bhoktā yaś ca prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the three abodes, that which is the enjoyed, and he who is declared as the enjoyer —

children.text: vadaitadubhayaṃ yas tu sa bhuñjāno na lipyate // MandUpK_1.5 //
children.translated_text: He who knows both of these, though enjoying, is not tainted. || MandUpK 1.5 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.5
triṣu dhāmasu jāgradādiṣu sthūlapraviviktānandākhyaṃ bhojyam ekaṃ tridhābhūtam /
yaś ca viśvataijasaprājñākhyo bhoktaikaḥ sa aham ityekatvenapratisaṃdhānāddraṣṭutvāviśeṣāc ca prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the enjoyer, who is one [reality] under the names of <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s>, is declared [to be one] because of the continuity [established] through the recognition 'I am the same,' and because there is no difference in the nature of the seer.

children.text: yo vedaitadubhayaṃ bhojyabhoktṛtayānekadhā bhinnaṃ sa bhuñjāno na lipyate /
children.translated_text: He who knows both of these — which are manifoldly divided as the enjoyed and the enjoyer — though enjoying, is not tainted.

children.text: bhojyasya sarvasyaikasya bhoktur bhojyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because all that is enjoyed is [itself] the object of enjoyment for the one enjoyer.

children.text: na hi yasya yo viṣayaḥ sa tena hīyate vardhate vā na hy agniḥ svaviṣayaṃ dagdhvā kāṣṭhādi tadvat //5//
children.translated_text: For that whose object something is — that is neither diminished nor increased by it. Just as fire, having burned its own object — wood and the like — [is neither diminished nor increased]; so too [is the Self]. || 5 ||

MandUpKC_1.5
In the three abodes — waking and the rest — the enjoyable, which is one [reality] become threefold under the names of gross, subtle, and bliss.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.6
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.6

children.text: prabhavaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ satām iti viniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: That [<s>Brahman</s>] is the origin of all existing things — this is the settled conclusion.

children.text: sarvaṃ janayati prāṇaś ceto 'ṃśūn puruṣaḥ pṛthak // MandUpK_1.6 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Prāṇa</s>] generates everything — the mind-rays; <s>Puruṣa</s> [projects them] separately. || MandUpK 1.6 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.6
satāṃ vidyamānānāṃ svenāvidyākṛtanāmarūpamāyāsvarūpeṇa sarvabhāvānāṃ viśvataijasaprājñabhedānāṃ prabhavotpattiḥ /
vakṣyati ca"vandhyāputro na tattvena māyayā vāpi jāyate"iti /
yadi hy asatām eva janma syād brahmaṇo 'vyavahāryasya grahaṇadvārābhāvādasatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
dṛṣṭaṃ ca rajjusarpādīnām avidyākṛtamāyābījotpannānāṃ rajjvādy ātmanā satvam /
na hi nirāspadā rajjusarpamṛgatṛṣṇikādayaḥ kvacid upalabhyante kenacit /
yathā rajjvāṃ prāksarpotpatte rajjvātmanāṃ sarpaḥ sanneva āsīd evaṃ sarvabhāvānām utpatteḥ prākprāṇabījātmanaiva satvam /
ityataḥ śrutir api vakti"brahmaivedam"(mu.u2.2.11)"ātmaivedam agra āsīt"(bṛ.u.1.4.1) iti /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 1.6: The origination — the production — of all existing entities, differentiated as <s>viśva</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>prājña</s>, through their own form of <s>māyā</s> consisting of name and form created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). And it will be stated: 'The son of a barren woman is not born either in reality or even through <s>māyā</s>.' For if birth were of non-existent things, then <s>Brahman</s>, being beyond transactional usage and having no door of apprehension, would be reduced to non-existence. And it is observed that rope-snakes and the like, which have arisen from the seed of <s>māyā</s> created by <s>avidyā</s>, have their existence as the rope and so forth. For rope-snakes, mirages, and the like are never perceived anywhere by anyone without a substratum. Just as, before the arising of the snake upon the rope, the snake existed as the very nature of the rope, so too before the origination of all entities, their existence was as the very nature of the seed, <s>Prāṇa</s>. Therefore scripture also declares: '<s>Brahman</s> alone is all this' (Muṇḍ. Up. 2.2.11), 'The <s>Ātman</s> alone was this in the beginning' (Bṛh. Up. 1.4.1).

children.text: sarvaṃ janayati prāṇaścetoṃ'śūnaṃśava iva raveś cidātmakasya puruṣasya cetorūpā jalārkasamāḥ prājñataijasaviśvabhedena devatiryagādidehabhedeṣu vibhāvyamānāś cetoṃśavoyetān puruṣaḥ pṛthag viṣayabhāvavilakṣaṇān agniviṣphuliṅgavat salakṣaṇāñjalārkavac ca jīvalakṣaṇāṃstvitarān sarvabhāvān prāṇo bījātmā janayati"yathorṇanābhiḥ"(mu.u.1.1.7)"yathāgneḥ kṣudrārvisphuliṅgāḥ"(bṛ.u.2.1.20) ityādiśruteḥ //6//
children.translated_text: [<s>Prāṇa</s>] generates everything — the mind-rays: just as the rays of the sun, the mind-forms of <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cidātmaka</s>), are like reflections of the sun in water, manifested in the differentiation of bodies — gods, animals, and the like — through the distinction of <s>prājña</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>viśva</s>; these mind-rays, <s>Puruṣa</s> [projects] separately — some, distinct from the nature of objects, bearing [their own] characteristics like sparks from fire, and others, like reflections of the sun in water, bearing the characteristics of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls); all these entities <s>Prāṇa</s>, whose nature is the seed, generates — as scripture states: 'As a spider [emits and withdraws its thread]' (Muṇḍ. Up. 1.1.7), 'As from a fire, tiny sparks [fly forth]' (Bṛh. Up. 2.1.20). || 6 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.7
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.7

children.text: vibhūtiṃ prasavaṃ tv anye manyante sṛṣṭicintakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, who reflect on creation, consider [it to be] a manifestation, a bringing forth;

children.text: svapnamāyāsarūpeti sṛṣṭir anyaiḥ vikalpitā // MandUpK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: By yet others, creation is imagined as being of the nature of dream and <s>māyā</s> (illusion). || MandUpK 1.7 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.7
vibhūtir vistāreśvarasya sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭicintakā manyante na tu paramārthacintakānāṃ sṛṣṭav ādara ity arthaḥ /
"indro māyābhiḥ pururūpeyate" (bṛ.u.2.5.19) iti śruteḥ /
na hi māyāvinaṃ sūtram ākāśe nikṣipya tena sāyudham āruhya cakṣurgocaratām atītya yuddhena khaṇḍaśaśchinnaṃ patitaṃ punarutthitaṃ ca paśyatāṃ tat kṛtaṃ māyādisatatvacintāyām ādaro bhavati /
tathaivāyaṃ māyāvinaḥ sūtraprasāraṇasamaḥ suṣuptasvapnādivikāsastadārūḍhamayāvisamaś ca tatsthaḥ prājñataijasādiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the same way, this [process is] comparable to the magician's extending of the rope — the unfolding through deep sleep, dream, and so forth; and comparable to the magician who has climbed upon it — the one situated thereon as <s>prājña</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and the like.

children.text: sūtratadārūḍhābhyāmanyaḥ paramārthamāyāvī sa eva bhūmiṣṭho māyāchanno 'dṛśyamāna eva sthito yathā tathā turīyākhyaṃ paramārthatattvam /
children.translated_text: The ultimate magician, who is other than the rope and the one who has climbed upon it, stands on the ground, concealed by <s>māyā</s>, unseen — just so is the ultimate reality called <s>Turīya</s> (the Fourth).

children.text: atas tac cintāyām evādaro mumukṣūṇāmāryāṇāṃ na niṣprayojanāyāṃ sṛṣṭav ādara ityataḥ sṛṣṭicintakānām evaite vikalpety āha svapnamāyāsarūpeti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is in the contemplation of that [<s>Turīya</s>] alone that the noble ones seeking liberation have regard, not in the purposeless [contemplation of] creation. Hence he says that these imaginations belong only to those who reflect on creation — '[creation is] of the nature of dream and <s>māyā</s>.'

children.text: svapnarūpā māyāsarūpā ceti //7//
children.translated_text: Of the nature of dream, and of the nature of <s>māyā</s>. || 7 ||

Commentary on MandUpK 1.7: Manifestation means expansion — creation of the Lord: thus think those who reflect on creation — but those who contemplate ultimate reality have no regard for creation, this is the meaning. [As] scripture [says]: '<s>Indra</s> assumes many forms through <s>māyā</s>' (Bṛh. Up. 2.5.19). For just as those who watch a magician cast a rope into the sky, climb up it armed, pass beyond the range of vision, fight, fall cut to pieces, and rise again — they have no regard for the investigation of the reality of the <s>māyā</s> and such [illusions] performed by him.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.8
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.8

children.text: icchāmātraṃ prabhoḥ sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭau viniścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Creation is merely the will of the Lord — thus those who are certain about creation [hold];

children.text: kālāt prasūtiṃ bhūtānāṃ manyante kālacintakāḥ // MandUpK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: Those who reflect on time consider the production of beings to be from time. || MandUpK 1.8 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.8
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 1.8:

children.text: icchāmātraṃ prabhoḥ satyasaṃkalpatvāt sṛṣṭir ghaṭādiḥ saṃkalpanāmātraṃ na saṃkalpanātiriktam /
children.translated_text: Creation is merely the will of the Lord, because He is of unfailing resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>) — [creation such as] pots and the like is mere willing, not anything beyond the act of willing.

children.text: kālād eva sṛṣṭir iti kecit //8//
children.translated_text: Others [hold that] creation is from time alone. || 8 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.9
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 1.9

children.text: bhogārthaṃ sṛṣṭir iti anye krīḍārtham iti cāpare /
children.translated_text: Others [say] creation is for the sake of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>); yet others [say it is] for the sake of sport (<s>krīḍā</s>).

children.text: devasyaiṣa svabhāvo 'yam āptakāmasya kā spṛhā // MandUpK_1.9 //
children.translated_text: This is the very nature of the <s>Deva</s> (God) — for one whose desires are fulfilled, what longing could there be? || MandUpK 1.9 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.9
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 1.9:

children.text: bhogārthaṃ krīḍārtham iti cānye sṛṣṭiṃ manyante /
children.translated_text: Others consider creation to be for the sake of enjoyment or for the sake of sport.

children.text: anayoḥ pakṣayor dūṣaṇaṃ devasyaiṣa svabhāvo 'yam iti devasya svabhāvapakṣam āśritya sarveṣāṃ vā pakṣāṇām āptakāmasya kā spṛheti /
children.translated_text: The refutation of both these views is [given by]: 'This is the very nature of the <s>Deva</s>' — either by adopting the position that it is the nature of God, or as a refutation of all positions: 'For one whose desires are fulfilled (<s>āptakāma</s>), what longing could there be?'

children.text: na hi rajjvādīnām avidyāsvabhāvavyatirekeṇa sarpādyābhāsatve kāraṇaṃ śakyaṃ vaktum //9//
children.translated_text: For indeed, it is not possible to state any cause for the appearance of snakes and the like upon ropes and the like, other than the very nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). || 9 ||

children.text: START MandUp 7
children.translated_text: START MandUp 7

children.text:
caturthaḥ pādaḥ kramaprāpto vaktavya ity āhanāntaḥprajñam ityādinā /
  sarvaśabdapravṛttinimittaśūnyatvāt tasya śabdānabhidheyatvam iti viśeṣapratiṣedhena eva ca turīyaṃ nirdidikṣati /
children.translated_text: The fourth <s>pāda</s> (quarter), which comes next in order, is to be stated — thus [the Upaniṣad] says beginning with 'not inwardly cognitive' and so forth. Because it is devoid of all grounds for the application of words, it is inexpressible by words; and it is <s>Turīya</s> (the Fourth) that [the Upaniṣad] wishes to indicate precisely through the negation of specific attributes.

children.text: śūnyam eva tarhi tat /
children.translated_text: Then is it mere void (<s>śūnya</s>)?

children.text: na mithyāvikalpasya nirnimittatvānupapatter na hi rajatasarpapuruṣamṛgatṛṣṇikādivikalpāḥ śuktikārajjusthāṇur ūṣarādi vyatirekeṇāvastvāspadāḥ śakyāḥ kalpayitum /
children.translated_text: No, because a false superimposition cannot be without a substratum. For the imaginations of silver, snake, person, mirage, and the like cannot be conceived as baseless without the substratum of mother-of-pearl, rope, post, desert, and the like.

children.text:
evaṃ tarhi prāṇādisarvavikalpāspadatvāt turīyasya śabdavācyatvam iti na pratiṣedhaiḥ pratyāyyatvam /
  udakādhārāder iva ghaṭādeḥ /
children.translated_text: If so, then since <s>Turīya</s> is the substratum of all imaginations such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, it should be expressible by words — so it should not be indicated through negations; just as a pot is [indicated as the container] of water and the like.

children.text:
na prāṇādivikalpasyāsatvāc chuktikādiṣv iva rajatādeḥ /
  na hi sadasatoḥ saṃbandhaḥ śabdapravṛttinimittabhāgavastutvāt /
  nāpi pramāṇāntaraviṣayatvaṃ svarūpeṇa gavādivad ātmano nirupādhikatvād /
  gavādivan nāpi jātimatvamadvitīyatvena sāmānyaviśeṣābhāvāt /
  nāpi kriyāvatvaṃ pācakādivadavikriyatvāt /
  nāpi guṇavatvaṃ nīlādivan nirguṇatvāt /
  ato nābhidhānena nirdeśam arhati /
children.translated_text: No, because the imaginations of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest are unreal, like silver in mother-of-pearl and the like. For there is no relation between the real and the unreal, since the ground for the application of words is [only] a real entity. Nor is [<s>Turīya</s>] an object of another means of knowledge in its own nature, like a cow, because the <s>Ātman</s> is without limiting adjuncts (<s>nirupādhika</s>). Nor does it possess universal class-nature (<s>jātimatva</s>) like a cow, because being non-dual, there is an absence of genus and species. Nor does it possess activity, like a cook, because it is actionless (<s>avikriya</s>). Nor does it possess qualities, like [something] blue, because it is without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). Therefore it does not merit designation by a name.

children.text: śaśaviṣāṇādisamatvān nirarthakatvaṃ tarhi /
children.translated_text: Then is it meaningless, like the horns of a hare?

children.text:
nātmatvāvagame turīyasyānātmatṛṣṇāvyāvṛttihetutvāc chuktikāvagama iva rajatatṛṣṇāyāḥ /
  na hi turīyasyātmatvāvagame satyavidyātṛṣṇādidoṣāṇāṃ sambhavo 'sti /
  na ca turīyasyā'tmatvānavagame kāraṇamasti sarvopaniṣadāṃ tādarthyenopakṣayāt /
  "tatvamasi"(chā.u.6.8.16)"ayamātmā brahma"(bṛ.u.2.5.19)"tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā"(chā.u.6.8.16)"yatsākṣādaṣarokṣādbrahma"(bṛ.u.3.4.1)"sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ"(mu.u.2.1.2) /
  "ātmaivedaṃ sarvam"(chā.u.7.25.2) ityādīnām /
children.translated_text: No, because when <s>Turīya</s> is realized as the <s>Ātman</s>, it serves as the cause for the cessation of the craving for the non-<s>Ātman</s>, just as the recognition of mother-of-pearl [causes the cessation] of the craving for silver. For when <s>Turīya</s> is realized as the <s>Ātman</s>, there is no possibility of the defects of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), craving, and the like. And there is no reason for the non-realization of <s>Turīya</s> as the <s>Ātman</s>, since all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> converge toward this purpose: 'You are That' (Chānd. Up. 6.8.16), 'This <s>Ātman</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' (Bṛh. Up. 2.5.19), 'That is the truth, that is the <s>Ātman</s>' (Chānd. Up. 6.8.16), 'That which is directly perceived, the immediate <s>Brahman</s>' (Bṛh. Up. 3.4.1), 'For it is unborn, both externally and internally' (Muṇḍ. Up. 2.1.2), '<s>Ātman</s> alone is all this' (Chānd. Up. 7.25.2), and so forth.

children.text:
so 'yam ātmā paramārthāparamārtharūpaś catuṣpāda ity uktas tasyāparamārtharūpam avidyākṛtaṃ rajjusarpādisamam uktaṃ pādatrayalakṣaṇaṃ bījāṅkurasthānīyam /
  athedānīṃ bījātmakaṃ paramārthasvarūpaṃ rajjusthānīyaṃ sarpādisthānīyoktasthānatrayānirākaraṇenāha nāntaḥ prajñamityādi /
children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s>, described as having four quarters, having both an ultimate and non-ultimate aspect — its non-ultimate aspect, created by <s>avidyā</s>, comparable to a rope-snake, has been described as the three quarters, standing in the relation of seed and sprout. Now, its ultimate nature, which is the seed-nature, comparable to the rope, is stated through the negation of the three states comparable to the snake and the like — [the Upaniṣad] says 'not inwardly cognitive' and so forth.

children.text:
nāntaḥprajñaṃ na bahiḥprajñaṃ nobhayataḥprajñaṃ na prajñānaghanaṃ na prajñaṃ nāprajñam |
  adṛṣṭam avyavahāryam agrāhyam alakṣaṇam acintyam avyapadeśyam ekātmapratyayasāraṃ prapañcopaśamaṃ śāntaṃ śivam advaitaṃ caturthaṃ manyante |
  sa ātmā sa vijñeyaḥ || MandUp_7 ||
children.translated_text: Not inwardly cognitive, not outwardly cognitive, not cognitive in both ways, not a mass of cognition, not cognitive, and not non-cognitive. Unseen, beyond transactional usage, ungraspable, without defining marks, unthinkable, indescribable, whose essence is the conviction of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>, the cessation of the phenomenal world, peaceful, auspicious, non-dual — [this] they consider to be the Fourth. That is the <s>Ātman</s>; that is to be known. || MandUp 7 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_7
  nanv ātmanaś catuṣpātvaṃ pratijñāya prādatrayakathanena eva caturthasyāntaḥ prajñādibhyo anyatve siddhe nāntaḥ prajña ityādi pratiṣedho 'narthakaḥ /
  na sarpādivikalpapratiṣedhena eva rajjusvarūpapratipattivattryavasthasya evātmanas turīyatvena pratipipādayiṣitatvāt /
  "tattvamasi"(chā.u.6.8.16) itivat /
  yadi hi tryavasthātmavilakṣaṇaṃ turīyam anyat tatpratipattidvārābhāvācchāstropadeśānarthakyaṃ śūnyatāpattir vā /
  rajjur iva sarpādibhirvikalpyamānā sthānatraye 'py ātmaika evāntaḥ prajñāditvena vikalpyate yadā tadāntaḥ prajñatvādipratiṣedhavijñānapramāṇasamakālamevātmany anarthaprapañcanivṛttilakṣaṇaphalaṃ parisamāptam iti turīyādhigame pramāṇāntaraṃ sādhanāntaraṃ vā ma mṛgyam /
  rajjusarpavivekasamakāla iva rajjvāṃ sarpanivṛttiphale sati rajjvadhigayasya /
  yeṣāṃ punas tamo 'panayavyatirekeṇa ghaṭādhigame pramāṇaṃ vyāpriyate teṣāṃ chedyāvayavasambandhaviyogavyatirekeṇāny anyatarāvayave 'picchidirvyā priyata ity uktaṃ syāt /
  yadā punarghaṭatamaso vivekakaraṇe pravṛttaṃ pramāṇamanupāditsitatamonivṛttiphalāvasānaṃ chidirivacchedyāvayavasaṃbandhavivekakaraṇe pravṛttā tadavayavadvaidhībhāvaphalāvasānā tathā nāntarīyakaṃ ghaṭavijñānaṃ na tat pramāṇaphalam /
  na ca tadvad apy ātmany adhyāropitāntaḥ prajñatvādivivekakaraṇe pravṛttasya pratiṣedhavijñānapramāṇasyānupāditsitāntaḥ prajñatvadinivṛttivyatirekeṇa turīye vyāpāra upapattiḥ /
  antaḥ prajñatvādinivṛttisamakālameva pramātṛtvādibhedanivṛtteḥ /
  tathā ca vakṣyati"jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyate"(māṇḍū.kā.1.18) iti /
  jñānasya dvaitanivṛttikṣaṇavyatirekeṇa kṣaṇāntarānavasthānāt /
  avasthāne cānavasthāprasaṅgād dvaitānivṛttiḥ /
  tasmāt pratiṣedhavijñānapramāṇavyāpārasamakālair vātmany adhyāropitāntaḥ prajñatvādyanarthānivṛttir iti siddham /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUp 7: Objection: having proposed that the <s>Ātman</s> has four quarters and having described [only] three quarters, the otherness of the Fourth from the inwardly cognitive and the rest is already established; therefore the negation 'not inwardly cognitive' and so forth is purposeless. Reply: no, because it is intended to demonstrate that the <s>Ātman</s> in its three states is itself <s>Turīya</s> — just as the rope's own nature is understood through the negation of the imaginations of snake and the like; [similarly] as in 'You are That' (Chānd. Up. 6.8.16). For if <s>Turīya</s> were something entirely different from the <s>Ātman</s> in its three states, then due to the absence of any door of apprehension, scriptural teaching would be purposeless, or the consequence of voidness would follow. Just as a rope is imagined as a snake and the like, so the one <s>Ātman</s> alone is imagined in its three states as inwardly cognitive and so forth; when [this is understood], simultaneously with the cognition that negates the inwardly cognitive nature and the rest, the result — the cessation of the purposeless phenomenal projection upon the <s>Ātman</s> — is complete. Therefore, in realizing <s>Turīya</s>, no other means of knowledge or other means of attainment need be sought — just as no [other means is needed] for one who has realized the rope, once the result of the cessation of the snake in the rope is attained simultaneously with the discrimination between the rope and the snake. For those who hold that a means of knowledge operates independently of the removal of darkness to apprehend a pot, it would follow that a cutting instrument would operate upon yet another part of an object even apart from the severing of the connection of the parts of the object to be cut. But when a means of knowledge, having been employed for discriminating between a pot and darkness, culminates in the result of the unintended removal of darkness — like a cutting instrument employed for discriminating the parts of an object to be cut, which culminates in the result of the bifurcation of those parts — then the knowledge of the pot is an inevitable [consequence], not the fruit of the means of knowledge [per se]. Likewise, for the means of knowledge consisting of the negating cognition, which is employed for discriminating the superimposed inwardly cognitive nature and the rest upon the <s>Ātman</s>, there is no operation upon <s>Turīya</s> apart from the unintended removal of the inwardly cognitive nature and the rest — because simultaneously with the cessation of the inwardly cognitive nature and the rest, the distinction of the knower and the like also ceases. And thus it will be said: 'When [non-duality] is known, duality does not exist' (Māṇḍ. Kā. 1.18). Because knowledge does not persist for a moment beyond the moment of the cessation of duality; and if it did persist, there would be an infinite regress, and duality would not cease. Therefore it is established that simultaneously with the operation of the means of knowledge consisting of the negating cognition, the purposeless projections of inwardly cognitive nature and the rest superimposed on the <s>Ātman</s> cease.

children.text:
nāntaḥ prajñam iti taijasapratiṣedho na bahiṣprajñam iti viśvapratiṣedhaḥ /
  na ubhayataḥ prajñam iti jāgratsvaprayorantarālāvasthāpratiṣedhaḥ /
  na prajñānaghanam iti suṣuptāvasthāpratiṣedho bījabhāvāvivekarūpatvāt /
  na prajñam iti yugapatsarvaviṣaprajñātṛtvapratiṣedhaḥ /
  nāprajñam iti caitanyapratiṣedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not inwardly cognitive' is the negation of <s>taijasa</s>; 'not outwardly cognitive' is the negation of <s>viśva</s>; 'not cognitive in both ways' is the negation of the intermediate state between waking and dream; 'not a mass of cognition' is the negation of the deep sleep state, because it is of the nature of the seed-state without discrimination; 'not cognitive' is the negation of being the cognizer of all objects simultaneously; 'not non-cognitive' is the negation [of the absence] of consciousness.

children.text:
kathaṃ punarantaḥ prajñatvādīnām ātmani gamyamānānāṃ rajjvādau sarpādivat pratiṣedhādasatvaṃ gamyata ity ucyate /
  jñasvarūpāviśeṣe 'pītaretaravyabhicārādrajjvādāv iva sarpadhārādivikalpita bhedavat sarvatrāvyabhicārājjñasvarūpasya satyatvam /
children.translated_text: But how is it understood that the inwardly cognitive nature and the rest, which are apprehended in the <s>Ātman</s>, are unreal through their negation, like a snake upon a rope? It is replied: although there is no difference in the nature of the knower [across states], since each [state] is absent in the others — just as the various imaginations of snake, stream, and the like upon a rope — the reality of the knower-nature [belongs to that] which is invariable everywhere, unlike the variable [imaginations].

children.text:
suṣupte vyabhicaratīti cen na /
  suṣuptasyānubhūyamānatvāt"na hi vijñātur vijñāter viparalopo vidyate"(bṛ.u.4.3.30) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: If one objects that [the knower-nature] is absent in deep sleep — no, because deep sleep is experienced [as having been undergone]; as scripture says: 'For there is no cessation of the knowing of the knower' (Bṛh. Up. 4.3.30).

children.text:
ata evādṛṣṭam /
  yasmād adṛṣṭaṃ tasmād avyavahāryam /
  agrāhyaṃ karmendriyaiḥ /
  alakṣaṇamaliṅgam ity etad ananumey ity arthaḥ /
  ata evācintyam /
  ata evāvyapadeśyaṃ śabdaiḥ /
  ekātmapratyayasāraṃ jāgradādisthāneṣv eko 'yam ātmetyavyabhicārī yaḥ pratyayastenānusaraṇīyam /
  athavaika ātmapratyayaḥ sāraṃ pramāṇaṃ yasya turīyasyādhigame tat turīyamekātmapratyayasāram /
  "ātmetyevopāsīta"(bṛ.u.1.4.7) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore [it is] 'unseen' (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>). Because it is unseen, it is 'beyond transactional usage' (<s>avyavahārya</s>). 'Ungraspable' (<s>agrāhya</s>) — by the organs of action. 'Without defining marks' (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) means without inferential marks — that is, it is not inferable. Therefore it is 'unthinkable' (<s>acintya</s>). Therefore it is 'indescribable' (<s>avyapadeśya</s>) by words. 'Whose essence is the conviction of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>' (<s>ekātmapratyayasāra</s>) — that invariable conviction 'this is one <s>Ātman</s>' which [persists] across the states of waking and so forth — by that [conviction <s>Turīya</s>] is to be traced. Alternatively: that whose essential means of knowledge (<s>sāra</s>) for the realization of <s>Turīya</s> is the single <s>Ātman</s>-conviction — that is <s>Turīya</s>, whose essence is the conviction of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>. As scripture says: 'One should meditate [upon it] as the <s>Ātman</s> alone' (Bṛh. Up. 1.4.7).

children.text:
antaḥ prajñatvādisthānidharmaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ kṛtaḥ /
  prapañca upaśamam iti jāgradādisthānadharmābhāvocyate /
ata eva śāntamavikriyaṃ śivaṃ yato 'dvaitaṃ bhedavikalparahitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is 'peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>) — without modification; 'auspicious' (<s>śiva</s>) — because it is non-dual (<s>advaita</s>), devoid of the imagination of differentiation.

children.text: caturthaṃ turīyaṃ manyante pratīyamānapādatrayarūpavailakṣaṇyāt /
children.translated_text: The Fourth (<s>Turīya</s>) — [so called because] they consider [it] the fourth, due to its distinctness from the nature of the three apparent quarters.

children.text: sa ātmā sa vijñeya iti pratīyamānasarpabhūchidradaṇḍādivyatiriktā yathā rajjus tathā tattvamasītyādivākyārtha ātmā"adṛṣṭo draṣṭā"(bṛ.u.3.7.23)"na hi draṣṭur dṛṣṭeviparilopo vidyate"(bṛ.u.4.3.23) ityādibhirukto yaḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is to be known — just as the rope is distinct from the apparent snake, the hole in the ground, the staff, and so on, so the meaning of sentences like '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art') is the <s>Ātman</s>, which has been spoken of through [statements such as] 'the unseen seer' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.7.23), 'for there is no cessation of the seeing of the seer' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23), and the like.

children.text: sa vijñeya iti bhūtapūrvagatyā jñāte dvaitābhāvaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: That is to be known — and upon knowing, in the manner of what has been established before, duality ceases to exist. || 7 ||

The negation of the properties of the superimposed states such as inwardly cognitive and the rest has been made. 'The cessation of the phenomenal world' (<s>prapañcopaśama</s>) — by this, the absence of the properties of the states of waking and so forth is stated.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.10
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.10

children.text: atraite ślokā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Here are the verses on this:

children.text: nivṛtteḥ sarvaduḥkhānām īśānaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The lord of the cessation of all sufferings, the sovereign, the imperishable,

children.text: advaitaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ devās turyo vibhuḥ smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_1.10 //
children.translated_text: The non-dual of all entities, the luminous one, the fourth (<s>Turya</s>), the all-pervading — so it is declared. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.10 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.10
prājñataijasaviśvalakṣaṇānāṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ nivṛtte īśānas turīya ātmā /
īśāna ity asya vyākhyānaṃ prabhur iti /
duḥkhanivṛttiṃ prati prabhur bhavatīty arthaḥ /
tad vijñānanimittatvād duḥkhanivṛtteḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.10: The fourth <s>Ātman</s> (<s>Turīya</s>) is the lord (<s>Īśāna</s>) of the cessation of all sufferings characterized by <s>Prājña</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Viśva</s>. The explanation of '<s>Īśāna</s>' is '<s>Prabhu</s>' (sovereign). The meaning is: he is the sovereign with respect to the cessation of suffering, because the cessation of suffering is contingent upon the knowledge of that [<s>Turīya</s>].

children.text: avyayo na vyeti svarūpān na vyabhicaratīti yāvat /
children.translated_text: 'Imperishable' (<s>avyaya</s>) — he does not depart from his own nature; that is, he does not deviate [from it].

children.text: etat kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: How is this known?

children.text: yasmād advaitaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ rajjusarpavanmṛṣātvāt sa eṣa devo dyotanāt turīyaś caturtho vibhuvyāpī smṛtaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: Because he is non-dual (<s>advaita</s>) of all entities — since [all entities are] false like a snake [projected] on a rope. This luminous one (<s>deva</s>), so called because of his self-luminosity (<s>dyotana</s>), the fourth (<s>Turīya</s>), is declared to be all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>). || 10 ||

children.text:
START MandUpK 1.11
viśvādīnāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvo nirūpyate turyayāthātmyāvadhāraṇārtham
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.11. The relation of genus and species among <s>Viśva</s> and the rest is examined, for the purpose of ascertaining the true nature of <s>Turya</s>.

children.text: kāryakāraṇabaddhau tāv iṣyete viśvataijasau /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> are held to be bound by cause and effect;

children.text: prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhas tu dvau tau turye na sidhyataḥ // MandUpK_1.11 //
children.translated_text: But <s>Prājña</s> is bound by cause alone — those two [i.e., cause and effect] do not obtain in <s>Turya</s>. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.11 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.11
kāryaṃ kriyata iti phalabhāvaḥ /
kāraṇaṃ karotīti bījabhāvaḥ /
tattvāgrahaṇān yathāgrahaṇābhyāṃ bījaphalabhāvābhyāṃ tau yathoktau viśvataijasau baddhau saṃgṛhītāviṣyete /
children.translated_text: Due to non-apprehension of reality and mis-apprehension of it — by these two states of seed and fruit — <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> as described are bound, that is, held fast.

children.text: prājñas tu bījabhāvenaiva baddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Prājña</s> is bound by the seed-state alone.

children.text: tattvāpratibodhamātram eva hi bījaṃ prājñatve nimittam /
children.translated_text: For indeed, mere non-awakening to reality is the seed that is the cause of the state of <s>Prājña</s>.

children.text: tato dvau tau bījaphalabhāvau tatvāgrahaṇān yathā grahaṇe turye na sidhyato na vidyete na sambhavata ity arthaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: Therefore, those two — the seed-state and the fruit-state, characterized by non-apprehension and mis-apprehension of reality — do not obtain, do not exist, are not possible in <s>Turya</s>. || 11 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.11: 'Effect' (<s>kārya</s>) is what is produced — the state of being a result. 'Cause' (<s>kāraṇa</s>) is what produces — the state of being a seed.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.12
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.12

children.text:
kathaṃ punaḥ kāraṇabaddhatvaṃ prājñasya turīye vā tattvāgrahaṇān yathāgrahaṇalakṣaṇau bandhau na sidhyata iti /
yasmāt
children.translated_text: But how is it that <s>Prājña</s> is bound by cause, while in <s>Turīya</s> the two bonds characterized by non-apprehension and mis-apprehension of reality do not obtain? Because —

children.text: nātmānaṃ na parāś caiva na satyaṃ na api cānṛtam /
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> cognizes nothing at all — neither the self, nor others,

children.text: prājñaḥ kiñcana saṃvetti turyaṃ tat sarvadṛk sadā // MandUpK_1.12 //
children.translated_text: neither truth nor falsehood either; <s>Turya</s> is the all-seeing, always. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.12 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.12
ātmavilakṣaṇam avidyābījaprasūtaṃ bāhyaṃ dvaitaṃ prājño na kiñcana saṃvetti tathā viśvataijasau /
tataś cāsau tattvāgrahaṇena tamasānyathā grahaṇabījabhūtena baddho bhavati /
yasmāt turīyaṃ tatsarvadṛksadā turīyādanyasyābhāvāt sarvadā sadaivaiti sarvaṃ ca tadddṛkceti sarvadṛk tasmān na tattvāgrahaṇalakṣaṇaṃ bījaṃ tatra /
tat prasūtasyānyathāgrahaṇasyāpyataivābhāvo na hi savitari sadā prākāśātmake tad viruddham aprakāśanam anyathā prakāśanaṃ vā sambhavati /
"na hi draṣṭur dṛṣṭer viparilopo vidyate"
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.12: <s>Prājña</s> cognizes nothing at all of external duality, which is different from the Self and sprung from the seed of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); likewise <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> [in deep sleep]. And therefore he is bound by the darkness of non-apprehension of reality, which is the seed of mis-apprehension.
