Since <s>Turīya</s> is the all-seeing always — because there is nothing other than <s>Turīya</s>, it is always, ever thus — and it sees all, hence 'all-seeing.' Therefore in it there is no seed characterized by non-apprehension of reality. And because of the absence of that [seed], mis-apprehension born from it is also absent. For indeed, in the sun, which is always of the nature of light, neither the contradictory [state of] darkness nor false illumination is possible. 'For there is no cessation of the seeing of the seer'

children.text: (bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23) — so the <s>śruti</s> declares.

children.text: atha vā jāgratsvapnayoḥ sarvabhūtāvasthaḥ sarvavastudṛgābhāsas turīyaiveti sarvadṛksadā"nānyad ato 'sti draṣṭṛ"(bṛ.u.3.8.11) ityādi śruteḥ //12//
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in waking and dream, [<s>Turīya</s>] abides as the substratum of all beings, appearing as the seer of all objects — it is indeed <s>Turīya</s> alone, and hence 'all-seeing, always,' as per the <s>śruti</s>: 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.8.11). || 12 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.13
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.13

children.text: dvaitasyāgrahaṇaṃ tulyam ubhayoḥ prājñaturyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The non-apprehension of duality is alike in both <s>Prājña</s> and <s>Turya</s>;

children.text: bījanidrāyutaḥ prājñaḥ sā ca turye na vidyate // MandUpK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is conjoined with the sleep of the seed — and that [sleep] does not exist in <s>Turya</s>. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.13 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.13
nimittāntaraprāptāśaṅkānivṛtyartho 'yaṃ ślokaḥ /
kathaṃ dvaitāgrahaṇasya tulyatvāt kāraṇabaddhatvaṃ prājñasya eva na turīyasyeti prāptāśaṅkā nivartyate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.13: This verse is for the purpose of removing a doubt that might arise from another ground. The doubt that arises — namely, how is it that only <s>Prājña</s> is causally bound and not <s>Turīya</s>, given that non-apprehension of duality is the same [in both]? — is being removed.

children.text: yasmādbījanidrāyutas tattvāpratibodho nidrā /
children.translated_text: Because [<s>Prājña</s>] is conjoined with the sleep of the seed: non-awakening to reality is 'sleep' (<s>nidrā</s>).

children.text: sa eva ca viśeṣapratibodhaprasavasya bījaṃ sā bījanidrā tayā yutaḥ prājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [non-awakening] itself is the seed of the arising of specific [mis-]cognition — that is the 'seed-sleep' (<s>bījanidrā</s>); conjoined with it is <s>Prājña</s>.

children.text: sadā dṛksvabhāvatvāt tattvāpratibodhalakṣaṇā nidrā turīye na vidyate 'to na kāraṇabandhastasminnityābhiprāyaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: Since [<s>Turya</s>] is always of the nature of seeing, the sleep characterized by non-awakening to reality does not exist in <s>Turya</s> — hence there is no causal bondage in it. This is the intended meaning. || 13 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.14
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.14

children.text: svapnanidrāyutāv ādyau prājñas tv asvapnanidrayā /
children.translated_text: The first two [<s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s>] are conjoined with dream and sleep; <s>Prājña</s>, however, with dreamless sleep.

children.text: na nidrāṃ naiva ca svapnaṃ turye paśyanti niścitaḥ // MandUpK_1.14 //
children.translated_text: Those established [in knowledge] see neither sleep nor dream in <s>Turya</s>. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.14 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.14
svapno 'nyathāgrahaṇaṃ sarpa iva rajjvām /
nidroktā tattvāpratibodhalakṣaṇaṃ tama iti /
tābhyāṃ svapnanidrābhyāṃ yuktau viśvataijasau /
atas tau kāryakāraṇabaddhāv ity uktau /
children.translated_text: Therefore they were said to be bound by both cause and effect.

children.text: prājñas tu svapnavarjitakevalaiva nidrayā yuta iti kāraṇabaddha ity uktam /
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s>, however, is conjoined with sleep alone, devoid of dream — hence he was said to be bound by cause [alone].

children.text: nobhayaṃ paśyanti turīye niścitā brahmavido viruddhatvāt savitarīva tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those established in <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge do not see either [dream or sleep] in <s>Turya</s>, because they are contradictory [to it], like darkness in the sun.

children.text: ato na kāryakāraṇabaddha ity uktas turīyaḥ //14//
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Turīya</s> has been declared to be not bound by cause and effect. || 14 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.14: 'Dream' (<s>svapna</s>) is mis-apprehension, like a snake [seen] on a rope. 'Sleep' (<s>nidrā</s>) has been described as the darkness characterized by non-awakening to reality. With these two — dream and sleep — <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> are conjoined.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.15
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.15

children.text: kadā turīye niścito bhavatītyucyate
children.translated_text: When does one become established in <s>Turya</s>? It is said —

children.text: anyathā gṛhṇataḥ svapno nidrā tattvam ajānataḥ /
children.translated_text: Dream [belongs to] one who mis-apprehends; sleep [belongs to] one who does not know reality.

children.text: viparyāse tayoḥ kṣīṇe turīyaṃ padam aśnute // MandUpK_1.15 //
children.translated_text: When the error of both is exhausted, one attains the state of <s>Turya</s>. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.15 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.15
svapnajāgaritayoranyathā rajvāṃ sarpa iva gṛhṇatastattvaṃ svapno bhavati /
nidrā tattvam ajānatas tisṛṣvavasthāsu tulyā /
svapnanidrayos tulyatvād viśvataijasayor ekarāśitvam /
anyathāgrahaṇaprādhānyāc ca guṇabhūtā nidreti tasmin viparyāsaḥ svapnaḥ /
tṛtīye tu sthānetattvājñānalakṣaṇā nidraiva kevalā viparyāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.15: For one who mis-apprehends — like a snake on a rope — in waking and dream, there is dream (<s>svapna</s>). Sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) is the same across all three states for one who does not know reality. Since dream and sleep are alike, <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> form a single group. And since mis-apprehension predominates, sleep is subsidiary to it — the error in that [pair] is dream. But in the third state, the error is solely sleep characterized by non-knowledge of reality.

children.text: atas tayoḥ kāryakāraṇasthānayor anyathāgrahaṇāgrahaṇalakṣaṇaviparyāse kāryakāraṇabandharūpe paramārthatatvapritabodhataḥ kṣīṇe turīyaṃ padam aśnute /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the error of both — the states of effect and cause, characterized by mis-apprehension and non-apprehension, which constitute bondage in the form of effect and cause — is exhausted through the awakening to ultimate reality, one attains the state of <s>Turya</s>.

children.text: tadobhayalakṣaṇaṃ bandharūpaṃ tatrāpaśyaṃs turīye niścito bhavatīty arthaḥ //15//
children.translated_text: Not seeing that bondage characterized by both [mis-apprehension and non-apprehension] in <s>Turya</s>, one becomes established in <s>Turya</s> — this is the meaning. || 15 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.16
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.16

children.text: anādimāyayā supto yadā jīvaḥ prabudhyate /
children.translated_text: When the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), asleep due to beginningless <s>māyā</s>, awakens,

children.text: ajam anidram asvapnam advaitaṃ budhyate tadā // MandUpK_1.16 //
children.translated_text: Then it realizes the unborn, sleepless, dreamless, non-dual [<s>Turya</s>]. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.16 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.16
yo 'yaṃ saṃsārī jīvaḥ sobhayalakṣaṇena tattvāpratibodharūpeṇa bījātmanānyathāgrahaṇalakṣaṇena cānādikālapravṛttena māyālakṣaṇena svapnena mamāyaṃ pitā putro 'yaṃ naptā kṣetraṃ paśavo 'ham eṣāṃ svāmī sukhī duḥkhī kṣayito 'ham anena vardhitaś cānena ity evaṃprakārān svapnān sthānadvaye 'pi paśyan suptaḥ /
yadā vedāntārthatattvābhijñena paramakāruṇikena guruṇā nāsyaivaṃ tvaṃ hetuphalātmakaḥ kiṃ tu tattvam asīti pratibodhyamānas tadaivaṃ pratibudhyate
katham? nāsmin bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ vā janmādibhāvavikāro 'sty ato 'jaṃ sabāhyābhyantarasarvabhāvikāravarjitam ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: How? Because no modification of being such as birth and the like — either external or internal — exists in it, [<s>Turya</s> is] unborn (<s>aja</s>), meaning devoid of all modifications of entities both external and internal.

children.text: yasmāj janmādikāraṇabhūtaṃ nāsminn avidyātamobījaṃ nidrā vidyata ity anidram /
children.translated_text: Since the sleep of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — the darkness which is the seed and cause of birth and the rest — does not exist in it, it is sleepless (<s>anidra</s>).

children.text: anidraṃ hi tat turīyamata evāsvapnaṃ tan nimittatvād anyathāgrahaṇasya /
children.translated_text: Being sleepless, that <s>Turīya</s> is therefore also dreamless (<s>asvapna</s>), since mis-apprehension is caused by that [sleep].

children.text: yasmāc cānidram asvapnaṃ tasmād ajam advaitaṃ turīyam ātmānaṃ budhyate tadā //16//
children.translated_text: And since it is sleepless and dreamless, therefore [the <s>jīva</s>] realizes the unborn, non-dual <s>Turīya Ātman</s>. || 16 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.16: This <s>jīva</s>, the transmigrating soul, seeing dreams of the following kind in both states [waking and dream] — 'this is my father,' 'this is my son,' 'this is my grandson,' 'these are my fields,' 'these are my cattle,' 'I am their master,' 'I am happy,' 'I am miserable,' 'I am ruined by this,' 'I have prospered through that' — [it is] asleep due to the dreamlike <s>māyā</s> that has been operative since beginningless time, characterized by both non-awakening to reality in the form of a seed and mis-apprehension. When, by a supremely compassionate teacher who knows the truth of <s>Vedānta</s>, it is awakened [with the instruction]: 'You are not thus, constituted of cause and effect; rather, <s>tat tvam asi</s> (That thou art)' — then it awakens thus.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.17
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.17

children.text: prapañcanivṛtyā cet pratibudhyate 'nivṛtte prapañce katham advaitam ity ucyate
children.translated_text: If [one says] one awakens through the cessation of the phenomenal world — [then] if the phenomenal world has ceased, how [can it be] non-dual? It is replied —

children.text: prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) were real, it would indeed cease — there is no doubt.

children.text: māyāmātram idaṃ dvaitam advaitaṃ paramārthataḥ // MandUpK_1.17 //
children.translated_text: This duality is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion); non-duality alone is the ultimate reality. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.17 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.17
satyam avaṃ syāt prapañco yadi vidyeta rajjvāṃ sarpa iva kalpitatvān na tu sa vidyate /
vidyamānaś cen nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If it were real, it would indeed cease — there is no doubt.

children.text: na hi rajjvāṃ bhrāntibuddhyā kalpitaḥ sarpo vidyamānaḥ sanvivekato nivṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: For a snake imagined on a rope through deluded cognition does not, being [truly] existent, cease through discrimination.

children.text: naiva māyā māyāvinā prayuktā tad darśināṃ cakṣurbandhāpagame vidyamānā satī nivṛttā /
children.translated_text: Nor does <s>māyā</s> (illusion) employed by a magician, when the eye-deception of the spectators is removed, cease as something that [truly] existed.

children.text: tathedaṃ prapañcākhyaṃ māyāmātraṃ dvaitaṃ rajjuvan māyāvivaccadvaitaṃ paramārthatas tasmān na kaścit prapañcaḥ pravṛtto nivṛtto vāstītīty abhiprāyaḥ //17//
children.translated_text: Likewise, this duality called the phenomenal world is mere <s>māyā</s>; like the rope [underlying the snake], like the magician [behind the illusion], it is non-dual in ultimate reality. Therefore no phenomenal world has ever arisen or ceased — this is the intended meaning. || 17 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.17: True, it would be so if the phenomenal world were real, like a snake on a rope — but since it is imagined, it does not [truly] exist.

children.text:
START MandUpK 1.18
nanu śāstā śāstraṃ śiṣya iti vikalpaḥ kathaṃ nivartata ity ucyate
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.18. But how does the differentiation of teacher, scripture, and student cease? It is said —

children.text: vikalpo vinivarteta kalpito yadi kenacit /
children.translated_text: The differentiation would cease if it were imagined by someone.

children.text: upadeśād ayaṃ vādo jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyate // MandUpK_1.18 //
children.translated_text: This teaching is [only] a provisional statement; when [reality is] known, duality does not exist. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.18 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.18
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.18:

children.text: vikalpo vinivarteta yadi kenacit kalpitaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: The differentiation would cease if it were imagined by someone.

children.text: yathāyaṃ prapañco māyārajjusarpavat tathāyaṃ śiṣyādi bhedavikalpo 'pi prāk pratibodhādevopadeśanimitto 'topadeśādayaṃ vādaḥ śiṣyaḥ śāstā śāstram iti /
children.translated_text: Just as this phenomenal world is like the <s>māyā</s>-snake on a rope, so too this differentiation of student and the rest is [only valid] prior to awakening, being occasioned by instruction. Therefore, this teaching — [the distinction of] student, teacher, and scripture — is [only] a provisional statement.

children.text: upadeśakārye tu jñāne nirvṛtte jñāte paramārthatatve dvaitaṃ na vidyate //18//
children.translated_text: But when the purpose of instruction — knowledge — has been accomplished, when the ultimate reality is known, duality does not exist. || 18 ||

children.text:
START MandUp 8
  abhidheyapradhāna oṃkāraś catuṣpādātmeti vyākhyāto yaḥ
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 8. Having explained <s>Oṃkāra</s> with the denotation as primary, as being the Self with four quarters,

children.text:
so 'yam ātmādhyakṣaram oṃkāraḥ |
  adhimātraṃ pādā mātrā mātrāśca pādā akāra ukāro makāra iti || MandUp_8 ||
children.translated_text: This very <s>Ātman</s>, with reference to the syllable, is <s>Oṃkāra</s>. With reference to the measures (<s>mātrā</s>), the quarters are the measures and the measures are the quarters: <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s>, <s>u</s>-<s>kāra</s>, and <s>ma</s>-<s>kāra</s>. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 8 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_8
  so 'yam ātmādhyakṣaramakṣaram adhikṛtyābhidhānaprādhānyena varṇyamāno 'dhyakṣaram /
kiṃ punas tadakṣaram ity āha oṃkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: What then is that syllable? He says: <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: so 'yam oṃkāraḥ pādaśaḥ pravibhajyamāno 'dhimātraṃ mātrām adhikṛtya vartata ity adhimātram /
children.translated_text: This <s>Oṃkāra</s>, being analyzed quarter by quarter, proceeds 'with reference to the measure' (<s>adhimātra</s>) — that is, having the measure (<s>mātrā</s>) as the basis.

children.text: katham? ātmano ye pādāsta oṃkārasya mātrāḥ /
children.translated_text: How? The quarters of the <s>Ātman</s> are the measures of <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: kās tāḥ? akārokāro makāra iti //8//
children.translated_text: What are they? <s>A</s>-<s>kāra</s>, <s>u</s>-<s>kāra</s>, and <s>ma</s>-<s>kāra</s>. || 8 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 8: 'This very <s>Ātman</s>, with reference to the syllable' — being described with the syllable (<s>akṣara</s>) as the basis, with the denotation as primary, 'with reference to the syllable.'

children.text: START MandUp 9
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 9

children.text: tatra viśeṣaniyamaḥ kriyate
children.translated_text: Here a specific determination is made:

children.text:
jāgaritasthāno vaiśvānaraḥ akāraḥ prathamā mātrāpterādimattvād vā |
  āpnoti ha vai sarvān kāmān ādiś ca bhavati ya evaṃ veda || MandUp_9 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose sphere is the waking state, is <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s>, the first measure, on account of 'pervading' (<s>āpti</s>) or on account of 'being first' (<s>ādimat</s>). One who knows thus indeed obtains all desires and becomes the first [among the great]. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 9 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_9
  jāgaritasthāno vaiśvānaro yaḥ sa oṃkārasyākāraḥ prathamā mātrā /
  kena sāmānyenety āha āpterāptirvyāptikāreṇa sarvā vāg vyāptā /
  "akāro vai sarvā vāk"(ai.ā.2 / 3 / 6) iti śruteḥ /
  tathā vaiśvānareṇa jagat"tasya ha vaitasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāḥ"(chā.u.5 / 18 / 2) ityādi śruteḥ /
abhidhānābhidheyayarekatvaṃ cāvocāma /
children.translated_text: And we have stated the identity of the signifier and the signified.

children.text: ādirasya vidyata ityādi madyathaivādimadakārākhyamakṣaraṃ tathaiva vaiśvānaras tasmād vā sāmānyād akāratvaṃ vaiśvānarasya /
children.translated_text: That which has a beginning (<s>ādi</s>) is '<s>ādimat</s>' — just as the syllable called <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s> has a beginning [i.e., is the first letter], so too <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [is the first state]. Therefore, from this similarity too, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is [identified with] <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s>.

children.text: tad ekatvavidaḥ phalam āha āpnoti ha vai sarvān kāmānādiḥ prathamaś ca bhavati mahatāṃ ya evaṃ veda yadoktam ekatvaṃ vedety arthaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: He states the fruit for one who knows this identity: 'One who knows thus indeed obtains all desires and becomes the first — the foremost among the great' — meaning, one who knows the identity as stated. || 9 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 9: <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose sphere is the waking state, is <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s>, the first measure of <s>Oṃkāra</s>. On what basis of similarity? He says: on account of 'pervading' (<s>āpti</s>) — by the act of pervading, all speech is pervaded [by <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s>]. '<s>A</s>-<s>kāra</s> is indeed all speech' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6) — so the <s>śruti</s> declares. Similarly, the world is pervaded by <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — 'Of this <s>Ātman Vaiśvānara</s>, the head alone is the excellent light' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.18.2) and so on, as the <s>śruti</s> states.

children.text: START MandUp 10
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 10

children.text: svapnasthānas taijasa ukāro dvitīyā mātrotkarṣād ubhayatvād vā |
children.translated_text: <s>Taijasa</s>, whose sphere is the dream state, is <s>u</s>-<s>kāra</s>, the second measure, on account of 'elevation' (<s>utkarṣa</s>) or on account of 'partaking of both' (<s>ubhayatva</s>).

children.text: utkarṣati ha vai jñānasaṃtatiṃ |
children.translated_text: One elevates indeed the stream of knowledge,

children.text: samānaś ca bhavati |
children.translated_text: and becomes equal [to all];

children.text: nāsyābrahmavit kule bhavati ya evaṃ veda || MandUp_10 ||
children.translated_text: no one ignorant of <s>Brahman</s> is born in the family of one who knows thus. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 10 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_10
  svapnasthānas taijaso yaḥ sa oṃkārasyokāro dvitīyā mātrā /
  kena sāmānyety āhotkarṣāt /
  akārād utkṛṣṭa iva hy ukāras tathā taijaso viśvād ubhayatvād akāramakārayor madhyasyokāras tathā viśvaprājñayor madhye taijaso 'tobhayabhāktvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 10: <s>Taijasa</s> (the luminous one), whose sphere is the dream state, is the <s>ukāra</s> (the letter 'u'), the second measure of <s>Oṃkāra</s>. By what similarity? By superiority (<s>utkarṣa</s>). Just as the <s>ukāra</s> is, as it were, superior to <s>akāra</s>, so too <s>Taijasa</s> is [superior] to <s>Viśva</s>. And because [<s>ukāra</s>] is intermediate between <s>akāra</s> and <s>makāra</s>, due to its being between both, so too <s>Taijasa</s> is intermediate between <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Prājña</s>—thus there is the similarity of partaking of both sides.

children.text: vidvatphalamucyate utkarṣati ha vai jñānasaṃtatim /
children.translated_text: The fruit for the knower is stated: 'He indeed elevates the stream of knowledge'—

children.text: vijñānasaṃtatiṃ vardhayatīty arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: he increases the stream of understanding.

children.text: samānas tulyaś ca mitrapakṣasyaiva śatrupakṣāṇām apy apradveṣyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: He becomes equal—that is, impartial—and becomes non-hateful even toward the parties of enemies, [being favorable] only toward the party of friends.

children.text: abrahmavidasya kule na bhavati ya evaṃ veda //10//
children.translated_text: No one who does not know <s>Brahman</s> is born in his family—[this is the fruit] for one who knows thus. ||10||

children.text: START MandUp 11
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 11

children.text:
suṣuptasthānaḥ prājño makāraḥ tṛtīyā mātrā miter apīter vā |
  minoti ha vā idaṃ sarvam apītiś ca bhavati ya evaṃ veda || MandUp_11 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> (the knower), whose sphere is deep sleep, is <s>makāra</s>, the third measure, [associated] either with measuring (<s>miti</s>) or with merging (<s>apīti</s>). He indeed measures all this, and he becomes the merging—one who knows thus. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 11 ||

children.text: MandUpC_11
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 11:

children.text:
suṣuptasthānaḥ prājño yaḥ sa oṃkārasya makāras tṛtīyā mātrā /
  kena sāmānyenety āha sāmānyamidam atra mito 'mitirmānaṃ mīyata iva viśvataijasau prājñena pralayotpattyoḥ /
  praveśanirgamābhyāṃ prastheneta yavās tathauṃkārasamāptau punaḥ prayoge ca praviśya nirgacchata ivākāroṃkārau makāre /
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> (the knower), whose sphere is deep sleep, is the <s>makāra</s>, the third measure of <s>Oṃkāra</s>. By what similarity? He states: the similarity here is this—'<s>mita</s>' means measurement; <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> are, as it were, measured by <s>Prājña</s> at the times of dissolution and origination. Through entering and exiting—just as grain [is measured] by a <s>prastha</s> measure—so too <s>akāra</s> and <s>ukāra</s> enter into and exit from <s>makāra</s> at the completion and re-commencement of the utterance of <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text:
apīter vā /
  apīty apy aya ekībhāvaḥ /
  oṃkāra uccāraṇe hy antyākṣara ekībhūtāvivākāra oṃkārau /
  tathā viśvataijasau suṣuptakāle prājñe /
  ato vā sāmānyād ekatvaṃ prājñam akārayoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Or from merging (<s>apīti</s>)': <s>apīti</s> means becoming one. For in the pronunciation of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, at the final syllable, <s>akāra</s> and <s>ukāra</s> become, as it were, one with [<s>makāra</s>]. Similarly, <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> [become one] in <s>Prājña</s> during deep sleep. Therefore, from this similarity too, the identity of <s>Prājña</s> with <s>makāra</s> [is established].

children.text: vidvatphalam āha minoti ha vedaṃ sarvaṃ jagad yāthātmyaṃ jānātīty arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruit for the knower is stated: 'He indeed measures (<s>minoti</s>)'—he knows the entire world as it truly is—that is the meaning.

children.text: apītiś ca jagat kāraṇātmā bhavatīty arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And he becomes the merging (<s>apīti</s>)'—he becomes the Self that is the cause of the universe—that is the meaning.

children.text: atrāv atrāvāntaraphalavacanaṃ pradhānasādhanastutyartham //11//
children.translated_text: Here, the statement of intermediate fruits serves the purpose of praising the principal means [of realization]. ||11||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.19
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.19

children.text: atraite ślokā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Here, these verses follow:

children.text: viśvasyātvavivakṣāyām ādisāmānyam utkṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: When it is intended to express the identity of <s>Viśva</s> [with <s>akāra</s>], the similarity of being first (<s>ādi</s>) is prominent;

children.text: mātrāsaṃpratipattau syād āptisāmānyam eva ca // MandUpK_1.19 //
children.translated_text: And when there is the recognition of the measure [as <s>akāra</s>], the similarity of attainment (<s>āpti</s>) alone [is prominent]. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.19 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.19
viśvasyātvamakāramātratvaṃ yadā vivakṣyate tadāditvasāmānyamuktanyāyenotkaṭamudbhṛtaṃ dṛśyata ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: When it is intended to express the identity of <s>Viśva</s> with the <s>akāra</s>-measure, the similarity of being first is prominent—that is, it is conspicuously evident according to the stated reasoning.

children.text: atvavivakṣāyāmity asya vyākhyānaṃ mātrāsaṃpratipattāv iti /
children.translated_text: The explanation of 'when the identity is intended' is 'when there is the recognition of the measure'—

children.text: viśvasyākāramātratvaṃ yadā saṃpratipadyata ity arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That is, when one recognizes <s>Viśva</s> as having the nature of the <s>akāra</s>-measure.

children.text: āptisāmānyam eva cotkaṭam ity anuvartate ca śabdāt //19//
children.translated_text: And the similarity of attainment is also prominent—this continues from the word 'and.' ||19||
Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.19:

children.text: START MandUpK 1.20
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.20

children.text: taijasasyotvavijñāna utkarṣo dṛśyate sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: In understanding <s>Taijasa</s> as the <s>ukāra</s>, the superiority (<s>utkarṣa</s>) is clearly seen;

children.text: mātrāsaṃpratipattau syād ubhayatvaṃ tathā vidham // MandUpK_1.20 //
children.translated_text: And when there is the recognition of the measure, the quality of being between both (<s>ubhayatva</s>) is likewise [clearly seen]. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.20 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.20
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.20:

children.text: taijasasyātvavijñānokāratvavivakṣāyāmutkarṣo dṛśyate sphuṭaṃ spaṣṭa ity artha ubhayatvaṃ ca sphuṭam eveti /
children.translated_text: When it is intended to express the identity of <s>Taijasa</s> with the <s>ukāra</s>-measure, the superiority is clearly—that is, distinctly—seen, and the quality of being between both is also clearly [seen].

children.text: pūrvavat sarvam //20//
children.translated_text: Everything else is as before. ||20||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.21
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.21

children.text: makārabhāve prājñasya mānasām anyam utkaṭam /
children.translated_text: In the identification of <s>Prājña</s> with <s>makāra</s>, measuring (<s>māna</s>) is the other prominent [similarity];

children.text: mātrāsaṃpratipattau tu layasāmānyam eva ca // MandUpK_1.21 //
children.translated_text: And when there is the recognition of the measure, the similarity of dissolution (<s>laya</s>) alone [is prominent]. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.21 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.21
makāratve prājñasya mitilayāvutkṛṣṭe sāmānya ity arthaḥ //21//
children.translated_text: In the identification with <s>makāra</s>, measuring and dissolution are the prominent similarities for <s>Prājña</s>—that is the meaning. ||21||
Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.21:

children.text: START MandUpK 1.22
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.22

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yat tulyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vetti niścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who knows with certainty the similarity that is common in the three states (<s>dhāman</s>)—

children.text: sa pūjyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vandyaś caiva mahāmuniḥ // MandUpK_1.22 //
children.translated_text: He is to be worshipped and honored by all beings; he is a great sage (<s>mahāmuni</s>). || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.22 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.22
yathoktasthānatraye yastulyam uktaṃ sāmānyaṃ vetyavam evaitad iti niścito yaḥ sa pūjyo vandyaś ca brahmavilloke bhavati //22//
children.translated_text: One who knows the stated similarity that is common in the aforesaid three states, being certain that 'this is indeed so'—he is to be worshipped and honored, and he exists in the world of <s>Brahman</s>. ||22||
Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.22:

children.text:
START MandUpK 1.23
yathoktaiḥ sāmānyair ātmapādānāṃ mātrābhiḥ sahaikatvaṃ kṛtvā yathoktam oṃkāraṃ pratipadya yo dhyāyati tam
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.23: Having established the identity of the quarters of the Self with the measures [of <s>Oṃkāra</s>] through the stated similarities, one who, having realized <s>Oṃkāra</s> as explained, meditates upon it—

children.text: akāro nayate viśvam ukāraś cāpi taijasam /
children.translated_text: The <s>akāra</s> leads to <s>Viśva</s>, and the <s>ukāra</s> [leads] to <s>Taijasa</s>;

children.text: makāraś ca punaḥ prājñaṃ nāmātre vidyate gatiḥ // MandUpK_1.23 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>makāra</s> again [leads] to <s>Prājña</s>; in the measureless (<s>amātra</s>), there is no destination. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.23 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.23
akāro nayate viśvaṃ prāpayati /
akārālambanam oṃkāraṃ vidvān vaiśvānaro bhavatīty arthaḥ /
tathākāras taijasam /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>ukāra</s> [leads] to <s>Taijasa</s>.

children.text: makāraś cāpi punaḥ prājñam /
children.translated_text: And the <s>makāra</s> again [leads] to <s>Prājña</s>.

children.text: ca śabdān nayata ity anuvartate /
children.translated_text: From the word 'and,' 'leads' continues [from the previous line].

children.text: kṣīṇe tu makāre bījabhāvakṣayādamātra oṃkāre gatir na vidyate kvacid ity arthaḥ //23//
children.translated_text: But when <s>makāra</s> ceases—due to the exhaustion of the seed-state—in the measureless (<s>amātra</s>) <s>Oṃkāra</s>, there is no destination anywhere—that is the meaning. ||23||

Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.23: The <s>akāra</s> leads—that is, brings—to <s>Viśva</s>. The meaning is: the wise person who contemplates <s>Oṃkāra</s> with <s>akāra</s> as the support becomes <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: START MandUp 12
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 12

children.text:
amātraś caturtho 'vyavahāryaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivo 'dvaitaḥ |
  evam oṃkāra ātmaiva |
  saṃviśaty ātmanātmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda || MandUp_12 ||
children.translated_text: The measureless (<s>amātra</s>) is the Fourth (<s>Turīya</s>), beyond transactional usage, the subsidence of the phenomenal world, auspicious, non-dual. Thus <s>Oṃkāra</s> is indeed the Self. One who knows thus enters the Self by the Self. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 12 ||

children.text:
MandUpC_12
  amātro mātrā yasya nāsti sa amātra oṃkāraś caturthas turīya ātmaiva kevalo 'bhidhānābhidheyarūpayor avāṅmanasayoḥ kṣīṇatvād avyavahāryaḥ /
  prapañca upaśamaḥ śivo 'dvaitaḥ saṃvṛtta evaṃ yathokta vijñānavatā prayukta oṃkāras trimātras tripāda ātmaiva /
  saṃviśaty ātmanā svenaiva /
  svaṃ pāramārthikam ātmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda /
  paramārthadarśī brahmavit tṛtīyaṃ bījabhāvaṃ dagdhvātmānaṃ praviṣṭa iti na puno jāyate turīyasyābījatvāt /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 12: The measureless (<s>amātra</s>)—that which has no measure—is the measureless <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the Fourth, the <s>Turīya</s>, the Self alone. It is beyond transactional usage (<s>avyavahārya</s>) because both the designating word and the designated object, which belong to the realm of speech and mind, have ceased. The phenomenal world has subsided; it is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>); it is non-dual (<s>advaita</s>). Thus, when correctly employed by the knower as described, <s>Oṃkāra</s> with its three measures and three quarters is indeed the Self. 'One enters the Self by the Self'—by one's own self alone. One [enters] one's own ultimate Self—one who knows thus. The seer of ultimate reality, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, having burned the third seed-state, enters the Self—and is not born again, because the <s>Turīya</s> (Fourth) is without seed.

children.text: na hi rajjusarpayor viveke rajjvāṃ praviṣṭaḥ sarpo buddhisaṃskārāt punaḥ pūrvavattad vivekinām utthāsyati /
children.translated_text: For indeed, when the rope and the imagined snake are discriminated, the snake that has entered the rope does not, from the mental impression, rise again as before for those who have discriminated.

children.text: mandamadhyamadhiyāṃ tu pratipannasādhakabhāvānāṃ sanmārgagāmināṃ saṃnyāsināṃ mātrāṇāṃ pādānāṃ ca kḷptasāmānyavidāṃ yathāvad upāsyamāna oṃkāro brahmapratipattaya ālambanī bhavati tathā ca vakṣyati'āśramās trividhāḥ'(mā.kā.3.16) ityādi //12//
children.translated_text: But for those of dull and middling intellect who have attained the status of aspirants following the right path—renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsins</s>) who know the established similarities of the measures and quarters—<s>Oṃkāra</s>, when properly meditated upon, becomes the support for the realization of <s>Brahman</s>. And thus it will be said: 'The stages of life are threefold' (<s>Kārikā</s> 3.16) and so on. ||12||

children.text: (iti māṇḍūkyamūlamantrabhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Thus ends the commentary on the root mantras of the <s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s>.)

children.text: START MandUpK 1.24
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.24

children.text: pūrvavad atraite ślokā bhavanti
children.translated_text: As before, here these verses follow:

children.text: oṃkāraṃ pādaśo vidyāt pādā mātrā na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter; the quarters are the measures, without doubt.

children.text: oṃkāraṃ pādaśo jñātvā na kiñcid api cintayet // MandUpK_1.24 //
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter, one should not think of anything whatsoever. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.24 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.24
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.24:

children.text: yathoktaiḥ sāmānyaiḥ pādaiva mātrā mātrāś ca pādās tasmād oṃṅkāraṃ pādaśo vidyād ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the stated similarities, the quarters are indeed the measures and the measures are the quarters; therefore, one should know <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter—that is the meaning.

children.text: evam oṃkāre jñāte dṛṣṭārtham adṛṣṭārthaṃ vā na kiñcit prayojanaṃ cintayet kṛtārthatvād ityarthaḥ //24//
children.translated_text: When <s>Oṃkāra</s> is thus known, one should not think of anything—whether for a seen (worldly) or unseen (transcendent) purpose—since the goal has been accomplished; that is the meaning. ||24||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.25
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.25

children.text: yuñjīta praṇave cetaḥ praṇavo brahma nirbhayam /
children.translated_text: One should fix the mind upon <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>); <s>Praṇava</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, the fearless.

children.text: praṇave nityayuktasya na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit // MandUpK_1.25 //
children.translated_text: For one who is ever absorbed in <s>Praṇava</s>, there is no fear anywhere. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.25 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.25
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.25:

children.text: yuñjīta samādadhyādyathāvyākhyāte paramārtharūpe praṇave ceto manaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should fix—that is, concentrate—the mind upon <s>Praṇava</s>, whose ultimate nature has been explained as described.

children.text: yasmāt praṇavo brahma nirbhayam /
children.translated_text: Because <s>Praṇava</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, the fearless.

children.text: na hi tatra sadā yuktasya bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit 'vidvān na bibheti kutaścana'(tai.u.2.9) iti śruteḥ //25//
children.translated_text: For indeed, one who is always absorbed therein has no fear anywhere, as the <s>śruti</s> states: 'The knower does not fear anything' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.9). ||25||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.26
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.26

children.text: praṇavo hy aparaṃ brahma praṇavaś ca paraḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is indeed the lower <s>Brahman</s>; and <s>Praṇava</s> is declared to be the higher [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: apūrvo 'nantaro 'bāhyo 'naparaḥ praṇavo 'vyayaḥ // MandUpK_1.26 //
children.translated_text: Without prior [cause], without interior, without exterior, without posterior—<s>Praṇava</s> is imperishable. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.26 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.26
parāpare brahmāṇi praṇavaḥ /
paramārthatā kṣīṇeṣu mātrāpādeṣu para evātmā brahmeti na pūrvaṃ kāraṇam asya vidyata ity apūrvaḥ /
nāsyāntaraṃ bhinnajātīyaṃ kiñcid vidyata ity anantaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without interior' (<s>anantara</s>) means that nothing of a different kind exists within it.

children.text: tathā bāhyam anyan na vidyata ity abāhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, nothing external exists [outside it]—hence 'without exterior' (<s>abāhya</s>).

children.text: aparaṃ kāryam asya na vidyata ity anaparaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without posterior' (<s>anapara</s>) means that no subsequent effect of it exists.

children.text: sabāhyābhyāntaro hy ajaḥ saindhavaghanavat prajñānaghana ityarthaḥ //26//
children.translated_text: Being without exterior and interior, it is unborn—a mass of pure consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), like a lump of salt—that is the meaning. ||26||

Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.26: <s>Praṇava</s> is both the higher and lower <s>Brahman</s>. In ultimate reality, when the measures and quarters have been dissolved, it is the higher Self, <s>Brahman</s> alone. 'Without prior cause' (<s>apūrva</s>) means that no antecedent cause of it is found.

children.text: START MandUpK 1.27
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.27

children.text: sarvasya praṇavo hy ādir madhyam antas tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is indeed the beginning, the middle, and the end of everything.

children.text: evaṃ hi praṇavaṃ jñātvā vyaśnute tad anantaram // MandUpK_1.27 //
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Praṇava</s> thus, one attains that [<s>Brahman</s>] immediately. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.27 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_1.27
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.27:

children.text: ādimadhyāntotpattisthitipralayāḥ sarvasyaiva /
children.translated_text: The beginning, middle, and end—origination, sustenance, and dissolution—belong to everything whatsoever.

children.text: māyāhastirajjusarpamṛgatṛṣṇikāsvapnādivad utpadyamānasya viyadādiprapañcasya yathā māyāvyādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a magical elephant, a rope-snake, a mirage, a dream, and the like—for the phenomenal world of space and the rest that appears to arise, [<s>Praṇava</s>] is like the magician and the rest [who are the substratum of the illusion].

children.text: evaṃ hi praṇavamātmānaṃ māyāvyādisthānīyaṃ jñātvā tatkṣaṇādeva tad ātmabhāvaṃ vyaśnuta ity arthaḥ //27//
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Praṇava</s>—that is, the Self—which stands in the position of the magician and the rest, one immediately attains that very Self-nature—that is the meaning. ||27||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.28
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.28

children.text: praṇavaṃ hīśvaraṃ vidyāt sarvasya hṛdi saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Praṇava</s> as the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), dwelling in the hearts of all.

children.text: sarvavyāpinam oṃkāraṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // MandUpK_1.28 //
children.translated_text: Having realized <s>Oṃkāra</s> as all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.28 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.28
sarvaprāṇijātasya smṛtipratyayāspade hṛdaye sthitam īśvaraṃ praṇavaṃ vidyāt sarvavyāpinaṃ vyomavad oṃkāram ātmānam asaṃsāriṇaṃ dhīro buddhimān matvā na śocati /
śokanimittān anupapatteḥ /
"tarati śokam ātmavit"(chā.u.7 / 1 / 3) ityādi śrutibhyaḥ //28//
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.28: One should know <s>Praṇava</s> as the Lord dwelling in the heart—the seat of memory and cognition—of all living beings. Having realized <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the Self, as all-pervading like space, free from transmigration (<s>asaṃsārin</s>), the wise, intelligent one does not grieve—because the conditions for grief do not obtain. [This is established] from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'The knower of the Self crosses over grief' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.1.3) and the like. ||28||

children.text: START MandUpK 1.29
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 1.29

children.text: amātro 'nantamātraś ca dvaitasyopaśamaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: The measureless (<s>amātra</s>), of infinite measure, the subsidence of all duality, auspicious—

children.text: oṃkāro vidito yena sa munir netāro janaḥ // MandUpK_1.29 //
children.translated_text: He by whom <s>Oṃkāra</s> is thus known is a sage (<s>muni</s>), not any other person. || <s>Kārikā</s> 1.29 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_1.29
amātras turīya oṃkāraḥ /
mīyate 'nayeti mātrā paricchittiḥ sānantā yasya sa anantamātraḥ /
naitāvatvam asya paricchettuṃ śakyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: its extent cannot be delimited.

children.text: sarvadvaita upaśamatvād eva śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because all duality subsides in it, it is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>).

children.text: oṃkaro yathā vyākhyāto vidito yena sa paramārthatatvasya mananān muniḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃkāra</s>, as explained, being known by whom—he is a sage (<s>muni</s>), from the contemplation (<s>manana</s>) of ultimate reality.

children.text: netaro janaḥ śāstravidapītyarthaḥ //29//
children.translated_text: Not any other person—not even one learned in the scriptures—that is the meaning. ||29||

Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 1.29: The measureless (<s>amātra</s>) <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the <s>Turīya</s> (Fourth). '<s>Mātrā</s>' means a measure, a delimitation. That whose [delimitation] is infinite (<s>ananta</s>) is of infinite measure (<s>anantamātra</s>).

children.text: Vaitathyaprakaraṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Vaitathyaprakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Unreality)

children.text: START MandUpK 2.1
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 2.1

children.text:
jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyata ityuktam,"ekamevādvitīyam"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 1) ityādi śrutibhyaḥ /
āgamamātraṃ tat /
tatropapattyāpi dvaitasya vaitathyaṃ śakyate 'vadhārayitum iti dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam ārabhyate
children.translated_text: It has been stated that when [<s>Brahman</s>] is known, duality does not exist, from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'One alone, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.1) and the like. That was based on scripture alone. To show that the unreality of duality can also be ascertained through reasoning, the second chapter is commenced:

children.text: vaitathyaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ svapna āhur manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise declare the unreality of all entities [seen] in dreams,

children.text: antaḥsthānāt tu bhāvānāṃ saṃvṛtatvena hetunā // MandUpK_2.1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the reason that the entities are located within the enclosed [body]. || <s>Kārikā</s> 2.1 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.1
vitathasya bhāvo vaitathyam, asatyatvam ityarthaḥ /
kasya? sarveṣāṃ bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ bhāvānāṃ padārthānāṃ svapna upalabhyamānānām, āhuḥ kathayanti, manīṣiṇaḥ pramāṇakuśalāḥ /
vaitathye hetumāhāntaḥsthānāt, antaḥ śarīrasya madhye sthānaṃ yeṣām /
tatra hi bhāvopalabhyante parvatahastyādayo na bahiḥ śarīrāt /
tasmāt te vitathā bhavitum arhanti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, they deserve to be unreal.

children.text: nanvapavarakādyantarupalabhyamānair ghaṭādibhiranaikāntiko hetur ityāśaṅkyāha saṃvṛtatvena hetuna iti /
children.translated_text: Lest one object that the reason is inconclusive, since pots and the like are perceived inside a room and yet are real—he says: 'because of the reason of being enclosed' (<s>saṃvṛtatvena</s>).

children.text: antaḥ saṃvṛtasthānād ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: because of being in an enclosed, interior location.

children.text: na hy antaḥ saṃvṛte dehento nāḍīṣu parvatahastyādīnāṃ saṃbhavo 'sti, na hi dehe parvataḥ, asti //1//
children.translated_text: For in the enclosed interior of the body, in the channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>), there is no possibility of mountains, elephants, and the like—for indeed, a mountain does not exist within the body. ||1||

Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 2.1: <s>Vaitathya</s> (unreality) is the state of being <s>vitatha</s> (unreal); the meaning is: falsity. Of what? Of all entities—both external and internal objects perceived in dreams. The wise (<s>manīṣiṇas</s>)—those skilled in the means of knowledge—declare [their unreality]. He states the reason for the unreality: 'because of their being located within'—that is, those whose location is within, in the interior of the body. For entities such as mountains and elephants are perceived there [in dreams], within [the body], not outside the body.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.2
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 2.2

children.text: svapnadṛśyānāṃ bhāvānāmantaḥ saṃvṛtasthānamityetad asiddham, yasmāt prācyeṣu supta udakṣu svapnān paśyann iva dṛśyata ityetad āśaṅkyāha
children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection that the claim of dream-objects having an internal enclosed location is unestablished—since one sleeping in the east appears to see dreams in the north—he says:

children.text: adīrghatvāc ca kālasya gatvā deśān na paśyati /
children.translated_text: And because of the shortness of time, one does not, having traveled, see those places;

children.text: pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvas tasmin deśe na vidyate // MandUpK_2.2 //
children.translated_text: And indeed everyone, upon waking, does not exist in that place [seen in the dream]. || <s>Kārikā</s> 2.2 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.2
na dehādbarhideśāntaraṃ gatvā svapnān paśyati /
yasmāt suptamātra eva dehadeśād yojanaśatāntarite māsamātraprāpye deśe svapnān paśyann iva dṛśyate /
na ca tad deśaprāpter āgamanasya dīrghaḥ kālo 'sti /
ato dārghatvāc ca kālasya na svapnadṛgdeśāntaraṃ gacchati /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 2.2: One does not go to another location outside the body to see dreams. For a person who is merely asleep is seen as if seeing dreams in a place that is a hundred yojanas distant from the location of the body and reachable only in a month's time. And there is not a long enough time to reach that place and return. Therefore, due to the length of time [required], the dream-seer does not go to another location.

children.text:
kiṃ ca pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvaḥ svapnadṛksvapnadarśanadeśe na vidyate /
yadi ca svapne deśāntaraṃ gacched yasmin deśe svapnān paśyet tatraiva pratibudhyeta /
na caitad asti /
children.translated_text: But this is not the case.

children.text: rātrau supto 'hanīva bhāvān paśyati, bahubhiḥ saṃgato bhavati, yaś ca saṃgataḥ tair gṛhyeta /
children.translated_text: At night, while asleep, one sees things as if during the day, encounters many people, and the one encountered would apprehend him.

children.text: na ca gṛhyate, gṛhītaścetvām adya tatropalabdhavanto vayam iti vayamiti brūyuḥ /
children.translated_text: But he is not apprehended; and if apprehended, they would say 'We found you there today.'

children.text: na caitad asti tasmān na deśāntaraṃ gacchati svapne //2//
children.translated_text: But this does not happen; therefore, one does not go to another location in dream. ||2||

Moreover, every person who has woken up is not found in the location of the dream-vision. If one went to another location in dream — to the place where one sees dreams — one would wake up in that very place.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.3
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.3

children.text: itaś ca svapnadṛśyā bhāvā vitathā yataḥ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the objects seen in dream are unreal, because —

children.text: abhāvaś ca rathādīnāṃ śrūyate nyāyapūrvakam /
children.translated_text: The non-existence of chariots and the like is declared in scripture, preceded by reasoning.

children.text: vaitathyaṃ tena vai prāptaṃ svapna āhuḥ prakāśitam // MandUpK_2.3 //
children.translated_text: The unreality thus established is said to be revealed in dream, say [the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>]. || Kārikā 2.3 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.3
abhāvaś caiva rathādīnāṃ svapnadṛśyānāṃ śrūyate nyāyapūrvakaṃ yuktitaḥ śrutau"na tatra rathāḥ"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 10) ity atra /
dehāntaḥ sthānasaṃvṛtatvādihetunā prāptaṃ vaikathyaṃ tad anuvādinyā śrutyā svapne svayañjyotiṣṭvapratipādanaparayā prakāśitamāhur brahmavidaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: The unreality established by reasons such as being confined within the body — this is said by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> to be revealed by the <s>śruti</s>, which restates [this conclusion] and whose primary purpose is to teach the self-luminosity of the Self in dream. ||3||

Commentary on Kārikā 2.3: The non-existence of chariots and the like — the objects seen in dream — is declared in scripture preceded by reasoning, that is, logically, in the <s>śruti</s> passage 'There are no chariots there' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.10).

children.text: START MandUpK 2.4
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.4

children.text: antasthānāt tu bhedānāṃ tasmāj jāgarite smṛtam /
children.translated_text: However, due to the differences being internal [in dream], the [unreality] is recognized in the waking state [as well].

children.text: yathā tatra tathā svapne saṃvṛtatvena bhidyate // MandUpK_2.4 //
children.translated_text: Just as there [in dream], so in the waking state — [the objects] differ only by being confined [within the body]. || Kārikā 2.4 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.4
jāgrad dṛśyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ vaitathyam iti pratijñā /
dṛśyatvād iti hetuḥ svapnadṛśyabhāvavad iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
yathā tatra svapne dṛśyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ vaitathyaṃ tathā jāgarite 'pi dṛśyatvam aviśiṣṭam iti hetūpanayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the objects perceived in dream are unreal, so too in the waking state, their perceptibility is not different — this is the application of the reason.

children.text: tasmāj jāgarite 'pi vaitathyaṃ smṛtam iti nigamanam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, unreality is recognized even in the waking state — this is the conclusion.

children.text: antaḥsthānāt saṃvṛtatvena ca svapnadṛśyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ jāgrad dṛśyebhyaḥ bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: The difference between dream-perceived objects and waking-perceived objects is due to being internal and being confined [within the body].

children.text: dṛśyatvam asatyatvaṃ cāviśiṣṭam ubhayatra //4//
children.translated_text: But their perceptibility and unreality are not different in either case. ||4||
Commentary on Kārikā 2.4: The proposition is: the objects seen in the waking state are unreal. The reason is: because they are objects of perception. The example is: like the objects seen in dream.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.5
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.5

children.text: svapnajāgaritasthāne hy ekam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise declare that the dream and waking states are one,

children.text: bhedānāṃ hi samatvena prasiddhenaiva hetunā // MandUpK_2.5 //
children.translated_text: Because of the well-known sameness of the differences [perceived in both], on the basis of an established reason. || Kārikā 2.5 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.5
prasiddhenaiva bhedānāṃ grāhyagrāhakatvena hetunā samatvena svapnajāgaritasthānayor ekatvamāhurvivekina iti pūrvapramāṇasiddhasyaiva phalam //5//
children.translated_text: By the well-known reason of the sameness of differences — namely, their nature as apprehended objects and apprehending subjects — the discriminating ones declare the oneness of the dream and waking states. This is merely the result of what was already established by the preceding proof. ||5||
Commentary on Kārikā 2.5

children.text: START MandUpK 2.6
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.6

children.text: itaś ca vaitathyaṃ jāgrad dṛśyānāṃ bhedānām ādyantayor abhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the unreality of the differences perceived in the waking state [is established] because of their non-existence at the beginning and end.

children.text: ādāvante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā /
children.translated_text: That which does not exist at the beginning and at the end does not [truly] exist in the present either.

children.text: vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo 'vitathā iva lakṣitāḥ // MandUpK_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Though similar to the unreal, they are perceived as if real. || Kārikā 2.6 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.6
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 2.6

children.text: yadādāv ante ca nāsti vastu mṛgatṛṣṇikādi tanmadhye 'pi nāsty ati niścitaṃ loke tatheme jāgrad dṛśyā bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: That which does not exist at the beginning and at the end — a real entity like a mirage and the like — does not exist in the middle either; this is firmly established in the world. Likewise are these differences perceived in the waking state.

children.text: ādyantayor abhāvād vitathair eva mṛgatṛṣṇikādibhiḥ sadṛśatvād vitathā eva tathāpi vitathā iva lakṣitā mūḍhair anātmavidbhiḥ //6//
children.translated_text: Due to their non-existence at the beginning and end, being similar to unreal things such as mirages, they are indeed unreal; yet they are perceived as if real by the deluded, by those who do not know the Self. ||6||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.7
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.7

children.text:
svapnadṛśyavajjāgaritadṛśyānām api satvam iti yad uktaṃ tad ayuktam /
yasmāj jāgrad dṛśyā annapānavāhanādayaḥ kṣutpipāsādinivṛttiṃ kurvanto gamanāgamanādikāryaṃ ca saprayojānā dṛṣṭāḥ /
na tu svapnadṛśyānāṃ tad asti /
tasmāt svapnadṛśyavad jāgrad dṛśyānām asatvaṃ manorathamātram iti /
children.translated_text: An objection: what has been said — that the objects perceived in the waking state are unreal like dream-perceived objects — is not correct. Because waking objects such as food, drink, vehicles, and the like are seen to be purposeful, bringing about the removal of hunger, thirst, and the like, and accomplishing functions such as coming and going. But this is not the case with dream-perceived objects. Therefore, to say that waking objects are unreal like dream objects, being mere fancy, is [wrong].

children.text:
tan na /
kasmāt? yasmāt
children.translated_text: That is not so. Why? Because —

children.text: saprayojanatā teṣāṃ svapne vipratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Their purposefulness is contradicted in dream.

children.text: tasmād ādyantavatvena mithyaiva khalu te smṛtāḥ // MandUpK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by virtue of having a beginning and end, they are indeed recognized as unreal. || Kārikā 2.7 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.7
saprayojanatā dṛṣṭā yā annapānādīnāṃ sā svapne vipratipadyate /
jāgarite hi bhuktvā pītvā ca tṛpto vinivartitatṛṭsuptamātra eva kṣutpipāsādyārtam ahorātroṣitaṃ bhuktavantam ātmānaṃ manyate /
yathā spapne bhuktvā pītvā ca tṛpta utthitas tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as in dream, having eaten and drunk and being satisfied, one wakes up [hungry] — similarly.

children.text: tasmād jāgrad dṛśyānāṃ svapne vipratipattir dṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the contradiction of waking objects is observed in dream.

children.text: ato manyāmahe teṣām apy asatvaṃ spapnadṛśyavadanāśaṅkanīyam iti /
children.translated_text: Hence we maintain that their unreality, like that of dream objects, should not be doubted.

children.text: tasmād ādyantavatvamubhayatra samānam iti mithyā iva khalu te smṛtāḥ //7//
children.translated_text: Therefore, having a beginning and an end is common to both — thus they are indeed recognized as unreal. ||7||

Commentary on Kārikā 2.7: The purposefulness observed of food, drink, and the like is contradicted in dream. For in the waking state, having eaten and drunk and being satisfied, the moment one falls asleep, one thinks oneself to be hungry, thirsty, and afflicted, having fasted for a whole day and night, even though one has eaten.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.8
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.8

children.text:
svapnajāgradbhedayoḥ samatvāj jāgradbhedānām asatvam iti yad uktaṃ tadasat /
kasmāt?
dṛṣṭāntasyāsiddhatvāt /
katham?
na hi jāgrad dṛṣṭā evaite bhedāḥ svapne dṛśyante /
kiṃ tarhi?
apūrvaṃ svapne paśyati, caturdantagajamārūṭhamaṣṭabhujamātmānaṃ manyate /
anyad apy evaṃprakāram apūrvaṃ paśyati svapne /
tan nānyenā asatā samam iti sadeva /
ato dṛṣṭānto 'siddhaḥ /
tasmātsvapnavajjāgaritasyāsatvamity ayuktam /
children.translated_text: An objection: what has been said — that waking differences are unreal because of the sameness of dream and waking differences — is incorrect. Why? Because the example is not established. How? For these very differences seen in the waking state are not seen in dream. Rather, in dream one sees something unprecedented — one considers oneself riding a four-tusked elephant, having eight arms. And one sees other such unprecedented things in dream. That [unprecedented content] is not similar to anything else that is unreal; therefore it is real. Hence the example is not established; therefore the unreality of waking [experience] like dream is unjustified.

children.text:
tan na, svapne dṛṣṭam apūrvaṃ yan manyase na tatsvataḥ siddham /
kiṃ tarhi?
children.translated_text: That is not so. What you consider unprecedented in dream is not self-existent. Rather —

children.text: apūrvaṃ sthānidharmo hi yathā svarganivāsinām /
children.translated_text: The unprecedented [content] is indeed a property of the locus (the dreamer), just as the attributes of the dwellers in heaven.

children.text: tānayaṃ prekṣate gatvā yathaiveha suśikṣitaḥ // MandUpK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: He goes [to that dream-location] and perceives those [objects], just like a well-instructed person here [in the waking world]. || Kārikā 2.8 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.8
apūrvaṃ sthānidharmo hi sthānino draṣṭur eva hi svapnasthānavato dharmaḥ /
yathā svarganivāsināmindrādīnāṃ sahasrākṣatvādi tathā svapnadṛśo 'pūrvo 'yaṃ dharmaḥ /
na svataḥ siddho draṣṭuḥ svarūpavat /
children.translated_text: It is not self-existent, unlike the intrinsic nature of the seer.

children.text: tānevaṃprakārānapūrvānsvacittavikalpānayaṃ sthānī svapnadṛksvapnasthāne gatvā prekṣate /
children.translated_text: These unprecedented mental imaginations — the dreamer, the occupant of the dream-location, having gone to the dream-location, perceives them.

children.text: yathaiveha loke suśikṣito deśāntaramārgastane mārgeṇa deśāntaraṃ gatvā tānpadārthānpaśyati tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as a well-instructed person in this world, being shown the way to another region, goes to that region by that path and sees those objects — in the same manner.

children.text: tasmādyathā sthānidharmāṇāṃ rajjusarpamṛgatṛṣṇikādīnāmasatvaṃ tathā svapnadṛṣyānāmapūrvāṇāṃ sthānidharmatvamevetyasattvamato na svapnadṛṣṭāntasyāsiddhatvam //8//
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the properties of the locus — the snake on the rope, the mirage, and the like — are unreal, so too the unprecedented dream-objects, being merely properties of the locus, are unreal. Hence the dream-example is not unestablished. ||8||

Commentary on Kārikā 2.8: 'The unprecedented is a property of the locus' — it is indeed a property of the locus, that is, of the dreamer who occupies the dream-location. Just as the thousand-eyed nature and the like are attributes of the dwellers in heaven such as <s>Indra</s> and others, so too this unprecedented attribute belongs to the dream-seer.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.9
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.9

children.text: apūrvatvāśaṅkā nirākṛtā svapnadṛṣṭāntasya punaḥ svapnatulyatāṃ jāgradbhedānāṃ prapañcayannāha
children.translated_text: Having refuted the objection of unprecedented content, he further elaborates on the dream-like nature of waking differences, saying —

children.text: svapnavṛttāv api tv antaś cetasā kalpitaṃ tv asat /
children.translated_text: Even in the dream state, what is internally imagined by the mind is unreal,

children.text: bahiś cetogṛhītaṃ sad dṛṣṭaṃ vaitathyam etayoḥ // MandUpK_2.9 //
children.translated_text: While what is externally apprehended by the mind is [considered] real — the unreality of both is observed. || Kārikā 2.9 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.9
svapnavṛttāv api svapnasthāne 'py antaś cetasā manorathasaṅkalpitam asat /
children.translated_text: Even in the dream state, what is internally imagined by the mind — a daydream or fancy — is [considered] unreal,

children.text: saṅkalpānantarasamakālam evādarśanāt tatraiva svapne bahiś cetasā gṛhītaṃ cakṣurādidvāreṇopalabdhaṃ ghaṭādi sat /
children.translated_text: Because it is not seen again immediately after the imagination. In that very dream, what is externally apprehended by the mind — perceived through the doorways of the eyes and other senses, such as a pot — is [considered] real.

children.text: ity eva satyam iti niścite 'pi sadasadvibhāgo dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though this distinction between real and unreal is firmly established [within the dream],

children.text: ubhayorapyantarbahiścetaḥ kalpitayorvaitathyameva dṛṣṭam //9//
children.translated_text: The unreality of both — the internally and externally imagined by the mind — is observed. ||9||
Commentary on Kārikā 2.9

children.text: START MandUpK 2.10
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.10

children.text: jāgradvṛttāvapi tv antaś cetasā kalpitaṃ tv asat /
children.translated_text: Even in the waking state, what is internally imagined by the mind is unreal,

children.text: bahiścetogṛhītaṃ sad yuktaṃ vaitathyam etayoḥ // MandUpK_2.10 //
children.translated_text: While what is externally apprehended by the mind is [considered] real — the unreality of both is justified. || Kārikā 2.10 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.10
sadasatorvaitathyaṃ yuktam, antarbahiścetaḥkalpitatvāviśeṣāditi vyākhyātamanyat //10//
children.translated_text: The unreality of the real and the unreal is justified, because there is no difference in their being imagined by the mind, whether internal or external — the rest is explained [as before]. ||10||
Commentary on Kārikā 2.10

children.text: START MandUpK 2.11
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.11

children.text: codaka āha
children.translated_text: An objector says —

children.text: ubhayor api vaitathyaṃ bhedānāṃ sthānayor yadi /
children.translated_text: If the unreality of differences in both states is [accepted],

children.text: ka etān budhyate bhedān ko vai teṣāṃ vikalpakaḥ // MandUpK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: Who then cognizes these differences? Who indeed is their imaginer? || Kārikā 2.11 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.11
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 2.11

children.text: svapnajāgratsthānayorbhedānāṃ yadi vaitathyaṃ ka etānarbahiścetaḥkalpitānbudhyate /
children.translated_text: If the differences imagined internally and externally by the mind in both the dream and waking states are unreal, who cognizes them?

children.text: ko vai teṣāṃ vikalpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who indeed is their imaginer?

children.text: smṛtijñānayoḥ ka ālambanamityabhiprāyaḥ, na cennirātmavāda iṣṭaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: The intention is: what is the basis of memory and knowledge? For otherwise, the doctrine of no-self would be implied [which is not intended]. ||11||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.12
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.12

children.text: kalpayaty ātmanātmānam ātmā devaḥ svamāyayā /
children.translated_text: The Self, the luminous one (<s>deva</s>), imagines himself by his own <s>māyā</s> (power of illusion);

children.text: sa eva budhyate bhedān iti vedāntaniścayaḥ // MandUpK_2.12 //
children.translated_text: He alone cognizes the differences — this is the settled conclusion of <s>Vedānta</s>. || Kārikā 2.12 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.12
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 2.12

children.text: svayaṃ svamāyayā svamātmānamātsā deva ātmanyeva vakṣyamāṇaṃ bhedākāraṃ kalpayati rajjvādāviva sarpādīn svayameva ta tānbudhyate bhedāṃstadvadevetyevaṃ vedāntaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: By his own <s>māyā</s>, the luminous Self (<s>deva</s>) imagines upon his own Self the forms of differences that will be described — just as [one imagines] snakes and the like upon a rope and the like. He himself then cognizes those differences — such is the settled conclusion of <s>Vedānta</s>.

children.text: nānyo 'sti jñānasmṛtyāśrayo na ca nirāspada eva jñānasmṛtī vaināśikānāmivetyabhiprāyaḥ //12//
children.translated_text: There is no other basis for knowledge and memory, nor are knowledge and memory without a basis, as the <s>Vaināśikas</s> (Buddhists) hold — this is the intention. ||12||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.13
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.13

children.text: saṅkalpayankena prakāreṇa kalpayatītyucyate
children.translated_text: Having [established that he] imagines, it is stated in what manner he imagines —

children.text: vikaroty aparān bhāvān antaścitte vyavasthitān /
children.translated_text: He manifests the various objects established within the mind,

children.text: niyatāṃś ca bahiścitta evaṃ kalpayate prabhuḥ // MandUpK_2.13 //
children.translated_text: And the determinate [objects] externally — thus the Lord (<s>Prabhu</s>) imagines. || Kārikā 2.13 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.13

vikaroti nānā karotyaparāṃl laukikān bhāvān padārthāñ śabdādīnanyāṃścāntaścitte vāsanārūpeṇa vyavasthitānavyākṛtān niyatāṃśca pṛthvyādīnaniyatāṃśca kalpanākālānbahiścittaḥ saṃstathāntaścitto manorathādilakṣaṇānityevaṃ kalpayati prabhurīśvara ātmetyarthaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: He manifests — makes diverse — the other worldly objects, things such as sound and the rest, as well as others established within the mind in the form of impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>), which are unmanifest. The determinate ones such as earth and the like, and the indeterminate ones characterized by daydreams and the like, which exist at the time of imagination — he being externally-minded and internally-minded, thus the Lord (<s>Prabhu</s>), meaning the Self (<s>Ātman</s>), imagines. ||13||
Commentary on Kārikā 2.13

children.text: START MandUpK 2.14
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.14

children.text: svapnavaccittaparikalpitaṃ sarvamityetadāśaṅkyate /
children.translated_text: An objection arises that everything is imagined by the mind, as in dream.

children.text: yasmāccittaparikalpitairmanorathādilakṣaṇaiścittaparicchedyaivailakṣaṇyaṃ bāhyānāmanyonyaparicchedyatvamiti //
children.translated_text: Since the distinguishing feature of external objects — their mutual delimitation — is itself delimited by mind-imagined things characterized by daydreams and the like, which are delimited only by the mind.

children.text: sā na yuktāśaṅkā /
children.translated_text: That objection is not valid.

children.text: cittakālā hi ye 'ntas tu dvayakālāś ca ye bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are internal, existing only during the time of thought (<s>cittakāla</s>), and those that are external, existing during the time of the pair (<s>dvayakāla</s>),

children.text: kalpitā eva te sarve viśeṣo nānyahetukaḥ // MandUpK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: Are all imagined; the difference [between them] has no other cause. || Kārikā 2.14 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.14
cittakālā hi ye 'ntastu cittaparicchedyāḥ, nānyaścittakālavyatirekeṇa paricchedakaḥ kālo yeṣāṃ te cittakālāḥ /
kalpanākāla evopalabhyanta ityarthaḥ /
dvayakālāśca bhedakālā anyonyaparicchedyāḥ /
yathāgodohanamāste, yāvadāste tāvadgāṃ dogdhi yāvadgāṃ dogdhi tāvadāste /
children.translated_text: For example, 'He sits for as long as the milking' — as long as he sits, so long he milks the cow; as long as he milks the cow, so long he sits.

children.text: tāvānayametāvānsa iti parasparaparicchedyaparicchedakatvaṃ bāhyānāṃ bhedānāṃ te dvayakalā antaścittakālā bāhyāśca dvayakālāḥ kalpitā eva te sarve /
children.translated_text: 'This one is of such measure, that one is of such measure' — this mutual delimitation of external differences constitutes their 'dual-time' nature. Both the internal 'thought-time' ones and the external 'dual-time' ones — they are all imagined.

children.text: na bāhyo dvayakālatvaviśeṣaḥ kalpitatvavyatirekeṇānyahetukaḥ /
children.translated_text: The specific feature of 'dual-time' in external objects has no other cause apart from being imagined.

children.text: atrāpi hi svapnadṛṣṭānto bhavatyeva //14//
children.translated_text: Here too, the dream-analogy applies. ||14||

Commentary on Kārikā 2.14: 'Those existing during the time of thought' — they are delimited by thought; there is no other time that delimits them apart from the time of thought. They are perceived only at the time of imagination — this is the meaning. 'Those existing during the time of the pair' — existing during the time of differentiation, mutually delimiting each other.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.15
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.15

children.text: avyaktā eva ye 'ntas tu sphuṭā eva ca ye bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are unmanifest internally, and those that are clearly manifest externally,

children.text: kalpitā eva te sarve viśeṣas tv indriyāntare // MandUpK_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Are all imagined; the difference lies only in the sense-organ [involved]. || Kārikā 2.15 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.15
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 2.15

children.text: yadapyantaravyaktatvaṃ bhāvānāṃ manovāsanāmātrābhivyaktānāṃ sphuṭatvaṃ vā bahiścakṣurādīndriyāntare viśeṣo nāsau bhedānāmastitvakṛtaḥ svapne 'pi tathā darśanāt /
children.translated_text: The unmanifest nature of internal objects — those manifest only as mental impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) — and the clear manifestness of external ones is a difference within the sense-organs (i.e., whether the mind or the eye and other organs are involved). This [difference] is not caused by the real existence of the differences, since the same is observed in dream.

children.text: kintarhi? indriyāntarakṛta eva /
children.translated_text: Rather, it is caused solely by the difference in sense-organs.

children.text: ataḥ kalpitā eva jāgtadbhāvā api svapnabhāvavaditi siddham //15//
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that even waking objects are imagined, like dream objects. ||15||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.16
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 2.16

children.text: bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ bhāvānāmitaretaranimittanaimittikatayā kalpanāyāṃ kiṃ mūlamityucyate
children.translated_text: What is the root of the imagination of external and internal objects as mutually related as cause and effect? It is stated —

children.text: jīvaṃ kalpayate pūrvaṃ vaco bhāvān pṛthagvidhān /
children.translated_text: First, he imagines the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), then the various objects, both

children.text: bāhyān ādhyātmikāṃś caiva yathāvidyas tathāsmṛtiḥ // MandUpK_2.16 //
children.translated_text: External and internal — as is one's knowledge, so is one's memory. || Kārikā 2.16 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.16
jīvaṃ hetuphalātmakam, ahaṃ karomi mama sukhaduḥkhe ityevaṃ lakṣaṇam, anevaṃlakṣaṇa eva śuddha ātmani rajjāviva sarpaṃ kalpayate pūrvam /
tatastādarthyena kriyākārakaphalabhedena prāṇādīnnānāvidhānbhāvānbāhyānādhyātmikāṃścaiva kalpate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in accordance with that purpose, [the Self] imagines various entities (<s>bhāvas</s>) — external and internal — differentiated as action, instrument, and result, such as <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest.

children.text: tatra kalpanāyāṃ ko heturityucyate /
children.translated_text: What is the cause of that imagination? It is stated:

children.text: yo 'sausvayaṅkalpito jīvaḥ sarvakalpanāyāmadhikṛtaḥ sa yathāvidyaḥ, yādṛśī vidyā vijñānamasyeti yathāvidyaḥ, tathāvidhaiva smṛtistasyeti tathāsmṛtirbhavati sa iti /
children.translated_text: That <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), which is itself imagined, is the agent of all imagination. He is 'as his knowledge' (<s>yathāvidya</s>) — that is, his knowledge or cognition is of such a nature; accordingly, his memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is of the same kind.

children.text: ato hetukalpanāvijñānātphalavijñānaṃ tato hetiphalasmṛtistatastadvijñānaṃ tadarthakriyākārakatatphalabhedavijñānāni tebhyastatsmṛtistatsmṛteśca punastadvijñānānītyevaṃ bāhyānādhyātmikāṃścetaretaranimittanaimittikabhāvenānekadhā kalpayate //16//
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the cognition that imagines the cause arises the cognition of the result; from that arise the memories of cause and result; from those memories arise cognitions of those [again]; cognitions of the differentiation of action, instrument, and result for that purpose; from those arise memories of those; and from those memories arise cognitions of those again — thus, in this manner, [the Self] imagines external and internal [phenomena] in manifold ways, as mutually related causes and effects. || 16 ||

Commentary on Kārikā 2.16: The <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — characterized by cause and effect, having the form of 'I act, mine is happiness and suffering' — upon the pure Self, which is not of such a nature, is first imagined, just as a snake upon a rope.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.17
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.17

children.text: tatra jīvakalpanā sarvakalpanāmūlamityuktaṃ saiva jīvakalpanā kiṃnimitteti dṛṣṭāntena pratipādayati
children.translated_text: It has been stated that the imagination of the <s>jīva</s> is the root of all imagination. Now, by means of an illustration, he demonstrates what is the cause of that very imagination of the <s>jīva</s>:

children.text: aniścitā yathā rajjur andhakāre vikalpitā /
children.translated_text: Just as a rope, undetermined in darkness, is imagined

children.text: sarpadhārādibhir bhāvais tadvad ātmā vikalpitaḥ // MandUpK_2.17 //
children.translated_text: As a snake, a stream of water, and other things — so too the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is imagined. || MandUpK 2.17 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.17
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_2.17

children.text: yathā loke svena rūpeṇāniścitānavadhāritaivameveti rajjurmandāndhakāre kiṃ sarpa udakadhārā daṇḍa iti vānekadhā vikalpitā bhavati pūrvaṃ svarūpāniścayanimittaṃ yadi hi pūrvameva rajjuḥ svarūpeṇa niścitā syāt, na sarpādivikalpo 'bhaviṣyad yathā svahastāṅgulyādiṣu, eṣa dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, a rope not ascertained in its true nature — not determined as 'it is just this' — in dim darkness, is imagined in multiple ways as 'Is it a snake? A stream of water? A stick?' — the prior non-ascertainment of its true nature being the cause [of the imagination]; for if the rope had been ascertained beforehand in its true nature, the imagination of a snake and the like would not have arisen, just as with one's own hand, fingers, and the like. This is the illustration.

children.text: tadvaddhetuphalādisaṃsāradharmānarthavilakṣaṇatayā svena viśuddhavijñaptimātrasattādvayarūpeṇāniścitatvājjīvaprāṇādyanantabhāvabhedairātmavikalpita ityeṣa sarvopaniṣadāṃ siddhāntaḥ //17//
children.translated_text: Similarly, because [the <s>Ātman</s>] is not ascertained in its own nature — which is distinct from the defects of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) such as cause, effect, and the like, being of the nature of pure consciousness alone, non-dual — [the <s>Ātman</s>] is imagined through the endless differentiations of <s>jīva</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, and the like. This is the established conclusion of all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. || 17 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.18
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.18

children.text: niścitāyāṃ yathā rajjvāṃ vikalpo vinivartate /
children.translated_text: When the rope is ascertained, the imagination ceases,

children.text: rajjur eveti cādvaitaṃ tadvad ātmaviniścayaḥ // MandUpK_2.18 //
children.translated_text: And [there arises the non-dual knowledge] 'It is only a rope' — similarly is the ascertainment of the <s>Ātman</s>. || MandUpK 2.18 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.18
rajjureveti niścaye sarvavikalpanivṛttau rajjureveti cādvaitaṃ yathā tathā 'neti neti'(bṛ.u.4.4.22) iti sarvasaṃsāradharmaśūnyapratipādakaśāstrajanitavijñānasūryālakakṛtātmaviniścayaḥ 'ātmaivedaṃ sarvam' (chā.u.7.25.2) 'apūrvamanaparamanantaramabāhyam' (bṛ.u.2.5.19) 'sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ'(mu.u.2.1.2) 'ajaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayaḥ'(bṛ.u.4.4.25) 'eka evādvayaḥ' iti //18//
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_2.18
When, upon the ascertainment 'It is only a rope,' all imagination ceases and [the knowledge] 'It is only a rope' — non-duality — [arises], similarly, the ascertainment of the <s>Ātman</s> is [produced] by the sun-ray of knowledge born from the scripture that establishes [the <s>Ātman</s> as] devoid of all attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>, [as expressed by] 'Not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.22): 'The <s>Ātman</s> alone is all this' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.25.2), 'Without prior, without posterior, without interior, without exterior' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.19), 'Both external and internal, indeed unborn' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2), 'Unaging, undying, immortal, fearless' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.25), 'One alone, non-dual.' || 18 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.19
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.19

children.text: yadyātmaika eveti niścayaḥ kathaṃ prāṇādibhiranantairbhāvairetaiḥ saṃsāralakṣaṇairvikalpita ity ucyate, śṛṇu
children.translated_text: If the ascertainment is that the <s>Ātman</s> alone [exists], then how is it imagined through these endless entities characterized by <s>saṃsāra</s>, such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest? Listen:

children.text: prāṇādibhir anantaiś ca bhāvair etair vikalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: By <s>prāṇa</s> and other endless entities, [the Self] is thus imagined;

children.text: māyaiṣā tasya devasya yayā saṃmohitaḥ svayam // MandUpK_2.19 //
children.translated_text: This is the <s>māyā</s> (illusive power) of that luminous [Self] (<s>deva</s>), by which he himself is deluded. || MandUpK 2.19 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.19
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_2.19

children.text: māyaiṣā tasyātmano devasya /
children.translated_text: This is the <s>māyā</s> of that <s>Ātman</s>, the luminous one (<s>deva</s>).

children.text: yathā māyāvinā vihitā māyā gaganamativimalaṃ kusumitaiḥ sapalāśaistarubhirākīrṇamiva karoti tatheyamapi devasya māyā yayāyaṃ svayamapi mohita iva mohito bhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>māyā</s> created by a magician makes the exceedingly pure sky appear as if filled with blossoming trees laden with leaves, so too this <s>māyā</s> of the luminous [Self] — by which he himself, as though deluded, becomes deluded.

children.text: 'mama māyā duratyayā'(gītā 7.14) ityuktam //19//
children.translated_text: 'My <s>māyā</s> is difficult to cross over' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 7.14) — thus it has been said. || 19 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.20-28
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.20-28

children.text: prāṇa iti prāṇavido bhūtānīti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath)' — say those who know <s>prāṇa</s>; 'It is the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>)' — say those who know them;

children.text: guṇā iti guṇavidas tattvānīti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.20 //
children.translated_text: 'It is the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)' — say those who know the <s>guṇas</s>; 'It is the <s>tattvas</s> (principles)' — say those who know them. || MandUpK 2.20 ||

children.text: pādā iti pādavido viṣayā iti ca tadvidaḥ /
