children.translated_text: 'It is the quarters (<s>pādas</s>)' — say those who know the quarters; 'It is the sense-objects (<s>viṣayas</s>)' — say those who know them;

children.text: lokā iti lokavido devā iti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.21 //
children.translated_text: 'It is the worlds (<s>lokas</s>)' — say those who know the worlds; 'It is the gods (<s>devas</s>)' — say those who know them. || MandUpK 2.21 ||

children.text: vedā iti vedavido yajñā iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is the <s>Vedas</s>' — say those who know the <s>Vedas</s>; 'It is the sacrifices (<s>yajñas</s>)' — say those who know them;

children.text: bhokteti ca bhoktṛvido bhojyam iti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2. 22 //
children.translated_text: 'It is the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>)' — say those who know the enjoyer; 'It is the enjoyed (<s>bhojya</s>)' — say those who know it. || MandUpK 2.22 ||

children.text: sūkṣma iti sūkṣmavidaḥ sthūla iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is the subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>)' — say those who know the subtle; 'It is the gross (<s>sthūla</s>)' — say those who know it;

children.text: mūrta iti mūrtavido 'mūrta iti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.23 //
children.translated_text: 'It has form (<s>mūrta</s>)' — say those who know form; 'It is formless (<s>amūrta</s>)' — say those who know it. || MandUpK 2.23 ||

children.text: kāla iti kālavido diśa iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is time (<s>kāla</s>)' — say those who know time; 'It is the directions (<s>diśas</s>)' — say those who know them;

children.text: vādā iti vādavido bhuvanānīti tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.24 //
children.translated_text: 'It is the doctrines (<s>vādas</s>)' — say those who know the doctrines; 'It is the worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>)' — say those who know them. || MandUpK 2.24 ||

children.text: mana iti manovido buddhir iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is the mind (<s>manas</s>)' — say those who know the mind; 'It is the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>)' — say those who know it;

children.text: cittam iti cittavido dharmādharmau ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.25 //
children.translated_text: 'It is consciousness (<s>citta</s>)' — say those who know consciousness; '<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>' — say those who know them. || MandUpK 2.25 ||

children.text: pañcaviṃśaka ity eke ṣaḍviśa iti cāpare /
children.translated_text: 'Twenty-five [principles]' — say some; 'Twenty-six' — say others;

children.text: ekatriṃśaka ity āhur ananta iti cāpare // MandUpK_2.26 //
children.translated_text: 'Thirty-one' — say [yet] others; 'Infinite' — say still others. || MandUpK 2.26 ||

children.text: lokāṃl lokavidaḥ prāhur āśramā iti tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Worlds' — declare those who know the worlds; '<s>Āśramas</s> (stages of life)' — say those who know them;

children.text: strīpuṃnapuṃsakaṃ laiṅgāḥ parāparam athāpare // MandUpK_2.27 //
children.translated_text: 'Female, male, and neuter' — say those who argue from gender-marks (<s>liṅga</s>); 'The higher and the lower' — say yet others. || MandUpK 2.27 ||

children.text: sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭivido laya iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>)' — say those who know creation; 'It is dissolution (<s>laya</s>)' — say those who know it;

children.text: sthitir iti sthitividaḥ sarve ceha tu sarvadā // MandUpK_2.28 //
children.translated_text: 'It is continuance (<s>sthiti</s>)' — say those who know continuance — and all these [views exist] here always. || MandUpK 2.28 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.28
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_2.28

children.text: prāṇaḥ prājño bījātmā tatkāryabhedā hītare sthatyantāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Prājña</s>, the seed-self; the others, up to 'continuance,' are differentiations of its effect.

children.text: anye ca sarve laukikāḥ sarvaprāṇiparikalpitā bhedā rajjvāmiva sarpādayas tacchūnya ātmanyātmasvarūpāniścayahetoravidyayā kalpitā iti piṇḍīkṛtor'thaḥ /
children.translated_text: And all other differentiations imagined by all beings in the world — like the snake and the like in the rope — are void of [reality in] the <s>Ātman</s>, being imagined in the <s>Ātman</s> by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) due to the non-ascertainment of the <s>Ātman's</s> true nature. This is the summarized meaning.

children.text: prāṇādiślokānāṃ pratyekaṃ padārthavyākhyāne phalguprayojanatvātsiddhapadārthatvācca yatno na kṛtaḥ //28//
children.translated_text: No effort has been made to explain the meaning of each word individually in the verses on <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, because the utility would be trifling and the meanings of the terms are well-established. || 28 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.29
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.29

children.text: kiṃ bahunā
children.translated_text: In brief:

children.text: yaṃ bhāvaṃ darśayed yasya taṃ bhāvaṃ sa tu paśyati /
children.translated_text: Whatever entity [a teacher] reveals to someone, that entity he sees;

children.text: taṃ cāvati sa bhūtvāsau tadgrahaḥ samupaiti tam // MandUpK_2.29 //
children.translated_text: And that [entity], having become [identified with] him, protects him — that grasping [of the entity] approaches him. || MandUpK 2.29 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.29
prāṇādīnāmanyatamamuktamanuktaṃ vānyaṃ bhāvaṃ padārthaṃ darśayedyasyācāryo 'nyo vāpta idameva tattvamiti sa taṃ bhāvamātmabhūtaṃ paśyatyayamahamiti vā mameti vā /
taṃ ca draṣṭāraṃ sa bhāvo 'vati yo darśito bhāvo 'sau bhūtvā rakṣati /
svenātmanā sarvato niruṇaddhi /
tasmingrahastadgrahastadabhiniveśaḥ /
idameva
children.translated_text: 'This alone

children.text: tattvamiti sa taṃ grahītāramupaiti /
children.translated_text: is the reality' — that [grasping] approaches the one who grasps.

children.text: tasyātmabhāvaṃ nigacchatītyarthaḥ //29//
children.translated_text: It comes to constitute his very self — this is the meaning. || 29 ||

MandUpKC_2.29
Whatever entity — one of the previously mentioned ones such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, whether stated or unstated — a teacher or other trustworthy person reveals to someone [saying] 'This alone is the reality,' he sees that entity as his very self [thinking] 'This is what I am' or 'This is mine.'
And that entity protects the seer — the entity that was shown, having become [identified with him], guards him;
it completely encloses [him] with its own nature.
Attachment to it — that grasping, that fixation —

children.text: START MandUpK 2.30
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.30

children.text: etair eṣo 'pṛthagbhāvaiḥ pṛthag eveti lakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [<s>Ātman</s>], though not separate from these [imagined entities], is characterized as separate indeed;

children.text: evaṃ yo veda tattvena kalpayet so 'viśaṅkitaḥ // MandUpK_2.30 //
children.translated_text: He who thus knows [this] in truth, imagines without hesitation. || MandUpK 2.30 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.30
etaiḥ prāṇādibhirātmano 'pṛthagbhūtairapṛthagbhāvaireṣa ātmā rajjuriva sarpādi vikalapnārūpaiḥ pṛthageveti lakṣito 'bhilakṣito niścito mūḍhairityarthaḥ /
vivekināṃ tu rajjvāmiva kalpitāḥ sarpādayo nātmavyatirekeṇa prāṇādayaḥ santītyabhiprāya idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā (bṛ.u.2.4.6, 4.5.7) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_2.30
By these — <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — which are not separate from the <s>Ātman</s>, which are non-separate entities, this <s>Ātman</s> — like the rope [imagined] with the snake and the like, which are of the nature of mere imagination — is characterized as 'separate indeed,' that is, determined [as separate] by the deluded — this is the meaning.
But for the discriminating, just as the snake and the like imagined in the rope [do not exist apart from the rope], so too <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest do not exist apart from the <s>Ātman</s> — this is the intended meaning, as the <s>śruti</s> says: 'All this is what this <s>Ātman</s> is' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.6, 4.5.7).

children.text: evamātmavyatirekeṇāsatvaṃ rajjusarpavadātmani kalpitānāmātmānaṃ ca kevalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ yo veda tattvena śrutito yuktitaśca sa aviśaṅkito vedārthaṃ vibhāgataḥ kalpayetkalpayatītyarthaḥ idamevaṃparaṃ vākyamado 'nyaparamiti /
children.translated_text: Thus, one who knows in truth — from scripture and from reasoning — the non-existence of [these entities] apart from the <s>Ātman</s>, like the snake in the rope, and [knows] the <s>Ātman</s> alone as free from all conceptual construction — he, without hesitation, 'imagines' — that is, he classifies — the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> [saying]: 'This passage has this meaning; that passage has that meaning.'

children.text:
na hyanadhyātmavidvedāñjñātuṃ śaknoti tattvataḥ /
'nahyanadhyātmavitkaścitkriyāphalamupāśnute' (manu.6 / 82) iti hi mānavaṃ vacanam //30//
children.translated_text:
For one who does not know the inner Self cannot truly know the <s>Vedas</s>.
'For one who does not know the inner Self never attains the fruit of action' (<s>Manusmṛti</s> 6.82) — thus says the text of <s>Manu</s>. || 30 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.31
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.31

children.text: yadetdvaitasyāsattvamuktaṃ yuktitastadetadvedāntapramāṇāvagatamityāha
children.translated_text: That the unreality of duality has been stated through reasoning — this is also known through the <s>Vedānta</s> as a means of valid knowledge. He says:

children.text: svapnamāye yathā dṛṣṭaṃ gandharvanagaraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: As seen in dream and illusion (<s>māyā</s>), as a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s> —

children.text: tathā viśvam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vedānteṣu vicakṣaṇaiḥ // MandUpK_2.31 //
children.translated_text: So has this entire universe been seen by the wise in the <s>Vedāntas</s>. || MandUpK 2.31 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.31
svapnaśca māyā ca svapnamāye 'sadvastvātmike 'satyau sadvastvātmika iva lakṣyete 'vivekibhiḥ /
yathā ca prasāritapaṇyā paṇagṛhaprāsādastrīpuñjanapadavyavahārākīrṇamiva gandharvanagaraṃ dṛśyamānameva sadakasmādabhāvatāṃ gataṃ dṛṣṭam, yathā ca svapnamāye dṛṣṭe 'sadrūpe, tathā viśvamidaṃ dvaitaṃ samastamasaddṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_2.31
Dream and illusion — <s>svapna</s> and <s>māyā</s> — are of the nature of unreal objects; being unreal, they appear as if they are real to the undiscriminating.
And just as a <s>Gandharva</s>-city — appearing as if filled with shops displaying merchandise, mansions, women, men, villages, and bustling activity — is seen and then suddenly ceases to exist; and just as dream and illusion are seen to be unreal in nature — so too this entire universe of duality, in its entirety, is seen as unreal.

children.text:
kvetyāha vedānteṣu /
"neha nānāsti kiñcana"(ka.u.2 / 1 / 11, bṛ.u.4 / 4 / 19) "indro māyābhiḥ"(bṛ.u.2 / 5 / 19) "ātmaivedamagra āsīt" (bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 17) "brahma vedamagra āsīt"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 10) "dvitīyādvai bhayaṃ bhavati"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 2) "na tu taddvitīyasti"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) "yatra svasya sarvamātmaivābhūt"(bṛ.u.4 / 5 / 15) ityādiṣu vicakṣaṇairnipuṇataravastudarśibhi paṇḍitairityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Where? He says: in the <s>Vedāntas</s>.
'There is no multiplicity here at all' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.11, <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.19); '<s>Indra</s> [appears in many forms] through his <s>māyā</s> powers' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.19); 'The <s>Ātman</s> alone was this in the beginning' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.17); '<s>Brahman</s> alone was this in the beginning' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.10); 'From a second, verily, fear arises' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.2); 'There is no second [for it]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23); 'Where everything has become the <s>Ātman</s> alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.15) — in such [passages], by the wise, that is, by scholars who are the most discerning seers of reality.

children.text: "tamaḥśvabhranibhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ varṣabudbudasannibham /
children.translated_text: 'Seen as resembling darkness and shadow, resembling a rain-bubble,

children.text: nāśaprāyaṃ sukhāddhīnaṃ nāśottaramabhāvagam"iti vyāsasmṛteḥ //31//
children.translated_text: Tending toward destruction, devoid of happiness, after destruction leading to non-existence' — thus says the <s>smṛti</s> of <s>Vyāsa</s>. || 31 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.32
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.32

children.text:
prakaraṇārthopasaṃhārārtho 'yaṃ ślaukaḥ /
yadā vitathaṃ dvaitamātmaivaikaḥ paramārthataḥ saṃstadedaṃ niṣpannaṃ bhavati sarvo 'yaṃ laukiko vaidikaśca vyavahāro 'vidyāviṣaya eveti /
children.translated_text:
This verse is for the purpose of summarizing the meaning of the chapter.
Since duality is unreal and the <s>Ātman</s> alone is the ultimate reality — when this is established, then this entire system of worldly and Vedic transaction falls within the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) alone.

children.text: tadā
children.translated_text: Then:

children.text: na nirodho na cotpattir na baddho na ca sādhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), no origination (<s>utpatti</s>); no one in bondage, no aspirant;

children.text: na mumukṣur na vai mukta ity eṣā paramārthatā // MandUpK_2.32 //
children.translated_text: No one seeking liberation, and none indeed liberated — this is the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthatā</s>). || MandUpK 2.32 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.32
na nirodhaḥ nirodhanaṃ nirodhaḥ pralayaḥ, utpattirjananam, baddhaḥ saṃsārī jīvaḥ, sādhako mādhanavānmokṣasya, mumukṣurmocanārthī, mukto vimuktabandhaḥ /
utpattipralayayorabhāvādbaddhādayo na santītyeṣā paramārthatā /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_2.32
<s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) means dissolution or destruction; <s>utpatti</s> is origination or birth; <s>baddha</s> (the bound) is the <s>jīva</s> in <s>saṃsāra</s>; <s>sādhaka</s> is one who has the means for liberation; <s>mumukṣu</s> is one who desires liberation; <s>mukta</s> is one whose bondage is dissolved.
Because origination and dissolution are non-existent, the bound and the rest do not exist — this is the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthatā</s>).

children.text:
kathamutpattipralayorabhāvaḥ, ityucyate, dvaitasyāsatvāt /
yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14) "ya iha nāneva paśyati"(ka.u.2 / 1 / 10,11) "ātmaivedaṃ sarvam"(chā.u.7 / 25 / 2) "brahmaivedaṃ sarvam"(nṛsiṃhottara.7)"ekamevādvitīyaṃ"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 1) "idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 6,4 / 5 / 7) ityādinānāśrutibhyo dvaitasyāsatvaṃ siddham /
children.translated_text:
How is it that origination and dissolution are non-existent? It is said: because of the non-existence of duality.
'Where there is duality, as it were' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14); 'He who sees multiplicity here, as it were' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.10-11); 'The <s>Ātman</s> alone is all this' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.25.2); '<s>Brahman</s> alone is all this'; 'One only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.1); 'All this is what this <s>Ātman</s> is' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.6, 4.5.7) — from these and other various <s>śrutis</s>, the non-existence of duality is established.

children.text:
sato hyutpattiḥ pralayo vā syānnāsataḥ śaśaviṣāṇāde /
nāpyadvaitamutpadyate līyate vā /
advayaṃ cotpattipralayavacceti vipratiṣiddham /
children.translated_text:
Origination or dissolution could apply to what is real, but not to what is unreal like the horn of a hare.
Nor does the non-dual originate or dissolve.
And [to say] that the non-dual has origination and dissolution would be self-contradictory.

children.text:
yastu punardvaitasaṃvyavahāraḥ sa rajjusarpavadātmani prāṇādilakṣaṇaḥ kalpita ityuktam /
na hi manovikalpanāyā rajjusarpādilakṣaṇāyā rajjvāṃ pralaya utpattirvā /
na ca manasi rajjusarpasyotpattiḥ pralayo vā na cobhayato vā /
tathā mānasatvāviśeṣāddvaitasya /
na hi niyate manasi suṣupte vā dvaitaṃ gṛhyate /
children.translated_text:
But the transactional dealings with duality — they are imagined in the <s>Ātman</s>, like the snake in the rope, characterized by <s>prāṇa</s> and the like — this has been stated.
For there is neither dissolution nor origination in the rope of the mental imagination characterized by the rope-snake and the like;
nor is there origination or dissolution of the rope-snake in the mind; nor from both [perspectives].
Similarly with duality, because there is no difference from [its being] mental [in nature].
For when the mind is restrained or in deep sleep, duality is not apprehended.

children.text:
ato manovikalpanāmātraṃ dvaitamiti siddham /
tasmādsūktaṃ dvaitasyāsatvānnirodhādyabhāvaḥ paramārthateti /
children.translated_text:
Therefore it is established that duality is merely a construction of the mind.
Hence it is well said: because of the non-existence of duality, the non-existence of cessation and the rest is the ultimate truth.

children.text:
yadyevaṃ dvaitābhāve śāstravyāpāro nādvaite virodhāt /
tathā ca satyadvaitasya vastutve pramāṇābhāvācchūnyavādaprasaṅgaḥ, dvaitasya cābhāvāt /
na; rajjusarpādivikalpanāyā nirāspadatvānupapattiriti pratyuktametatkathamujjīvayasītyāha rajjurapi sarpavikalpasyāspada bhūtā vikalpitaiveti dṛṣṭāntānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text:
If this is so, then in the absence of duality, scriptural activity would have no scope — since it would conflict with non-duality.
And thus, if the non-dual reality truly exists, since there would be no means of valid knowledge [for it], the consequence of nihilism (<s>śūnyavāda</s>) [would follow], and because duality does not exist.
[Objection:] No; it has already been replied that the imagination [of the rope-snake] cannot be without a basis [i.e., the rope]. How can you revive [this objection]? [The opponent] says: Even the rope, which serves as the basis of the snake-imagination, is itself imagined — so the illustration itself fails.

children.text:
na; vikalpanākṣaye 'vikalpitasyāvikalpitatvādeva sattopatteḥ /
rajjusarpavadasattvamiti cet? na, ekāntenāvikalpitatvādavikalpitarajjvaṃśavatprāk sarpābhāvavijñānāt /
vikalpayituśca prāgvikalpanotpatteḥ siddhatvābhyupagamādasatvānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text:
No; because upon the cessation of imagination, that which is 'un-imagined' has existence precisely because it is un-imagined.
[Objection:] If [the rope] is unreal like the rope-snake? No; because it is absolutely un-imagined, like the un-imagined portion of the rope prior to the knowledge of the absence of the snake.
And because the one who imagines is accepted as established prior to the arising of imagination, the claim of non-existence is untenable.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ svarūpevyāpārābhāve śāstrasya dvaitavijñānanivartakatvam?
children.translated_text: But how can scripture, in the absence of activity regarding its own nature, be effective in removing the cognition of duality?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
rajjvāṃ sarpādivadātmani dvaitasyāvidyādhyastatvāt /
katham? sukhyahaṃ duḥkhī mūḍho jāto mṛto jīrṇo dehavān paśyāmi vyakto 'vyaktaḥ kartā phalī saṃyukto viyuktaḥ kṣīṇo vṛddhohaṃ mamaita ityevamādayaḥ sarva ātmanyadhyāropyante /
ātmaiteṣvanugataḥ sarvatrāvyabhicārāt /
yathā sarpadhārādibhedeṣu rajjuḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault, because duality is superimposed upon the <s>Ātman</s> through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), like a snake upon a rope. How? 'I am happy, I am miserable, I am deluded, I am born, I am dead, I am aged, I have a body, I see, I am manifest, I am unmanifest, I am the doer, I am the experiencer, I am conjoined, I am separated, I am diminished, I am increased, this is mine' — all such [attributions] are superimposed upon the <s>Ātman</s>. The <s>Ātman</s> is what runs through all these [states], being invariable everywhere — just as the rope [runs through] the various imaginations of snake, stream, and the like.

children.text:
yadā caivaṃ viśeṣyasvarūpapratyayasya siddhatvānna kartavyatvaṃ śāstreṇa /
akṛtakartṛ ca śāstraṃ kṛtānukāritve 'prāmāṇam /
yato 'vidyādhyāropitasukhitvādiviśeṣapratibandhādevātmanaḥ svarūpeṇānavasthānaṃ svarūpāvasthānaṃ ca śreya iti sukhitvādinivartakaṃ śāstram ātmanyasukhitvādipratyayakaraṇena neti netyasthūlādivākyaiḥ /
ātmasvarūpavadasukhitvādyapi sukhitvādibhedeṣu nānuvṛtto 'sti dharmaḥ /
yadyanuvṛttaḥ syānnādhyāropitasukhitvādilakṣaṇo viśeṣaḥ /
yathoṣṇatvaguṇaviśeṣavatyagnau śītatā /
children.translated_text: Just as coldness [cannot be attributed to] fire, which possesses the specific quality of heat.

children.text: tasmānnirviśeṣa evātmani sukhitvādayo viśeṣāḥ kalpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the specific attributes of happiness and the like are imagined upon the <s>Ātman</s>, which is indeed without specific attributes.

children.text: yattvasukhitvādiśāstramātmanastatsukhitvādi viśeṣanivṛtyarthameveti siddham /
children.translated_text: And the scripture teaching non-happiness and the like regarding the <s>Ātman</s> serves precisely for the removal of those specific attributes of happiness and the like — this is established.

children.text: "siddhaṃ tu nivartakatvāt"ityāgamavidāṃ sūtram //32//
children.translated_text: 'It is established, because [scripture] serves as a remover' — this is the <s>sūtra</s> of those who know the tradition (<s>āgama</s>). || 32 ||

And since the cognition of the nature of the qualified [entity] is already established, it is not something to be accomplished by scripture. And scripture that would create something uncreated, or that would merely imitate what is already accomplished, would lack authority. Since the <s>Ātman</s>'s non-abiding in its own nature is due to the obstruction of the specific attributes such as happiness and the like superimposed through <s>avidyā</s>, and since abiding in one's own nature is the highest good, scripture operates to remove happiness and the like by producing the cognition of non-happiness and the like in the <s>Ātman</s>, through statements like '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) and 'not gross' and so forth. Just as the nature of the <s>Ātman</s> [is invariable], so too non-happiness and the like do not have any property that persists across the various [states of] happiness and the like. If [such a property] did persist, the specific attribute characterized by superimposed happiness and the like would not [be superimposed].

children.text: START MandUpK 2.33
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.33

children.text: pūrvaślokārthasya hetumāha
children.translated_text: He states the reason for the meaning of the previous verse:

children.text: bhāvair asadbhir evāyam advayena ca kalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [<s>Ātman</s>] is imagined by unreal entities and by the non-dual [<s>Ātman</s>] itself;

children.text: bhāvā apy advayenaiva tasmād advayatā śivā // MandUpK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: The entities too are imagined by the non-dual alone — therefore, non-duality is auspicious. || MandUpK 2.33 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.33
yathā rajjvāmasadbhiḥ sapradhārādibhiradvayena ca rajjudravyeṇa satāyaṃ sarpa iyaṃ dhārā daṇḍo 'yamiti vā rajjudravyameva kalpyata evaṃ prāṇādibhiranantairasadbhirevāvidyamānaiḥ, na paramārthataḥ na hyapracalite manasi kaścidbhāva upalakṣayituṃ śakyate kenacit; na cātmanaḥ pracalanamasti; pracalitasyaivopalabhyamānā bhāvā na paramārthataḥ santaḥ kalpayituṃ śakyāḥ ato 'sadbhireva prāṇādabhāvairadvayena ca paramārthasatātmanā rajjuvattarvavikalpāspadabhūtenāyaṃ svayamevātmā kalpitaḥ; sadaikasvabhāvo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 2.33: Just as upon a rope, by the unreal [imaginations of] snake, stream, and the like, and by the non-dual rope-substance, which is real, the rope-substance itself is imagined as 'this is a snake,' 'this is a stream,' 'this is a stick' — so too by the innumerable unreal, non-existent [entities] such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — not in ultimate reality, for when the mind does not fluctuate, no entity whatsoever can be perceived by anyone; and there is no fluctuation of the <s>Ātman</s>; the entities perceived [only] when [the mind] has fluctuated cannot be imagined as ultimately real — therefore, by these unreal non-entities such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, and by the non-dual, ultimately real <s>Ātman</s>, which serves as the substratum of those imaginations like a rope, this <s>Ātman</s> itself is imagined — though being eternally of one nature.

children.text: te ca prāṇādibhāvāṃ apyadvayenaiva satātmanā vikalpitāḥ /
na hi nirāspadā kācitkalpanopalabhyate; ataḥ sarvakalpanāspadatvātsvenātnādvayasyāvyabhicārātkalpanāvasthāyāmapyadvayatā śivā /
children.translated_text: For no imagination is ever perceived without a substratum. Therefore, because [the non-dual <s>Ātman</s>] is the substratum of all imaginations, and because of the invariability of the non-dual [<s>Ātman</s>] by its own nature, non-duality is auspicious even in the state of imagination.

children.text: kalpanā eva tvaṃśivāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the imaginations themselves are inauspicious,

children.text: rajjusarpādivattrāsādikāriṇyo hi tāḥ /
children.translated_text: for they cause fear, like rope-snakes and the like.

children.text: advayatābhayātaḥ saiva śivā //33//
children.translated_text: Non-duality, being without fear, is therefore auspicious. || 33 ||
And those entities such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest are also imagined by the non-dual, real <s>Ātman</s> alone.

children.text: START MandUpK 2.34
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.34

children.text:
kutaścādvayatā śivā? nānābhūtaṃ /
pṛthaktvamanyasyānyasmādyatra dṛṣṭaṃ tatrāśivaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Why is non-duality auspicious? [Because:] wherever multiplicity — the separateness of one thing from another — is seen, there would be inauspiciousness.

children.text: nātmabhāvena nānedaṃ na svenāpi kathañcana /
children.translated_text: This [world] is not manifold by the nature of the <s>Ātman</s>, nor even by its own [nature] in any way;

children.text: na pṛthaṅ nāpṛthak kiñcid iti tattvavido viduḥ // MandUpK_2.34 //
children.translated_text: Nothing is either separate or non-separate — thus the knowers of reality know. || MandUpK 2.34 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.34
na hyatrādvaye paramārthasatyātmani prāṇādisaṃsārajātamidaṃ jagadātmabhāvena paramārthasvarūpeṇa nirīpyamāṇaṃ nānā vastvantarabhūtaṃ bhavati /
yathā rajjusvarūpeṇa prakāśena nirūpyamāṇo na nānābhūtaḥ kalpitaḥ sarpo 'sti tadvat /
nāpi svena prāṇādyātmanedaṃ vidyate /
kadācidapi rajjusarpavatkalpitatvādeva /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 2.34: For here, in this non-dual, ultimately real <s>Ātman</s>, this world consisting of <s>saṃsāra</s> beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, when examined from the standpoint of the <s>Ātman</s>'s ultimate nature, does not become manifold — a separate thing. Just as a snake imagined [upon a rope], when examined in the light of the rope's own nature, does not exist as manifold. Nor does this [world] exist by its own nature as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — because, like a rope-snake, it is imagined.

children.text: tathānyonyaṃ na pṛthakprāṇādi vastu yathāśvānmahiṣaḥ pṛthagvidyata evam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest are not separate from each other — not in the way that a buffalo is separate from a horse.

children.text: ato 'stvānnāpṛthagvidyate 'nyonyaṃ pareṇa vā kiñcidity evaṃ paramārthatattvamātavido brāhmaṇā viduḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, nothing exists as either non-separate from each other or from the supreme [<s>Ātman</s>] — thus do the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who know the ultimate reality know.

children.text: ato 'śivahetutvābhāvādadvayataiva śivetyabhiprāyaḥ //34//
children.translated_text: Therefore, since there is no cause of inauspiciousness, the purport is that non-duality alone is auspicious. || 34 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.35
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.35

children.text: tadetatsamyagdarśanaṃ stūyate
children.translated_text: This right vision is now praised:

children.text: vītarāgabhayakrodhair munibhir vedapāragaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By sages free from desire, fear, and anger, who have reached the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: nirvikalpo hy ayaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ prapañcopaśamo 'dvayaḥ // MandUpK_2.35 //
children.translated_text: this [<s>Ātman</s>] has been seen as without any differentiation, as the cessation of the phenomenal world, as non-dual. || MandUpK 2.35 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.35

vigatarāgabhayadveṣakrodhādisarvadaiṣaiḥ sarvadā munibhirmananaśīlairvivekibhirvedapāragairavagatavedārthatattvairjñānibhirni rvikalpaḥ sarvavikalpaḥ śūnyo 'mātmā dṛṣṭa upalabdho vedāntārthatatparaiḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ prapañco dvaitabhedavistārastasyopaśamo 'bhāvo yasminsa ātmā prapañcopaśamo 'ta evādvayo vigatadoṣaireva paṇḍitairvedāntārthatatparaiḥ saṃnyasibhiḥ paramātmā draṣṭuṃ śakyaḥ, nānyai rāgādikaluṣitacetobhiḥ svapakṣapātidarśanaistārkikādibhirityābhiprāyaḥ //35//
children.translated_text: By those who are forever free from all defects — desire, fear, hatred, anger, and the rest — by sages given to reflection, by the discriminating, by those who have reached the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s>, who have understood the truth of the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, by the knowers — the <s>Ātman</s> has been seen, perceived, as being without any differentiation, devoid of all imagined distinctions, by those devoted to the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s> — [as] the cessation of the phenomenal world, the phenomenal expansion being the spread of duality's distinctions, whose cessation, i.e., absence, [characterizes] that <s>Ātman</s> — which is the cessation of the phenomenal world, and therefore non-dual. The supreme <s>Ātman</s> can be seen only by those learned ones free from defects, devoted to the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s>, who are <s>saṃnyāsins</s> (renunciants) — not by others whose minds are tainted by desire and the like, such as logicians and the like who are partial to their own doctrines. || 35 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 2.35:

children.text: START MandUpK 2.36
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.36

children.text: yasmātsarvānarthapraśamarūpatvādadvayaṃ śivamabhayam
children.translated_text: Since the non-dual is auspicious and fearless, being of the nature of the cessation of all misfortune,

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viditvainam advaite yojayet smṛtim /
children.translated_text: therefore, having thus known this, one should fix one's memory on non-duality;

children.text: advaitaṃ samanuprāpya jaḍavallokam ācaret // MandUpK_2.36 //
children.translated_text: having attained non-duality, one should move about in the world like one inert. || MandUpK 2.36 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_2.36
ata evaṃ viditvainamadvaite smṛtiṃ yojayet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having known this thus, one should fix one's memory (<s>smṛti</s>) on non-duality.

children.text: advaitāvagamāyaiva smṛtiṃ kuryādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should exercise memory solely for the realization of non-duality — this is the meaning.

children.text: taccādvaitamavagamyāhamasmi paraṃ brahmeti viditvāśanāyādyatītaṃ sākṣādaparokṣādajamātmānaṃ sarvalokavyavahārātītaṃ jaḍavallokamācaret /
children.translated_text: And having realized that non-duality, knowing 'I am the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,' having known the <s>Ātman</s> that is beyond hunger and the rest, directly and immediately perceived, unborn, transcending all worldly transactions — one should move about in the world like one inert.

children.text: aprakhyāpayannātmānamahamevaṃvidha ityabhiprāyaḥ //36//
children.translated_text: Not proclaiming oneself [by thinking] 'I am of such a [realized] nature' — this is the purport. || 36 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 2.36:

children.text: START MandUpK 2.37
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.37

children.text: kayā caryayā lokamācaredityāha
children.translated_text: With what conduct should one move about in the world? To this he says:

children.text: niḥstutir nirnamaskāro niḥsvadhākāra eva ca /
children.translated_text: Without praise, without salutation, without the utterance of <s>svadhā</s>,

children.text: calācalaniketaś ca yatir yādṛcchiko bhavet // MandUpK_2.37 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yati</s> (renunciant), with both the moving and the unmoving as his dwelling, should live spontaneously. || MandUpK 2.37 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.37
stutinamaskārādisarvakarmavarjitastyaktasarvabāhyaiṣaṇaḥ pratipannaparamahaṃsapārivrājya ityabhiprāyaḥ"etaṃ vai tamātmānaṃ viditvā"(bṛ.u.3 / 5 / 1) ityādiśruteḥ;"tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ"(gītā 5 / 17) ityādismṛteśca calaṃ śarīraṃ pratikṣaṇamanyathābhāvāt, acalamātmatattvam, yadākadācidbhojanādivyavahāranimittamākāśavadacalaṃ svarūpamātmatattvamātmano niketamāśrayamātmasthitiṃ vismṛtyāhamiti manyate yadā tadā calo deho niketo yasya sa ayamevaṃ calācalaniketo vidvānna punarbāhyaviṣayāśrayaḥ; sa ca yādṛcchiko bhaved yadṛcchāprāptakaupīnacchādanagrāsamātradehasthitirityarthaḥ //37//
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 2.37: Having abandoned all actions such as praise, salutation, and the rest, having relinquished all external desires, having undertaken the supreme <s>paramahaṃsa</s> (the highest order of) renunciation — this is the purport. As scripture says: 'Having known this very <s>Ātman</s>' (Bṛh. Up. 3.5.1) and so forth. And from <s>smṛti</s>: 'Their intellect absorbed in That, their self identified with That, established in That, devoted to That as the supreme goal' (Gītā 5.17) and so forth. The body is moving — because it changes from moment to moment; the truth of the <s>Ātman</s> is unmoving. When, on occasion, due to some transaction such as eating and the like, forgetting the unmoving, space-like true nature of the <s>Ātman</s> as his abode, his resting-place, his abiding-in-the-<s>Ātman</s>, one thinks 'I' [identifying with the body] — then the moving body is his dwelling. This knower, whose dwelling is both the moving and the unmoving, is not dependent on external objects. And he should live spontaneously (<s>yādṛcchika</s>) — meaning that his bodily sustenance consists merely of a loincloth, covering, and food obtained by chance. || 37 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 2.38
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 2.38

children.text: tattvam ādhyātmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā tattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu bāhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen the truth inwardly (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), and having seen the truth externally,

children.text: tattvībhūtas tadārāmas tattvād apracyuto bhavet // MandUpK_2.38 //
children.translated_text: one should become identified with the truth, delight in the truth, and remain undeviated from the truth. || MandUpK 2.38 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_2.38
bāhyaṃ pṛthivyāditatvaṃ ādhyātmikaṃ ca dehādilakṣaṇaṃ rajjusarpādivatsvapnamāyādivacca asat"vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam" (chā.u.6 / 1 / 4) ityādiśruteḥ /
ātmā ca sabāhyābhyantaro hyajo 'pūrvo 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsna ākāśavatsarvagataḥ sūkṣmo 'calo nirguṇo niṣkalo niṣkriyaḥ"tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi"(chā.u.6 / 8 / 16) iti śruteḥ /
ityevaṃ tattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tattvībhūtastadārāmo na bāhyaramaṇo yathātattvadarśī kaściccittamātmatvena pratipannaścittacalanamanucalitamātmānaṃ manyamānastatattvāccalitaṃ dehādibhūtamātmānaṃ kadācinmanyate pracyuto 'hamātmatattvādidānīmiti; samāhite cu manasi kadācittattvabhūtaṃ prasannātmānaṃ manyata idānīmasmi tattvībhūta iti; na tadātmavidbhavet /
ātmana ekarūpattvātsvarūpapracyavanāsambhavācca /
sadaiva brahmāsmītyapracyuto bhavettattvātsadāpracyutātmatattvadarśano bhavedityabhiprāyaḥ"śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ"(gītā 12 / 18) "samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu"(gītā 13 / 17) ityādi smṛteḥ //38//
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 2.38: The external truth — earth and the other [elements] — and the internal truth — characterized by the body and the like — [are both] unreal, like rope-snakes and the like, like dreams, <s>māyā</s>, and the like, as scripture says: 'A modification is but a name, a verbal handle' (Chānd. Up. 6.1.4) and so forth. And the <s>Ātman</s> is 'both externally and internally unborn, without prior [existence], without inner [division], without outer [limitation], complete, all-pervading like space, subtle, unmoving, without qualities, without parts, without action' — as scripture says: 'That is the truth, that is the <s>Ātman</s>, you are That' (Chānd. Up. 6.8.16). Having thus seen the truth, one becomes identified with the truth, delighting in it, not delighting externally. But if someone who considers himself a seer of truth, having accepted the mind as the <s>Ātman</s>, considers the fluctuation of the mind as the fluctuation of the <s>Ātman</s>, and sometimes thinks 'my <s>Ātman</s> has become the body and the like, having deviated from the truth' and then, when the mind is composed, sometimes thinks 'now I am identified with the truth, my <s>Ātman</s> is serene' — such a person would not be a knower of the <s>Ātman</s>. Because the <s>Ātman</s> is of one nature, deviation from one's own nature is impossible. One should remain undeviated from the truth — always [knowing] 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' — meaning one should always be a seer of the truth of the <s>Ātman</s>, from which there is no deviation. As <s>smṛti</s> says: 'The wise see the same in a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a dog-eater' (Gītā 5.18), 'Equal toward all beings' (Gītā 13.27), and so forth. || 38 ||

children.text: Advaitaprakaraṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Advaitaprakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Non-Duality)

children.text: START MandUpK 3.1
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.1

children.text:
oṃkāranirṇaya uktaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivodvaita ātmeti pratijñāmātreṇa /
jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyata iti ca /
tatra dvaitābhāvastu vaitathyaprakaraṇena svapnamāyāgandharvanagarādidṛṣṭāntairdṛśyatvādyantavattvādihetubhistarkeṇa ca pratipāditā /
advaitaṃ kimāgamamātreṇa pratipattavyamāhosvittarkeṇāpītyata āha- śakyate tarkeṇāpi jñātum; tatkathamityadvaitaprakaraṇamārabhyata upāsyopāsānādibhedajātaṃ sarvaṃ vitathaṃ kevalaścātmādvayaḥ paramārtha iti sthitamatīte prakaraṇe; yataḥ-
children.translated_text: The determination of <s>Oṃkāra</s> has been stated: the cessation of the phenomenal world, auspicious, non-dual <s>Ātman</s> — by way of mere assertion. And [it was stated that] 'when [non-duality] is known, duality does not exist.' There, the absence of duality was established in the <s>Vaitathya</s> (Unreality) chapter through illustrations of dream, <s>māyā</s>, celestial city, and the like, through reasons such as being perceived, having a beginning and end, and the like, and through reasoning. The question arises: is non-duality to be understood through scripture alone, or through reasoning as well? To this he says: it can be known through reasoning also. How then? The <s>Advaitaprakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on Non-Duality) is commenced. The position established in the preceding chapter [is that] the entire collection of distinctions — worshipper, worshipped, and the like — is unreal, and the <s>Ātman</s> alone, non-dual, is the ultimate reality. Since —

children.text: upāsanāśrito dharmo jāte brahmaṇi vartate /
children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> (spiritual practice) that depends on worship operates within the domain of <s>Brahman</s> conceived as born;

children.text: prāgutpatter ajaṃ sarvaṃ tenāsau kṛpaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_3.1 //
children.translated_text: before [any] origination, everything is unborn — therefore, such a one is called pitiable. || MandUpK 3.1 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.1
upāsanāśrita upāsanāmātmano mokṣasādhanatvena gata upāsako 'haṃ mamopāsyaṃ brahma /
tadupāsanaṃ kṛtvā jāte brahmaṇīdānīṃ vartamāno 'jaṃ brahma śarīrapātādūrdhvaṃ pratapatsye prāgutpatteścājamidaṃ sarvamahaṃ ca /
yadātmako 'haṃ prāgutpatteridānīṃ jāto jāte brahmaṇi ca vartamāna upāsanayā punastadeva pratipatsya ityevamupāsanāśrito dharmaḥ sādhako yenaivaṃ kṣudrabrahmavittenāsau kāraṇena kṛpaṇo dīno 'lpakaḥ smṛto nityājabrahmadarśibhirityabhiprāyaḥ /
"yadvācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāgabhyudyate /
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate"(ke.u.1 / 4) ityādiśrutestalavakāraṇām //1//
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.1: One who depends on worship — a worshipper who has resorted to worship as the means to liberation of the self, [thinking] 'I am the worshipper, <s>Brahman</s> is what I worship; having performed that worship, I, who exist in <s>Brahman</s> that has been born, will now attain the unborn <s>Brahman</s> after the fall of this body; and before origination, all this was unborn, and so was I; what I was in nature before origination, now being born and abiding in born <s>Brahman</s>, I shall attain that same [state] again through worship' — such a <s>dharma</s> depending on worship is the practitioner, and for this very reason — namely, being a knower of a limited <s>Brahman</s> — he is called pitiable (<s>kṛpaṇa</s>), wretched, small, by those who see the eternally unborn <s>Brahman</s> — this is the purport. As the scripture of the <s>Talavakāras</s> [says]: 'That which is not expressed by speech, by which speech is expressed — know that alone to be <s>Brahman</s>, not what people worship here' (Kena Up. 1.4) and so forth. || 1 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.2
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.2

children.text: sabāhyābhyantaramajamātmānaṃ pratipattumaśaknuvannavidyayā dīnamātmānaṃ manyamāno jāto 'haṃ jāte brahmaṇi varte tadupāsanāśritaḥ sanbrahma pratipatsya ityevaṃ pratipannaḥ kṛpaṇo bhavati yasmāt-
children.translated_text: Unable to realize the <s>Ātman</s> that is unborn, both externally and internally, considering oneself pitiable through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [thinking] 'I am born, I abide in born <s>Brahman</s>, depending on worship I shall attain <s>Brahman</s>' — one who has thus understood becomes pitiable. Because —

children.text: ato vakṣyāmy akārpaṇyam ajāti samatāṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall speak of that which is free from pitiableness, unborn, and has attained equality;

children.text: yathā na jāyate kiñcij jāyamānaṃ samantataḥ // MandUpK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: how nothing whatsoever is born, though appearing to be born everywhere. || MandUpK 3.2 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.2
ato vakṣyāmyakārpaṇyakṛpaṇabhāvamajaṃ brahma /
taddhi kārpaṇyāspadam"yatrānyo 'nyatpaśyatyanyacchṛṇotyanyadvijānāti tadalpaṃ martyamasat"(chā.u.7 / 24 / 1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tadviparītaṃ sabāhyābhyantaramajakārpaṇyaṃ bhūmākhyaṃ brahma /
yatprāpyāvidyākṛtasarvakārpaṇyanivṛttistatkārpaṇyaṃ vakṣyāmītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.2: Therefore I shall speak of that which is free from pitiableness — the unborn <s>Brahman</s>. For that [state of pitiableness] is indeed the domain of pitiableness, as scripture says: 'That which sees another, hears another, knows another — that is small, mortal, unreal' (Chānd. Up. 7.24.1) and so forth. The opposite of that — [<s>Brahman</s>] that is both externally and internally unborn, free from pitiableness, called '<s>Bhūman</s>' (the Infinite) — having attained which, the cessation of all pitiableness created by <s>avidyā</s> [occurs]: I shall speak of that freedom from pitiableness — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadajāti, avidyamānā jātirasya samatāṃ gataṃ sarvasāmyaṃ gatam /
kasmāt? avayavavaiṣamyābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the absence of inequality among parts.

children.text: yaddhi sāvayavaṃ vastu tadavayavavaiṣamyaṃ gacchajjāyata ityucyate /
children.translated_text: For a thing that has parts is said to be born when it undergoes inequality among its parts.

children.text: idaṃ tu niravayavatvātsamatāṃ gatamiti na kaiścidavayavaiḥ sphuṭatyatojātyakārpaṇyam /
children.translated_text: But this [<s>Brahman</s>], being without parts, has attained equality — it does not burst forth through any parts — therefore [it is] unborn and free from pitiableness.

children.text: samantataḥ samantādyathā na jāyate kiñcidalpamapi na sphuṭati rajjusarpavadavidyākṛtadṛṣṭyā jāyamānaṃ yena prakāreṇa na jāyate sarvato 'jameva brahma bhavati tathā taṃ prakāraṃ śṛṇvityarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: From all sides — just as nothing whatsoever, not even the slightest, is born or issues forth — like the snake on a rope, that which from the perspective created by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) appears to be born, by whatever manner it is not born — <s>Brahman</s> is entirely unborn (<s>aja</s>). 'Listen to that manner' — this is the meaning. ||2||
That [<s>Brahman</s>] is <s>ajāti</s> (without birth) — birth is non-existent for it — and it has attained equality, having reached complete sameness.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.3
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.3

children.text:
ajāti brahmakārpaṇyaṃ vakṣyāmīti pratijñātam /
tatsiddhyarthaṃ hetuṃ dṛṣṭāntaṃ ca vakṣyāmītyāha-
children.translated_text: Having promised 'I shall declare the non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>,' he now says 'I shall state the reason and the illustration for establishing that' —

children.text: ātmā hy ākāśavajjīvair ghaṭākāśair ivoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) is described by the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) as like space — just as pot-space (<s>ghaṭākāśa</s>) [describes space].

children.text: ghaṭādivac ca saṃghātair jātāv etan nidarśanam // MandUpK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: And [it is described] through the aggregates like pots and the like — this is the illustration for [apparent] birth. || Kārikā 3.3 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.3
ātmā paro hi yasmādākāśavatsūkṣmo niravayavaḥ sarvagata ākāśavadukto jīvaiḥ kṣetrajñairghaṭākāśairiva ghaṭākāśatulya udita uktaḥ sa evākāśasamaḥ para ātmā /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 3.3: The supreme Self, being like space — subtle, without parts, all-pervading — is said to be spoken of by the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls, field-knowers) as comparable to pot-space: that very supreme Self is like great space, and is spoken of as comparable to pot-space.

children.text:
atha vā ghaṭākāśairyathākāśa udita utpannastathā paro jīvātmabhirutpannaḥ /
jīvātmanāṃ parasmādātmana utpattiryā śrūyate vedānteṣu sā mahākāśādghaṭākāśotpattisamā na paramārtha ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, just as space is said to be born from pot-space, so too the supreme [Self] is said to be born from individual souls. The birth of individual souls from the supreme Self that is heard of in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts is comparable to the birth of pot-space from great space — it is not the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). This is the intention.

children.text: tasmādevākāśādghaṭādayaḥ saṃghātā yathetpadyanta evamākāśasthānīyātparamātmanaḥ pṛthivyādibhūtasaṃghātā ādhyātmikāśca kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇā rajjusarpavadvikalpitā jāyante /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as from space — represented by pots and the like — aggregates such as pots arise, similarly from the supreme Self — which occupies the position of space — the aggregates of elements such as earth, as well as the individual bodily and sensory apparatus, arise as imagined, like a snake on a rope.

children.text: ata ucyate ghaṭādivacca saṃghātairudita iti /
children.translated_text: Hence it is said: 'And [it is described] through the aggregates like pots and the like.'

children.text: yadā mandabuddhipratipādayiṣayā śrutyātmano jātirucyate jīvādīnāṃ tadā jātāvupagamyamānāyāmetannidarśanaṃ dṛṣṭānto yathoditākāśavadityādiḥ //3//
children.translated_text: When scripture speaks of the birth of the Self, of <s>jīvas</s> and the like, with the intention of instructing those of dull intellect, then, when birth is provisionally accepted, this is the illustration — 'as space is spoken of,' and so forth. ||3||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.4
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.4

children.text: ghaṭādiṣu pralīneṣu ghaṭākāśādayo yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as, when pots and the like are dissolved, pot-spaces and the like

children.text: ākāśe saṃpralīyante tadvaj jīvā ihātmani // MandUpK_3.4 //
children.translated_text: Merge into space, so too the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) [merge] here into the Self. || Kārikā 3.4 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.4
yathā ghaṭādyutpattyā ghaṭākāśādyutpattiḥ; yathā vā ghaṭādipralaye ghaṭākāśādipralayastadvaddehādisaṃghātotpattyā jīvotpattistatpralaye ca jīvānāmihātmani pralayo na svata ityarthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: Just as from the production of pots and the like arises the [apparent] production of pot-space and the like; and just as upon the dissolution of pots and the like there is the dissolution of pot-space and the like — similarly, through the production of aggregates such as the body, there is the [apparent] production of the <s>jīva</s>, and upon their dissolution, the dissolution of <s>jīvas</s> here into the Self — not inherently. This is the meaning. ||4||
Commentary on Kārikā 3.4

children.text: START MandUpK 3.5
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.5

children.text: sarvadeheṣvātmaikatva ekasmiñjananamaraṇasukhādimatyātmani sarvātmanāṃ tatsambandhaḥ kriyāphalasāṅkaryaṃ ca syāditi ya āhurdvaitinastānpratīdamucyate-
children.translated_text: Those dualists who say: 'If the Self is one in all bodies, then in one Self possessing birth, death, happiness, and the like, all selves would be connected with those [experiences], and there would be a confusion of actions and their results' — to counter them, this is said:

children.text: yathaikasmin ghāṭākāśe rajodhūmādibhir yute /
children.translated_text: Just as, when one pot-space is associated with dust, smoke, and the like,

children.text: na sarve saṃprayujyante tadvaj jīvāḥ sukhādibhiḥ // MandUpK_3.5 //
children.translated_text: Not all [pot-spaces] are associated [with them] — so too the <s>jīvas</s> with happiness and the like. || Kārikā 3.5 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.5
yathaikasminghaṭākāśe rajodhūmādibhiryute saṃyukte na sarve ghaṭākāśādayastadrajodhūmādibhiḥ saṃyujyante tadvajjīvāḥ sukhādibhiḥ /
nanveka evātmā?
bāḍham; nanu na śrutaṃ tvayākāśavatsarvasaṃghāteṣveka evātmeti?
yadyeka evātmā tarhi sarvatra sukhī duḥkhī ca syāt?
na cedaṃ sākhyacodyaṃ sambhavati /
na hi sāṃkhya ātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhādimattvamicchati buddhisamavāyābhyupagamātsukhaduḥkhādīnām /
na copalabdhisvarūpasyātmano bhedakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇamasti /
bhedābhāve pradhānasya pārārthyānupapattiriti cet; na pradhānakṛtasyārthasyātmanyasamavāyāt /
yadi hi pradhākṛto bandho mokṣo vārthaḥ puruṣeṣu bhedena samavaiti tataḥ pradhānasya pārārthyamātmaikatve nopapadyata iti yuktā puruṣabhedakalpanā /
na ca sākhyairbandho mokṣo vārthaḥ puruṣasamaveto 'bhyupagamyate /
nirviśeṣāśca cetanamātrā ātmāno 'bhyupagamyante /
ataḥ puruṣasattāmātraprayuktameva pradhānasya pārārthyaṃ siddhaṃ na tu puruṣabhedaprayuktamiti /
ataḥ puruṣabhedakalpanāyāṃ na pradhānasya pārārthyaṃ hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 3.5: Just as, when one pot-space is associated — connected — with dust, smoke, and the like, not all pot-spaces and the like are associated with that dust, smoke, and the like, so too the <s>jīvas</s> with happiness and the like. 'But is not the Self one?' Indeed. 'But have you not heard that the Self is one in all aggregates, like space?' If the Self is indeed one, then it would be happy and suffering everywhere? This objection of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> is not tenable. For the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> do not accept that the Self possesses happiness, suffering, and the like, since they maintain that [these belong to] <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) in conjunction [with the Self]. And there is no valid means of knowledge for imagining plurality in the Self, whose essential nature is mere cognition. If it is objected that without plurality [of selves], the purposefulness-for-another (<s>pārārthya</s>) of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) cannot be established — no, because the purpose accomplished by <s>Pradhāna</s> does not inhere in the Self. For if bondage or liberation — the purpose accomplished by <s>Pradhāna</s> — inhered in the individual souls distinctly, then the imagining of plurality of <s>puruṣas</s> would be justified on the ground that the purposefulness-for-another of <s>Pradhāna</s> cannot be established with the oneness of the Self. But bondage or liberation as a purpose is not accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> as inhering in <s>puruṣa</s>. And the selves are accepted as being without distinction, mere consciousness. Therefore, the purposefulness-for-another of <s>Pradhāna</s> is established merely by the existence of <s>puruṣa</s>, not by the plurality of <s>puruṣas</s>. Hence the purposefulness-for-another of <s>Pradhāna</s> is not a reason for imagining plurality of <s>puruṣas</s>.

children.text:
na cānyatpuruṣabhedakalpanāyāṃ pramāṇamasti sākhyānām /
parasattāmātrameva caitannimittīkṛtya svayaṃ badhyate mucyate ca pradhānam /
paraścopalabdhimātrasattāsvarūpeṇa pradhānapravṛttau heturnakenacidviśeṣeṇeti kevalamūḍhatayaiva puruṣabhedakalpanā vedārthaparityāgaśca /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> have no other valid means for imagining plurality of <s>puruṣas</s>. It is merely by taking the existence of the other [i.e., consciousness] as the occasion that <s>Pradhāna</s> itself binds and liberates itself. And the other, by its essential nature as mere cognition-existence, is the cause of <s>Pradhāna</s>'s activity — not through any specific distinction. Therefore, the imagining of plurality of <s>puruṣas</s> is merely out of confusion, and constitutes an abandonment of the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text:
ye tvāhurvaiśeṣikādaya icchādaya ātmasamavāyina iti, tadapyasat /
smṛtihetūnāṃ saṃskārāṇāmapradeśavatyātmanyasamavāyāt /
ātmamanaḥ saṃyogācca smṛtyutpatteḥ smṛtiniyamānupapatti /
yugapadvā sarvasmṛtyutpattiprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for what the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others say — that desire and the like inhere in the Self — that too is incorrect. Because the <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), which are the causes of memory, cannot inhere in the Self which has no spatial parts. And since memory arises from the conjunction of Self and mind, the regularity of memory cannot be accounted for. Or else, all memories would arise simultaneously.

children.text:
na ca bhinnajātīyānāṃ sparśādihīnānāmātmanāṃ mana ādibhiḥ saṃbandho yuktaḥ /
na ca dravyādrūpādayo guṇāḥ karmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyā vā bhinnāḥ santi pareṣām /
yadi hyatyantabhinnā eva dravyātsyuricchādayaścātmanastathā ca sati dravyeṇa teṣāṃ sambandānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is not reasonable that the Self — which is of a different category and devoid of touch and the like — should be connected with the mind and other [instruments]. And according to the opponents, qualities such as form and the like, as well as action, generality, particularity, and inherence, do not exist as distinct from substance. For if desire and the like were absolutely different from the Self as substance, then their connection with substance would be impossible.

children.text:
ayutasiddhānāṃ samavāyalakṣaṇaḥ sambandho na virudhyata iti cet, na /
icchādibhyo 'nityebhya ātmano nityasya pūrvasiddhatvānnāyutasiddhatvopapattiḥ /
ātmanāyutasiddhatve cecchādīnāmātmagatamahatvavannityatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
sa cāniṣṭaḥ /
ātmano 'nirmokṣaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: If it is said that inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) — the relation between things that are inseparably connected (<s>ayutasiddha</s>) — is not contradictory: no, because the Self, being eternal, is already established prior to desire and the like, which are non-eternal — hence the inseparable connection is not tenable. If desire and the like were inseparably connected with the Self, they would be permanent like the magnitude (<s>mahatva</s>) belonging to the Self — and that is undesirable, because it would entail the impossibility of liberation for the Self.

children.text:
samavāyasya ca dravyādanyatve sati dravyeṇa sambandhāntaraṃ vācyaṃ yathā dravyaguṇayoḥ /
samavāyo nityasambandha eveti na vācyamiti cettathā ca samavāyasambandhavatāṃ nityasambandhaprasaṅgātpṛthaktvānupapatti /
atyantapṛthaktve ca dravyādīnāṃ sparśavadasparśadravyayoriva ṣaṣṭyarthānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And if inherence is different from substance, then another relation between it and substance must be stated, as between substance and quality. If it is said that inherence is an eternal relation and so need not be stated — then, for those possessing the inherence-relation, the consequence of eternal connection would arise, and separateness would be impossible. And if substances and the like were absolutely separate, the relationship indicated by the sixth case-ending (possessive) would be impossible, just as between a tangible and an intangible substance.

children.text: icchādyupajanāpāyavadguṇatve cātmano 'nityatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
dehaphalādivatsāvayavatvaṃ vikriyāvatvaṃ ca dehādivadeveti doṣāvaparihāryau /
children.translated_text: And the defects of having parts like the body, fruits, and the like, and of being subject to modification like the body and the like, would be unavoidable.

children.text: yathā tvākāśasyāvidyādhyāropitarajodhūmamalavatvādidoṣavatvaṃ tathātmano 'vidyādhyāropitabuddhyādyupādhikṛtasukhaduḥkhādidoṣavatve bandhamokṣādayo vyavahārikā na virudhyante /
children.translated_text: But just as the contamination of space by dust, smoke, impurity, and the like is superimposed through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), so too when the defects of happiness, suffering, and the like — caused by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the rest, superimposed through ignorance — are attributed to the Self, the conventional dealings of bondage, liberation, and the like are not contradicted.

children.text: sarvavādibhiravidyākṛtavyavahārābhyupagamātparamārthānabhyupagamācca /
children.translated_text: Because all schools accept that conventional usage is created by ignorance, and do not accept it as the ultimate reality.

children.text: tasmādātmabhedaparikalpanā vṛthaiva tārkikaiḥ kriyata iti //5//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the imagining of plurality of selves is done entirely in vain by the logicians. ||5||
And if the Self were a substance with qualities that arise and perish like desire and the like, the consequence of the Self's impermanence would follow.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.6
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.6

children.text: kathaṃ punarātmabhedanimitta iva vyavahāra ekasminnātmanyavidyākṛta upapadyata iti, ucyate-
children.translated_text: How then is conventional usage, as if caused by plurality of the Self, established as created by ignorance in the one Self? It is stated —

children.text: rūpakāryasamākhyāś ca bhidyante tatra tatra vai /
children.translated_text: Forms, functions, and names differ here and there,

children.text: ākāśasya na bhedo 'sti tadvaj jīveṣu nirṇayaḥ // MandUpK_3.6 //
children.translated_text: But there is no difference in space — so too is the conclusion regarding the <s>jīvas</s>. || Kārikā 3.6 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.6
yathehākāśa ekasminghaṭakarakāpavarakādyākāśānāmalpatvamahatvādirūpāṇi bhidyante tathā kāryamudakāharaṇadhāraṇaśayanādisamākhyāśca ghaṭākāśakarakākāśa ityādyāstatkṛtāśca bhinnā dṛśyante /
tatra tatra vai vyavahāraviṣaya ityarthaḥ /
sarvo 'yamākāśo rūpādibhedakṛto vyavahāro na paramārtha eva /
children.translated_text: All this conventional usage pertaining to space, created by differences in form and the like, is not the ultimate reality.

children.text: paramārthatastvākāśasya na bhedosti /
children.translated_text: In ultimate reality, however, there is no difference in space.

children.text: na cākāśabhedanimitto vyavahāro 'styantareṇa paropādhikṛtaṃ dvāram /
children.translated_text: And there is no conventional usage caused by differences in space without the doorway created by external limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>).

children.text: yathaitattadveddahopādhibhedakṛteṣu jīveṣu ghaṭākāśasthānīyeṣvātmasu nirūpaṇātkṛto buddhimadbhirnirṇayo niścaya ityarthaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: Just as this is so, in the <s>jīvas</s> — which occupy the position of pot-space — that are constituted by the adjunct-differences of body and the like, the conclusion determined by the wise is this — this is the meaning. ||6||

Commentary on Kārikā 3.6: Just as in the one space, the forms of pot-space, pitcher-space, room-space, and the like — such as smallness, largeness, and so on — differ, and likewise their functions — carrying water, storing, sleeping, and the like — and their names, such as 'pot-space,' 'pitcher-space,' and so on, and the [things] produced by those [adjuncts] are seen as different. 'Here and there' means 'in the sphere of conventional usage.'

children.text: START MandUpK 3.7
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.7

children.text: nanu tatra paramārthakṛta eva ghaṭākāśādiṣu rūpakāryādibhedavyavahāra iti? naitadasti, yasmāt
children.translated_text: But surely the conventional usage of differences in form, function, and the like among pot-spaces is ultimately real? This is not so, because —

children.text: nākāśasya ghaṭākāśo vikārāvayavau yathā /
children.translated_text: Pot-space is neither a modification nor a part of [infinite] space.

children.text: naivātmanaḥ sadā jīvo vikārāvayavau tathā // MandUpK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>jīva</s> is never a modification or a part of the Self. || Kārikā 3.7 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.7
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 3.7

children.text: paramārthākāśasya ghaṭākāśo na vikāraḥ; yathā suvarṇasya rucakādiryathā vāpāṃ phenabudbudahimādiḥ; nāpyavayavo yathā vṛkṣasya śākhādiḥ /
children.translated_text: Pot-space is not a modification of the ultimately real space — as a bracelet and the like are of gold, or as foam, bubbles, frost, and the like are of water. Nor is it a part — as a branch and the like are of a tree.

children.text: na tathā0kāśasya ghaṭākāśo vikārāvayavau yathā tathā naivātmanaḥ parasya paramārthasato mahākāśasthānīyasya ghaṭākāśasthānīyo jīvaḥ sadā sarvadā yathoktadṛṣṭāntavanna vikāro nāpyavayavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as pot-space is neither a modification nor a part of space, so too the <s>jīva</s> — which occupies the position of pot-space — is never, at any time, a modification or a part of the supreme, ultimately real Self — which occupies the position of great space — as shown by the stated illustration.

children.text: ata ātmabhedakṛto vyavahāro mṛṣaivetyarthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: Therefore, conventional usage based on the plurality of the Self is entirely false — this is the meaning. ||7||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.8
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.8

children.text:
yasmādyathā ghaṭākāśādibhedabuddhinibandhano rūpakāryādibhedavyavahārastathā dehobādhijīvabhedakṛto janmamaraṇādivyavahāraḥ /
tasmāttatkṛtameva kleśakarmaphalamalavatvamātmano na paramārthata ityetamarthaṃ dṛṣṭāntena pratipipādayiṣannāha-
children.translated_text: Since the conventional usage of birth, death, and the like, caused by the differentiation of body-limiting-adjunct-<s>jīva</s>, is like the conventional usage of differences in form, function, and the like, which is based on the notion of differences in pot-space and the like — therefore, the contamination of the Self by afflictions, actions, and their fruits is caused by that [limiting adjunct] alone and is not ultimately real. Wishing to illustrate this meaning by an example, he says —

children.text: yathā bhavati bālānāṃ gaganaṃ malinaṃ malaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as for children, the sky becomes dirty with impurities,

children.text: tathā bhavaty abuddhānām ātmāpi malino malaiḥ // MandUpK_3.8 //
children.translated_text: So too for the unwise, the Self becomes dirty with impurities. || Kārikā 3.8 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.8
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 3.8

children.text: yathā bhavati loke bālānāmavivekināṃ gaganamākāśaṃ ghanarajodhūmādimalārmalinaṃ malavanna gaganaṃ malavadyāthātmyavivekinām, tathā bhavatyātmā paro 'pi yo vijñātā pratyakkleśakarmaphalamalairmalino 'buddhānāṃ pratyagātmavivakerahitānāṃ nātmavivekavatām /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, for children — the undiscriminating — the sky, space, appears dirty with impurities of clouds, dust, smoke, and the like — but the sky is not really possessed of impurities for those who discern its true nature — so too the supreme Self, the inner knower, appears contaminated by the impurities of afflictions, actions, and fruits for the unwise — those devoid of discrimination regarding the inner Self — but not for those who discriminate regarding the Self.

children.text: nahyūṣaradeśastṛḍvatprāṇyadhyāropitodakaphenataraṅgādimāṃstathā nātmābudhāropitakleśādimalairmalino bhavatītyarthaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: Just as a salt-desert does not become endowed with superimposed water, foam, and waves imagined by a thirsty being, so too the Self does not become contaminated by the impurities of afflictions and the like superimposed by the unwise — this is the meaning. ||8||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.9
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.9

children.text: punarapyuktamevārthaṃ prapañcayati-
children.translated_text: He further elaborates the same point already stated —

children.text: maraṇe saṃbhave caiva gatyāgamanayor api /
children.translated_text: In death and birth, in going and coming,

children.text: sthitau sarvaśarīreṣu ākāśenāvilakṣaṇaḥ // MandUpK_3.9 //
children.translated_text: And in abiding in all bodies — [the Self] is not different from space. || Kārikā 3.9 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.9
ghaṭākāśajanmanāśagamanāgamanasthitivatsarvaśarīreṣvātmano janmamaraṇādirākāśenāvilakṣaṇaḥ pratyetavya ityarthaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: Just as with the birth, destruction, going, coming, and abiding of pot-space, [the Self's] birth, death, and the like in all bodies should be understood as not different from space — this is the meaning. ||9||
Commentary on Kārikā 3.9

children.text: START MandUpK 3.10
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.10

children.text: saṃghātāḥ svapnavat sarve ātmamāyāvisarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All aggregates, like dream[-objects], are projected by the <s>māyā</s> of the Self.

children.text: ādhikye sarvasāmye vā nopapattir hi vidyate // MandUpK_3.10 //
children.translated_text: Whether there is superiority or equality [among them], no valid reasoning exists [to establish their reality]. || Kārikā 3.10 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.10
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 3.10

children.text: ghaṭādisthānīyāstu dehādisaṃghātāḥ svapnadṛśyadehādivanmāyāvikṛtadehādivaccātmamāyāvisarjitāḥ; ātmano māyāvidyā tayā pratyupasthāpitā na paramārthataḥ santītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The aggregates of body and the like — which occupy the position of pots and the like — are like the bodies and the like seen in dream, and like the bodies and the like produced by <s>māyā</s> (magic) — they are projected by the <s>māyā</s> (ignorance) of the Self; that is, they are presented by the Self's <s>māyā</s>-ignorance and do not ultimately exist — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadyādhikyamadhikabhāvastirgdehādyapekṣayā devādikāryakaraṇasaṃghātānāṃ yadi vā sarveṣāṃ samataiva naiṣāmupapattiḥ sambhavaḥ sadbhāpratipādako heturvidyate nāsti, hi yasmāttasmādavidyākṛtā eva na paramārthataḥ santītyarthaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: Whether there is superiority — a state of being greater — of the aggregates of divine bodies, senses, and the like compared to animal bodies and the like, or whether there is equality among all of them, no valid reasoning — no proof establishing their real existence — exists for these. The reason is that they are created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and do not ultimately exist — this is the meaning. ||10||

children.text:
START MandUpK 3.11
utpattyādivarjitasyādvayasyātmatatvasya śrutipramāṇakatvapradarśanārthaṃ vākyānyupanyasyante-
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 3.11: In order to demonstrate that the truth of the Self, which is non-dual and free from origination and the like, has <s>śruti</s> (scripture) as its authority, [the following] passages are cited —

children.text: rasādayo hi ye kośā vyākhyātās taittirīyake /
children.translated_text: The sheaths such as the sheath of food (<s>rasa</s>) and the rest, which are explained in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s> (Taittirīya Upaniṣad),

children.text: teṣām ātmā paro jīvaḥ khaṃ yathā saṃprakāśitaḥ // MandUpK_3.11 //
children.translated_text: Among them, the <s>jīva</s> as the supreme Self is revealed like space. || Kārikā 3.11 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.11
rasādayo 'nnarasamayaḥ prāṇamaya ityevamādayaḥ kośā iva kośā asyāderivottarottarasyāpekṣayā bahirbhāvātpūrvapūrvasya vyākhyātā vispaṣṭamākhyātāstaittirīyake taittirīyakaśākhopaniṣadvallyāṃ teṣāṃ kośānāmātmā yenātmanā pañcāpi kośā ātmavanto 'ntaratamena, sa hi sarveṣāṃ jīvananimittatvājjīvaḥ /
ko 'sāvityāha-para evātmā yaḥ pūrvam"satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma"(tai.u.2 / 1) iti prakṛtaḥ /
yasmādātmanaḥ spapnamāyādivadākāśādikrameṇa rasādayaḥ kośalakṣaṇāḥ saṃghātā ātmamāyāvisarjitā ityuktam /
children.translated_text: Since from that <s>Ātman</s>, like dream or <s>māyā</s> (illusion), through the sequence beginning with space (<s>ākāśa</s>), the aggregates characterized as sheaths, beginning with taste (<s>rasa</s>), are projected by the <s>Ātman</s>'s own <s>māyā</s> — so it has been stated.

children.text: sa ātmāsmābhiryathā khaṃ tatheti saṃprakāśitaḥ"ātmā hyākāśavat"(advaita.3) ityādiślaukaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Ātman</s> has been illuminated by us as being like space (<s>kha</s>), through verses such as 'the <s>Ātman</s> is indeed like space' (<s>Advaita</s> [Kārikā] 3) and the like.

children.text: na tārkikaparikalpitātmavatpuruṣabuddhipramāṇagamya ityabhiprāyaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: The intention is: [the <s>Ātman</s>] is not accessible through the means of knowledge — <s>puruṣa</s> (soul), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) — as conceived by the logicians (<s>tārkikas</s>). || 11 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.11: The sheaths (<s>kośas</s>), beginning with the food-sheath (<s>annarasamaya</s>), the vital-breath sheath (<s>prāṇamaya</s>), and so forth, each outer one explained as if an outer sheath relative to the succeeding inner one, are clearly described in the <s>Taittirīya</s> — in the section (<s>vallī</s>) of the <s>Taittirīyaka</s> branch <s>Upaniṣad</s>. The <s>Ātman</s> of those sheaths — that by which all five sheaths are ensouled, being the innermost — he indeed is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), being the cause of life for all of them. Who is he? He says: the supreme <s>Ātman</s> himself, who was introduced earlier [in the text] as 'truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1).

children.text: START MandUpK 3.12
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.12

children.text: dvayor dvayor madhujñāne paraṃ brahma prakāśitam /
children.translated_text: In the honey-knowledge (<s>madhu-jñāna</s>), through pairs [of cosmic and individual aspects], the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is illuminated,

children.text: pṛthivyāmudare caiva yathākāśaḥ prakāśitaḥ // MandUpK_3.12 //
children.translated_text: Just as space is revealed [to be one] in the earth and in the belly. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.12 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.12
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.12:

children.text: kiṃ cādhidaivamadhyātmaṃ ca tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣaḥ pṛthivyādyantargato yo vijñātā para evātmā brahma sarvamiti dvayordvayorādvaitakṣayātparaṃ brahma prakāśitam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>puruṣa</s> (being), luminous and immortal, who exists within the cosmic (<s>adhidaiva</s>) and individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) [aspects] — the earth and so on — who is the knower, is the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, is <s>Brahman</s>, is everything. Through the resolution of duality in each pair [of cosmic and individual], the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is illuminated.

children.text: kvetyāha- brahmavidyākhyaṃ madhvamṛtamamṛtatvaṃ modanahetutvādvijñāyate yasminniti madhujñānaṃ madhubrāhmaṇaṃ tasminnityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where? He says: in the <s>madhu-jñāna</s> (honey-knowledge) — the honey, which is <s>amṛta</s> (immortality), the cause of bliss because it is known; the knowledge in which [this is understood] is the <s>madhu-jñāna</s>, i.e., the <s>Madhu Brāhmaṇa</s> [section of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>] — in that, is the meaning.

children.text: kimivetyāha-pṛthivyāmudare caiva yathaika ākāśo 'numānena prakāśito loke tadvadityarthaḥ //12//
children.translated_text: Like what? He says: just as one and the same space is revealed by inference in the earth and in the belly — so too in the world, is the meaning. || 12 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.13
jīvātmanor ananyatvam abhedena praśasyate /
children.translated_text: The non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and the <s>Ātman</s> (Supreme Self) is praised as identity;

children.text: nānātvaṃ nindyate yac ca tad evaṃ hi samañjasam // MandUpK_3.13 //
children.translated_text: The plurality [posited by others] is censured — for this alone is consistent. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.13 ||
BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.13

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.13
yadyuktitaḥ śrutitaśca nirdhāritaṃ jīvasya parasya cātmano jīvātmanoranyatvamabhedena praśasyate stūyateśāstreṇa vyāsādibhiśca /
yacca sarvaprāṇisādhāraṇaṃ svābāvikaṃ śāstrabahiṣkṛtaiḥ kutārkikairviracitaṃ nānātvadarśanaṃ nindyate"na tu taddvītīyamasti"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) "dvitīyādvai bhayaṃ bhavati"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 2) "udaramantaraṃ kurute, ata tasya bhayaṃ bhavati"(tai.u.2 / 7 / 1) "idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 6, 4 / 5 / 7) "mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati"(ka.u.2 / 1 / 10) ityādivākyaiścānyaiśca brahmavidbhiḥ /
yaccaitattadevaṃ hi samañjasamṛjvavabodhaṃ nyāyyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this [non-duality] is thus consistent — straightforward in understanding, reasonable — this is the meaning.

children.text: yāstu tārkikaparikalpitāḥ kudṛṣṭayastā anṛjvyo nirūpyamāṇā na ghaṭanāṃ prāñcantītyabhiprāyaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: The intention is: but the false views constructed by logicians are crooked and, when examined, do not hold together. || 13 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.13: The non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, which has been established through reasoning and scripture, is praised — extolled — by the scriptures and by [teachers] such as <s>Vyāsa</s> and others, as identity. And the view of plurality, which is common to all beings [in their natural state], innate, and constructed by false logicians outside the scriptures, is censured — by [scriptural] statements such as 'There is no second thing besides it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23), 'From a second indeed fear arises' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.2), 'He who makes even the slightest difference, for him there is fear' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.7.1), 'All this is indeed the <s>Ātman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.6, 4.5.7), 'Death after death does he attain who sees as if there is plurality here' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.10), and by other knowers of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.14
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.14

children.text: jīvātmanoḥ pṛthaktvaṃ yat prāgutpatteḥ prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: The separateness of the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Ātman</s> that is proclaimed before creation

children.text: bhaviṣyadvṛtyā gauṇaṃ tan mukhyatvaṃ hi na yujyate // MandUpK_3.14 //
children.translated_text: Is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>), with reference to a future state — its literalness is indeed not tenable. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.14 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.14
nanu śrutyāpi jīvaparamātmanoḥ pṛthaktvaṃ yatprāgutpatterutpatyarthopaniṣadvākyebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ prakīrtitaṃ karmakāṇḍe 'nekaśaḥ kāmabhedata idaṅkāmo 'daḥkāma iti; paraśca"sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyām"(ṛ.saṃ.10 / 12 / 1) ityādimantravarṇaiḥ; tatra kathaṃ karmajñānakāṇḍavākyavirodhe jñānakāṇḍavākyārthasyaivaikatvasya sāmañjasyamavadhāryata iti?
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.14: But [one might object]: the separateness of the <s>jīva</s> and the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, which is proclaimed before creation — that is, prior to the <s>Upaniṣad</s> passages dealing with creation — in the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual section) in many places through distinctions of desires such as 'desiring this,' 'desiring that'; and concerning the supreme [being] through mantra-words such as 'He supported the earth and the sky' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 10.12.1) and the like — in that case, how can the meaning of the <s>jñānakāṇḍa</s> (knowledge section) passages alone, namely oneness, be established as consistent when there is contradiction between the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> and <s>jñānakāṇḍa</s> passages?

children.text:
atrocyate-"yato ve9māni bhūtāni jāyante"(tai.u.3 / 1) "yathāgneḥ kṣudrā visphuliṅgāḥ"(bṛ.u.2 / 1 / 10) "tasmādvai9tasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ"(tai.u.2 / 1 / 2) "tadaikṣata"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 3) "tattejosṛjata"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 3) ityādyutpattyarthopaniṣadvākyebhyaḥ prākpṛthaktvaṃ karmakāṇḍe prakīrtitiṃ yattanna paramārtham /
kiṃ tarhi? gauṇaṃ mahākāśaghaṭākāśādibhedavat /
yathaudanaṃ pacatīti bhaviṣyadvṛttyā yadvat /
na hi bhedavākyānāṃ kadācidapi mukhyabhedārthatvamupapadyate /
svābhāvikāvidyāvatprāṇibhedadṛṣṭyanuvāditvādātmabhedavākyānām /
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: the separateness proclaimed in the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> prior to the <s>Upaniṣad</s> passages dealing with creation — such as 'From which indeed these beings are born' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1), 'As from a fire tiny sparks' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.10), 'From that <s>Ātman</s> space was born' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2), 'It willed' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.3), 'It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.3) — that is not ultimately real. What then? It is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>), like the [seeming] difference between the great space and the space in a pot. Just as [the expression] 'he cooks rice' [uses the future-referring sense where rice is not yet cooked], so too [the passages on separateness use a prospective sense]. For the literal meaning of separateness can never be established for the passages on difference, since the passages on the difference of the Self are merely restatements of the perception of difference held by beings endowed with natural <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text:
iva copāniṣatsūtpattipralayādivākyairjīvaparamātmanorekatvameva pratipipādayiṣitam"tattvamasi" (chā.u.6 / 8 -16)"anyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmīti na sa veda"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 10) ityādibhiḥ /
ata upaniṣatsv ekatvaṃ śrutyā pratipādayiṣitaṃ bhaviṣyatīti bhāvinīmekavṛttimāśritya loke bhedadṛṣṭyanuvādo gauṇa evetyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Rather, through the <s>Upaniṣad</s> passages on creation, dissolution, and the like, the identity alone of the <s>jīva</s> and the supreme <s>Ātman</s> is intended to be established — through [texts] such as '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' ('That thou art,' <s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8-16) and 'He who thinks "He is different, I am different" — he does not know' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.10). Therefore, since the <s>Upaniṣads</s> intend to establish oneness through scripture, and relying on the future-oriented [culminating] understanding of oneness, the restatement of worldly perception of difference is figurative alone — this is the intention.

children.text:
atha vā"tadaikṣata" (chā.u.6 / 2 / 3) "tattojo 'sṛjata"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 3) ityādyutpatteḥ prāk"ekamevādvitīyam"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 2) ityekatvaṃ prakīrtitam /
