tadeva ca"tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi"(chā.u.6 / 8 -16) ityekatvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tāṃ bhaviṣyadvṛttipekṣya yajjīvātmanoḥ pṛthaktvaṃ yatra kvacidvākye gamyamānaṃ tadgauṇam, yathodanaṃ pacatīti tadvat //14//
children.translated_text: Alternatively: before creation — 'It willed' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.3), 'It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.3) — oneness is proclaimed: 'One only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.2). And that same oneness will be [reaffirmed]: 'That is the truth, that is the <s>Ātman</s>, <s>tat tvam asi</s>' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8-16). With reference to that future-oriented [reaffirmation], whatever separateness of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Ātman</s> is understood from any passage, that is figurative — just like 'he cooks rice.' || 14 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.15
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.15

children.text:
nanu yadyutpatteḥ prāgajaṃ sarvamekamevādvitīyaṃ tathāpyutpatterūrdhvaṃ jātamidaṃ sarvaṃ jīvāśca bhinnā iti, maivam; anyārthatvādutpattiśrutīnām /
pūrvamapi parihṛtya evāyaṃ doṣaḥ svapnavadātmamāyāvisarjitāḥ saṃghātā ghaṭākāśotpattibhedādivajjīvānāmutpattibhedādiriti /
ita evotpattibhedādiśrutibhya ākṛṣye7ha punarutpattiśrutīnāmaidaṃparyapratipipādayiṣayopanyāsaḥ-
children.translated_text: But if everything was unborn, one only without a second before creation, then after creation everything that has arisen and the <s>jīvas</s> are different — [the reply is:] not so, because the creation passages have a different purpose. This fault has been addressed previously too — the aggregates projected by the Self's <s>māyā</s>, like dream, and the difference in the creation of <s>jīvas</s>, like the difference in the creation of pot-space and the like. Drawing upon these creation passages, this presentation is made here again in order to establish the purport of the creation passages —

children.text: mṛllohavisphuliṅgādyaiḥ sṛṣṭir yā coditānyathā /
children.translated_text: The creation that is taught through [the examples of] clay, iron, sparks, and the like, and in other ways,

children.text: upāyaḥ so 'vatārāya nāsti bhedaḥ kathañcana // MandUpK_3.15 //
children.translated_text: Is a means for introduction [to the truth of non-duality] — there is no real difference whatsoever. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.15 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.15
mṛllokavisphuliṅgādidṛṣṭāntopanyāsaiḥ sṛṣṭiryā coditā prakāśitānyathānyathā ca sa sarvaḥ sṛṣṭiprakāro jīvaparamātmaikatvabuddhyavatārayopāyo 'smākam /
yathā prāṇasaṃvāde vāgādyāsurapāpmavedhādyākhyāyikā kalpitā prāṇavaiśiṣṭyabodhāvatārāya /
tadapyasiddhamiti cet /
na; śākhābhedeṣvanyathānyathā ca prāṇādisaṃvādaśravaṇāt /
yadi hi saṃvādaḥ paramārtha evābhūdekarūpa eva saṃvādaḥ sarvaśākhāsvaśroṣyata viruddhānekaprakāreṇa nāśroṣyata /
śrūyate tu; tasmānna tādarthyaṃ saṃvādaśrutīnām /
tathotpattivākyāni pratyetavyāni /
kalpasargabhedātsaṃvādaśrutīnāmutpattiśrutīnāṃ ca pratisargamanyathātvamiti cet?
na; niṣprayojanatvādyathoktabuddhyavatāraprayojanavyatirekeṇa /
na hyanyaprayojanavattvaṃ saṃvādotpattiśrutīnāṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum /
children.translated_text: For no other purpose of the dispute and creation passages can be conceived.

children.text: tathātvapratipattaye dhyānārthamiti cenna; kalahotpattipralayānāṃ pratipatteraniṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text: If [one says] their purpose is meditation for the realization of that [truth] — no, because the realization of [real] strife, creation, and dissolution is undesirable [as an object of meditation].

children.text: tasmādutpattyādiśrutaya ātmaikatvabuddhyavatārāyaiva nānyārthāḥ kalpayituṃ yuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the creation passages and the like are fit to be construed only as means for introducing the understanding of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>, and no other meaning should be imposed on them.

children.text: ato nāstyutpattyādikṛto bhedaḥ kathañcana //15//
children.translated_text: Hence there is no difference whatsoever produced by creation and the like. || 15 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.15: The creation that is illuminated — set forth through the examples of clay, iron, sparks, and the like — in various ways, all these modes of describing creation are, for us, a means for the introduction of the understanding of the oneness of <s>jīva</s> and supreme <s>Ātman</s>. Just as in the dispute of the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>), the story of speech and the other [faculties] piercing the demons of sin was constructed for the purpose of introducing [the understanding of] the pre-eminence of <s>prāṇa</s>. If [one says] that too is unproven — no, because in different branches [of the <s>Veda</s>], the dispute of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest is heard in different ways. For if the dispute were ultimately real, the dispute would have been heard in one and the same form in all branches, and would not have been heard in multiple contradictory forms. But it is heard [in various forms]; therefore, the purpose of the dispute passages is not [historical] factuality. The creation passages should be understood in the same way. If [one argues that] the differences in the dispute passages and creation passages are due to differences in cosmic cycles (<s>kalpas</s>) and creations (<s>sargas</s>) — no, because that serves no purpose beyond the stated purpose of introducing the understanding [of oneness].

children.text: START MandUpK 3.16
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.16

children.text:
yadi para evātmā nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāva ekaḥ paramārthaḥ san"ekamevādvitīyam" (chā.u.6 / 2 / 2) ityādiśrutibhyo 'sadanyatkimartheyamupāsanopadiṣṭā"ātmā vā9re draṣṭavyaḥ"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 5) "ya ātmāpahatapāpmā"(chā.u.8 / 7 / 1,3) "sa kratuṃ kurvīta"(chā.u.3 / 14 / 1) "ātmetyevopāsīta"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 7) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ, karmāṇi cāgnihotrādīni?
śṛṇu tatra kāraṇam-
children.translated_text: If the supreme <s>Ātman</s> alone is of the nature of eternally pure, awakened, and free, the one ultimate reality, 'one only without a second' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.2) — as [established] from these and other <s>śrutis</s>, with nothing else being [ultimately] real — then for what purpose is meditation taught [in texts] such as 'The <s>Ātman</s> indeed is to be seen' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.5), 'The <s>Ātman</s> free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.7.1, 3), 'Let him form the resolve' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.14.1), 'One should meditate on the <s>Ātman</s> alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.4.7) — and rituals such as the <s>agnihotra</s> and the like? Hear the reason for that —

children.text: āśramāstrividhā hīnamadhyamotkṛṣṭadṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The stages of life (<s>āśramas</s>) are threefold: for those of inferior, middling, and superior vision.

children.text: upāsanopadiṣṭeyaṃ tadartham anukampayā // MandUpK_3.16 //
children.translated_text: This meditation is taught for their sake, out of compassion. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.16 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.16
upāsanopadiṣṭeyaṃ tadarthaṃ mandamadhyamadṛṣṭyāśramādyarthaṃ karmāṇi ca, na cātmaika evādvitīya iti niścitottamadṛṣṭyarthaṃ dayālunā vedenānukampayā sanmārgagāḥ santaḥ kathamimāmuttamāmekatvadṛṣṭiṃ prāpnuyuriti /
"yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano matam /
tadeva brhama tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate"(ke.u.1 / 4) "tattvamasi"(chā.u.6 / 8 -16)"ātmaivedaṃ sarvam"(chā.u.7 / 25 / 3) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ //16//
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.16: This meditation is taught for their sake — for the sake of those of dull and middling vision in the [various] stages of life — and so are rituals. But it is not for the purpose of the one who has the settled, superior vision of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s> alone as non-dual. By the compassionate <s>Veda</s>, out of mercy — [thinking] 'how may those on the right path attain this supreme vision of oneness?' — [these teachings are given]. [As confirmed by:] 'That which the mind does not think, by which, they say, the mind is thought — know that alone as <s>Brahman</s>, not this which [people] worship here' (<s>Kena Upaniṣad</s> 1.4), '<s>tat tvam asi</s>' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8-16), 'The <s>Ātman</s> alone is all this' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.25.3), and other <s>śrutis</s>. || 16 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.17
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.17

children.text:
śāstropapattibhyāmavadhāritatvādadvayātmadarśanaṃ samyagdarśanaṃ tadbāhyatvānmithyādarśanamanyat /
itaśca mithyādarthanaṃ dvaitīnāṃ rāgadveṣādidoṣāspadatvāt /
katham?
children.translated_text: Since the vision of the non-dual <s>Ātman</s> has been ascertained through scripture and reasoning as right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), all other [views] are false vision, being external to it. And the vision of the dualists is false for another reason too — because it is the locus of defects such as attachment and aversion. How?

children.text: svasiddhāntavyavasthāsu dvaitino niścitā dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: The dualists, firmly established in the positions of their own doctrines,

children.text: parasparaṃ virudhyante tairayaṃ na virudhyate // MandUpK_3.17 //
children.translated_text: Contradict one another — this [non-dual view] is not contradicted by them. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.17 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.17
svasiddhāntavyavasthāsu svasiddhāntaracanāniyameṣu kapilakaṇādabuddharhatādidṛṣṭyanusāriṇo dvaitino niścitāḥ /
evamevaiṣa paramārtho nānyatheti tatra tatrānuraktāḥ pratipakṣaṃ cātmanaḥ paśyantastaṃ dviṣanta ityevaṃ rāgadveṣopetāḥ svasiddhāntadarśananimittam eva parasparamanyonyaṃ virudhyante /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.17: Those who follow the views of <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Arhat</s> (Jain), and others — the dualists, firmly established in the positions of their own doctrines, in the fixed arrangements of their own systems — [thinking] 'This alone is the ultimate truth, not otherwise' — being attached to their respective [views] and seeing their own opponents, they hate them. Thus, endowed with attachment and aversion caused by their own doctrinal views, they contradict one another, mutually.

children.text: tairanyonyavirodhibhirasmadīyo 'yaṃ vaidikaḥ sarvānanyatvādātmaikatvadarśanapakṣo na virudhyate yathā svahastapādādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By these mutually contradicting [dualists], our Vedic position of the vision of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>, since all are non-different [from it], is not contradicted — just as [one is not contradicted] by one's own hands, feet, and the like.

children.text: evaṃ rāgadveṣādidoṣānāspadātmaikatvabuddhireva samyagdarśanamityabhiprāyaḥ //17//
children.translated_text: The intention is: thus, the understanding of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>, which is not a locus for defects such as attachment and aversion, is alone the right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>). || 17 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.18
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.18

children.text: kena hetunā tairna virudhyata ityucyate-
children.translated_text: For what reason is [our view] not contradicted by them? It is said —

children.text: advaitaṃ paramārtho hi dvaitaṃ tadbheda ucyate /
children.translated_text: Non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) is the ultimate reality; duality is said to be its modification.

children.text: teṣām ubhayathā dvaitaṃ tenāyaṃ na viruddhyate // MandUpK_3.18 //
children.translated_text: For them [the dualists], duality exists in both ways [i.e., whether they take it as real or unreal] — therefore this [non-dual view] is not contradicted by them. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.18 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.18
advaitaṃ paramārtho hi yasmādadvaitaṃ nānātvaṃ tasyādvaitasya bhedastadbhedastasya kāryamityarthaḥ /
"ekamevādvitīyam"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 2) "tattejo 'sṛjata"(chā.u.6 / 2 / 3) iti śruterūpapatteśca svacittaspandanābhāve samādhau mūrchāyāṃ suṣuptau cābhāvāt /
atastadbheda ucyate dvaitam /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.18: Non-duality is the ultimate reality — since non-duality [is the truth], plurality; the modification of that non-duality, its product — that is the meaning of 'its modification is said to be duality.' [This is established] from the <s>śruti</s> 'One only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.2) and 'It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.2.3), from reasoning, and from [duality's] absence in <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) when the fluctuations of one's own mind have ceased, in fainting, and in deep sleep. Therefore, duality is said to be its modification.

children.text:
dvaitināṃ tu teṣāṃ paramārthataścāparamārthataścobhayathāpi dvaitameva /
yadi ca teṣāṃ bhrāntānāṃ dvaitadṛṣṭirasmākamadvaitadṛṣṭirabhrāntānām, tenāyaṃ hetunāsmatpakṣe na virudhyate taiḥ /
"indro māyābhiḥ ṣururūpa īyate" (bṛ.u.2 / 5 / 11) "na tu taddvitīyamasti"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: But for those dualists, duality exists both ways — both ultimately and non-ultimately. If their deluded vision sees duality and our undeluded vision sees non-duality, then for this reason our position is not contradicted by them. [As the <s>śruti</s> states:] '<s>Indra</s> by his <s>māyā</s> powers assumes many forms' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.11), 'There is no second thing besides it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23).

children.text: yathā mattagajārūḍha unmattaṃ bhūmiṣṭhaṃ prati gajārūḍhohaṃ gajaṃ vāhaya māṃ pratīti bruvāṇamapi taṃ prati na vāhayatyavirodhabuddhyā tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as one mounted on a mad elephant, when a madman standing on the ground says 'I am mounted on an elephant, drive the elephant toward me,' does not drive [the elephant] toward him, thinking there is no [real] opposition — so too [is the non-dualist's position unassailable].

children.text: tataḥ paramārthato brahmavidātmaiva dvaitinām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in ultimate reality, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is the very Self of the dualists.

children.text: tenāyaṃ hetunāsmatpakṣo na viruddhyate taiḥ //28//
children.translated_text: For this reason, our position is not contradicted by them. || 18 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.19
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.19

children.text: dvaitamadvaitabheda ityukte dvaitamapyadvaitavatparamārthasaditi syāt kasyacidāśaṅketyata āha-
children.translated_text: When it is said that duality and non-duality are different, someone might suspect that duality too is ultimately real like non-duality. Therefore he says—

children.text: māyayā bhidyate hy etan nānyathājaṃ kathañcana /
children.translated_text: For this [non-dual reality] is differentiated by <s>māyā</s> (illusion); the unborn is never [differentiated] otherwise in any way.

children.text: tattvato bhidyamāne hi martyatām amṛtaṃ vrajet // MandUpK_3.19 //
children.translated_text: For if it were differentiated in reality, the immortal would become mortal. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.19 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.19
yatparamārthasadadvaitaṃ māyayā bhidyate hyetacaimirikānekacandravadrajjuḥ sarpadhārādibhirbhedairiva na paramārthato niravayavatvādātmanaḥ /
sāvayavaṃ hyavayavānyathātvena bhidyate /
yathā mṛd ghaṭādibhedaiḥ /
tasmānniravayavamajaṃ nānpathā kathañcana kenacidapi prakāreṇa na bhidyata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.19: That which is ultimately real and non-dual is differentiated by <s>māyā</s> alone—like [the appearance of] multiple moons in an illusory mirage, or like a rope [appearing as] a snake, a stream of water, and the like—not in ultimate reality, because the Self is without parts. For only what has parts can be differentiated through the alteration of its parts—as clay [is differentiated] into pots and the like. Therefore, the partless, unborn [Self] is not differentiated otherwise—not in any way whatsoever by any means—this is the intended meaning.

children.text: tattvato bhidyamāne hyamṛtamajamadvayaṃ svabhāvataḥ sanmartyatāṃ vrajet; yathāgniḥ śītatām /
children.translated_text: For if it were differentiated in reality, the immortal, unborn, non-dual [Self], being immortal by its very nature, would become mortal—just as fire would become cold.

children.text: taccāniṣṭaṃ svabhāvavaiparītyagamanam, sarvapramāṇavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: And that is unacceptable—the reversal of one's own nature—because it contradicts all means of valid knowledge.

children.text: ajamavyayamātmatattvaṃ māyayaiva bhidyate na paramārthataḥ /
children.translated_text: The unborn, imperishable Self-reality is differentiated by <s>māyā</s> alone, not in ultimate reality.

children.text: tasmānna paramārthasadadvaitam //19//
children.translated_text: Therefore, duality is not ultimately real. ||19||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.20
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.20

children.text: ajātasyaiva bhāvasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who argue [for creation] desire the birth of that which is indeed unborn;

children.text: ajāto hy amṛto bhāvo martyatāṃ katham eṣyati // MandUpK_3.20 //
children.translated_text: How can an unborn, immortal entity come to be mortal? || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.20 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.20
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.20:

children.text: ye tu punaḥ kecidupaniṣadvyākhyātāro brahmavādino vāvadūkā ajātasyaivātmatattvasya amṛtasya svabhāvato jātim utpattimicchanti paramārthata eva teṣāṃ jātaṃ cettadeva martyatāmeṣyatyavaśyam /
children.translated_text: But those who are expositors of the <s>Upaniṣads</s> or verbose advocates of <s>Brahman</s>—whoever desires the birth, the origination, of the very Self-reality that is unborn and immortal by nature, as being ultimately real—if it were born for them, then that very thing would inevitably become mortal.

children.text: sa cājāto hyamṛto bhāvaḥ svabhāvataḥ sannātmā kathaṃ martyatāmeṣyati? na kathañcana martyatvaṃ svabhāvavaiparītyameṣyatītyarthaḥ //20//
children.translated_text: And how would that unborn, immortal entity—the Self that exists by its very nature—come to be mortal? It would never come to mortality, never come to the reversal of its nature—this is the meaning. ||20||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.21
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.21

children.text: yasmāt-
children.translated_text: Because—

children.text: na bhavaty amṛtaṃ martyaṃ na martyam amṛtaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The immortal does not become mortal, nor the mortal immortal;

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathañcid bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_3.21 //
children.translated_text: A change in one's own nature will never occur in any way. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.21 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.21
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.21:

children.text: na bhavatyamṛtaṃ lokenāpi martyamamṛtaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The immortal does not become mortal even in the conventional world, nor the mortal [become] immortal.

children.text: tataḥ prakṛteḥ svabhāvasyānyathābhāvaḥ svataḥ pracyutirna kathañcidbhaviṣyati, agnerivauṣṇyasya //21//
children.translated_text: Therefore, a change from one's nature—a deviation from one's own essential character—will never occur in any way, just as heat [cannot deviate from the nature] of fire. ||21||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.22
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.22

children.text: svabhāvenāmṛto yasya bhāvo gacchati martyatām /
children.translated_text: For one whose entity, immortal by nature, comes to be mortal—

children.text: kṛtakenāmṛtas tasya kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalaḥ // MandUpK_3.22 //
children.translated_text: How will that which is 'made' immortal remain unchanging? || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.22 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.22
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.22:

children.text: yasya punarvādinaḥ svabhāvenāmṛto bhāvo martyatāṃ gacchati paramārthato jāyate tasya prāgutpatteḥ sa bhāvaḥ svabhāvato 'mṛta iti pratijñā mṛṣaiva /
children.translated_text: For the arguer whose entity, immortal by nature, comes to be mortal—that is, is born in ultimate reality—the claim that the entity was immortal by nature before origination is simply false.

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi kṛtakenāmṛtastasya bhāvaḥ? kṛtakenāmṛtaḥ sa kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalo 'mṛtasvabhāvastathā na kathañcitsthāsyatyātmajātivādinaḥ sarvadājaṃ nāma nāstyeva; sarvametanmartyam /
children.translated_text: How then would that entity be immortal through some fabrication? If it is 'made' immortal [artificially], how would it remain unchanging, of immortal nature? It would never remain so. For the one who asserts the birth of the Self, the unborn simply never exists at all; everything is mortal.

children.text: ato 'nirmokṣaprasaṅga ityabhiprāyaḥ //22//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the consequence would be that liberation is impossible—this is the intended meaning. ||22||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.23
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.23

children.text:
nanvajātivādinaḥ sṛṣṭipratipādikā śrutirna saṃgacchate prāmāṇyam?
bāḍhaṃ vidyate sṛṣṭipratipādikā śrutiḥ; sā tvanyaparā /
upāyaḥ sa avatārāyetyavocāma /
idānīmukte 'pi parihāre punaścodyaparihārau vivakṣitārthaṃ prati sṛṣṭiśrutyakṣarāṇāmānulomyavirodhāśaṅkāmātraparihārārthau-
children.translated_text: But does not the <s>śruti</s> that teaches creation conflict with the view of non-origination in terms of authoritativeness? Indeed, <s>śruti</s> teaching creation does exist; but it has a different purport. We have said that it is a means, an approach for introducing [the truth]. Now, even though the refutation has been stated, an objection and its resolution are presented once more, for the purpose of removing even the suspicion of conflict with the letter of the creation-<s>śruti</s> as regards the intended meaning—

children.text: bhūtato 'bhūtato vāpi sṛjyamāne samā śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether [the world is] created from something real or from something unreal, the <s>śruti</s> is the same;

children.text: niścitaṃ yuktiyuktaṃ ca yat tad bhavati netarat // MandUpK_3.23 //
children.translated_text: What is ascertained and consonant with reason—that alone holds, not the other. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.23 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.23
bhūtataḥ paramārthataḥ sṛjyamāne vastunyabhūtato māyayā vā māyāvineva sṛjyamāne vastuni samā tulyā sṛṣṭiśrutiḥ /
nanu gauṇamukhyayormukhye śabdārthapratapattiryuktā /
na, anyathā sṛṣṭeraprasiddhatvānniṣprayojanatvāccetyavocāma /
avidyāsṛṣṭaviṣayaiva sarvā gauṇī mukhyā ca sṛṣṭirna paramārthataḥ"sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ"(mu.u.2 / 1 / 2) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.23: Whether the thing being created is [created] from something real—that is, ultimately—or from something unreal, through <s>māyā</s>, like [the creation of] a magician—the creation-<s>śruti</s> is the same, equal. But should not the primary meaning of the word be accepted when both primary and secondary [meanings] are possible? No, because, as we have said, creation is otherwise unknown [in its ultimate sense] and would be purposeless. All creation—whether figurative or primary—has its domain only in what is created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), not in ultimate reality, according to the <s>śruti</s>: 'Being without exterior and interior, it is unborn' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2).

children.text: tasmācchrutyā niścitaṃ yadekamevādvitīyamajamamṛtamiti yuktiyuktaṃ ca yuktyā ca sampannaṃ tadevetyavocāma pūrvairgranthaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what is ascertained by <s>śruti</s>—that it is one alone without a second, unborn, immortal—and what is also consonant with reason—we have said this in the preceding sections.

children.text: tadeva śrutyartho bhavati netaratkadācidapi //23//
children.translated_text: That alone is the meaning of <s>śruti</s>, never the other at any time. ||23||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.24
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.24

children.text: kathaṃ śrutuniścayaḥ? ityāha-
children.translated_text: How is the ascertainment from <s>śruti</s> [established]? He says—

children.text: neha nāneti cāmnāyād indro māyābhir ity api /
children.translated_text: 'There is no diversity here'—from this scriptural text; and '<s>Indra</s> [appeared in many forms] through <s>māyā</s>';

children.text: ajāyamāno bahudhā māyayā jāyate tu saḥ // MandUpK_3.24 //
children.translated_text: 'Remaining unborn, he is born in many ways through <s>māyā</s>.' || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.24 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.24
yadi hi bhūtata eva sṛṣṭiḥ syāttataḥ satyameva nānā vastviti tadabhāvapradarśanārthamāmnāyo na syāt /
asti ca"neha nānāsti kiñcana"(ka.u.2 / 1 / 11) ityādirāmnāyo dvaitabhāvapratiṣedhārthaḥ /
tasmādātmaikatvapratipatyarthā kalpitā sṛṣṭirabhūtaiva prāṇasaṃvādavat /
"indro māyābhiḥ" (bṛ.u.3 / 5 / 19) ityabhūtārthapratipādakena māyāśabdena vyapadeśāt /
nanu prajñāvacano māyāśabdaḥ /
satyam; indriyaprajñāyā avadyāmayatvena māyātvabhyupagamādadoṣaḥ /
māyābhirindriyaprajñābhir avidyārūpābhirityarthaḥ"ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate"iti śruteḥ, tasmānmāyayaiva jāyate tu sa /
tu śabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ- māyayaiveti /
na hyajāyamānatvaṃ bahudhā janmacaikatra sambhavati, agnāviva śaityamoṣṇyaṃ ca /
phalavatvāccātmaikatvadarśanameva śrutiniścitor'thaḥ"tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ"(ī.u.7) ityādimantravarṇāt;"mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti"(ka.u.2 / 1 / 10) iti ninditatvācca sṛṣṭyādibhedadṛṣṭeḥ //24//
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.24: If creation were ultimately real, then the diversity of things would be truly real, and there would be no scriptural text for the purpose of demonstrating its non-existence. But there is indeed the scripture 'There is no diversity here whatsoever' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.11) and the like, for the purpose of negating the existence of duality. Therefore, creation is devised for the purpose of realizing the oneness of the Self—it is itself unreal, like the parable of the <s>prāṇa</s>-competition. [This is so] because of the designation by the word '<s>māyā</s>' in '<s>Indra</s> [appeared] through <s>māyās</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.19), which conveys an unreal meaning. But is not the word '<s>māyā</s>' a term for knowledge (<s>prajñā</s>)? True; but since the sense-knowledge (<s>indriyaprajñā</s>) is accepted as being <s>māyā</s> by virtue of being faulty and deceptive, there is no fault. The meaning is: through <s>māyās</s>—through sense-knowledges that are of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). From the <s>śruti</s> 'remaining unborn, he is born in many ways,' therefore he is born through <s>māyā</s> alone. The word 'tu' (but) serves the purpose of emphasis—meaning 'through <s>māyā</s> alone.' For unborn-ness and manifold birth cannot coexist in one and the same [entity], just as cold and heat cannot [coexist] in fire. And because it is fruitful, the vision of the oneness of the Self is alone the ascertained meaning of <s>śruti</s>, from scriptural passages such as 'What delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who sees oneness?' (<s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> 7) and the like; and because the vision of diversity through creation and the like is condemned [in passages such as] 'He goes from death to death' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.10). ||24||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.25
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.25

children.text: saṃbhūter apavādāc ca saṃbhavaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: From the negation of [the meditation on] creation (<s>saṃbhūti</s>), creation is denied;

children.text: ko nv enaṃ janayed iti kāraṇaṃ pratiṣidhyate // MandUpK_3.25 //
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed could bring this into being?'—thereby the cause is denied. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.25 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.25
"andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśati ye sambhūtimupāsate"(ī.u.12) iti saṃbhūterupāsyatvāpavādātsaṃbhavaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
na hi paramārthataḥ saṃbhūtāyāṃ saṃbhūtau tadapavāda upapadyate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.25: From the negation of <s>saṃbhūti</s> (creation) as an object of meditation [in the text] 'Into blind darkness enter those who worship <s>saṃbhūti</s> (creation)' (<s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> 12), creation is denied. For if creation were ultimately real, its negation would not be proper.

children.text:
nanu vināśena saṃbhūteḥ samuccayavidhyarthaḥ saṃbhūtyapavādaḥ /
yathā"andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye 'vidyāmupāsate"(ī.u.9) iti /
children.translated_text: But is not the negation of <s>saṃbhūti</s> for the purpose of enjoining the combination of <s>saṃbhūti</s> with destruction (<s>vināśa</s>)—as in 'Into blind darkness enter those who worship <s>avidyā</s>' (<s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> 9)?

children.text: satyameva devatādarśanasya saṃbhūtiviṣayasya vināśaśabdavācyasya karmaṇaḥ samuccayavidhānārthaḥ saṃbhūtyapavādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truly, the negation of <s>saṃbhūti</s> is for the purpose of enjoining the combination of deity-meditation—the domain of <s>saṃbhūti</s>—with <s>karma</s> (ritual action), which is denoted by the word '<s>vināśa</s>' (destruction).

children.text:
tathāpi vināśākhyasya karmaṇaḥ svābhāvikājñānapravṛttirūpasya mṛtyoratitaraṇārthatvam /
evaṃ hyeṣaṇādvayarūpānmṛtyoraśuddherviyuktaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃskṛtaḥ syādato mṛtyoratitaraṇārthādevatādarśanakarmasamuccayalakṣaṇā hyavidyā /
children.translated_text: Even so, the <s>karma</s> called 'destruction'—which is of the nature of natural ignorance in action—serves the purpose of transcending death. For thus a person, freed from the impure death that has the form of the twofold desire (<s>eṣaṇā</s>), becomes purified. Therefore <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), characterized by the combination of deity-meditation and <s>karma</s>, serves to transcend death.

children.text:
evameva eṣaṇālakṣaṇāvidyāyā mṛtyoratitīrṇasya viraktasyopaniṣacchāstrārthālocanaparasya nāntarīyakī paramātmaikatvavidyotpattiriti pūrvabhāvinīmavidyāmapekṣya paścādbhāvinī brahmavidyāmṛtatvasādhanaikena puruṣeṇa sambadhyamānāvidyayā samuccīyata ityucyate /
ato 'nyārthatvādamṛtatvasādhanaṃ brahmavidyāmapokṣya nindārthaṃ eva bhavati saṃbhūtyapavādaḥ /
yadyapyaśuddhiviyogahetur atanniṣṭhatvāt /
ata eva saṃbhūter apavādātsaṃbhūterāpekṣikameva sattvamiti paramārthasadātmaikatvamapekṣya amṛtākhyaḥ saṃbhavaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: Just so, for one who has transcended death in the form of <s>avidyā</s> characterized by desire, who is dispassionate, and who is devoted to contemplating the meaning of the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> teaching—the arising of the knowledge of the oneness of the supreme Self is inevitable. Thus <s>avidyā</s>, which precedes [<s>vidyā</s>], is said to be 'combined' with <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>), which follows and is the means to immortality, in one and the same person. Therefore, setting aside <s>brahmavidyā</s>, which is the means to immortality and has a different purpose, the negation of <s>saṃbhūti</s> is for the purpose of censure alone—even though it is the cause of the removal of impurity—because its goal does not rest in that [creation-meditation]. For this very reason, from the negation of <s>saṃbhūti</s>, the existence of <s>saṃbhūti</s> is only relative, and with reference to the ultimate reality of the oneness of the Self, the creation called 'immortal' is denied.

children.text:
evaṃ māyānirmitasyaiva jīvasyāvidyayā pratyupasthāpitasyāvidyānāśe svabhāvarūpatvātparamārthataḥ ko nvenaṃ janayet /
na hi rajjvāmavidyāropitaṃ sarpaṃ punarvivekato naṣṭaṃ janayetkaścit /
tathā na kaścidenaṃ janayediti ko nvityākṣepārthatvātkāraṇaṃ pritaṣidhyate /
avidyodbhūtasya naṣṭasya janayitṛkāraṇaṃ na kiñcidastītyabhiprāyaḥ"nāyaṃ kutaścinna babhūva kaścit"(ka.u.1 / 2 / 18) iti śruteḥ //25//
children.translated_text: Thus, for the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) that was itself produced by <s>māyā</s> and presented by <s>avidyā</s>, upon the destruction of <s>avidyā</s>—since it is of the nature of its own true form in ultimate reality—who indeed could bring it into being? For no one can bring back into being a snake that was superimposed on a rope through ignorance and that has been destroyed by discrimination. Similarly, no one can bring this [Self] into being—thus, because 'who indeed' serves the purpose of denial, the cause is negated. The purport is: for that which arose from <s>avidyā</s> and has been destroyed, there is no producing cause whatsoever. [This is supported by] the <s>śruti</s>: 'This one came from nowhere, and no one came from this' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.18). ||25||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.26
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.26

children.text: sa eṣa neti netīti vyākhyātaṃ nihnute yataḥ /
children.translated_text: This very one [is described as] 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>)—since [the <s>śruti</s>] negates whatever has been explained,

children.text: sarvam agrāhyabhāvena hetunājaṃ prakāśate // MandUpK_3.26 //
children.translated_text: Everything [is seen to be] unborn, shining forth by the reason of being ungraspable. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.26 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.26
sarvaviśeṣapratiṣedhena"athāta ādeśo neti neti"(bṛ.u.2 / 3 / 6) iti pratipāditasyātmano durbodhyatvaṃ manyamānā śrutiḥ punaḥ punarupāyāntaratvena tasyaiva pratipipādayiṣayā yadvyākhyātaṃ tatsarvaṃ nihnate, grāhyaṃ janimadbuddhiviṣayamapalapati /
arthāt"sa eṣa neti neti"(bṛ.u.3 / 1 / 26) ityātmano 'dṛśyatāṃ darśayantī śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.26: Considering that the Self, which has been taught through the negation of all qualifications as 'Now therefore the teaching: not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.3.6), is difficult to comprehend, the <s>śruti</s>, wishing to teach the same [truth] again and again through alternative means, negates all that has been explained—it denies [anything as being] graspable, an object of cognition, or subject to birth. The purport is that the <s>śruti</s>, 'This is that Self, [described as] not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.26), showing the imperceptibility of the Self,

children.text: upāyasyopeyaniṣṭhatāmajānata upāyatvena vyākhyātasyopeyavadgrāhyatā mā bhūdityagrāhyabhāvena hetunā kāraṇena nihnuta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: lest what was explained as a means be grasped as if it were the goal itself—not knowing that the means culminates in the goal—by the reason of being ungraspable, [the <s>śruti</s>] negates [it]. The meaning is [that it negates it].

children.text: tataścaivamupāyasyopeyaniṣṭhatāmeva jānata upeyasya ca nityaikarūpatvamiti tasyasabāhyābhyantaramajamātmatattvaṃ prakāśate svayameva //26//
children.translated_text: And thus, for one who knows precisely that the means culminates in the goal, and that the goal is eternally of one nature—the Self-reality, which is unborn, without exterior and interior, shines forth of its own accord. ||26||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.27
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.27

children.text:
evaṃ hi śrutivākyaśataiḥ sabāhyābhyantaramajamātmatattvamadvayaṃ na tato 'nyadastīti niścitametat /
yuktyā cā7dhunaitadeva punarnirdhāryata ityāha-
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, through hundreds of scriptural statements, it has been ascertained that the Self-reality is unborn, non-dual, without exterior and interior—nothing other than that exists. And now this very [truth] is again established through reasoning. He says—

children.text: sato hi māyayā janma yujyate na tu tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the birth of what exists [occurs] through <s>māyā</s> alone, not in reality;

children.text: tattvato jāyate yasya jātaṃ tasya hi jāyate // MandUpK_3.27 //
children.translated_text: That from which one who is born is born—for that which is born, it is indeed [already] born. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.27 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.27
tatraitatsyātsadāgrāhyameva cedasadevātmatattvamiti /
tanna, kāryagrahaṇāt /
yathā sato māyāvino māyayā janma kāryam /
evaṃ jagato janma kāryaṃ gṛhyamāṇaṃ māyāvinamiva paramārthasantam ātmānaṃ jagajjanmamāyāspadam avagamayati /
yasmātsato hi vidyamānātkāraṇānmāyānirmitasya hastyādikāryasyeva jagajjanma yujyate nāsataḥ kāraṇāt /
na tu tattvata evātmano janma yujyate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.27: Here one might think: if the Self-reality is always ungraspable, then the Self-reality simply does not exist. That is not so, because its effects are perceived. Just as the birth—the effect—of a really existing magician [is produced] through <s>māyā</s>, so too the perceived birth of the world, being an effect, indicates the Self as ultimately real—like the magician—as the locus of the <s>māyā</s> of world-creation. Since the birth of the world—like the effect of an elephant produced by <s>māyā</s> from an existing cause—is proper only from an existing cause, not from a non-existing one. But the birth of the Self itself is not proper in reality.

children.text:
atha vā sato vidyamānasya vastuno rajjvādeḥ sarpādivan māyayā janma yujyate na tu tattvato yathā tathāgrāhyasyāpi sata evātmano rajjusarpavajjagadrūpeṇa māyayā janma yujyate /
na tu tattvata evājasyātmano janma /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: just as for an existing thing like a rope, there is birth [of appearances] like a snake through <s>māyā</s>, not in reality—so too, for the Self which, though ungraspable, truly exists, there is birth in the form of the world through <s>māyā</s>, like the rope-snake. But the birth of the unborn Self is not [real] in reality.

children.text: yasya punaḥ paramārthasadajamātmatattvaṃ jagadrūpeṇa jāyate vādino nahi tasyājaṃ jāyata iti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ virodhāt /
children.translated_text: But for the arguer who maintains that the ultimately real, unborn Self-reality is born in the form of the world—it is impossible to say that the unborn is born, due to the contradiction.

children.text: tatastasyārthājjātaṃ jāyata ityāpannaṃ tataścānavasthā jātājjāyamānatvena /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for him it necessarily follows that what is born is born from [something already] born—and thus there is an infinite regress, since what is born would always be born from what is [already] born.

children.text: tasmādajamekamevātmatattvamiti siddham //27//
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the Self-reality is one, unborn alone. ||27||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.28
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.28

children.text: asato māyayā janma tattvato naiva yujyate /
children.translated_text: The birth of a non-existent [entity] through <s>māyā</s> or in reality is never proper;

children.text: vandhyāputro na tattvena māyayā vāpi jāyate // MandUpK_3.28 //
children.translated_text: A barren woman's son is not born either in reality or through <s>māyā</s>. || <s>Kārikā</s> 3.28 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.28
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 3.28:

children.text: asadvādināmasato bhāvasya māyayā tattvato vā na kathañcana janma yujyate, adṛṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text: For the proponents of non-existence (<s>asadvādins</s>), the birth of a non-existent entity through <s>māyā</s> or in reality is not proper in any way whatsoever, since it is never observed.

children.text: na hi vandhyāputro māyayā tattvato vā jāyate tasmādatrāsadvādo dūrata evānupapanne7tyarthaḥ //28//
children.translated_text: For indeed, a barren woman's son is not born either through <s>māyā</s> or in reality. Therefore, the doctrine of non-existence (<s>asadvāda</s>) is far removed from [logical] validity—this is the meaning. ||28||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.29
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 3.29

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ sato māyayaiva janmetyucyate-
children.translated_text: How then is it said that birth [occurs] from what exists through <s>māyā</s> alone?—

children.text: yathā svapne dvayābhāsaṃ spandate māyayā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in dream, the mind vibrates with the appearance of duality through <s>māyā</s> (illusion),

children.text: tathā jāgraddvayābhāsaṃ spandate māyayā manaḥ // MandUpK_3.29 //
children.translated_text: So too in waking, the mind vibrates with the appearance of duality through <s>māyā</s>. || MandUpK 3.29 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.29
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_3.29

children.text: yathā rajjvāṃ vikalpitaḥ sarpo rajjurūpeṇāvekṣyamāṇaḥ sannevaṃ manaḥ paramārthavijñaptyātmarūpeṇāvekṣyamāṇaṃ sad grāhyagrāhakarūpeṇa dvayābhāsaṃ spandate svapne māyayā, rajjvāmiva sarpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the snake imagined in the rope, when examined in the form of the rope, [is found to be nothing but the rope] — so too the mind, when examined in the form of the ultimate reality, which is pure consciousness (<s>vijñapti</s>), vibrates with the appearance of duality in the form of the grasped and the grasper in dream, through <s>māyā</s> — like the snake in the rope.

children.text: tathā tadvadeva jāgrajjāgarite spandate māyayā manaḥ spandata ivetyarthaḥ //29//
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the same way, in waking, the mind vibrates through <s>māyā</s> — 'vibrates as it were' is the meaning. || 29 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.30
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.30

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ manaḥ svapne na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is non-dual, yet appears as duality in dream — of this there is no doubt;

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ tathā jāgran na saṃśayaḥ // MandUpK_3.30 //
children.translated_text: The mind is non-dual, yet appears as duality in waking likewise — of this there is no doubt. || MandUpK 3.30 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.30
rajjurūpeṇa sarpa iva paramārthata ātmarūpeṇādvayaṃ saddvayābhāsaṃ manaḥ svapne na saṃśayaḥ /
na hi svapne hastyādi grāhyaṃ tadgrāhakaṃ vā cakṣurādidvayaṃ vijñānavyatirekeṇāsti /
jāgradapi tathaivetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_3.30
Like the snake in the form of the rope, in ultimate reality, in the form of the <s>Ātman</s>, [the mind is] non-dual, yet it appears as duality in dream — of this there is no doubt.
For in dream, neither the elephant and the like as objects grasped, nor the eye and other [senses] as graspers — neither of these dualities exist apart from consciousness.
In waking too, it is just so — this is the meaning.

children.text: paramārthasadvijñānamātrāviśeṣāt //30//
children.translated_text: Because there is no difference [between the two states] in terms of ultimate reality being consciousness alone. || 30 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.31
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.31

children.text:
rajjusarpavadvikalpanārūpaṃ dvaitarūpeṇa mana evetyuktam /
tatra kiṃ pramāṇamityanvayavyatirekalakṣaṇamanumānamāha /
katham-
children.translated_text: It has been stated that duality is of the nature of imagination, like the rope-snake — it is the mind itself in the form of duality. What is the proof for this? He states the inference based on positive and negative concomitance. How?

children.text: manodṛśyam idaṃ dvaitaṃ yat kiñcit sacarācaram /
children.translated_text: This duality, whatever it is — moving and unmoving — is perceived by the mind;

children.text: manaso hy amanībhāve dvaitaṃ naivopalabhyate // MandUpK_3.31 //
children.translated_text: For when the mind becomes 'no-mind,' duality is never apprehended. || MandUpK 3.31 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.31
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_3.31

children.text: tena hi manasā vikalpyamānena dṛśyaṃ manodṛśyamidaṃ dvaitaṃ sarvaṃ mana iti pratijñā /
children.translated_text: By that mind which imagines, this entire duality is perceived — 'duality is perceived by the mind' — this is the proposition that [all duality] is mind.

children.text: tadbhāve bhāvāttadabhāve 'bhāvāt /
children.translated_text: [This is established] because of [duality's] presence when [the mind] is present, and its absence when [the mind] is absent.

children.text: manaso hyamanībhāve nirodhe vivekadarśanābhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ rajjvāmiva sarpe layaṃ gate vā suṣupte dvaitaṃ naivopalabhyata ityabhāvātsiddhaṃ dvaitasyāsatvamityarthaḥ //31//
children.translated_text: When the mind becomes 'no-mind' — that is, when it is restrained through the practice of discrimination and dispassion, or when it dissolves as in the [case of a] snake in a rope, or in deep sleep — duality is never apprehended. From this absence, the non-existence of duality is established — this is the meaning. || 31 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.32
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.32

children.text: kathaṃ punaramanībhāvaḥ? ity ucyate-
children.translated_text: But how does the mind become 'no-mind'? It is stated:

children.text: ātmasatyānubodhena na saṃkalpayate yadā /
children.translated_text: When, through the realization that the <s>Ātman</s> alone is real (<s>ātmasatyānubodha</s>), one no longer imagines,

children.text: amanastāṃ tadā yāti grāhyābhāve tadagraham // MandUpK_3.32 //
children.translated_text: Then [the mind] reaches the state of 'no-mind'; in the absence of the graspable, it becomes non-grasping. || MandUpK 3.32 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.32
ātmaiva satyamātmasatyaṃ mṛttikāvat"vācāraṃbhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyam"(chā.u.6 / 1 / 4) iti śrutes tasya śāstrācāryopadeśamanvavabodha ātmasatyānubodhaḥ /
tena saṃkalpyābhāvatayā na saṃkalpyate, dāhyābhāve jvalanamivāgneḥ, yadā yasminkāle tadā tasminkāle 'manastāmamanobhāvaṃ yāti; grāhyābhāve tanmano 'grahaṃ grahaṇavikalpanāvarjitamityarthaḥ //32//
children.translated_text: Through that [realization], since there is nothing [left] to be imagined, one does not imagine — like fire [that cannot burn] in the absence of fuel. At that time, the mind reaches the state of 'no-mind' — the state of being no-mind. In the absence of the graspable, that mind becomes non-grasping — that is, free from the imagination of grasping. || 32 ||

MandUpKC_3.32
The <s>Ātman</s> alone is real — this is <s>ātmasatya</s>, like clay [in the example]: 'The modification is merely a name, a verbal handle; clay alone is real' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.1.4) — so says the <s>śruti</s>. The realization of that, through the instruction of scripture and teacher, is <s>ātmasatyānubodha</s> (the awakening to the reality of the <s>Ātman</s>).

children.text: START MandUpK 3.33
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.33

children.text: yadyasadidaṃ dvaitaṃ kena svamajamātmatattvaṃ vibudhyate? ity ucyate-
children.translated_text: If this duality is unreal, by what is the unborn reality of the <s>Ātman</s> realized? It is stated:

children.text: akalpamajaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyābhinnaṃ pracakṣate /
children.translated_text: Knowledge is without conceptual construction (<s>akalpa</s>), unborn (<s>aja</s>), non-different from the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) — so they declare;

children.text: brahma jñeyam ajaṃ nityam ajenājaṃ vibudhyate // MandUpK_3.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, the knowable, is unborn and eternal — the unborn is realized by the unborn. || MandUpK 3.33 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.33
akalpakaṃ sarvakalpanāvarjitamata evājaṃ jñānaṃ jñaptimātraṃ jñeyena paramārthasatā brahmaṇābhinnaṃ pracakṣate kathayanti brahmavidaḥ /
na hi vijñāturvijñāterviparilopo vidyate 'gnyuṣṇavat"vijñānamānandaṃ brahma"(bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 28) "satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma"(tai.u.2 / 1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_3.33
[Knowledge is] without conceptual construction (<s>akalpa</s>) — devoid of all imagination — and therefore unborn; knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), which is mere awareness (<s>jñaptimātra</s>), is non-different from the knowable, which is <s>Brahman</s> that is ultimately real — so declare, so say, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>.
For there is no destruction of the knowledge of the knower, just as there is no [destruction] of the heat of fire. [This is known] from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'Consciousness, bliss, <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.28), 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1), and so on.

children.text: tasyaiva viśeṣaṇaṃ brahma jñeyaṃ yasya svasya tadidaṃ brahmajñeyamauṣṇyasyevāgnivadabhinnam /
children.translated_text: The qualification of that very [knowledge]: '<s>Brahman</s> is the knowable' — this <s>Brahman</s>-knowable is non-different [from knowledge], like heat from fire.

children.text: tenātmasvarūpeṇājena jñānenājaṃ jñeyamātmatattvaṃ svayameva vibudhyate 'vagacchati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by that unborn knowledge, which is the very nature of the <s>Ātman</s>, the unborn knowable — the reality of the <s>Ātman</s> — is realized, that is, understood by itself.

children.text: nityaprakāśasvarūpa iva savitā nityavijñānaikarasaghanatvānna jñānāntaramapekṣata ityarthaḥ //33//
children.translated_text: Like the sun, whose nature is eternal luminosity, being of the nature of eternal consciousness, a solid mass of a single flavor — it does not depend on any other knowledge. This is the meaning. || 33 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.34
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.34

children.text:
ātmasatyānubodhena saṅkalpamakurvadbāhyaviṣayābhāve nirindhanāgnivatpraśāntaṃ nigṛhītaṃ niruddhaṃ mano bhavatītyuktam /
evaṃ ca manaso hyamanībhāve dvaitābhāvaścoktaḥ /
tasyaivam-
children.translated_text: It has been stated that through the realization of the reality of the <s>Ātman</s>, when one ceases to imagine, the mind — in the absence of external objects, like fire without fuel — becomes pacified, restrained, controlled. And thus it has been said that when the mind becomes 'no-mind,' duality ceases. Of that very [restrained mind]:

children.text: nigṛhītasya manaso nirvikalpasya dhīmataḥ /
children.translated_text: The activity of the restrained mind, free from all conceptual construction, belonging to the wise one —

children.text: pracāraḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ suṣupte 'nyo na tatsamaḥ // MandUpK_3.34 //
children.translated_text: That is to be specially known; [the activity] in deep sleep is different and not the same as that. || MandUpK 3.34 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.34
nigṛhītasya niruddhasya manaso nirvikalpasya sarvakalpanāvarjitasya dhīmato vivekavataḥ pracāro yaḥ sa tu pracāro viśeṣeṇa jñeyo yogibhiḥ /
nanu sarvapratyayābhāve yādṛśaḥ suṣuptasthasya manasaḥ pracārastādṛśa eva niruddhasyāpi pratyayābhāvāviśeṣātkiṃ tatra vijñeyamiti /
children.translated_text: But surely, in the absence of all mental states (<s>pratyaya</s>), the activity of the mind in deep sleep is of the same kind as that of the restrained mind, since there is no difference in the absence of mental states — so what is there to be specially known?

children.text: atrocyate- naivam; yasmātsuṣupte 'nyaḥ pracāro 'vidyāmohatamograstasyāntarlīnānekānarthapravṛttibījavāsanāvato manasa ātmasatyānubodhahutāśavipluṣṭāvidyānarthapravṛttibījasya niruddhasyānya eva praśāntasarvakleśarajasaḥ svatantraḥ pracāraḥ /
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: not so; because the activity in deep sleep is different. The mind in deep sleep is swallowed by the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and delusion, with the seeds of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of manifold harmful tendencies lying dormant within — while the activity of the restrained mind, whose seeds of harmful tendencies rooted in <s>avidyā</s> have been burned by the fire of the realization of the reality of the <s>Ātman</s>, free from all the dust of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), is entirely different and autonomous.

children.text: ato na tatsamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is not the same as that.

children.text: tasmādyuktaḥ sa vijñātumityabhiprāyaḥ //34//
children.translated_text: Hence it is proper that it should be [specially] known — this is the intended meaning. || 34 ||

MandUpKC_3.34
The activity of the restrained — that is, controlled — mind, free from all conceptual construction — devoid of all imagination — belonging to the wise one, the one endowed with discrimination — that activity is to be specially known by <s>yogins</s>.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.35
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.35

children.text: pracārabhede hetumāha-
children.translated_text: He states the reason for the difference in activity:

children.text: līyate hi suṣupte tan nigṛhītaṃ na līyate /
children.translated_text: In deep sleep, indeed, [the mind] dissolves; [but] the restrained [mind] does not dissolve.

children.text: tad eva nirbhayaṃ brahma jñānalokaṃ samantataḥ // MandUpK_3.35 //
children.translated_text: That itself is the fearless <s>Brahman</s>, the light of knowledge, [pervading] everywhere. || MandUpK 3.35 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.35
līyate suṣupto hi yasmātsarvābhiravidyādipratyayabījavāsanābhiḥ saha tamorūpamaviśeṣarūpaṃ bījabhāvamāpadyate tadvivekavijñānapūrvakaṃ niruddhaṃ nigṛhītaṃ sanna līyate tamobījabhāvaṃ nāpadyate /
tasmādyuktaḥ pracārabhedaḥ suṣuptasya samāhitasya manasaḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_3.35
In deep sleep, [the mind] dissolves — because, together with all the seed-impressions of <s>avidyā</s> and other cognitions, it assumes a state of seeds, an undifferentiated form of darkness. But when restrained through prior discriminative knowledge, the controlled mind does not dissolve — it does not assume the state of seeds of darkness.
Therefore, the difference in activity between the mind in deep sleep and the concentrated mind is justified.

children.text:
yathā grāhyagrāhakāvidyākṛtamaladvayavarjitaṃ tadā paramadvayaṃ brahmaiva tatsaṃvṛttamityatastadeva nirbhayaṃ dvaitagrahaṇasya bhayanimittasyābhāvat /
śāntamabhayaṃ brahma, yadvidvānna bibheti kutaścana /
children.translated_text:
Since, when freed from the twofold impurity of the grasped and the grasper created by <s>avidyā</s>, [the mind] has become the supreme non-dual <s>Brahman</s> itself — therefore it is fearless, because of the absence of the apprehension of duality, which is the cause of fear.
'<s>Brahman</s> is peaceful and fearless' — the wise one does not fear anything.

children.text: tadeva viśeṣyate jñāptirjñānamātmasvabhāvacaitanyaṃ tadeva jñānamālokaḥ prākāśo yasya tadbrahma jñānālokaṃ vijñānaikarasaghanamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That very [<s>Brahman</s>] is further qualified: <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) or awareness (<s>jñapti</s>), the inherent consciousness of the <s>Ātman</s> — that itself is the light (<s>āloka</s>), the illumination, of which — that <s>Brahman</s> is the light of knowledge, a solid mass of a single flavor of consciousness. This is the meaning.

children.text: samantataḥ samantāsarvato vyomavannairantaryeṇa vyāpakamityarthaḥ //35//
children.translated_text: 'Everywhere' (<s>samantataḥ</s>) means on all sides — pervading everywhere without interruption, like space. This is the meaning. || 35 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.36
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.36

children.text: ajam anindram asvapnam anāmakam arūpakam /
children.translated_text: Unborn (<s>aja</s>), free from sleep (<s>anidra</s>), free from dream (<s>asvapna</s>), without name (<s>anāmaka</s>), without form (<s>arūpaka</s>),

children.text: sakṛdvibhātaṃ sarvajñaṃ nopacāraḥ kathañcana // MandUpK_3.36 //
children.translated_text: Shining once and for all (<s>sakṛdvibhāta</s>), omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>) — no figurative attribution (<s>upacāra</s>) applies to it in any way. || MandUpK 3.36 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.36
janmanimittābhāvātsabāhyābhyantaramajam /
avidyānimittaṃ hi janma rajjusarpavadityavocāma /
sā cāvidyātmasatyānubodhena niruddhā yato 'jamata evānidram /
avidyālakṣaṇānādirmāyā nidrā /
svāpātprabuddhau'dvaiyasvarūpeṇātmanāto 'svapnam /
aprabodhakṛte hyasyanāmarūpe /
prabodhācca te rajjusarpavadvinaṣṭha iti na nāmnābhidhīyate brahma rūpyate vā na kenacitprakāreṇetyanāmakarūpakaṃ ca tat /
"yato vāco nivartante"(tai.u.2 / 4 / 1) ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_3.36
Because of the absence of the cause of birth, [<s>Brahman</s>] is unborn (<s>aja</s>) — both externally and internally.
For we have said that birth is caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), like the rope-snake.
And that <s>avidyā</s> has been restrained by the realization of the reality of the <s>Ātman</s> — hence unborn; and therefore also free from sleep (<s>anidra</s>).
The beginningless <s>māyā</s>, characterized by <s>avidyā</s>, is sleep (<s>nidrā</s>).
Having awakened from that sleep to the non-dual nature of the <s>Ātman</s> — hence free from dream (<s>asvapna</s>).
For name and form belong to [the state of] non-awakening;
and through awakening, they are destroyed like the rope-snake — hence <s>Brahman</s> is not designated by any name, nor is it given form in any manner — thus it is without name and without form.
As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'From which words turn back' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.1), and so on.

children.text:
kiṃ ca sakṛdvibhātaṃ sadaiva vibhātaṃ sadā bhārūpamagrahaṇānyathāgrahaṇāvirbhāvatirobhāvavarjitatvāt /
grahaṇāgrahaṇe hi rātryahanī tamaścāvidyālakṣaṇaṃ sadāprabhātatve kāraṇam /
tadabhāvānnityacaitanyabhārūpatvācca yuktaṃ sakṛdvibhātamiti /
ata eva sarvaṃ ca tajjñasvarūpaṃ ceti sarvajñam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is all (<s>sarva</s>) and its nature is that of the knower (<s>jña</s>) — hence omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>).

children.text: neha brahmaṇyevaṃvidha upacaraṇamupacāraḥ kartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in <s>Brahman</s>, no figurative attribution (<s>upacāra</s>) of the kind described should be made,

children.text: yathānyeṣāmātmasvarūpavyatirekeṇa samādhānādyupacāraḥ /
children.translated_text: unlike in the case of others, where figurative attribution such as <s>samādhāna</s> (concentration) and the like is [applied] as different from the nature of the <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvatvādbrahmaṇaḥ kathañcana na kathañcidapi kartavyasaṃbhavo 'vidyānāśa ityarthaḥ //36//
children.translated_text: Because <s>Brahman</s> is by nature eternally pure, awakened, and free — no action of any kind whatsoever is possible [with regard to it]; the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> [alone is what occurs] — this is the meaning. || 36 ||

Moreover, 'shining once and for all' (<s>sakṛdvibhāta</s>) means eternally shining, always of the nature of light — because it is free from the appearance and disappearance [that would result from] apprehension, misapprehension, manifestation, and concealment.
For apprehension and non-apprehension [respectively constitute] day and night; and darkness, characterized by <s>avidyā</s>, is the cause [that would prevent] eternal luminosity.
Since that [darkness] is absent, and because [<s>Brahman</s>] is of the nature of eternal consciousness and light, it is fitting [to say] 'shining once and for all.'

children.text: START MandUpK 3.37
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.37

children.text: anāmakatvādyuktārthasiddhaye hetumāha-
children.translated_text: To establish the meaning already stated — the namelessness, etc. [of <s>Brahman</s>] — he states the reason:

children.text: sarvābhilāpavigataḥ sarvacintāsamutthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond all speech, arisen from all thought,

children.text: supraśāntaḥ sakṛjjyotiḥ samādhir acalo 'bhayaḥ // MandUpK_3.37 //
children.translated_text: Supremely peaceful, eternally luminous, [it is] <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), immovable, fearless. || MandUpK 3.37 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.37
abhilapyate 'nenetyabhilāpo vākkaraṇaṃ sarvaprakārasyābhidhānasya, tasmādvigataḥ /
vāgatropalakṣaṇārthā sarvabrahmakaraṇavarjita ityetat /
tathā sarvacintāsamutthitaḥ /
cintyate 'nayeti cintā buddhistasyāḥ samutthito 'ntaḥ karaṇavarjita ityarthaḥ"aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhro hyakṣarātparataḥ paraḥ" (mu.u.2 / 1 / 2) ityādiśruteḥ /

yasmātsarvaviṣayavarjito 'taḥ supraśāntaḥ, sakṛjjyotiḥ sadaiva jyotirātmacainyasvarūpeṇa, samādhiḥ samādhinimittaprajñāvagamyatvāt, samādhīyate 'sminniti vā samādhiḥ, acalo 'vikriyaḥ, ata evābhayo vikriyābhāvāt //37//
children.translated_text: Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is devoid of all objects, it is supremely peaceful (<s>supraśānta</s>); 'eternally luminous' (<s>sakṛjjyoti</s>) means always light, in the nature of the consciousness of the <s>Ātman</s>; it is <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) because it is known through the wisdom born of <s>samādhi</s>, or because [everything] is absorbed in it; immovable (<s>acala</s>) means without modification; and therefore fearless (<s>abhaya</s>), because of the absence of modification. || 37 ||

MandUpKC_3.37
That which is spoken of is speech (<s>abhilāpa</s>) — that is, the instrument of the voice, [representing] all forms of verbal designation — and [<s>Brahman</s>] has gone beyond that (<s>vigata</s>).
'Speech' here is illustrative [of all external organs] — the meaning is: [<s>Brahman</s>] is devoid of all <s>Brahman</s>-[level] external organs.
Likewise, 'arisen from all thought' (<s>sarvacintāsamutthita</s>) — <s>cintā</s> (thought) means the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), by which one thinks; [<s>Brahman</s>] has risen above that — meaning, [it is] devoid of the internal organ. As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'Without breath, without mind, pure, higher than the high imperishable' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2), and so on.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.38
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.38

children.text: yasmādbrahmaiva samādhiracalo 'bhaya ityuktaḥ-
children.translated_text: Since it has been said that <s>Brahman</s> itself is <s>samādhi</s>, immovable, and fearless —

children.text: graho na tatra notsargaś cintā yatra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is no grasping there, nor any releasing; where no thought exists,

children.text: ātmasaṃsthaṃ tadā jñānam ajāti samatāṃ gatam // MandUpK_3.38 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge then is established in the <s>Ātman</s>, unborn, having reached equality (<s>samatā</s>). || MandUpK 3.38 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.38
na tatra tasminbrahmaṇi graho grahaṇamupādānam, notsarga utsarjanaṃ hānaṃ vā vidyate /
yatra hi vikriyā tadviṣayatvaṃ vā tatra hānopādāne syātāṃ na taddvayamiha brahmaṇi saṃbhavati /
vikārahetoranyasyābhāvānniravayavatvācca /
ato na tatra hānopādāna ityarthaḥ /
cintā yatra na vidyate /
sarvaprakāraiva cintā na saṃbhavati yatrāmanastvātkutastatra hānopādāna ityarthaḥ /
yadaivātmasatyānubodho jātastadaivātmasaṃsthaṃ viṣayābhāvādagnyuṣṇavadātmanyeva sthitaṃ jñānam, ajāti jātivarjitam, samatāṃ gataṃ paraṃ sāmyamāpannaṃ bhavati /
yadādau pratijñātamato vakṣyāmyakārpaṇyamajāti samatāṃ gatamitīdaṃ tadupapattitaḥ śāstrataścoktamupasaṃhriyate, ajāti samatāṃ gatamiti /
etasmādātmasatyānubodhātkārpaṇyaviṣayamanyat"yo vai9tadakṣaraṃ gārgyaviditvāsmāllaukātpraiti sa kṛpaṇaḥ"(bṛ.u.3 / 8 / 10) iti śruteḥ /
prāpyaitatsarvaḥ kṛtakṛtyo brāhmaṇo bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ //38//
children.translated_text: Having attained this, every <s>brāhmaṇa</s> becomes one who has accomplished all that is to be accomplished — this is the intended meaning. || 38 ||

MandUpKC_3.38
In that <s>Brahman</s>, there is no grasping — no taking up or acquiring; and no releasing — no abandoning or relinquishing.
For where there is modification or objectification, there acquiring and abandoning could exist — but neither of those two is possible in <s>Brahman</s>.
Because of the absence of any other cause of modification, and because [<s>Brahman</s>] is without parts.
Hence there is no acquiring or abandoning — this is the meaning.
'Where no thought exists' — thought of every kind is impossible where there is no mind — so how could there be acquiring or abandoning? This is the meaning.
When indeed the awakening to the reality of the <s>Ātman</s> has arisen, then knowledge is established in the <s>Ātman</s> — abiding in the <s>Ātman</s> alone, like the heat of fire, due to the absence of objects. [It is] unborn (<s>ajāti</s>) — devoid of birth; having reached equality (<s>samatā</s>) — having attained supreme equanimity.
What was proposed at the beginning — 'Therefore I shall speak without meanness (<s>akārpaṇya</s>), having reached the equality of the unborn' — this is now summarized, having been established through reasoning and scripture: 'unborn, having reached equality.'
From this awakening to the reality of the <s>Ātman</s>, anything else is the object of meanness — 'He who, O <s>Gārgī</s>, departs from this world without knowing this Imperishable — he is a wretched one' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.8.10) — so says the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.39
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.39

children.text: yadyapīdamitthaṃ paramārthatattvam-
children.translated_text: Although this is the ultimate truth of the highest reality —

children.text: asparśayogo vai nāma durdarśaḥ sarvayogibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>yoga</s> called '<s>asparśa</s>' (contactless) is indeed difficult to see for all <s>yogins</s>;

children.text: yogino bibhyati hy asmād abhaye bhayadarśinaḥ // MandUpK_3.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yogins</s> are afraid of it indeed, seeing fear in what is fearless. || MandUpK 3.39 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.39
asparśayogo nāmāyaṃ sarvasaṃbandhākhyasparśavarjitatvādasparśayogo nāma vai smaryate prasiddhamupaniṣatsu /
duḥkhena dṛśyata iti durdarśaḥ sarvairyogibhir vedāntavihitavijñānarahitaiḥ sarvayogibhiḥ /
ātmasatyānubodhāyāsalabhya evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_3.39
This <s>asparśa-yoga</s> — so named because it is devoid of all contact (<s>sparśa</s>), meaning all connection [with objects] — is indeed well-known, remembered in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>.
It is difficult to see — that is, difficult to realize — for all <s>yogins</s>, meaning all practitioners of yoga who lack the knowledge established in the <s>Vedānta</s>.
The meaning is: it is attainable only through the effort of realizing the reality of the <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: yogino bibhyati hyasmātsarvabhayavarjitādapyātmanāśarūpamimaṃ yogaṃ manyamānā bhayaṃ kurvanty abhaye 'sminbhayadarśino bhayanimittātmanāśadarśanaśīlā avivekina ityarthaḥ //39//
children.translated_text: <s>Yogins</s> are afraid of this [<s>yoga</s>], which is devoid of all fear — thinking that this <s>yoga</s> consists in the destruction of the self, they create fear. In this fearless [state], they see fear — they are characterized by the habit of seeing fear in the form of self-annihilation, being undiscriminating. This is the meaning. || 39 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.40
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.40

children.text:
yeṣāṃ punarbrahmasvarūpavyatirekeṇa rajjusarpavat kalpitameva mana indriyādi ca na paramārthato vidyate teṣāṃ brahmasvarūpāṇāmabhayaṃ mokṣākhyā cākṣayā śāntiḥ svabhāvata eva siddhā nānyāyattā nopacāraḥ kathañcanetyavocāma /
ye tvato 'nye yogino mārgagā hīnamadhyamadṛṣṭayo mano 'nyadātmavyatiriktamātsaṃbandhi paśyanti teṣāmātmasatyānubodharahitānām-
children.translated_text: But for those for whom the mind, senses, and the like — like a rope-snake — are merely imagined apart from the nature of <s>Brahman</s> and do not exist in ultimate reality, fearlessness and the imperishable peace called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) are established by their very nature, not dependent on anything else, and not merely figurative in any way — this is what we have said. But for those other <s>yogins</s> who follow the [ordinary] path, who hold inferior and intermediate views, who see the mind as something other than the <s>Ātman</s>, as related to the <s>Ātman</s> — for them, who lack the realization of the truth of the <s>Ātman</s> —

children.text: manaso nigrahāyattam abhayaṃ sarvayoginām /
children.translated_text: fearlessness for all <s>yogins</s> depends on the restraint of the mind;

children.text: duḥkhakṣayaḥ prabodhaś cāpy akṣayā śāntir eva ca // MandUpK_3.40 //
children.translated_text: so too the cessation of suffering, awakening, and imperishable peace. || MandUpK 3.40 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.40
manaso nigrahāyattamabhayaṃ sarveṣāṃ yoginām /
children.translated_text: Fearlessness for all <s>yogins</s> depends on the restraint of the mind.

children.text: kiṃ ca duḥkhakṣayo 'pi, na hyātmasaṃbandhini manasi pracalite duḥkhakṣayo 'sty avivekinām /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the cessation of suffering also [depends on it]; for those who lack discrimination, when the mind, which is related to the <s>Ātman</s>, fluctuates, there is no cessation of suffering.

children.text: kiṃ cātmaprabodho 'pi manonigrahāyatta eva /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the awakening of the <s>Ātman</s> also depends on the restraint of the mind.

children.text: tathākṣayāpi mokṣākhyā śāntis teṣāṃ manonigrahāyattaiva //40//
children.translated_text: Likewise, the imperishable peace called liberation also depends, for them, on the restraint of the mind alone. || 40 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 3.40:

children.text: START MandUpK 3.41
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.41

children.text: utseka udadher yadvat kuśāgreṇaikabindunā /
children.translated_text: Just as the draining of the ocean, drop by drop, with the tip of a blade of <s>kuśa</s> grass,

children.text: manaso nigrahas tadvad bhaved aparikhedataḥ // MandUpK_3.41 //
children.translated_text: so too would be the restraint of the mind — through unflagging [effort]. || MandUpK 3.41 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.41
manonigraho 'pi teṣāmudadheḥ kuśāgreṇaikabinduno9tsecanena śoṣaṇavyavasāyavadvyavasāyavatāmanavasannāntaḥ karaṇānāmanirvedādaparikhedato bhavatītyarthaḥ //41//
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.41: The restraint of the mind for them is like the resolve to dry up the ocean by scooping it out drop by drop with the tip of a <s>kuśa</s> grass blade — it is possible for those of resolute determination whose inner faculties have not sunk, through unflagging effort, that is, through perseverance — this is the meaning. || 41 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.42
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.42

children.text: kimaparikhinnavyavasāyamātrameva manonigraha upāyaḥ? na, ityucyate /
children.translated_text: Is mere unflagging determination the only means for the restraint of the mind? No, it is said:

children.text: upāyena nigṛhṇīyād vikṣiptaṃ kāmabhogayoḥ /
children.translated_text: One should restrain the mind, [when it is] distracted toward desire and enjoyment, by a [specific] means;

children.text: suprasannaṃ laye caiva yathā kāmo layas tathā // MandUpK_3.42 //
children.translated_text: and [restrain it] when it is well-settled in absorption (<s>laya</s>) too — for absorption is [as problematic] as desire. || MandUpK 3.42 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.42
aparikhinnavyavasāyavānsan vakṣyamāṇenopāyena kāmabhogaviṣayeṣu vikṣiptaṃ mano nigṛhṇīyānnirundhyādātmanyevetyarthaḥ /
kiṃ ca līyate 'sminniti suṣupto layastasmiṃllaye ca suprasannam āyāsavarjitaṃ apī7tyetat, nigṛhṇīyādityanuvartate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.42: Being of unflagging determination, one should restrain — that is, check — the mind, distracted toward the objects of desire and enjoyment, by the means to be stated, [withdrawing it] into the <s>Ātman</s> alone — this is the meaning. Moreover, <s>laya</s> — deep sleep, in which [the mind] dissolves — when the mind is well-settled, i.e., free from effort, in that <s>laya</s> also, the word 'restrain' continues [from above].

children.text: suprasannaṃ cetkasmānnigṛhyata ityucyate /
children.translated_text: If it is well-settled, why should it be restrained? It is said:

children.text: yasmādyathā kāmo 'narthahetustathā layo 'pi /
children.translated_text: Because just as desire is a cause of harm, so too is <s>laya</s> (absorption).

children.text: ataḥ kāmaviṣayasya manaso nigrahavallayādapi niroddhavyamityarthaḥ //42//
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the mind directed toward desirable objects must be restrained, so too must it be drawn away from <s>laya</s> — this is the meaning. || 42 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.43
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.43

children.text: kaḥ sa upāyaḥ? ityucyate-
children.translated_text: What is that means? It is said:

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sarvam anusmṛtya kāmabhogān nivartayet /
children.translated_text: Recollecting that all [phenomenal existence] is suffering, one should turn [the mind] away from the enjoyment of desires;

children.text: ajaṃ sarvamanusmṛtya jātaṃ naiva tu paśyati // MandUpK_3.43 //
children.translated_text: recollecting that all is unborn, one does not see anything as born. || MandUpK 3.43 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.43
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.43:

children.text: sarvaṃ dvaitamavidyāvijṛmbhitaṃ duḥkhamevetyanusmṛtya kāmabhogātkāmanimitto bhoga icchāviṣayastasmādviprasṛtaṃ mano nivartayedvairāgyabhāvanayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Recollecting that all duality, being a manifestation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), is nothing but suffering, one should turn the mind away from the enjoyment of desires — enjoyment caused by desire, whose object is craving — through the cultivation of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), this is the meaning.

children.text: ajaṃ brahmasarvamityetacchāstrācāryopadeśato 'nusmṛtya tadviparītaṃ dvaitajātaṃ naiva tu paśyati, abhāvāt //43//
children.translated_text: Recollecting from the teaching of scripture and teacher that all is unborn <s>Brahman</s>, one does not see the opposite — duality as born — because it is non-existent. || 43 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.44
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.44

children.text: laye saṃbodhayec cittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should awaken the mind [when it has fallen] into <s>laya</s> (absorption); when distracted, one should calm it again;

children.text: sakaṣāyaṃ vijānīyāt samaprāptaṃ na cālayet // MandUpK_3.44 //
children.translated_text: one should recognize [the mind] when it is tainted by <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion); when it has attained equanimity, one should not disturb it. || MandUpK 3.44 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.44
evamanena jñānābhyāsavairāgyadvayopāyena laye suṣupte līnaṃ saṃbodhayenmana ātmavivekadarśanena yojayet /
cittaṃ mana ityanarthāntaram /
vikṣiptaṃ ca kāmabhogeṣu śamayetpunaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when distracted toward the objects of desire and enjoyment, one should calm it again.

children.text: eva punaḥ punarabhyasyato layātsaṃbodhitaṃ viṣayebhyaśca vyāvartitaṃ nāpi sāmyāpannamantarālāvasthaṃ sakaṣāyaṃ sarāgaṃ bījasaṃyuktaṃ mana iti vijānīyāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, as one practices again and again — [the mind] awakened from <s>laya</s> and withdrawn from sense objects — when it has not yet attained equanimity but is in an intermediate state, one should recognize it as tainted by <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion), possessing attachment, connected with the seed [of desire].

children.text: tato 'pi yatnataḥ sāmyamāpādayet /
children.translated_text: From that [state] too, one should bring it to equanimity with effort.

children.text: yadā tu samaprāptaṃ bhavati samaprāptyabhimukhībhavatītyarthaḥ, tatastanna vicālayedviṣayābhimukhaṃ na kuryādityarthaḥ //44//
children.translated_text: But when it has attained equanimity — meaning when it has become favorably inclined toward equanimity — then one should not disturb it, meaning one should not direct it toward objects. || 44 ||

Commentary on MandUpK 3.44: Thus, through this twofold means of knowledge-practice and dispassion (<s>jñānābhyāsa</s> and <s>vairāgya</s>), one should awaken the mind [when it has] dissolved in <s>laya</s>, deep sleep, and engage it in the vision of the discrimination of the <s>Ātman</s>. <s>Citta</s> (mind) is synonymous with <s>manas</s>.

children.text: START MandUpK 3.45
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.45

children.text: nāsvādayet sukhaṃ tatra niḥsaṅgaḥ prajñayā bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should not savor the pleasure therein; one should become detached through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>);

children.text: niścalaṃ niścarac cittam ekīkuryāt prayatnataḥ // MandUpK_3.45 //
children.translated_text: one should, with effort, unify the mind — [which is] unmoving [in nature yet] moving outward. || MandUpK 3.45 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_3.45
samādhitsato yogino yatsukhaṃ jāyate tannākhādayet, tatra na rajyetetyarthaḥ /
kathaṃ tarhi? niḥsaṅgo niḥspṛhaḥ prajñayā vivekabuddhyā yadupalabhyate sukhaṃ tadavidyāparikalpitaṃ mṛṣaiveti vibhāvayet /
tato 'pi sukharāgānnigṛhṇīyādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.45: The pleasure that arises for the <s>yogin</s> who is striving to attain <s>samādhi</s> — one should not savor it, meaning one should not be attached to it. How then? Being detached, free from craving, through <s>prajñā</s> (discriminative wisdom), one should discern: 'The pleasure that is perceived is imagined by <s>avidyā</s> and is false' — thus one should see it clearly. Even from the attachment to that pleasure, one should restrain [the mind] — this is the meaning.

children.text: yathā punaḥ sukharāgānnivṛttaṃ niścalasvabhāvaṃ sanniścaradbahirnirgacchadbhavati cittaṃ tatastato niyamyoktopāyenātmanyevaikīkuryātprayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind, withdrawn from the attachment to pleasure, being of an unmoving nature, nevertheless moves outward — goes outward — then, restraining it from there through the means stated, one should with effort unify it in the <s>Ātman</s> alone.

children.text: cittasvarūpasattāmātramevāpādayedityarthaḥ //45//
children.translated_text: One should bring it to the state of being merely the essence of the mind's own nature — this is the meaning. || 45 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.46
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.46

children.text: yadā na līyate cittaṃ na ca vikṣipyate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind does not dissolve [into <s>laya</s>], nor is distracted again,

children.text: aniṅganam anābhāsaṃ niṣpannaṃ brahma tat tadā // MandUpK_3.46 //
children.translated_text: unmoving, without appearance — that is <s>Brahman</s> accomplished. || MandUpK 3.46 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.46

yathoktopāyena nigṛhītaṃ cittaṃ yadā suṣuöe na Öīyatena ca punarviṣayeṣuvikṣipyate, aniṅganamacalaṃ nivātapradīpakalpam, anābhāsaṃ na kenacitkalpitena viṣayabhāvenāvabhāsata iti, yadaivaṃlakṣaṇaṃ cittaṃ tadā niṣpannaṃ brahma bahmasvarūpeṇa niṣpannaṃ cittaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ //46//
children.translated_text: When the mind, restrained through the means described, does not dissolve into deep sleep and is not distracted toward objects again; unmoving — still, like a flame in a windless place; without appearance — not appearing as any imagined object-form; when the mind is of such character, then it is <s>Brahman</s> accomplished — meaning the mind has become established in the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. || 46 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 3.46:

children.text: START MandUpK 3.47
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.47

children.text: svasthaṃ śāntaṃ sanirvāṇam akathyaṃ sukham uttamam /
children.translated_text: Self-established, peaceful, with <s>nirvāṇa</s>, inexpressible, the supreme bliss,

children.text: ajam ajena jñeyena sarvajñaṃ paricakṣate // MandUpK_3.47 //
children.translated_text: unborn, [one] with the unborn knowable, all-knowing — thus they describe [it]. || MandUpK 3.47 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.47
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 3.47:

children.text: yathoktaṃ paramārthasukhamātmasatyānubodhalakṣaṇaṃ svasthaṃ svātmani sthitam, śāntaṃ sarvānarthopaśamarūpam, sanirvāṇaṃ nirvṛtinirmāṇaṃ kaivalyaṃ saha nirvāṇena vartate, taccākathyaṃ na śakyate kathayitum, atyantāsādhāraṇaviṣayatvāt, sukhamuttamaṃ niratiśayaṃ hi tadyogipratyakṣameva /
