children.translated_text: The supreme bliss described above, characterized by the realization of the truth of the <s>Ātman</s>, is self-established — abiding in one's own <s>Ātman</s>; peaceful — of the nature of the cessation of all misfortune; with <s>nirvāṇa</s> — accompanied by extinction, i.e., liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>); and it is inexpressible — it cannot be communicated, because its object is utterly unique; the supreme, unsurpassable bliss — for it is directly perceived only by <s>yogins</s>.

children.text: na jātamityajaṃ yathā viṣayaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: It is not born, hence unborn — like the objects [of knowledge].

children.text: ajenānutpannena jñeyenāvyatiriktaṃ satsvena sarvajñarūpeṇa sarvajñaṃ brahmaiva sukhaṃ paricakṣate kathayanti brahmavidaḥ //47//
children.translated_text: Identical with the unborn, unproduced knowable, all-knowing by its own nature as omniscient — the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> describe that bliss as <s>Brahman</s> itself. || 47 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 3.48
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 3.48

children.text:
sarvo 'pyayaṃ manonigrahādirmṛllohādivatsṛṣṭirupāsanā coktā paramārthasvarūpapratipatyupāyatvena na paramārthasatyeti /
paramārthasatyaṃ tu
children.translated_text: All this — the restraint of the mind and so forth — like creation from clay, iron, and the like, as well as worship, has been stated as a means to the realization of the ultimate reality, not as ultimately real in itself. The ultimately real is:

children.text: na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: No <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) whatsoever is born; there is no origination for it;

children.text: etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiñcin na jāyate // MandUpK_3.48 //
children.translated_text: this is that supreme truth, wherein nothing whatsoever is born. || MandUpK 3.48 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_3.48
na kaścijjāyate jīvaḥ kartā bhoktā ca notpadyate kenacidapi prakāreṇa /
children.translated_text: No <s>jīva</s> whatsoever is born; neither agent nor experiencer arises in any manner whatsoever.

children.text: ataḥ svabhāvato 'jasyāsyaikasyātmanaḥ saṃbhavaḥ kāraṇaṃ na vidyate nāsti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for this [<s>Ātman</s>] that is unborn by nature, being one, there is no origination — no cause exists.

children.text: yasmānna vidyate 'sya kāraṇaṃ tasmānna kaścijjāyate jīva ityetat /
children.translated_text: Since no cause exists for it, therefore no <s>jīva</s> whatsoever is born — this is the conclusion.

children.text: pūrveṣūpāyatvenoktānāṃ satyānāmetattaduttamaṃ satyaṃ yasminsatyasvarūpe brahmaṇyaṇumātramapi kiñcinna jāyata iti //48//
children.translated_text: Among the truths stated as means in the preceding [verses], this is the supreme truth — that in the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>, not even the slightest thing whatsoever is born. || 48 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 3.48:

children.text: Alātaśāntiprakaraṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Alātaśāntiprakaraṇa</s> (Chapter on the Quenching of the Firebrand)

children.text:
oṃkāranirṇayadvāreṇāgamataḥ pratijñātasyādvaitasya bāhyaviṣayabhedavaitathyācca siddhasya punaradvaite śāstrayuktibhyāṃ sākṣānnirdhāritasyaitaduttamaṃ satyamityupasaṃhāraḥ kṛto 'nte /
tasyaitatyāgamārthasyādvaitadarśanasya pratipakṣabhūtā dvaitino vaināśikāśca teṣāṃ cānyonyavirodādrāgadveṣādikleśāspadaṃ darśanamiti mithyādarśanatvaṃ sūcitam /
kleśānāspadatvātsamyagdarśanamityadvaitadarśanaṃ stūyate /
tadiha vistareṇānyonyaviruddhatayāsamyagdarśanatvaṃ pradarśya tatpratiṣedhenādvaitadarśanasiddhirupasaṃhartavyāvītanyāyenetyalātaśānd irārabhyate /
children.translated_text: The non-duality asserted through the investigation of <s>Oṃkāra</s> from scripture, established through the unreality of external objects in the <s>Vaitathya</s> [chapter], and then directly determined in the <s>Advaita</s> [chapter] through scripture and reasoning, was concluded at the end [with the statement] 'this is the supreme truth.' The opponents of this teaching of non-duality — the dualists and the nihilists (<s>vaināśikas</s>) — and through their mutual contradictions, [it was] indicated that [their] view is a basis for the afflictions of attachment, aversion, and the like, and therefore constitutes false vision. Because it is free from the basis of afflictions, right vision — the vision of non-duality — is praised. Here, by demonstrating at length that [the rival views] are mutually contradictory and therefore constitute wrong vision, and by negating them, the establishment of the non-dual vision is to be concluded according to the method already employed — thus the <s>Alātaśānti</s> [chapter] is commenced.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.1
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.1

children.text:
tatrādvaitadarśanasampradāyakartur advaitasvarūpeṇaiva namaskārārtho 'yamādyaślokaḥ /
ācāryapūjā hyabhipretārthasiddhyartheṣyate śāstrārambhe /
children.translated_text: Therein, this first verse serves the purpose of salutation to the originator of the tradition of the non-dual vision, in the very form of non-duality. For the worship of the teacher is desired at the commencement of a treatise for the attainment of the intended purpose.

children.text: jñānenākāśakalpena dharmānyo gaganopamān /
children.translated_text: Through knowledge like space, [he knew] the <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that are like the sky,

children.text: jñeyābhinnena saṃbuddhas taṃ vande dvipadāṃ varam // MandUpK_4.1 //
children.translated_text: non-different from the knowable — to that awakened one, the best among bipeds, I bow. || MandUpK 4.1 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.1
ākāśeneṣadasamāptamākāśakalpamākāśatulyametat /
tenākāśakalpena jñānena, kim? dharmānātmanaḥ, kiṃviśiṣṭāngaganopamāngaganamupamā yeṣāṃ te gaganopamāstānātmano dharmān /
jñānasyaiva punarviśeṣaṇam- jñeyairdharmairātmabhirabhinnamagnyuṣṇavatsavitṛprakāśavacca jñānaṃ tena jñeyābhinnena jñānenākāśakalpena jñeyātmasvarūpāvyatiriktena gaganopamāndharmānyaḥ saṃbuddhaḥ saṃbuddhavāniti, ayameveśvaro yo nārāyaṇākhyastaṃ vande 'bhivādaye dvipadāṃ varaṃ dvipadopalakṣitānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ varaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣottamamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.1: 'Like space' — this [compound means] comparable to space, equal to space. Through that knowledge which is like space — what [did he know]? The <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) of the <s>Ātman</s> — of what character? 'Like the sky' — those whose comparison is the sky, i.e., comparable to the sky — those phenomena of the <s>Ātman</s>. A further qualification of knowledge: knowledge that is non-different from the knowable phenomena, the <s>Ātman</s> — like heat from fire, like light from the sun — through that knowledge which is like space, non-different from the knowable, i.e., not distinct from the nature of the knowable <s>Ātman</s>, [he knew] the phenomena comparable to the sky: he who has thus fully awakened — this very one is the Lord called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — to him I bow, the best among bipeds — the foremost among beings designated as bipeds, the Supreme Being (<s>Puruṣottama</s>) — this is the purport.

children.text: upadeṣṭṛnamaskāramukhena jñānajñeyajñātṛbhedarahitaṃ paramārthadarśanamiha prakaraṇe pratipipādayiṣitaṃ pratipakṣapratiṣedhadvāreṇa pratijñātaṃ bhavati //1//
children.translated_text: Through the vehicle of salutation to the teacher, the ultimate vision that is devoid of the distinction of knowledge, knowable, and knower is proposed as the subject to be established in this chapter, through the negation of opposing views. || 1 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.2
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.2

children.text: adhunā9dvaitadarśanayogasya namaskārastatstutaye-
children.translated_text: Now, the salutation to the <s>yoga</s> of the non-dual vision, for its praise:

children.text: asparśayogo vai nāma sarvasattvasukho hitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Asparśayoga</s> (the yoga of non-contact) by name, beneficial and conducive to the happiness of all beings,

children.text: avivādo 'viruddhaś ca deśitas taṃ namāmy aham // MandUpK_4.2 //
children.translated_text: free from dispute, non-contradictory — thus it has been taught; to that [yoga] I bow. || MandUpK 4.2 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.2
sparśanaṃ sparśaḥ sambandho na vidyate yasya yogasya kenacitkadācidapi sa asparśayogo brahmasvabhāva eva, vai nāmeti brahmavidāmasparśayoga ityevaṃprasiddha ityarthaḥ /
sa ca sarvasattvasukhaḥ /
bhavati kaścidatyantasukhasādhanaviśiṣṭo 'pi duḥkharūpaḥ, yathā tapaḥ /
ayaṃ tu na tathā /
kiṃ tarhi sarvasattvānāṃ sukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.2: Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) means connection — that <s>yoga</s> for which no connection with anything whatsoever exists at any time is <s>asparśayoga</s>, which is indeed the very nature of <s>Brahman</s>. '<s>Vai nāma</s>' means: among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, it is thus well-known as '<s>asparśayoga</s>' — this is the meaning. And it is conducive to the happiness of all beings. There are certain things that, though distinguished as means to the highest bliss, are painful in nature, like austerity (<s>tapas</s>). But this is not like that. Rather, it is happiness for all beings.

children.text: tatheha bhavati kaścidviṣayopabhogaḥ sukho na hito 'yaṃ tu sukho hitaśca nityamapracalitasvabhāvatvāt kiṃ cāvivādo viruddha vadanaṃ vivādaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraheṇa yasminna vidyate sa avivādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, here there is some sense-enjoyment that is pleasant but not beneficial; but this [<s>asparśayoga</s>] is both pleasant and beneficial, because of its eternally unshifting nature. Moreover, it is free from dispute — disputation is arguing through the adoption of thesis and counter-thesis; that in which this does not exist is free from dispute.

children.text: kasmāt? yato 'viruddhaśca /
children.translated_text: Why? Because it is non-contradictory.

children.text: ya īdṛśo yogo deśita upadiṣṭaḥ śāstreṇa taṃ namāmyahaṃ praṇamāmītyarthaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Such a <s>yoga</s> has been taught — instructed — by the scripture; to that I bow, meaning I prostrate — this is the meaning. || 2 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.3
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.3

children.text: kathaṃ dvaitinaḥ parasparaṃ virudhyante? ityucyate /
children.translated_text: How do the dualists contradict each other? It is said:

children.text: bhūtasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ kecid eva hi /
children.translated_text: Certain disputants indeed desire the birth of what [already] exists;

children.text: abhūtasyāpare dhīrā vivadantaḥ parasparam // MandUpK_4.3 //
children.translated_text: others, [who consider themselves] wise, disputing among themselves, [desire the birth] of what does not exist. || MandUpK 4.3 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.3
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.3:

children.text: bhūtasya vidyamānasya vastuno jātimutpattimicchanti vādinaḥ kecideva hi sāṃkhyā na sarvaṃ eva dvaitinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Certain disputants — the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, not all dualists — desire the birth, the origination, of what exists, of a real, existing thing.

children.text: yasmādabhūtasyāvidyamānasyāpare vaiśeṣikā naiyāyikāśca dhīrā dhīmantaḥ prajñābhimānina ityartho vivadanto viruddhaṃ vadanto hyanyenyamicchanti jetumityabhiprāyaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: Since others — the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and <s>Naiyāyikas</s> — who are wise, meaning who pride themselves on their intelligence, disputing, speaking contradictory [things], indeed desire to defeat one another — this is the purport. || 3 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.4
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.4

children.text: tairevaṃ viruddhavadanenānyonyapakṣapratiṣedhaṃ kurvadbhiḥ kiṃ khyāpitaṃ bhavatyucyate-
children.translated_text: What is made known by them through such contradictory statements, each negating the other's position? It is said:

children.text: bhūtaṃ na jāyate kiñcid abhūtaṃ naiva jāyate /
children.translated_text: What exists is not born; what does not exist is also never born;

children.text: vivadanto 'dvayā hy evam ajātiṃ khyāpayanti te // MandUpK_4.4 //
children.translated_text: thus disputing, these [dualists], though [themselves] non-dual, proclaim [the doctrine of] non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>). || MandUpK 4.4 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.4
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.4:

children.text: bhūtaṃ vidyamānaṃ vastu na jāyate kiñcidvidyamānatvādevātmavadityevaṃ vadannasadvādī sāṃkhyapakṣaṃ pratiṣedhati sajjanma /
children.translated_text: The one who holds that an existent thing is not born — [arguing] 'An existent, really existing entity is not born, because it already exists, like the Self' — speaking thus, the proponent of non-existence (<s>asadvādin</s>) refutes the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position of the birth of the existent (<s>sajjanma</s>).

children.text: tathābhūtamavidyamānamavidyamānatvānnaiva jāyate śaśaviṣāṇavadityevaṃ vadansāṃkhyo 'pyasaddhādipakṣamasajjanma pratiṣedhati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, [the Sāṃkhya argues:] 'A non-existent, non-existing thing is never born, because it is non-existent, like a hare's horn' — speaking thus, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> too refutes the position of the Buddhists and others — the birth of the non-existent (<s>asajjanma</s>).

children.text: vivadanto viruddhaṃ vadanto 'dvayā advaitino hyete 'nyonyasya pakṣau sadasatorjanmanī pratiṣedhanto 'jātimanutpattimarthātkhyāpayanti prakāśayanti te //4//
children.translated_text: These non-dualists (<s>advaitins</s>), disputing and speaking contradictory things, by mutually refuting each other's positions on the birth of the existent and the non-existent, implicitly proclaim — illuminate — non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>). ||4||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.5
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.5

children.text: khyāpyamānām ajātiṃ tair anumodāmahe vayam /
children.translated_text: We approve the non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) proclaimed by them.

children.text: vivadāmo na taiḥ sārdham avivādaṃ nibodhata // MandUpK_4.5 //
children.translated_text: We do not dispute with them — understand that which is free from dispute. || Kārikā 4.5 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.5
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.5

children.text: tairevaṃ khyāpyamānāmajātimevamastvityanumodāmahe kevalaṃ na taiḥ sārdhaṃ vivadāmaḥ pakṣapratipakṣagrahaṇena; yathā te 'nyonyamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The non-origination thus proclaimed by them — 'let it be so' — we approve. However, we do not dispute with them by taking up thesis and counter-thesis, as they do with each other — this is the intention.

children.text: atastamavivādaṃ vivādarahitaṃ paramārthadarśanamanujñātamasmābhirnibodhata he śiṣyāḥ //5//
children.translated_text: Therefore, understand that vision of ultimate reality which is free from dispute, which has been sanctioned by us — O students! ||5||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.6
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.6

children.text: ajātasyaiva dharmasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The proponents wish [to assert] the birth of that which is by nature unborn (<s>ajāta</s>).

children.text: ajāto hy amṛto dharmo martyatāṃ katham eṣyati // MandUpK_4.6 //
children.translated_text: How can that which is unborn and immortal by nature come to mortality? || Kārikā 4.6 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.6
sadasadvādinaḥ sarve 'pīti purastātkṛtabhāṣyaślokaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: All proponents, whether of existence or non-existence — this is the verse for which the commentary was composed earlier. ||6||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.6

children.text: START MandUpK 4.7-8
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.7-8

children.text: na bhavaty amṛtaṃ martyaṃ na martyam amṛtaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The immortal does not become mortal, nor does the mortal become immortal.

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathañcid bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.7 //
children.translated_text: A change in one's essential nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) will never occur in any way. || Kārikā 4.7 ||

children.text: svabhāvenāmṛto yasya dharmo gacchati martyatām /
children.translated_text: For one whose nature (<s>dharma</s>) is by its own nature immortal and yet comes to mortality —

children.text: kṛtakenāmṛtas tasya kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalaḥ // MandUpK_4.8 //
children.translated_text: How will the [supposedly] artificial immortality remain stable and unchanging for that one? || Kārikā 4.8 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.7-8
uktārthānāṃ ślokānāmihopanyāsaḥ paravādipakṣāṇāmanyonyavirodhakhyāpitānutpatyanumodanapradarśanārthaḥ //7-8//
children.translated_text: The presentation here of these verses, whose meaning has already been stated, is for the purpose of demonstrating the approval of non-origination that is revealed by the mutual contradiction of the opponents' positions. ||7-8||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.7-8

children.text: START MandUpK 4.9
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.9

children.text: yasmāllaukikyapi prakṛtirna viparyeti, kāsāvityāha-
children.translated_text: Since even in the worldly [domain], essential nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) does not change, what is it? He says —

children.text: sāṃsiddhikī svābhāvikī sahajā akṛtā ca yā /
children.translated_text: That which is [established] through accomplishment (<s>sāṃsiddhikī</s>), inherent (<s>svābhāvikī</s>), innate (<s>sahajā</s>), and not made by anyone (<s>akṛtā</s>) —

children.text: prakṛtiḥ seti vijñeyā svabhāvaṃ na jahāti yā // MandUpK_4.9 //
children.translated_text: That is to be known as <s>prakṛti</s> (essential nature) — that which does not abandon its own nature. || Kārikā 4.9 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.9
samyaksiddhiḥ saṃsiddhistatra bhavā sāṃsiddhikī yathā yogināṃ siddhānām aṇimādyaiśvaryaprāptiḥ prakṛtiḥ /
sā bhūtabhaviṣyatkālayorapi yogināṃ na viparyeti tathaiva sā /
tathā svābhāvikī dravyasvabhāvata eva yathāgnyādīnām uṣṇaprakāśādilakṣaṇā, sāpi na kālāntare vyabhicarati deśāntare ca /
tathā sahajā ātmanā sahaiva jātā yathā pakṣyādīnāmākāśagamanādilakṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.9: <s>Sāṃsiddhikī</s> — 'that which arises from perfect accomplishment (<s>saṃsiddhi</s>)' — like the attainment of supernatural powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the like by accomplished yogins; that is a <s>prakṛti</s>. And that does not change for yogins in past and future times either — such is its nature. Likewise, <s>svābhāvikī</s> — arising from the very nature of a substance — such as the nature of heat and light for fire and the like; that too does not deviate at another time or place. Likewise, <s>sahajā</s> — 'born together with oneself' — such as the capacity to fly through space for birds and the like.

children.text: anyāpi yā kācidakṛtā kenacinna kṛtā yatāpāṃ nimnadeśagamanādilakṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: And also any other [nature] that is <s>akṛtā</s> — 'not made by anyone' — such as the tendency of water to flow to lower ground.

children.text: anyāpi yā kājitsvabhāvaṃ na jahāti sā sarvā prakṛtiriti vijñeyā loke /
children.translated_text: And any other [nature] that does not abandon its essential character — all that is to be known as <s>prakṛti</s> in the world.

children.text: mithyākalpiteṣu laukikeṣvapi vastuṣu prakṛtirnānyathā bhavati kimutājasvabhāveṣu paramārthavastuṣvamṛtatvalakṣaṇā prakṛtirnānyathā bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: Even in falsely imagined worldly objects, essential nature does not become otherwise — how much less, then, does the essential nature of ultimate realities (<s>paramārthavastus</s>), whose nature is non-origination, characterized by immortality, become otherwise! This is the intention. ||9||

children.text:
START MandUpK 4.10
kiṃviṣayā punaḥ sā prakṛtiryasyā anyathābhāvo vādibhiḥ kalpyate kalpanāyāṃ vā ko doṣa ityāha-
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.10: What is the subject of that essential nature whose alteration is imagined by the proponents, and what is the defect in [their] imagination? He says —

children.text: jarāmaraṇanirmuktāḥ sarve dharmāḥ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: All entities (<s>dharmas</s>) are by their own nature free from old age and death.

children.text: jarāmaraṇam icchantaś cyavante tanmanīṣayā // MandUpK_4.10 //
children.translated_text: Those who conceive of old age and death fall from [their true nature] through that very conception. || Kārikā 4.10 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.10
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.10

children.text: jarāmaraṇanirmuktāḥ- jarāmaraṇādisarvavikriyāvarjitā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Free from old age and death' means free from all modifications including old age, death, and the rest — this is the meaning.

children.text: ke ? sarve dharmāḥ sarva ātmāna ityetatsvabhāvataḥ prakṛtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who? All entities — all selves — this is what is meant — by their own nature, by their essential nature (<s>prakṛti</s>).

children.text: evaṃsvabhāvāḥ santo dharmājarāmaraṇamicchanta icchanta ivecchantorajjvāmiva sarpamātmani kalpayantaścyavante svabhāvataścalantītyarthaḥ, tanmanīṣayā janmamaraṇacintayā tadbhāvabhāvitatvādoṣeṇetyarthaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: Being of such nature, those entities who conceive of — or seem to conceive of — old age and death, imagining [them] upon the Self like a snake upon a rope, fall — deviate from their own nature. The meaning is: through that very conception of birth and death, by the defect of being conditioned by that very thought-pattern. ||10||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.11
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.11

children.text: kathaṃ sajjātivādibhiḥ sāṃkhyairanupapannamucyata ityāha vaiśeṣikaḥ-
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> says: how is it said that the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position of the birth of the existent is untenable? —

children.text: kāraṇaṃ yasya vai kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya jāyate /
children.translated_text: For one whose effect is the cause [itself], the cause [must also be said to] be born.

children.text: jāyamānaṃ katham ajaṃ bhinnaṃ nityaṃ kathaṃ ca tat // MandUpK_4.11 //
children.translated_text: If [the cause is said to be] born, how [can it be called] unborn? And if [the effect is] different [from the cause], how [can it be called] eternal? || Kārikā 4.11 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.11
kāraṇaṃ mṛdvadupādānalakṣaṇaṃ yasya vādino vai kāryaṃ kāraṇameva kāryākāreṇa pariṇamate yasya vādina ityarthaḥ, tasyājameva satprādhānādi kāraṇaṃ mahadādikāryarūpeṇa jāyata ityarthaḥ /
mahadādyākāreṇa cejjāyamānaṃ pradhānaṃ kathamajamucyate tairvipratiṣiddhaṃ cedaṃ jāyate 'jaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.11: 'The cause, having the character of a material cause like clay' — for the proponent whose effect is the cause itself, that is, the cause transforms into the form of the effect — this is the meaning. For that proponent, the unborn, the eternally existent <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like, as cause, is born in the form of the effect <s>Mahat</s> (cosmic intellect) and the like — this is the meaning. And if <s>Pradhāna</s>, being born in the form of <s>Mahat</s> and the like, how is it called 'unborn' by them? This is contradictory — 'it is born' and 'it is unborn.'

children.text: nityaṃ ca tairucyate pradhānaṃ bhinnaṃ vidīrṇaṃ sphuṭitamekadeśena satkathaṃ nityaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Pradhāna</s> is called eternal by them — yet being split open, burst apart in one part — how can it be eternal? This is the meaning.

children.text: na hi sāvayavaṃ ghaṭādy ekadeśasphuṭanadharmi nityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ loka ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For nothing that has parts, like a pot, which has the property of splitting in one part, is seen to be eternal in the world — this is the meaning.

children.text: vidīrṇaṃ ca syādekadeśenājaṃ nityaṃ cety etadvipratiṣiddhaṃ tairabhidhīyata ityabhiprāyaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: The intention is: that it should be split apart in one part and yet be unborn and eternal — this is stated by them contradictorily. ||11||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.12
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.12

children.text: uktasyaivārthasya spaṣṭīkaraṇārthamāha-
children.translated_text: For the purpose of clarifying the stated meaning, he says —

children.text: kāraṇād yady ananyatvam ataḥ kāryam ajaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If there is non-difference of the effect from the cause, and therefore the effect is unborn,

children.text: jāyamānād dhi vai kāryāt kāraṇaṃ te kathaṃ dhruvam // MandUpK_4.12 //
children.translated_text: Then how can the cause be permanent when the effect from which [it is non-different] is being born? || Kārikā 4.12 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.12
kāraṇādajātkāryasya yadyananyatvamiṣṭaṃ tvayā tataḥ kāryamajamiti prāptam /
children.translated_text: If the non-difference of the effect from the unborn cause is accepted by you, then it follows that the effect is unborn.

children.text: idaṃ cānyadvipratiṣiddhaṃ kāryamajaṃ ceti tava /
children.translated_text: And this is another contradiction on your part — that the effect [is born] and yet is unborn.

children.text: kiṃ cānyatkāryakāraṇayonanyatve jāyamānāddhi vai kāryakāraṇamananyannityaṃ dhruvaṃ ca te kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if there is non-difference of cause and effect, then how could the cause, being non-different from the effect that is being born, be eternal and permanent according to you?

children.text: na hi kukkuṭyā ekadeśaḥ pacyata ekadeśaḥ prasavāya kalpyate //12//
children.translated_text: For one cannot conceive that one part of a hen is cooked while another part is set aside for laying eggs. ||12||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.12

children.text: START MandUpK 4.13
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.13

children.text: kiṃ cānyam-
children.translated_text: Furthermore —

children.text: ajād vai jāyate yasya dṛṣṭāntas tasya nāsti vai /
children.translated_text: For one who holds that the effect is born from the unborn [cause], there is indeed no illustration.

children.text: jātāc ca jāyāmānasya na vyavasthā prasajyate // MandUpK_4.13 //
children.translated_text: And for one who holds that [the effect] is born from what is [itself] born, there is no end to the regress. || Kārikā 4.13 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.13
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.13

children.text: ajādanutpannādvastuno jāyate yasya vādinaḥ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭānttastasya nāsti vai, dṛṣṭāntābhāver'thādajānna kiñcijjāyata iti siddhaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the proponent who holds that an effect is born from an unborn, unoriginated entity, there is indeed no illustration. From the absence of an illustration, it is implicitly established that nothing whatsoever is born from the unborn — this is the meaning.

children.text: yadā punarjātājjāyamānasya vastuno 'bhyupagamas tadapyanyasmāj jātāttadapyanyasmāditi na vyāvasthā prasajyate /
children.translated_text: When, however, the acceptance is that [the effect] is born from something [already] born, then that too [must be born] from another born thing, and that from yet another — thus there is no end to the regress.

children.text: anavasthānaṃ syādityarthaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: There would be an infinite regress — this is the meaning. ||13||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.14
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.14

children.text: "yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūt"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 18) iti paramārthato dvaitābhāvaḥ śrutyoktastamāśrityāha-
children.translated_text: Relying on the <s>śruti</s> 'Where indeed everything has become the Self alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.18), which states the ultimate absence of duality, he says —

children.text: hetor ādiḥ phalaṃ yeṣām ādir hetuḥ phalasya ca /
children.translated_text: For those who hold that the effect is the beginning of the cause, and the cause is the beginning of the effect —

children.text: hetoḥ phalasya cānādiḥ kathaṃ tair upavarṇyate // MandUpK_4.14 //
children.translated_text: How can the beginninglessness of cause and effect be described by them? || Kārikā 4.14 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.14
hetordharmāderādiḥ kāraṇaṃ dehādisaṃghātaḥ phalaṃ yeṣāṃ vādinām /
children.translated_text: For those proponents who hold that the effect — the aggregate of body and the like — is the beginning (i.e., cause) of the cause, namely <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the like;

children.text: tathādiḥ kāraṇaṃ heturdharmādharmādiḥ phalasya ca dehādisaṃghātasya /
children.translated_text: And that the cause — <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the like — is the beginning of the effect, namely the aggregate of body and the like;

children.text: evaṃ hetuphalayoritaretarakāryakāraṇatvenādimattvaṃ bruvadbhirevaṃ hetoḥ phalasya cānāditvaṃ kathaṃ tairupavarṇyate? vipratiṣiddhamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those who speak of cause and effect as having a beginning through their being mutually related as cause and effect of each other — how can the beginninglessness of cause and effect be described by them? It is contradictory — this is the meaning.

children.text: na hi nityasya kūṭasthasyātmano hetuphalātmatā sambhavati //14//
children.translated_text: For the eternal, immutable Self cannot possibly have the nature of cause and effect. ||14||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.14

children.text: START MandUpK 4.15
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.15

children.text: kathaṃ tairviruddhamabhyupagamyata ityucyate-
children.translated_text: How is the contradiction accepted by them? It is stated —

children.text: hetor ādiḥ phalaṃ yeṣām ādir hetuḥ kalasya ca /
children.translated_text: For those who hold that the effect is the beginning of the cause, and the cause is the beginning of the effect,

children.text: tathā janma bhavet teṣāṃ putrāj janma pitur yathā // MandUpK_4.15 //
children.translated_text: Birth would be for them as the birth of a father from his son. || Kārikā 4.15 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.15
hetujanyādeva phalāddhetorjanmābhyupagacchatāṃ teṣāmīdṛśo virodha ukto bhavati yathā putrājjanma pituḥ //15//
children.translated_text: For those who accept that the birth of the cause is from the effect that is itself produced by the cause — such a contradiction is stated as being like the birth of a father from his son. ||15||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.15

children.text: START MandUpK 4.16
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.16

children.text: yathokto virodho na yukto 'bhyupagantumiti cenmanyase-
children.translated_text: If you think the stated contradiction need not be accepted —

children.text: saṃbhave hetuphalayor eṣitavyaḥ kramas tvayā /
children.translated_text: The sequence of cause and effect must be sought by you,

children.text: yugapatsaṃbhave yasmād asaṃbandho viṣāṇavat // MandUpK_4.16 //
children.translated_text: Because if they arise simultaneously, there is no [causal] connection, like [the two] horns [of a cow]. || Kārikā 4.16 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.16
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.16

children.text: saṃbhave hetuphalayorutpattau krama eṣitavyastvayānyeṣṭavyo hetu ; pūrvaṃ paścātphalaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: In the production of cause and effect, the sequence must be sought by you — another [sequence] must be sought: the cause first, then the effect.

children.text: itaśca yugapatsaṃbhave yasmāddhetuphalayoḥ kāryakāraṇatvenāsaṃbandhaḥ, yathā yugapatsaṃbhavatoḥ savyetaragoviṣāṇayoḥ //16//
children.translated_text: And for this further reason: if cause and effect arise simultaneously, there is no connection between them as cause and effect — just as the right and left horns of a cow, which arise simultaneously, [have no causal relation]. ||16||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.17
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.17

children.text: kathamasaṃbandhaḥ? ityāha-
children.translated_text: How is there no connection? He says —

children.text: phalād utpadyamānaḥ san na te hetuḥ prasidhyati /
children.translated_text: A cause that is being produced from the effect does not become established for you.

children.text: aprasiddhaḥ kathaṃ hetuḥ phalam utpādayiṣyati // MandUpK_4.17 //
children.translated_text: How can an unestablished cause produce an effect? || Kārikā 4.17 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.17
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.17

children.text: janyātsvato 'labdhātmakāt phalādutpadyamānaḥ sañśaśaviṣāṇāderivāsato na hetuḥ prasidhyati janma na labhate /
children.translated_text: A cause being produced from an effect that has not yet obtained its own existence — like something from a hare's horn, from the non-existent — does not become established, does not attain birth.

children.text: alabdhātmako 'prasiddhaḥ sañśaśaviṣāṇādikalpastava kathaṃ phalamutpādayiṣyati? na hītaretarāpekṣasiddhyoḥ śaśaviṣāṇakalpayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvena saṃbandhaḥ kvacid dṛṣṭaḥ, anyathā vetyabhiprāyaḥ //17//
children.translated_text: And one that has not obtained its own existence, that is unestablished, that is like a hare's horn according to you — how will it produce an effect? For nowhere is a causal connection seen between things like hare's horns, whose existence depends on each other — or [seen] in any other way. This is the intention. ||17||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.18
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.18

children.text: yadi hetoḥ phalāt siddhiḥ phalasiddhiś ca hetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the establishment of the cause depends on the effect, and the establishment of the effect depends on the cause,

children.text: katarat pūrvaniṣpannaṃ yasya siddhir apekṣayā // MandUpK_4.18 //
children.translated_text: Which of the two was produced first, on whose prior establishment the [other's] establishment depends? || Kārikā 4.18 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.18

asaṃbandhatādoṣeṇāpodite 'pi hetuphalayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāve yadi hetuphalayoranyonyasiddhirabhyupagamyata eva tvayā kataratpūrvaniṣpannaṃ hetuphalayoryasya paścādbhāvinaḥ siddhiḥ syātpūrvasiddhyapekṣayā tad brūhītyarthaḥ //18//
children.translated_text: Even though the causal relationship between cause and effect has been refuted by the defect of the absence of connection, if the mutual establishment of cause and effect is still accepted by you — then state which of the two, cause or effect, was produced first, on whose prior establishment the later one's establishment would depend — this is the meaning. ||18||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.18

children.text: START MandUpK 4.19
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.19

children.text: athaitanna śakyate vaktumiti manyase-
children.translated_text: If you think this cannot be stated —

children.text: aśaktir aparijñānaṃ kramakopo 'tha vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is either inability, or failure to comprehend, or the overthrow of the [causal] sequence.

children.text: evaṃ hi sarvathā buddhair ajātiḥ paridīpitā // MandUpK_4.19 //
children.translated_text: Thus indeed has non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) been illuminated in every way by the wise. || Kārikā 4.19 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.19
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.19

children.text: seyamaśaktiraparijñānaṃ tattvāviveko mūḍhatetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: This inability is a failure to comprehend — a lack of discrimination regarding the truth, meaning confusion.

children.text: atha vā yo 'yaṃ tvayoktaḥ kramo hetoḥ phalasya siddhiḥ phalācca hetoḥ siddhiritītaretarānantaryalakṣaṇastasya kopo viparyāso 'nyathābhāvaḥ syādityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the sequence that you have stated — the establishment of the cause from the effect and of the effect from the cause, characterized by mutual succession — there would be its overthrow, reversal, becoming otherwise. This is the intention.

children.text: evaṃ hetuphalayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvānupapatterajātiḥ sarvasyānutpattiḥ paridīpitā prakāśitānyonyapakṣadoṣaṃ bruvadbhirvādibhirbuddhaiḥ paṇḍitairityarthaḥ //19//
children.translated_text: Thus, from the impossibility of establishing the causal relationship between cause and effect, non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) — the non-production of everything — has been illuminated, revealed, by the proponents, the wise, the learned, who speak of the defects in each other's positions. This is the meaning. ||19||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.20
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.20

children.text:
nanu hetulayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāva ityasmābhiruktaṃ śabdamātramāśritya cchalamidaṃ tvayoktaṃ putrājjanma pituryathā, viṣāṇavaccāsaṃbandha ityādi /
na hyasmābhirasiddhāddhetoḥ phalasiddhirasiddhādvā phalāddhetusiddharabhyupagatā /
kiṃ tarhi? bījāṅkuravatkāryakāraṇabhāvo 'bhyupagamyata iti /
children.translated_text: An objection: we have said that there is a causal relationship between cause and effect — taking refuge merely in our words, this sophistry has been stated by you: 'Birth would be as the birth of a father from his son,' 'Like horns, there is no connection,' and the like. For we do not accept that the establishment of the cause depends on an unestablished effect, or that the establishment of the effect depends on an unestablished cause. Rather, the causal relationship is accepted as being like that of seed and sprout.

children.text: atrocyate-
children.translated_text: To this it is replied —

children.text: bījāṅkurākhyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ sadā sādhyasamo hi sa /
children.translated_text: The illustration called 'seed and sprout' is always equivalent to what is to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>).

children.text: na hi sādhyasamo hetuḥ siddhau sādhyasya yujyate // MandUpK_4.20 //
children.translated_text: For a reason that is equivalent to the thesis cannot logically serve to establish the thesis. || Kārikā 4.20 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.20
bījāṅkurākhyā dṛṣṭānto yaḥ sa sādhyena tulyo mametyabhiprāyaḥ /
nanu pratyakṣaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo bījāṅkurayoranādiḥ? na, pūrvasya pūrvasyāparavadādimattvābhyupagamāt /
yathedānīmutpanno 'paro 'ṅkuro bījādādimānbījaṃ cāparamanyasmādaṅkurāditi krameṇotyannatvādādimat /
evaṃ pūrvaḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuro bījaṃ ca pūrvaṃ pūrvamādimadeviti pratyekaṃ sarvasya bījāṅkurajātasyādimattvātkasyacidapyanāditvānupapatti /
evaṃ hetuphalānām /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.20: The illustration called 'seed and sprout' is, in my view, equivalent to what is to be proved — this is the intention. 'But is not the causal relationship between seed and sprout perceptible and beginningless?' No, because the earlier and earlier [member of the pair] is accepted as having a beginning, like the later one. Just as a sprout now produced is born from a seed and has a beginning, and the seed [has a beginning] from another sprout — thus, by tracing back step by step, each one has a beginning. Similarly, each earlier sprout and each earlier seed has a beginning. Therefore, since every individual member of the seed-sprout series has a beginning, the beginninglessness of any [single member] is untenable. Similarly for cause and effect.

children.text:
atha bījāṅkurasantateranādimattvamiti cet? na, ekatvānupapatteḥ /
na hi bījāṅkuravyatirekeṇa bījāṅkurasantatirnāmaikābhyupagamyate hetuphalasantatirvā tadanāditvavādibhis tasmātsūktaṃ hetoḥ phalasya cānādiḥ kathaṃ tairupavarṇyata iti /
tathā cānyadapyanupapatternacchalamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And likewise, because of other logical impossibilities too—[this theory] is nothing but a sophism—this is the purport.

children.text: na ca loke sādhyasamo hetuḥ sādhyasiddhau siddhinimittaṃ prayujyate pramāṇakuśalairityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the world, a proof that is equally unestablished as the thesis (<s>sādhyasama</s>) is not employed by those skilled in the means of valid knowledge as the means for establishing the thesis—that is the meaning.

children.text: heturiti dṛṣṭānto 'trābhipretaḥ, gamakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Here the word 'reason' (<s>hetu</s>) is intended to mean 'example' (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), because it serves to convey [understanding].

children.text: prakṛto hi dṛṣṭānto na heturiti //20//
children.translated_text: For what is under discussion is the example, not the logical reason. ||20||

But what if the seed-sprout series is beginningless? No, because its unity cannot be established. For indeed, no one who maintains the beginninglessness of the cause-effect series accepts something called 'the seed-sprout series' as a unity apart from the seed and sprout, or a 'cause-effect series' [as such]. Therefore, it is well said: how can they describe the cause and the effect as beginningless?

children.text:
START MandUpK 4.21
kathaṃ buddhairajātiḥ paridīpitetyāha-
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.21: How is non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) illuminated by the wise? He says—

children.text: pūrvāparāparijñānam ajāteḥ paridīpakam /
children.translated_text: The non-cognition of [the relation of] prior and posterior is the illumination of non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>);

children.text: jāyamānād dhi vai dharmāt kathaṃ pūrvaṃ na gṛhyate // MandUpK_4.21 //
children.translated_text: For how is the prior [cause] not apprehended from a thing that is being born? || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.21 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.21
yadetaddhetuphalayoḥ pūrvāparāparijñānaṃ taccaitadajāteḥ paridīpakamavabodhakamityarthaḥ /
jāyamāno hi ceddharmo gṛhyate, kathaṃ tasmātpūrvaṃ kāraṇaṃ na gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: For if a thing is apprehended as being born, how is its prior [cause] not apprehended?

children.text: avaśyaṃ jāyamānasya grahītrā tajjanakaṃ grahītavyam /
children.translated_text: The perceiver of a thing being born must necessarily perceive its producer.

children.text: janyajanakayoḥ saṃbandhasyānapetatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the relationship between the produced and the producer is inseparable.

children.text: tasmādajātiparidīpakaṃ tadityarthaḥ //21//
children.translated_text: Therefore, that [non-cognition of the prior-posterior relation] is the illumination of non-origination—that is the meaning. ||21||

Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.21: This non-cognition of the prior and posterior [relation] between cause and effect—that indeed is the illumination, the revelation, of non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>)—that is the meaning.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.22
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.22

children.text: itaśca na jāyate kiñcit, yajjāyamānaṃ vastu-
children.translated_text: Moreover, nothing is born—for a thing that appears to be born—

children.text: svato vā parato vāpi na kiñcid vastu jāyate /
children.translated_text: Neither from itself nor from another does any entity come into being;

children.text: sad asat sadasad vāpi na kiñcid vastu jāyate // MandUpK_4.22 //
children.translated_text: Neither as existent, nor as non-existent, nor as both existent and non-existent does any entity come into being. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.22 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.22
svataḥ parata ubhayato vā sadasatsadasadvā na jāyate na tasya kenacidapi prakāreṇa janma saṃbhavati /
na tāvatsvayamevāpariniṣpannātsvataḥ svarūpātsvayameva jāyate yathā ghaṭastasmādeva ghaṭāt /
nāpi parato 'nyasmādanyo yathā ghaṭātpaṭaḥ paṭātpaṭāntaram /
tathā nobhayataḥ, virodhāt; yathā ghaṭapaṭābhyāṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭo vā na jāyate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.22: From itself, from another, from both, or as existent, non-existent, or both—it is not born; its birth is not possible in any manner whatsoever. First, it is not born from itself—from its own unaccomplished form, by itself—as a pot [cannot be born] from that very pot. Nor from another—as one different from another, as a cloth from a pot, or a second cloth from a cloth. Nor from both, due to the contradiction—just as a pot or cloth is not born from [both] a pot and cloth [together].

children.text:
nanu mṛdo ghaṭo jāyate pituśca putraḥ /
satyam, asti jāyata iti pratyayaḥ śabdaśca mūḍhānām /
tāveva śabdapratyayau vivekibhiḥ parīkṣyete kiṃ satyameva tāvuta mṛṣeti /
yāvatā parīkṣyamāṇe śabdapratyaviṣayaṃ vastu ghaṭaputrādilakṣaṇaṃ śabdamātrameva tat /
"vācārambhaṇam"(chā.u.6 / 1 / 4) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: But surely a pot is born from clay, and a son from a father! True—there exists the cognition and the word 'is born' for the deluded. Those very cognitions and words are examined by the discriminating: are they real or false? To the extent that the thing—the object of the word and cognition, characterized as pot, son, and the like—when examined, is nothing but a mere word. [This is established] from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Modification is merely a name, a verbal handle' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.1.4).

children.text:
saccenna jāyate sattvānmṛtpitrādivad /
yadyasattathāpi na jāyate 'sattvādeva śaśaviṣāṇādivat /
atha sadasattathāpi na jāyate viruddhasyaikasyāsaṃbhavāt /
ato na kiñcadvastu jāyata iti siddham /
children.translated_text: If [the entity] is existent, it is not born [anew], because it already exists—like clay, father, and the like. If it is non-existent, even so it is not born, precisely because it is non-existent—like a hare's horn and the like. If it is both existent and non-existent, even so it is not born, because a single thing having contradictory [natures] is impossible. Therefore, it is established that no entity whatsoever is born.

children.text: yeṣāṃ punarjanireva jāyata iti kriyākārakaphalaikatvam abhyupagamyate kṣaṇikatvaṃ ca vastunaḥ, te dūrata eva nyāyāpetāḥ /
children.translated_text: As for those who accept that birth itself is what is born—[maintaining] the identity of action, agent, and result, and the momentariness of things—they are far removed from logical propriety.

children.text: idamitthamityavadhāraṇakṣaṇāntarānavasthānādananubhūtasya smṛtyanupapatteśca //22//
children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of the thing persisting at the next moment [after its ascertainment as] 'this is such,' and because of the impossibility of memory of what has not been experienced. ||22||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.23
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.23

children.text:
kiṃ ca hetuphalayoranāditvamabhyupagacchatā tvayā balāddhetuphalayorajanmaivābhyupagataṃ syāt /
tatkatham?
children.translated_text: Moreover, in accepting the beginninglessness of cause and effect, you have virtually been forced to accept the very non-origination of cause and effect. How so?

children.text: hetur na jāyate 'nādeḥ phalaṃ cāpi svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The cause is not born from [an effect that has] no beginning; and the effect too, by its very nature;

children.text: ādir na vidyate yasya tasya hy ādir na vidyate // MandUpK_4.23 //
children.translated_text: That which has no beginning—for that indeed no beginning is found. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.23 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.23
anāderādirahitātphalāddheturna jāyate /
na hyanutpannādanādeḥ phalāddhetorjanmeṣyate tvayā /
phalaṃ cādirahitādanāderhetorajātsvabhāvata eva nirnimittaṃ jāyata iti nābhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.23: From the effect that has no beginning—that is, that lacks a beginning—the cause is not born. For you would not maintain that the cause is born from an effect that is unoriginated and beginningless. And the effect is not accepted as arising without cause, spontaneously, from a cause that lacks a beginning and is unborn by nature.

children.text: tasmādanāditvamabhyupagacchatā tvayā hetuphalayorajanmāvābhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in accepting the beginninglessness [of the series], you have virtually accepted the non-origination of cause and effect.

children.text: yasmādādiḥ kāraṇaṃ na vidyate yasya loke tasya hyādiḥ pūrvoktā jātirna vidyate /
children.translated_text: For that whose beginning—whose cause—is not found in the world, for that indeed no beginning—no birth as previously described—is found.

children.text: kāraṇavata eva hyādirabhyupagamyate nākāraṇavataḥ //23//
children.translated_text: For only that which has a cause is accepted as having a beginning, not that which has no cause. ||23||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.24
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.24

children.text: uktasyaivārthasya dṛḍhīkaraṇacikīrṣayā punarākṣipati-
children.translated_text: With the desire to reinforce the very point already made, he raises an objection again—

children.text: prajñapteḥ sanimittatvam anyathā dvayanāśataḥ /
children.translated_text: Cognition (<s>prajñapti</s>) has an object (<s>sanimittatva</s>); otherwise, there would be the destruction of duality;

children.text: saṃkleśasyopalabdheś ca paratantrāstitā matā // MandUpK_4.24 //
children.translated_text: From the perception of affliction, the existence of the dependent [external reality] (<s>paratantra</s>) is held. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.24 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.24
prajñānaṃ prajñaptiḥ śabdādipratītistasyāḥ sanimittatvam; nimittaṃ kāraṇaṃ viṣaya ityetatsannimittatvaṃ saviṣatvaṃ svātmavyatiriktaviṣayatetyetat pratijānīmahe /
na hi nirviṣayā prajñaptiḥ śabdādipratītiḥ syāt, tasyāḥ sanimittatvāt /
anyathā nirviṣayatve śabdasparśanīlapītalohitādipratyayavaicitryasya dvayasya nāśato nāśo 'bhāvaḥ prasajyetetyarthaḥ /
na ca pratyayavaicitryasya dvayasyābhāvo 'sti pratyakṣatvāt /
ataḥ pratyavaicitryasya dvayasya darśānāt, pareṣāṃ tantraṃ paratantramityanyaśāstram, tasya paratantrasya paratantrāśrayasya bāhyārthasya jñānavyatiriktasyāsthitā matābhipretā /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.24: <s>Prajñapti</s> (cognition) means the awareness of sound and the like. Its having an object (<s>sanimittatva</s>)—the object, the cause, the content—this objectivity means having content other than its own self. We assert this. For cognition—the awareness of sound and the like—cannot be without an object, since it has an object. Otherwise—in the absence of an object—the destruction, the non-existence, of duality, of the variety of cognitions such as sound, touch, blue, yellow, red, and the like, would follow—that is the meaning. But the non-existence of the duality, the variety of cognitions, does not obtain, since it is directly perceived. Therefore, from the observation of the duality—the variety of cognitions—the <s>paratantra</s> (the dependent reality), [belonging to] the other system (<s>paraṃ tantram</s>), meaning the other school's doctrine—the existence of the external object, the locus of the dependent [reality], which is distinct from consciousness, is held to be intended.

children.text:
na hi prajñapteḥ prakāśamātrasvarūpāyā nīlapītādibāhyālambanavaicitryamantareṇa svabhāvabhedenaiva vaicitryaṃ saṃbhavati /
sphaṭikasyeva nīlādyupādhyāśrayairvinā vaicitryaṃ na ghaṭata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is not possible that <s>prajñapti</s> (cognition), whose essential nature is mere luminosity, could have variety through its own essential differentiation, without the variety of external supports such as blue, yellow, and the like—just as a crystal cannot have variety without the supports of blue and other [color-reflecting surfaces]—this is the purport.

children.text:
itaśca paratantrāśrayasya bāhyārthasya jñānavyatiriktasyāstitā /
saṃkleśanaṃ saṃkleśo duḥkhamityarthaḥ /
upalabhyate hyagnidāhādinimittaṃ duḥkham /
yadyagnyādibāhyaṃ dāhādinimittaṃ vijñānavyatiriktaṃ na syāttato dāhādiduḥkhaṃ nopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: If the external cause of burning and the like—fire and the like, distinct from consciousness—did not exist, then the suffering of burning and the like would not be perceived.

children.text: upalabhyate tu /
children.translated_text: But it is perceived.

children.text: atastena manyamahe 'sti bāhyor'tha iti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, on this basis we hold that the external object exists.

children.text: na hi vijñānamātre saṃklośo yuktaḥ, anyatrādarśanādityabhiprāyaḥ //24//
children.translated_text: For in mere consciousness alone, affliction is not reasonable, since it is not observed elsewhere [i.e., without an external cause]—this is the purport. ||24||

Moreover, there is the existence of the external object distinct from consciousness, which is the locus of the dependent [reality]. '<s>Saṃkleśa</s>' means affliction—that is, suffering. For suffering caused by fire-burning and the like is perceived.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.25
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.25

children.text: atrocyate-
children.translated_text: To this it is replied—

children.text: prajñapteḥ sanimittatvam iṣyate yuktidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: The objectivity of cognition is accepted from the standpoint of reasoning;

children.text: nimittasyānimittatvam iṣyate bhūtadarśanāt // MandUpK_4.25 //
children.translated_text: But the objectlessness of the object is accepted from the standpoint of ultimate reality (<s>bhūtadarśana</s>). || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.25 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.25
bāḍhamevaṃ prajñapteḥ sanimittatvaṃ dvayasaṃkleśopalabdhiyuktidarśanādiṣyate tvayā /
sthirībhava tāvattvaṃ yuktidarśanaṃ vastunastathātvābhyupagame kāraṇamityatra /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.25: Indeed, the objectivity of cognition is accepted by you from the standpoint of reasoning based on duality, affliction, and perception. Be steady, then, in this: that the standpoint of reasoning is the ground for accepting the thingness of things.

children.text: brūhi kiṃ tata iti /
children.translated_text: Tell me—what follows from that?

children.text:
ucyate /
nimittasya prajñaptyālambanābhimatasya ghaṭāderanimittatvamanālambanatvaṃ vaicitryāhetutvamiṣyate 'smābhiḥ /
katham? bhūtadarśanātparamārthadarśanādityetat /
na hi ghaṭo yathābhūtamṛdrūpadarśane sati tadvyatirekeṇāsti, yathāśvānmahiṣaḥ paṭo vā tantuvyatirekeṇa, tantavaścāṃśuvyatirekeṇetyevamuttarottara bhūtadarśana āśabdapratyayanirodhānnaiva nimittamupalabhāmaha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is replied: the objectlessness of the object—the supposed support of cognition, such as pot and the like—meaning its being without support, without being the cause of variety, is accepted by us. How? From the standpoint of ultimate reality (<s>bhūtadarśana</s>)—that is, from the perception of things as they truly are. For indeed, a pot does not exist apart from clay when clay is seen as it truly is—just as a buffalo [does not exist] apart from a horse, or a cloth apart from threads, or threads apart from fibers. Thus, proceeding to ever more ultimate levels of reality, until the cessation of words and cognitions, we find no object at all—that is the meaning.

children.text: athavā bhūtadarśanādbāhyārthasyānimittatvamiṣyate, rajjvādāviva sarpāderityarthaḥ /
bhrāntidarśanaviṣayatvācca nimittasyānimittatvaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: And because the object is the domain of erroneous perception, the object would be objectless.

children.text: tadabhāve 'bhāvān na hi suṣuptasamāhitamuktānāṃ bhrāntidarśanābhāva ātmavyatirikto bāhyor'tha upalabhyate /
children.translated_text: In its absence—in the absence [of error]—no external object distinct from the Self is perceived for those in deep sleep, in meditative absorption (<s>samāhita</s>), or the liberated, where erroneous perception is absent.

children.text: na hyunmattāvagataṃ vastvanunmattairapi tathābhūtaṃ gamyate /
children.translated_text: For indeed, what is apprehended by the deluded is not apprehended as such by the non-deluded.

children.text: etena dvayadarśanaṃ saṃkleśopalabdhiśca pratyuktā //25//
children.translated_text: By this, the [arguments from] duality-perception and affliction-perception are answered. ||25||
Alternatively, the objectlessness of the external object is accepted from the standpoint of ultimate reality—just as a snake [is objectless] upon a rope and the like—that is the meaning.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.26
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.26

children.text: yasmānnāsti bāhyaṃ nimittamataḥ-
children.translated_text: Since there is no external object, therefore—

children.text: cittaṃ na saṃspṛśaty arthaṃ nārthābhāsaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The mind does not touch an object, nor an appearance of an object either;

children.text: abhūto hi yataś cārtho nārthābhāsas tataḥ pṛthak // MandUpK_4.26 //
children.translated_text: For the object is indeed unreal, and the appearance of the object is not separate [from the mind]. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.26 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.26
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.26:

children.text: cittaṃ na spṛśatyarthaṃ bāhyālambanaviṣayam, nāpyarthābhāsaṃ cittatvātsvapnacittavat /
children.translated_text: The mind does not touch an object—an external support—nor an appearance of an object, because it is consciousness, like the mind in dream.

children.text: abhūto hi jāgarite 'pi svapnārthavadeva bāhyaḥ śabdādyartho yata uktahetutvācca /
children.translated_text: For even in the waking state, the external object of sound and the like is unreal, just like a dream-object, and because of the reasons already stated.

children.text: nāpyarthābhāsaścittātpṛthakcittameva hi ghaṭādyarthavadavabhāsate yathā svapne //26//
children.translated_text: Nor is the appearance of an object separate from the mind—for the mind itself appears as pot-objects and the like, just as in dream. ||26||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.27
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.27

children.text:
nanu viparyāsastarhyasati ghaṭādau ghaṭādyābhāsatā cittasya /
tathā ca satyaviparyāsaḥ kvacidvaktavya iti /
atrocyate-
children.translated_text: But then, there would be error (<s>viparyāsa</s>)—the mind appearing as pot and the like when pot and the like do not [really] exist. And if so, some veridical [cognition] must be posited in contrast [to the error]. To this it is said—

children.text: nimittaṃ na sadā cittaṃ saṃspṛśaty adhvasu triṣu /
children.translated_text: The mind never touches an object in the three periods of time;

children.text: animitto viparyāsaḥ kathaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.27 //
children.translated_text: How can there be error for it when there is no [real] object? || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.27 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.27
nimittaṃ viṣayamatītānāgatavartamānādhvasu triṣvapi sadā cittaṃ na spṛśedeva hi /
yadi hi kvacit saṃspṛśet sa aviparyāsaḥ paramārtha iti /
atastadapekṣayāsati ghaṭe ghaṭādyābhāsatā viparyāsaḥ syānna tu tadasti kadācidapi cittasyārthasaṃsparśanam /
tasmādanimitto viparyāsaḥ kathaṃ tasya cittasya bhaviṣyati; na kathañcidviparyāso 'stītyabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.27: The mind never touches an object—a content—in any of the three periods of time: past, future, or present. For if it were to touch [an object] at some time, that would be the non-error, the ultimate reality; and in contrast to that, the appearance of pot and the like in the absence of a pot would be error. But that [contact with an object] never exists at any time for the mind. Therefore, how would there be error for that mind without [a real] object? There is no error whatsoever—this is the purport.

children.text: ayameva hi svabhāvaścittasya yadutāsati nimitte ghaṭādau tadvadavabhāsanam //27//
children.translated_text: For this is the very nature of the mind: to appear as pot and the like in the absence of a [real] object [such as] pot and the like. ||27||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.28
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.28

children.text:
prajñapteḥ sanimittatvamityādyetadantaṃ vijñānavādino bauddhastha vacanaṃ bāhyārthavādipakṣapratiṣedhaparamācāryeṇānumoditam /
tadeva hetuṃ kṛtvā tatpakṣapratiṣedhāya tadidamucyate-
children.translated_text: [The argument] from 'cognition has an object' up to this point is the statement of the <s>Vijñānavādin</s> (consciousness-only) Buddhists, aimed at negating the position of the external-object proponents, which was endorsed by the teacher [<s>Gauḍapāda</s>]. Now, taking that very [argument] as the basis, for the purpose of negating that [Buddhist] position too, this is said—

children.text: tasmān na jāyate cittaṃ cittadṛśyaṃ na jāyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mind is not born, and what is seen by the mind is not born;

children.text: tasya paśyanti ye jātiṃ khe vai paśyanti te padam // MandUpK_4.28 //
children.translated_text: Those who see its birth see indeed a footprint in the sky. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.28 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.28
yasmādasatyeva ghaṭādau ghaṭādyābhāsatā cittasya vijñānavādinābhyupagatā tadanumoditam asmābhirapi bhūtadarśanāt, tasmāttasyāpi cittasya jāyamānāvabhāsatāsatyeva janmani yuktā bhavitumityato na jāyate cittam, yathā cittadṛśyaṃ na jāyate /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.28: Since the <s>Vijñānavādin</s> has accepted that the mind's appearing as pot and the like when pot and the like do not truly exist—and we too have endorsed this from the standpoint of ultimate reality—therefore, even for that mind itself, since it appears as being born when its birth is unreal, it is reasonable [to conclude that] the mind is not born—just as what is seen by the mind is not born.

children.text: atastasya cittasya ye jātiṃ paśyanti vijñānavādinaḥ kṣaṇikatvaduḥkhitvaśūnyatvānātmatvādi ca, tenaiva cittena cittasvarūpaṃ draṣṭumaśakyaṃ paśyantaḥ khe vai paśyanti te padaṃ pakṣyādīnām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who see the birth of that mind—the <s>Vijñānavādins</s> who see its momentariness, suffering-nature, voidness, non-self nature, and the like—seeing the nature of mind through that very mind, which is impossible—they see indeed a footprint in the sky, [a footprint] of birds and the like.

children.text: ata itarebhyo 'pi dvaitibhyo 'tyantasāhasikā ityartho ye 'pi śūnyavādinaḥ paśyanta eva sarvaśūnyatāṃ svadarśanasyāpi śūnyatāṃ svadarśanasyāpi śūnyatāṃ pratijānate te tato 'pi sāhasikatarāḥ khaṃ muṣṭināpi jighṛkṣanti //28//
children.translated_text: Therefore, they are even more extremely audacious than other dualists—this is the meaning. As for the <s>Śūnyavādins</s> (voidness-proponents) who, while seeing, assert the total voidness of everything, including the voidness of their own view—they are even more audacious still; they wish to grasp the sky with their fist! ||28||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.29
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.29

children.text: uktairhetubhirajamekaṃ brahmeti siddhaṃ yatpunarādau pratijñātaṃ tatphalopasaṃhārārthoyaṃ ślokaḥ-
children.translated_text: Through the reasons stated, it has been established that <s>Brahman</s> is unborn and one. The following verse serves to conclude with the result of what was proposed at the beginning—

children.text: ajātaṃ jāyate yasmād ajātiḥ prakṛtis tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the unborn appears to be born, therefore non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) is its nature (<s>prakṛti</s>);

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathañcid bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.29 //
children.translated_text: A change from one's nature will never occur in any way. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.29 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.29
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.29:

children.text: ajātaṃ yaccittaṃ brahmaiva jāyata iti vādibhiḥ parikalpyate tadajātaṃ jāyate yasmādajātiḥ prakṛtistasya /
children.translated_text: The unborn mind, which is <s>Brahman</s> itself, is imagined by disputants as 'being born.' That unborn [mind] appears to be born—since non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) is its nature.

children.text: tatastasmādajātarūpāyāḥ prakṛteranyathābhāvo janma na kathañcidbhaviṣyati //29//
children.translated_text: Therefore, from its nature that is of the form of the unborn, a change—birth—will never occur in any way. ||29||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.30
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.30

children.text: ayaṃ cāpara ātmanaḥ saṃsāramokṣayoḥ paramārthasadbhāvavādināṃ doṣa ucyate-
children.translated_text: And this is another fault attributed to those who maintain the ultimate reality of both <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) of the Self—

children.text: anāder antavattvaṃ ca saṃsārasya na setsyati /
children.translated_text: The finitude of the beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> will not be established;

children.text: anantatā cādimato mokṣasya na bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.30 //
children.translated_text: And the infinity of <s>mokṣa</s> that has a beginning will not obtain. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.30 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.30
anāderatītakoṭirahitasya saṃsārasyāntavattvaṃ samāptirna setsyati yuktitaḥ siddhiṃ nopayāsyati /
na hyanādiḥ sannantavānkaścitpadārtho dṛṣṭo loke /
bījāṅkurasaṃbandhanairantaryavicchedo iṣṭa iti cet, nai7kavastvabhāvenāpoditvāt /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.30: The finitude — the termination — of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), which is beginningless, having no prior limit, will not be established through reasoning, will not attain proof. For nothing in the world that is beginningless is observed to have an end. If [one argues that] an unbroken continuity of seed-and-sprout relation is accepted — [the reply is:] that is refuted by the non-existence of any single [ultimately real] entity.

children.text: tathānantatāpi vijñānaprāptikālaprabhavasya mokṣasyādimato na bhaviṣyati, ghaṭādiṣvadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the infinitude of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which has a beginning — arising at the time of the attainment of knowledge — will not hold, since it is not observed in pots and the like [which, having a beginning, also have an end].

children.text: ghacādivināśavadavastutvādadoṣa iti cet, tathā ca mokṣasya paramārthasadbhāvapratijñāhāniḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one says] there is no fault since, like the destruction of a pot, [<s>mokṣa</s>] is non-substantial — then [the consequence is] the abandonment of the claim that <s>mokṣa</s> has ultimate real existence.

children.text: asattvādeva śaśaviṣāṇasyevādimattvābhāvaśca //30//
children.translated_text: And because it is non-existent, like a hare's horn, the absence of a beginning [for <s>mokṣa</s>] would also follow. || 30 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.31-32
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.31-32

children.text: ādāvante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā /
children.translated_text: What does not exist at the beginning and at the end, is likewise [non-existent] in the present too.

children.text: vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo 'vitathā iva lakṣitāḥ // MandUpK_4.31 //
children.translated_text: Though similar to unreal things, they are regarded as if they were real. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.31 ||

children.text: saprayojanatā teṣāṃ svapne vipratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Their purposefulness is contradicted in dream;

children.text: tasmād ādyantavattvena mithyaiva khalu te smṛtāḥ // MandUpK_4.32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by virtue of having a beginning and an end, they are certainly considered false. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.32 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.31-32
vaitathye kṛtavyākhyānau ślokāviha saṃsāramokṣābhāvaprasaṅgena paṭhitau //31-32 //
children.translated_text: These two verses, which have been explained in the <s>Vaitathya</s> [chapter], are cited here in connection with the [discussion of the] non-existence of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>mokṣa</s>. || 31-32 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.31-32:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.33
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.33

children.text: sarve dharmā mṛṣā svapne kāyasyāntanidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: All phenomena (<s>dharmas</s>) are false in dream, as demonstrated by [their occurrence] within the body;

children.text: saṃvṛtte 'smin pradeśe vai bhūtānāṃ darśanaṃ kutaḥ // MandUpK_4.33 //
children.translated_text: In this enclosed space, whence could the perception of beings come? || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.33 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.33
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.33:

children.text: nimittasyānimittatvamiṣyate bhūtadarśanādityayamarthaḥ prapañcyata etaiḥ ślokaiḥ //33//
children.translated_text: The meaning — that the cause is accepted as being uncaused, from the observation of [dream] beings — is elaborated through these verses. || 33 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.34
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.34

children.text: na yuktaṃ darśanaṃ gatvā kālasyāniyamād gatau /
children.translated_text: The perception [of going to distant places in dream] is not valid, like in waking — because there is no fixed rule of time in the going;

children.text: pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvas tasmin deśe na vidyate // MandUpK_4.34 //
children.translated_text: And indeed, upon awakening, everyone finds that they are not in that place. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.34 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.34
jāgarite gatyāgamanakālo niyato deśaḥ pramāṇato yastasyā niyamānniyamasyābhāvātsvapne na deśāntarāgamanamityarthaḥ //34//
children.translated_text: In waking, the time and distance of going and coming are fixed and measurable; because of the absence of such fixity in dream, there is no actual going to another place [in dream] — this is the meaning. || 34 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.34:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.35
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.35

children.text: mitrādyaiḥ saha saṃmantrya saṃbuddhau na prapadyate /
children.translated_text: Having deliberated with friends and others [in dream], upon awakening one does not find [those agreements];

children.text: gṛhītaṃ cāpi yat kiñcit pratibuddho na paśyati // MandUpK_4.35 //
children.translated_text: And whatever one has grasped [in dream], one does not see upon awakening. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.35 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.35
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.35:

children.text: mitrādyaiḥ saha saṃmantrya tadeva mantraṇaṃ pratibuddhau na prapadyate /
children.translated_text: Having deliberated with friends and others, that very deliberation is not found upon awakening.

children.text: gṛhītaṃ ca yatkiñciddhiraṇyādi na prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: And whatever one has grasped — gold and the like — one does not obtain [upon awakening].

children.text: ataśca na deśāntaraṃ gacchanti svapne //35//
children.translated_text: Therefore, one does not [actually] go to another place in dream. || 35 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.36
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.36

children.text: svapne cāvastukaḥ kāyaḥ pṛthag anyasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: And in dream, the body is unsubstantial, because another [body] is seen separately.

children.text: yathā kāyas tathā sarvaṃ cittadṛśyam avastukam // MandUpK_4.36 //
children.translated_text: Just as the [dream] body, so everything perceived by the mind is unsubstantial. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.36 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.36
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.36:

children.text: svapne cāṭandṛśyate yaḥ kāyaḥ sa avastukastato 'nyasya svāpadeśastasya pṛthakkāyāntarasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: The body that is seen in dream is unsubstantial, because another body — a body different from the sleeper's own — is seen separately.

children.text: yathā svapnadṛśyaḥ kāyo 'saṃstathā sarvaṃ cittadṛśyamavastukaṃ jāgarite 'pi cittadṛśyatvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the body seen in dream is unreal, so too everything perceived by the mind is unsubstantial — even in the waking state, because it is perceived by the mind — this is the meaning.

children.text: svapnasamatvādasajjāgaritamapīti prakaraṇārthaḥ //36//
children.translated_text: The purport of the section is: waking too is unreal, like dream. || 36 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.37
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.37

children.text: itaścāsatvaṃ jāgradvastunaḥ-
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the unreality of waking objects [is established as follows] —

children.text: grahaṇāj jāgaritavat taddhetuḥ svapna iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Because [the waking world] is grasped like waking, dream is held to be its effect;

children.text: tad dhetutvāt tu tasyaiva sajjāgaritam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.37 //
children.translated_text: But because it [dream] is its effect, the waking [world] is held to be real only in that [dream]. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.37 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.37
jāgaritavajjāgaritasye7va grahaṇādgrāhyagrāhakarūpeṇāsvapnasya tajjāgaritaṃ heturasya svapnasya sa svapnastaddhetujāgaritakāryamiṣyate /
taddhetutvājjāgaritakāryatvāttasyaiva svapnadṛśya eva sajjāgaritaṃ na tvanyeṣām /
yathā svapna ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.37: Because dream grasps [things] in the form of subject and object just like waking, that waking is the cause of this dream — that dream is held to be the effect of waking as its cause. Because it is its effect — because it is the effect of waking — the waking [state] is real only within that dream itself, not for others. The intention is: just as dream [is real only within dream].

children.text: yathā svapnaḥ svapnadṛśya eva sansādhāraṇavidyamānavastuvadavabhāsate tathā tatkāraṇatvātsādhāraṇavidyamānavastuvadavabhāsamānaṃ na tu sādhāraṇaṃ vidyamānavastu svapnavadevetyabhiprāyaḥ //37//
children.translated_text: Just as dream, though existing only in dream, appears like a commonly available real object, so too waking, being its cause, appears like a commonly available real object — but it is not a commonly available real thing, just like dream itself — this is the intention. || 37 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.38
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.38

children.text:
nanu svapnakāraṇatve 'pi jāgaritavastuno na svapnavadavastutvam /
atyantacalo hi svapno jāgaritaṃ tu sthiraṃ lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: But even if [the waking state] is the cause of dream, the waking object is not unsubstantial like dream. For dream is extremely unstable, whereas waking is observed to be stable.

children.text:
satyamevamavivekināṃ syāt /
vivekināṃ tu na kasyacidvastuna utpādaḥ prasiddhe 'taḥ-
children.translated_text: True, it would be so for the undiscriminating. But for the discriminating, the origination of any entity is not established. Therefore —

children.text: utpādasyāprasiddhatvād ajaṃ sarvam udāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: Since origination is not established, all things are declared to be unborn (<s>aja</s>).

children.text: na ca bhūtād abhūtasya saṃbhavo 'sti kathañcana // MandUpK_4.38 //
children.translated_text: And the arising of a non-existent thing from an existent [cause] is never possible in any way. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.38 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.38
aprasiddhatvādutpādasyātmaiva sarvamityajaṃ sarvamudāhṛtaṃ vedānteṣu"sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ"(mu.u.2 / 1 / 2) iti /
yadyapi manyase jāgaritāstato 'satsvapno jāyata iti tadasat /
children.translated_text: Even if you think that the unreal dream arises from the real waking [state] — that is not so.

children.text: na bhūtādvidyamānāda bhūtasyāsataḥ sambhavo 'sti loke /
children.translated_text: The arising of a non-existent thing from an existent [cause] does not occur in the world.

children.text: na hyasataḥ śaśaviṣāṇādeḥ sambhavo dṛṣṭaḥ kathañcidapi //38//
children.translated_text: For the arising of a non-existent thing like a hare's horn has never been observed in any way whatsoever. || 38 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.38: Since origination is not established, the Self alone is everything; therefore, all things are declared to be unborn in the <s>Vedāntas</s> (<s>Upaniṣads</s>) — 'Without exterior and interior, it is unborn' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2).

children.text: START MandUpK 4.39
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.39

children.text: nanūktaṃ tvayaiva svapno jāgaritakāryamiti tatkathamutpādo 'prasiddha ityucyate?
children.translated_text: But you yourself have said that dream is the effect of waking — so how can you say that origination is not established?

children.text: śṛṇu tatra yathā kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'smābhirabhipreta iti-
children.translated_text: Hear, then, in what sense the cause-and-effect relation is intended by us —

children.text: asaj jāgarite dṛṣṭvā svapne paśyati tanmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen what is unreal in waking, one, pervaded by that [impression], sees [the same] in dream;

children.text: asatsvapne 'pi dṛṣṭvā ca pratibuddhau na paśyati // MandUpK_4.39 //
children.translated_text: And having seen what is unreal in dream too, upon awakening one does not see it. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.39 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.39
asadavidyamānaṃ rajjusarpadvikalpitaṃ vastu jāgarite dṛṣṭvā tadbhāvabhāvitastanmayaḥ svapne 'pi jāgaritavadgrāhyagrāhakarūpeṇa vikalpayanpaśyati /
children.translated_text: Having seen an unreal, non-existent object — imagined like a rope-snake — in the waking state, one who is pervaded by that impression (<s>tanmaya</s>), in dream too, imagines [things] in the form of subject and object, just as in waking — one 'sees' [them].

children.text: tathāsatsvapne 'pi dṛṣṭvā ca pratibuddhau na paśyatyavikalpayan /
children.translated_text: Similarly, having seen what is unreal in dream too, upon awakening one does not see [it], not imagining [it].

children.text: ca śabdāttathā jāgarite 'pi dṛṣṭvā svapne na paśyati kadācidityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And by the word 'ca' (and): similarly, having seen [something] in waking, one sometimes does not see [it] in dream — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasmājjāgaritaṃ svapnaheturucyate na tu paramārthasaditi kṛtvā //39//
children.translated_text: Therefore, waking is called the cause of dream, but not as something ultimately real. || 39 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.39:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.40
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.40

children.text: paramārthatastu na kasyacitkenacidapi prakāreṇa kāryakāraṇabhāva upapadyate katham?-
children.translated_text: But in ultimate reality, the cause-and-effect relation does not hold for anything in any way whatsoever. How? —

children.text: nāsty asaddhetukam asat sadasaddhetukaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: A non-existent [thing] does not have a non-existent cause; nor [does] a real [thing] have an unreal cause, likewise;

children.text: sac ca saddhetukaṃ nāsti saddhetukam asat kutaḥ // MandUpK_4.40 //
children.translated_text: A real [thing] does not have a real cause either — whence, then, could a non-existent [thing] have a real cause? || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.40 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.40
nāstyasaddhetukamasacchaśaviṣāṇādi hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ yasyāsata eva svakusumādestadasaddhatukamasanna vidyate /
children.translated_text: A non-existent [thing] does not have a non-existent cause: a non-existent thing — a hare's horn and the like — being the cause of another non-existent thing — its own flower and the like — such [causation] does not exist.

children.text: tathā sadapi ghaṭādivastv asaddhetukaṃ śaśaviṣāṇādikāryaṃ nāsti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, a real thing — a pot and the like — does not have an unreal cause; nor is a hare's horn and the like the effect [of something real].

children.text: tathā sacca vidyamānaṃ ghaṭādi vidyamānaghaṭādivastvantarakāryaṃ nāsti /
children.translated_text: Similarly, a real thing — a pot and the like — is not the effect of another real thing — another [real] pot and the like.

children.text: satkāryamasatkuta eva sambhavati? na cānyaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ sambhavati śakyo vā kalpayitum? ato vivekināmasiddha eva kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ kasya cidityabhiprāyaḥ //40//
