children.translated_text: How then could a non-existent effect arise from a real [cause]? No other cause-and-effect relation is possible or conceivable. Therefore, the intention is that for the discriminating, the cause-and-effect relation is simply not established for anything. || 40 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.40:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.41
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.41

children.text: punarapi jāgratsvapnayorasatorapi kāryakāraṇabhāvāśaṅkāmapanayann āha-
children.translated_text: Once again, removing the suspicion of a cause-and-effect relation even between the unreal waking and dream, he says —

children.text: viparyāsād yathā jāgrad acintyān bhūtavat spṛśet /
children.translated_text: Just as in waking, through error, one contacts inconceivable [things] as if they were real,

children.text: tathā svapne viparyāsād dharmāṃs tatraiva paśyati // MandUpK_4.41 //
children.translated_text: So too in dream, through error, one sees phenomena there alone [in dream itself]. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.41 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.41

viparyāsādavivekato yathā jāgrajjāgarite 'cintyānbhāvānaśakyacintanīyān rajjusarpādīn bhūtavatparamārthavatspṛśanniva vikalpayedityarthaḥ kaścidyathā, tathā svapne viparyāsāddhastyādīndharmān paśyanniva vikalpayati; tatraiva paśyati na tu jāgaritādutpadyamānānityarthaḥ //41//
children.translated_text: Through error — through non-discrimination — just as someone in waking imagines inconceivable things — unthinkable things like a rope-snake — as if they were real, as if ultimately real, 'contacting' them, i.e., imagining — so too in dream, through error, one imagines — 'seeing' — phenomena like elephants and the like; one sees them there alone [in dream], not as arising from the waking state — this is the meaning. || 41 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.41:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.42
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.42

children.text: upalambhāt samācārād asti vastutvavādinām /
children.translated_text: Due to perception (<s>upalambha</s>) and practical behavior (<s>samācāra</s>), the proponents of the existence of real entities [argue that duality exists];

children.text: jātis tu deśitā buddhair ajātes trasatāṃ sadā // MandUpK_4.42 //
children.translated_text: But birth (<s>jāti</s>) is taught by the wise (<s>buddhas</s>) for those who are always frightened of the unborn (<s>ajāti</s>). || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.42 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.42
yāpi buddhairadvaitavādibhirjātirdeśitopadiṣṭā, upalambhanam upalambhastasmādupalabdherityarthaḥ, samācārādvarṇāśramādidharmasamācaraṇāt, tābhyāṃ hetubhyāmastivastutvavādinām asti vastubhūva ityevaṃ vadanaśīlānāṃ dṛḍhāgrahavatāṃ śraddadhānānāṃ mandavivekināmanarthepāyatvena sā deśitā jātiḥ /
tāṃ gṛhṇantu tāvat /
children.translated_text: Let them grasp that [teaching of birth] for now.

children.text: vedāntābhyāsināṃ tu svayamevājādvayātmaviṣayo viveko bhaviṣyatīti na tu paramārthabuddhyā /
children.translated_text: For those who practice <s>Vedānta</s>, the discrimination regarding the unborn, non-dual Self-reality will arise of its own accord — but [the teaching of birth is] not with the understanding that [birth is] ultimately real.

children.text: te hi śrotriyāḥ sthūlabuddhitvādajāter ajātivastunaḥ sadā trasyantyātmanāśaṃ manyamānā avivekina ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those learned ones (<s>śrotriyas</s>), being of coarse understanding, are always frightened of the unborn (<s>ajāti</s>) — of the unborn reality — thinking that the Self is annihilated, being undiscriminating — this is the meaning.

children.text: upāyaḥ sa avatārāyetyuktam //42//
children.translated_text: 'It is a means for introduction' — so it has been said. || 42 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.42: The birth (<s>jāti</s>) that has been taught — instructed — by the wise, the proponents of non-duality (<s>advaitavādins</s>), is taught because of perception (<s>upalambha</s>) — because things are perceived — and because of practical behavior (<s>samācāra</s>) — because of the observance of duties pertaining to <s>varṇas</s> (castes), <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), and the like. For these two reasons, that birth is taught as a means for leading those of firm [mistaken] conviction who say 'real entities exist' — the faithful but of dull discrimination — so that they may [eventually] reach the truth, since it serves to avert [the ultimate] harm.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.43
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.43

children.text: ajātes trasatāṃ teṣām upalambhād viyanti ye /
children.translated_text: For those who, frightened of the unborn, deviate due to perception [of duality],

children.text: jātidoṣā na setsyanti doṣo 'py alpo bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.43 //
children.translated_text: The defects of [the teaching of] birth will not be established; and even any defect will be slight. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.43 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.43
ye caivamupalambhātsamācarāccājāterajātivastunastrasanto 'stivastvityadvayādātmano viyanti viruddhaṃ yanti dvaitaṃ pratipadyanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, due to perception and practical behavior, being frightened of the unborn reality, deviate from the non-dual Self — go in the opposite direction, adopt duality — this is the meaning.

children.text: teṣāmajātestrasatāṃ śraddhadhānānāṃ sanmārgāvalambināṃ jātidoṣā jātyupalambhakṛtā doṣā na setsyanti siddhiṃ nopayāsyanti, vivekamārgapravṛttatvāt /
children.translated_text: For them — those frightened of the unborn, who are faithful and adhering to the right path — the defects of birth, the defects produced by the perception of birth, will not be established, will not attain fruition — because they have entered the path of discrimination.

children.text: yadyapi kaściddoṣaḥ syātso 'pyalpa eva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Even if there be some defect, it will be only slight.

children.text: samyagdarśanāpratipattihetuka ityarthaḥ //43//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: [it will be slight] because it is due to the non-attainment of right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>). || 43 ||
Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.43:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.44
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.44

children.text:
nanūpalambhasamācārayoḥ pramāṇatvādastyeva dvaitaṃ vastviti, na; upalambhasamācārayorvyabhicārāt /
kathaṃ vyabhicāra ityucyate-
children.translated_text: But [the objection is:] since perception and practical behavior are valid means of knowledge, duality as a real entity does exist. No — because perception and practical behavior are subject to deviation. How is the deviation? It is said —

children.text: upalambhāt samācārān māyāhastī yathocyate /
children.translated_text: Due to perception and practical behavior, a magical elephant (<s>māyāhastī</s>) is spoken of [as real];

children.text: upalambhāt samācārād asti vastu tathocyate // MandUpK_4.44 //
children.translated_text: Due to perception and practical behavior, [duality as] a real entity is similarly spoken of. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.44 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.44
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.44:

children.text: upalabhyate hi māyāhastī hastīva hastinamivātra samācaranti, bandhanārohaṇādihāstisambandhibhirdharmairhastīti cocyate 'sannapi yathā tathaivopalambhātsamācārāddvaitaṃ bhedarūpamasti vastvityucyate /
children.translated_text: A magical elephant (<s>māyāhastī</s>) is perceived like a [real] elephant; people conduct themselves toward it with behaviors appropriate to an elephant — tying, mounting, and the like; and it is spoken of as 'an elephant,' though it is unreal — just so, due to perception and practical behavior, duality in the form of difference is spoken of as 'a real entity.'

children.text: tasmānnopalambhasamācārau dvaitavastusadbhāve hetu bhavata ityabhiprāyaḥ //44//
children.translated_text: Therefore, perception and practical behavior cannot serve as proof for the real existence of duality — this is the intention. || 44 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.45
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.45

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ paramārthasadvastu yadāspadā jātyāhyasadbuddhaya ityāha-
children.translated_text: What then is the ultimately real entity, upon which the cognitions of birth and the like, though unreal, are based? He says —

children.text: jātyābhāsaṃ calābhāsaṃ vastvābhāsaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Appearing as birth (<s>jātyābhāsa</s>), appearing as movement (<s>calābhāsa</s>), appearing as substance (<s>vastvābhāsa</s>) — likewise,

children.text: ajācalam avastutvaṃ vijñānaṃ śāntam advayam // MandUpK_4.45 //
children.translated_text: [It is in reality] unborn, unmoving, non-substantial — consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), peaceful, non-dual. || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.45 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.45
ajāti sajjātivadavabhāsata iti jātyābhāsam /
tadyathā devadatto jāyata iti /
calābhāsaṃ calamivābhāsata iti /
yathā sa eva devadatto gacchatīti /
vastvābhāsaṃ vastu dravyaṃ dharmi tadvadavabhāsata iti vastvābhāsam /
yathā sa eva devadatto gauro dīrgha iti jāyate devadattaḥ spandate dīrgho gaura ityevamavabhāsate /
children.translated_text: 'That same <s>Devadatta</s> is fair, tall' — <s>Devadatta</s> is born, moves, is tall, is fair — thus it appears.

children.text: paramārthatastvajamacalamavastutvamadravyaṃ ca kiṃ tadevaṃprakāram? vijñānaṃ vijñaptiḥ /
children.translated_text: But in ultimate reality, it is unborn, unmoving, non-substantial, not a substance. What is this thing of such a nature? <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness, cognition).

children.text: jātyādirahitatvācchāntam /
children.translated_text: Because it is devoid of birth and the like, it is peaceful (<s>śānta</s>).

children.text: ata evādvayaṃ ca tadittarthaḥ //45//
children.translated_text: And for that very reason it is non-dual (<s>advaya</s>) — this is the meaning. || 45 ||

Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.45: Being unborn, it appears as if possessing birth — hence 'appearing as birth' (<s>jātyābhāsa</s>). For example, '<s>Devadatta</s> is born.' 'Appearing as movement' (<s>calābhāsa</s>) — it appears as if moving. For example, 'That same <s>Devadatta</s> goes.' 'Appearing as substance' (<s>vastvābhāsa</s>) — it appears as if it were a substance (<s>dravya</s>), a substratum of qualities. For example,

children.text: START MandUpK 4.46
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.46

children.text: evaṃ na jāyate cittam evaṃ dharmā ajāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the mind (<s>citta</s>) is not born; thus, phenomena (<s>dharmas</s>) are declared to be unborn.

children.text: evam eva vijānanto na patanti viparyaye // MandUpK_4.46 //
children.translated_text: Those who know precisely thus do not fall into error (<s>viparyaya</s>). || <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.46 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.46
evaṃ yathoktebhyo hetubhyo na jāyate cittamevaṃ dharmā ātmano 'jāḥ smṛtā brahmavidbhiḥ /
dharmā iti bahuvacanaṃ dehabhedānuvidhāyitvādadvayasyaivopacārataḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.46: Thus, for the reasons stated, the mind (<s>citta</s>) is not born; thus, the <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) of the Self are declared to be unborn by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. The plural 'dharmas' is used figuratively, because of conformity with the differentiation of bodies, although [the Self] is non-dual.

children.text: evameva yathoktaṃ vijñānaṃ jātyādirahitamadvayamātmatattvaṃ vijānantastyaktabāhyaiṣaṇāḥ punarnapatantyavidyādhvāntasāgare viparyaye /
children.translated_text: Those who know precisely thus — that <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), devoid of birth and the like, is the non-dual Self-reality as described — having abandoned all external desires, do not fall again into the ocean of the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — into error (<s>viparyaya</s>).

children.text: "tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ" (ī.u.7) ityādi mantravarṇāt //46//
children.translated_text: [As confirmed by] the mantra-text: 'What delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who sees oneness?' (<s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> 7). || 46 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.47
children.translated_text: BEGIN <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.47

children.text: yathoktaṃ paramārthadarśanaṃ prapañcayiṣyannāha-
children.translated_text: Wishing to elaborate on the perception of ultimate reality as stated, he says —

children.text: ṛjuvakrādikābhāsam alātaspanditaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a firebrand, when set in motion, appears as straight, curved, and so on,

children.text: grahaṇagrāhakābhāsaṃ vijñānaspanditaṃ tathā // MandUpK_4.47 //
children.translated_text: So too consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), when set in motion, appears as the grasped and the grasper. || MandUpK 4.47 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.47
yathā hi loka ṛjuvakrādiprakārābhāsamalātaspanditamulkācalanaṃ tathā grahaṇagrāhakābhāsaṃ viṣayiviṣayābhāsamityarthaḥ /
kiṃ tadvijñānaspanditam /
children.translated_text: What is that? It is the vibration of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).

children.text: spanditamiva spanditamavidyayā /
children.translated_text: It vibrates 'as it were' — that is, [it appears to vibrate] through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: na hyacasya vijñānasya spandanamasti /
children.translated_text: For in reality, consciousness, being unborn, has no vibration.

children.text: ajācalamiti hyuktam //47//
children.translated_text: For it has been said to be unborn and immovable. || 47 ||

MandUpKC_4.47
Just as in the world, the movement of a firebrand — a whirling torch — appears in the form of straight, curved, and other shapes, so too [consciousness] appears as the grasped and the grasper — that is, as object and subject. This is the meaning.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.48
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.48

children.text: aspandamānam alātam anābhāsam ajaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as the firebrand, when not in motion, is without appearances and unborn,

children.text: aspandamānaṃ vijñānam anābhāsam ajaṃ tathā // MandUpK_4.48 //
children.translated_text: So too consciousness, when not in motion, is without appearances and unborn. || MandUpK 4.48 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.48
aspandamānaṃ spandanavarjitaṃ tadevālātamṛjvādyākāreṇājāyamānamanābhāsamajaṃ yathā; tathāvidyayā spandamānamavidyoparame 'spandamānaṃ jātyādyākāreṇānābhāsamajamacalaṃ bhaviṣyitītyarthaḥ //48//
children.translated_text: When not in motion — that is, devoid of movement — that very firebrand, not being born in the form of straight shapes and the like, is without appearances and unborn; similarly, [consciousness,] which [appears to] vibrate through <s>avidyā</s>, upon the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, being not in motion, not appearing in the form of birth and the like — it will be without appearances, unborn, and immovable. This is the meaning. || 48 ||
MandUpKC_4.48

children.text: START MandUpK 4.49
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.49

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: alāte spandamāne vai nābhāsā anyato bhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the firebrand is in motion, indeed the appearances do not come from elsewhere;

children.text: na tato 'nyatra nispandān nālātaṃ praviśanti te // MandUpK_4.49 //
children.translated_text: Nor, from it when motionless, do they go elsewhere; nor do they enter the firebrand. || MandUpK 4.49 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.49
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.49

children.text: tasminnevālāte spandamāna ṛjuvakrādyābhāsā alātādanyataḥ kutaścidāgatyālāte naiva bhavantī7ti nānyatobhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: In that very firebrand, when it is in motion, the appearances of straight, curved, and other shapes do not come from somewhere else outside and then come to be in the firebrand — hence they are 'not from elsewhere' (<s>nānyatobhuvaḥ</s>).

children.text: na ca tasmānnispandādalātādanyatra nirgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor do they, from that motionless firebrand, go out to somewhere else.

children.text: na ca nispandamalātameva praviśanti te //49//
children.translated_text: Nor do they enter the motionless firebrand itself. || 49 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.50
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.50

children.text: kiṃ ca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: na nirgatā alātāt te dravyatvābhāvayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: They have not gone out from the firebrand, because of the impossibility of their being substances;

children.text: vijñāne 'pi tathaiva syur ābhāsasyāviśeṣataḥ // MandUpK_4.50 //
children.translated_text: The same applies to consciousness — because there is no difference in the [nature of] appearances. || MandUpK 4.50 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.50
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.50

children.text: na nirgatā alātātta ābhāsā gṛhādivaddravyatvābhāvayogato dravyasyabhāvo dravyatvam, tadabhāvo dravyatvābhāvaḥ, dravyatvābhāvayogato dravyatvābhāvayuktairvastutvābhāvādityarthaḥ, vastuno hi praveśādi sambhavati nāvastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: The appearances have not gone out from the firebrand — because of the impossibility of their being substances, like a house or the like. The absence of substance is the absence of substantiality; 'because of the impossibility of the absence of substantiality' means because of the absence of real entity-nature — for entry and the like are possible for a real thing, not for an unreal thing. This is the meaning.

children.text: vijñāno 'pi jātyādyābhāsāstathaiva syurābhāsasyāviśeṣatastulyatvāt //50//
children.translated_text: The appearances of birth and the like in consciousness too are the same — because there is no difference in the [nature of] appearances, that is, because they are alike. || 50 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.51-52
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.51-52

children.text: kathaṃ tulyatvamityāha-
children.translated_text: How are they alike? He says —

children.text: vijñāne spandamāne vai nābhāsā anyatobhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: When consciousness is in motion, indeed the appearances do not come from elsewhere;

children.text: na tato 'nyatra nispandān na vijñānaṃ viśanti te // MandUpK_4.51 //
children.translated_text: Nor, from it when motionless, do they go elsewhere; nor do they enter consciousness. || MandUpK 4.51 ||

children.text: na nirgatās te vijñānād dravyatvābhāvayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: They have not gone out from consciousness, because of the impossibility of their being substances;

children.text: kāryakāraṇatābhāvād yato 'cintyāḥ sadaiva te // MandUpK_4.52 //
children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of a cause-effect relationship, they are always inconceivable. || MandUpK 4.52 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.51-52
alātena samānaṃ sarvaṃ vijñānasya /
sadācalatvaṃ tu vijñānasya viśeṣaḥ /
jātyādyābhāsa vijñāne 'cale kiṅkṛtā ityāha /
kāryakāraṇatābhāvājjanyajanakatvānupapatterabhāvarūpatvādacintyāste yataḥ sadaiva /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_4.51-52
Everything regarding consciousness is the same as with the firebrand.
However, the special feature of consciousness is that it is always immovable.
What then produces the appearances of birth and the like in immovable consciousness? He says:
Because of the impossibility of a cause-effect relationship — because of the impossibility of being produced and producer — and because they are of the nature of non-existence, they are inconceivable always.

children.text: yathāsatsvṛjvādyābhāseṣv ṛjvādibuddhirdṛṣṭālātamātre tathāstveva jātyādiṣu vijñānamātre jātyādibuddhirmṛṣaiveti samudāyārthaḥ //51-52 //
children.translated_text: Just as when the straight and other appearances are unreal, the cognition of 'straight' and the like is [seen to be] based on the mere [movement of the] firebrand — so too, the cognition of birth and the like, [based] on mere consciousness, regarding [the appearances of] birth and the like, is indeed false. This is the combined meaning. || 51-52 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.53
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.53

children.text: ajamekamātmatattvamiti sthitaṃ tatra yairapi kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ kalpyate teṣām /
children.translated_text: It is established that the reality of the <s>Ātman</s> is unborn and one. Now, for those who even so imagine a cause-effect relationship —

children.text: dravyaṃ dravyasya hetuḥ syād anyad anyasya caiva hi /
children.translated_text: A substance would be the cause of [another] substance, and one thing of another indeed;

children.text: dravyatvam anyabhāvo vā dharmāṇāṃ nopapadyate // MandUpK_4.53 //
children.translated_text: But substantiality or otherness of [these] <s>dharmas</s> (entities) is not tenable. || MandUpK 4.53 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.53
dravyaṃ dravyasyānyasyānyaddhetuḥ kāraṇaṃ syānna tu tasyaiva tat /
children.translated_text: A substance would be the cause of another substance, of something different — but not of that very thing itself.

children.text: nāpyadravyaṃ kasyacitkāraṇaṃ svatantraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ loke /
children.translated_text: Nor is a non-substance independently seen in the world as a cause of anything.

children.text: na ca dravyatvaṃ dharmāṇāmātmānāmupapadyate 'nyatvaṃ vā kutaścidyenānyasya kāraṇatvaṃ kāryatvaṃ vā pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: And substantiality of these <s>dharmas</s> — of these selves — is not tenable, nor is otherness from anything by which one could become the cause or effect of another.

children.text: ato 'dravyatvādananyatvācca na kasyacitkāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ vātmetyarthaḥ //53//
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the absence of substantiality and because of the absence of otherness, nothing is the effect or cause of the <s>Ātman</s>. This is the meaning. || 53 ||
MandUpKC_4.53

children.text: START MandUpK 4.54
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.54

children.text: evaṃ na cittajā dharmāś cittaṃ vāpi na dharmajam /
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>dharmas</s> (entities) are not born from the mind (<s>citta</s>), nor is the mind born from <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: evaṃ hetuphalājātiṃ praviśanti manīṣiṇaḥ // MandUpK_4.54 //
children.translated_text: Thus the wise enter into the non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) of cause and effect. || MandUpK 4.54 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.54
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.54

children.text: evaṃ yathoktebhyo hetubhya ātmavijñānasvarūpameva cittamiti na cittajā bāhyadharmā nāpi bāhyadharmajaṃ cittam /
children.translated_text: Thus, for the reasons stated — since the mind is nothing but the nature of the consciousness of the <s>Ātman</s> — external <s>dharmas</s> are not born from the mind, nor is the mind born from external <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: vijñānasvarūpābhāsamātratvātsarvadharmāṇām /
children.translated_text: Because all <s>dharmas</s> are merely appearances of the nature of consciousness.

children.text: evaṃ na hetoḥ phalaṃ jāyate nāpi phalāddheturiti hetuphalayorajātiṃ hetuphalājātiṃ praviśantyadhyavasyanty ātmani hetuphalayorabhāvameva pratipadyante brahmavida ityarthaḥ //54//
children.translated_text: Thus, an effect is not born from a cause, nor a cause from an effect — entering into the non-origination of cause and effect (<s>hetuphalājāti</s>), the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> ascertain — that is, they understand — the very non-existence of cause and effect in the <s>Ātman</s>. This is the meaning. || 54 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.55
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.55

children.text: ye punarhetuphalayorabhiniviṣṭāsteṣāṃ kiṃ syādityucyate- dharmādharmākhyasya hetorahaṃ kartā mama dharmādharmau tatphalaṃ kālāntare kvacitprāṇinikāye jāto bhokṣya iti-
children.translated_text: But for those who are fixated on cause and effect, what would happen? It is said: [thinking] 'I am the doer of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are mine; their fruit [I shall enjoy]; at some future time, born in some species of beings, I shall enjoy [the fruits]' —

children.text: yāvad dhetuphalāveśas tāvad dhetuphalodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as there is fixation on cause and effect, so long is there the arising of cause and effect;

children.text: kṣīṇe hetuphalāveśe nāsti hetuphalodbhavaḥ // MandUpK_4.55 //
children.translated_text: When the fixation on cause and effect is exhausted, there is no arising of cause and effect. || MandUpK 4.55 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.55
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.55

children.text: yāvaddhetuphalayorāveśo hetuphalāgraha ātnyadhyāropaṇaṃ taccittatetyarthaḥ,tāvaddhetuphalayorudbhavo dharmādharmayosattphalasya cānucchedena pravṛttirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as there is fixation on cause and effect — grasping of cause and effect, superimposition on the <s>Ātman</s>, which constitutes that [deluded] mind — so long is there the arising of cause and effect, meaning the uninterrupted continuation of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and their fruits. This is the meaning.

children.text: yadā punarmantrauṣadhivīryeṇeva grahāveśo yathoktādvaitadaśanenāvidyodbhūtahetuphalāveśo 'panīto bhavati tadā tasminkṣīṇe nāsti hetuphalodbhavaḥ //55//
children.translated_text: But when, just as possession by a spirit is removed through the power of mantras, herbs, and the like, the fixation on cause and effect — born of <s>avidyā</s> — is removed through the previously described vision of non-duality, then, when that is exhausted, there is no arising of cause and effect. || 55 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.56
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.56

children.text: yadi hetuphalodbhavastadā ko doṣa ityucyate-
children.translated_text: If there is the arising of cause and effect, what is the fault? It is said —

children.text: yāvad dhetuphalāveśaḥ saṃsāras tāvadāyataḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as there is fixation on cause and effect, so long does <s>saṃsāra</s> extend;

children.text: kṣīṇe hetuphalāveśe saṃsāraṃ na prapadyate // MandUpK_4.56 //
children.translated_text: When the fixation on cause and effect is exhausted, one does not enter <s>saṃsāra</s>. || MandUpK 4.56 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.56
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.56

children.text: yāvatsamyagdarśanena hetuphalāveśo na nivartate 'kṣīṇaḥ saṃsārastāvadāyato dīrgho bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as the fixation on cause and effect is not removed by right vision — that is, is not exhausted — <s>saṃsāra</s> extends, that is, becomes long. This is the meaning.

children.text: kṣīṇe punarhetiphalāveśe saṃsāraṃ na prapadyate kāraṇābhāvāt //56//
children.translated_text: But when the fixation on cause and effect is exhausted, one does not enter <s>saṃsāra</s>, because of the absence of its cause. || 56 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.57
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.57

children.text: nanvajādātmano 'nyannāstyeva tatkathaṃ hetuphalayoḥ saṃsārasya cotpattivināśāvucyete tvayā?
children.translated_text: But if nothing other than the unborn <s>Ātman</s> exists at all, then how can you speak of the origination and destruction of cause and effect and of <s>saṃsāra</s>?

children.text: śṛṇu-
children.translated_text: Listen —

children.text: saṃvṛtyā jāyate sarvaṃ śāśvataṃ nāsti tena vai /
children.translated_text: From the conventional standpoint (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), everything is born; nothing is eternal by that [standpoint];

children.text: sadbhāvena hy ajaṃ sarvam ucchedas tena nāsti vai // MandUpK_4.57 //
children.translated_text: From the standpoint of ultimate reality (<s>sadbhāva</s>), everything is unborn — hence there is no annihilation. || MandUpK 4.57 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.57
saṃvṛtyā saṃvaraṇaṃ saṃvṛtiravidyāviṣayo laukiko vyavahārastā saṃvṛtyā jāyate sarvam /
tenāvidyāviṣaye śāśvataṃ nityaṃ nāsti vai /
children.translated_text: Therefore, within the domain of <s>avidyā</s>, nothing is eternal or permanent.

children.text: ata utpattivināśalakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāra āyata ityucyate /
children.translated_text: Hence <s>saṃsāra</s>, characterized by origination and destruction, is said to be extended.

children.text: paramārthasadbhāvena tvajaṃ sarvamātmaiva yasmāt /
children.translated_text: But from the standpoint of ultimate reality (<s>sadbhāva</s>), everything is unborn — it is the <s>Ātman</s> alone.

children.text: ato jātyabhāvāducchedastena nāsti vai kasyaciddhetuphalāderityarthaḥ //57//
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the absence of birth, there is no annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>) of anything — of cause, effect, or anything else. This is the meaning. || 57 ||

MandUpKC_4.57
<s>Saṃvṛti</s> means concealment — the worldly transaction that is the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); from that conventional standpoint, everything is born.

children.text: START MandUpK 4.58
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.58

children.text: dharmā ya iti jāyante jāyante te na tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> (entities) that are said to be born — they are not born in reality;

children.text: janma māyopamaṃ teṣāṃ sā ca māyā na vidyate // MandUpK_4.58 //
children.translated_text: Their birth is like <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and that <s>māyā</s> too does not exist. || MandUpK 4.58 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.58
ye 'pyātmāno 'nye ca dharmā jāyanta iti kalpyante ta ityevaṃ prakārā yathoktā saṃvṛtinirdiśyata iti saṃvṛtyaiva dharmā jāyante; na te tattvataḥ paramārthatoya jāyante /
yatpunastatsaṃvṛtyā janma teṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ yathoktānāṃ yathā māyayā janma tathā tanmāyopamaṃ pratyetavyam /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_4.58
Those <s>dharmas</s> — both selves and other entities — that are imagined to be born: they, being of the nature described, as stated from the conventional standpoint — it is only from the conventional standpoint that <s>dharmas</s> are born; they are not born in reality (<s>tattvataḥ</s>), that is, in ultimate truth. And that birth, from the conventional standpoint, of those <s>dharmas</s> as described — just as birth by <s>māyā</s> — so that should be understood as being like <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: māyā nāma vastu tarhi? naivam; sā ca māyā na vidyate, māyetyavidyamānasyākhyetyabhiprāyaḥ //58//
children.translated_text: Is <s>māyā</s> then a real thing? Not at all — 'and that <s>māyā</s> does not exist.' The intended meaning is: <s>māyā</s> is just a name for what does not exist. || 58 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.59
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.59

children.text: kathaṃ māyopamaṃ teṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ janmetyāha-
children.translated_text: How is the birth of those <s>dharmas</s> like <s>māyā</s>? He says —

children.text: yathā māyāmayād bījāj jāyate tanmayoṅkuraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as from a seed that is produced by <s>māyā</s>, a sprout made of <s>māyā</s> is born —

children.text: nāsau nityo na cocchedī tadvad dharmeṣu yojanā // MandUpK_4.59 //
children.translated_text: That [sprout] is neither eternal nor annihilated — the same reasoning applies to [all] <s>dharmas</s>. || MandUpK 4.59 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.59

yathā māyāmayādbījājjāyate tanmayo māyāmayo 'ṅkuro nāsāṅkuro nityo na cocchedī vināśī vābhūtatvāttadvadeva dharmeṣu janmanāśādiyojanā yuktir na tu paramārthato dharmāṇāṃ janma nāśo vā yujyata ityarthaḥ //59//
children.translated_text: Just as from a seed made of <s>māyā</s>, a sprout made of <s>māyā</s> is born — that sprout is neither eternal nor annihilated, because it never [truly] existed — the same reasoning applies to [all] <s>dharmas</s> regarding birth, destruction, and the like; but the birth or destruction of <s>dharmas</s> in ultimate reality is not tenable. This is the meaning. || 59 ||
MandUpKC_4.59

children.text: START MandUpK 4.60
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.60

children.text: nājeṣu sarvadharmeṣu śāśvatāśāśvatābhidhā /
children.translated_text: With regard to all <s>dharmas</s> that are unborn, the designation 'eternal' or 'non-eternal' does not apply;

children.text: yatra varṇā na vartante vivekas tatra nocyate // MandUpK_4.60 //
children.translated_text: Where words (<s>varṇas</s>) do not operate, discrimination cannot be spoken of there. || MandUpK 4.60 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.60
paramārthatastvātmasvajeṣu nityaikarasavijñaptimātrasattākeṣu śāśvato 'śāśvata ita vā nābhidhā nābhidhānaṃ pravartata ityarthaḥ /
yatra yeṣu varṇyante yairarthāste varṇāṃ śabdā na pravartante 'bhidhātuṃ prakāśayituṃ na pravartanta ityarthaḥ /
idamevamiti viveko viviktatā tatra nityo 'nitya iti nocyate /
"yato vāco nivartante"(tai.u.2 / 4 / 1) iti śruteḥ //60//
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_4.60
In ultimate reality, with respect to [<s>dharmas</s>] that are unborn, whose existence is of the nature of the <s>Ātman</s> — being of the nature of mere eternal, uniform consciousness — the designation 'eternal' or 'non-eternal' does not operate, does not apply. This is the meaning.
Where — in which [<s>dharmas</s>] — <s>varṇas</s> (words), by which meanings are described, those words or sounds, do not operate — do not function to designate or illuminate. This is the meaning.
[Where there is] discrimination — 'this is such and such' — that discrimination, that distinctness — [whether] 'eternal' or 'non-eternal' — is not spoken of there.
As the <s>śruti</s> says: 'From which words turn back' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.1). || 60 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.61-62
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.61-62

children.text: yathā svapne dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ calati māyayā /
children.translated_text: Just as in dream, the mind (<s>citta</s>) moves with the appearance of duality through <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: tathā jāgrad dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ calati māyayā // MandUpK_4.61 //
children.translated_text: So too in waking, the mind moves with the appearance of duality through <s>māyā</s>. || MandUpK 4.61 ||

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ svapne na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is non-dual yet appears as duality in dream — of this there is no doubt;

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ tathā jāgran na saṃśayaḥ // MandUpK_4.62 //
children.translated_text: The mind is non-dual yet appears as duality in waking likewise — of this there is no doubt. || MandUpK 4.62 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.61-62
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.61-62

children.text: yatpunarvāggocaratvaṃ paramārthato 'dvayasya vijñānamātrasya tanmanasaḥ spandanamātraṃ na paramārthata iti /
children.translated_text: The fact that the non-dual [reality], which is mere consciousness, comes within the range of speech in ultimate reality — that is merely the vibration of the mind, not [anything] in ultimate reality.

children.text: uktārthau ślokau //61-62 //
children.translated_text: These two verses state what has already been explained. || 61-62 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.63
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.63

children.text: itaśca vāggocarasyābhāvo dvaitasya-
children.translated_text: From this further follows the non-existence of duality that comes within the range of speech —

children.text: svapnadṛk pracaran svapne dikṣu vai daśasu sthitān /
children.translated_text: The dreamer, wandering in the dream, sees living beings situated in the ten directions,

children.text: aṇḍajān svedajān vāpi jīvān paśyati yān sadā // MandUpK_4.63 //
children.translated_text: Whether born from eggs or born from sweat — those beings he always sees. || MandUpK 4.63 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.63
svapnānpaśyatīti svapnadṛkpracaranparyaṭansvapne svapnasthāne dikṣu vai daśasu sthitānvartamānāñjīvānprāṇino 'ṇḍajānsvedajānvā yānsadā paśyati //63//
children.translated_text: The dream-seer — one who sees dreams — wandering, moving about in the dream, in the dream-state, sees living beings — creatures — situated, existing in the ten directions, whether born from eggs or born from sweat — those he always sees. || 63 ||
MandUpKC_4.63

children.text: START MandUpK 4.64
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.64

children.text: yadyevaṃ tataḥ kim? ucyate-
children.translated_text: If so, then what [follows]? It is said —

children.text: svapnadṛkcittadṛśyās te na vidyante tataḥ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Those [beings], being perceived by the dream-seer's mind, do not exist apart from it;

children.text: tathā tad dṛśyam evedaṃ svapnadṛkcittam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.64 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, that which is perceived is indeed this — [it is] accepted as the mind of the dream-seer. || MandUpK 4.64 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.64
svapnadṛśaścittaṃ svapnadṛkcittaṃ tena dṛśyāste jīvāstatastasmātsvapnadṛkcittātpṛthaṅna vidyante na santītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings, perceived by the mind of the dream-seer — the dream-seer's mind — do not exist, do not have being, apart from that mind of the dream-seer. This is the meaning.

children.text: cittameva hyanekajīvādibhedākāreṇa vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: For the mind alone is imagined in the form of the manifold differentiation of beings and the like.

children.text: tathā tadapi svapnadṛkcittamidaṃ taddṛśyameva, tena svapnadṛśā dṛśyaṃ taddṛśyam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, that mind of the dream-seer too is that which is perceived — that which is seen by that dream-seer.

children.text: ataḥ svapnadṛgvyatirekeṇa cittaṃ nāma nāstītyarthaḥ //64//
children.translated_text: Therefore, apart from the dream-seer, there is nothing called 'mind.' This is the meaning. || 64 ||
MandUpKC_4.64

children.text: START MandUpK 4.65-66
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.65-66

children.text: carañ jāgarite jāgrad dikṣu vai daśasu sthitān /
children.translated_text: Moving about in the waking state, the waking person sees beings situated in the ten directions,

children.text: aṇḍajān svedajān vāpi jīvān paśyati yān sadā // MandUpK_4.65 //
children.translated_text: Whether born from eggs or born from sweat — those beings he always sees. || MandUpK 4.65 ||

children.text: jāgrac cittekṣaṇīyās te na vidyante tataḥ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Those [beings], being objects of the waking mind, do not exist apart from it;

children.text: tathā tad dṛśyam evedaṃ jāgrataś cittam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.66 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, that which is perceived is indeed this — [it is] accepted as the mind of the waking person. || MandUpK 4.66 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.65-66
children.translated_text: MandUpKC_4.65-66

children.text: jāgrato dṛśyā jīvāstaccittāvyatiriktāścittekṣaṇīyatvātsvapnadṛkcittekṣaṇīyajīvavat /
children.translated_text: The beings perceived by the waking person, not different from his mind, are [merely] objects of the mind — just as the beings that are objects of the dream-seer's mind.

children.text: tacca jīvekṣaṇātmakaṃ cittaṃ draṣṭuravyatiriktaṃ draṣṭudṛśyatvātsvapnacittavat /
children.translated_text: And that mind, whose nature is the perception of beings, is not different from the perceiver — because it is an object of the perceiver, like the dream-mind.

children.text: uktārthamanyat //65-66 //
children.translated_text: The rest states what has already been explained. || 65-66 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.67
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.67

children.text: ubhe hy anyonyadṛśye te kiṃ tad astīti cocyate /
children.translated_text: Both [mind and beings] are indeed perceived by each other; 'What then exists?' — it is also asked.

children.text: lakṣaṇāśūnyam ubhayaṃ tan mate naiva gṛhyate // MandUpK_4.67 //
children.translated_text: Both are devoid of distinguishing characteristics — [hence] that is not truly apprehended in this view. || MandUpK 4.67 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.67
jīvacitta ubhe cittacaitye te 'nyonyadṛśya itaretaragamye /
jīvādiviṣayāpekṣaṃ hi cittaṃ nāma bhavati /
children.translated_text:
MandUpKC_4.67
Both — the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and the mind (<s>citta</s>) — are mutually perceived, mutually accessible.
For the mind is designated as such only in dependence on objects such as the <s>jīva</s> and the like.

children.text:
cittāpekṣaṃ hi jīvādi dṛśyam /
ataste 'nyenyadṛśye /
tasmānna kiñcidastīti cocyate cittaṃ vā cittekṣaṇīyaṃ vā kiṃ tadastīti vivekinocyate /
na hi svapne hastī hasticittaṃ vā vidyate tathehāpi vivekināmityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the <s>jīva</s> and the like, as objects of perception, are dependent on the mind. Therefore, one thing is not perceived by another thing. Hence it is said that nothing exists — [but then] does the mind exist, or does what is perceived by the mind exist? Thus the discriminating person asks. For just as in a dream neither the elephant nor the cognition of the elephant exists, so too here — this is the purport.

children.text: katham? lakṣaṇāśūnyaṃ lakṣyate 'nayeti lakṣaṇā pramāṇaṃ pramāṇaśūnyamubhayaṃ cittaṃ caityaṃ dvayaṃ yatastanmatenaiva taccittatayaiva tadgṛhyate /
children.translated_text: How? Both [the mind and its object] are devoid of defining marks — <s>lakṣaṇā</s> means that by which [something] is characterized, i.e., a means of knowledge — [both are] devoid of means of knowledge. The mind and the perceived — the duality — since that [duality] is grasped by its own nature, i.e., as mind alone.

children.text: na hi ghaṭamatiṃ pratyākhyāya ghaṭo gṛhyate nāpi ghaṭaṃ pratyākhyāya ghaṭamatiḥ /
children.translated_text: For a pot is not grasped by rejecting the cognition of the pot, nor is the cognition of the pot [grasped] by rejecting the pot.

children.text: na hi tatra pramāṇaprameyabhedaḥ śakyate kalpayitumityabhiprāyaḥ //67//
children.translated_text: For the distinction of means of knowledge and object of knowledge cannot be imagined therein — this is the purport. || 67 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.68-70
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.68-70

children.text: yathā svapnamayo jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>jīva</s> born of dream is born and also dies,

children.text: tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca // MandUpK_4.68 //
children.translated_text: so too all these <s>jīvas</s> come into being and cease to be. || MandUpK 4.68 ||

children.text: yathā māyāmayo jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>jīva</s> produced by <s>māyā</s> is born and also dies,

children.text: tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca // MandUpK_4.69 //
children.translated_text: so too all these <s>jīvas</s> come into being and cease to be. || MandUpK 4.69 ||

children.text: yathā nirmitako jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>jīva</s> created [by magical powers] is born and also dies,

children.text: tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca // MandUpK_4.70 //
children.translated_text: so too all these <s>jīvas</s> come into being and cease to be. || MandUpK 4.70 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.68-70
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.68-70:

children.text: māyāmayo māyāvinā yaḥ kṛto nirmitako mantrauṣadhyādibhirniṣpāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Produced by <s>māyā</s>' means created by a magician; 'created' (<s>nirmitaka</s>) means produced through mantras, herbs, and the like.

children.text: svapnamāyānirmitakā aṇḍajātayo jīvā yatā jāyante mriyante ca tachā manuṣyādilakṣaṇā avidyamānā eva citta vikalpanāmātrā ityartaḥ //68-70 //
children.translated_text: Just as the dream, <s>māyā</s>, and magically created classes of <s>jīvas</s> are born and die, so too those characterized as humans and the like — being non-existent, they are merely imaginations of the mind — this is the meaning. || 68-70 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.71
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.71

children.text: na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: No <s>jīva</s> whatsoever is born; there is no origination for it;

children.text: etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiñcin na jāyate // MandUpK_4.71 //
children.translated_text: this is that supreme truth, wherein nothing whatsoever is born. || MandUpK 4.71 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.71
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.71:

children.text: vyavahārasatyaviṣaye jīvānāṃ janmamaraṇādīḥ svapnādi jīvavadityuktam /
children.translated_text: With respect to the domain of conventional truth, the birth and death and the like of <s>jīvas</s> have been described as being like dream-<s>jīvas</s> and the like.

children.text: uttamaṃ tu paramārthasatyaṃ na kaścijjāyate jīva iti /
children.translated_text: But the supreme, ultimate truth is that no <s>jīva</s> whatsoever is born.

children.text: uktārthamanyat //71//
children.translated_text: The rest has already been explained. || 71 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.72
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.72

children.text: cittaspandikam evedaṃ grāhyagrāhakavad dvayam /
children.translated_text: This duality, appearing as the grasped and the grasper, is nothing but the vibration of the mind;

children.text: cittaṃ nirviṣayaṃ nityam asaṅgaṃ tena kīrtitam // MandUpK_4.72 //
children.translated_text: the mind is without object, eternal, and therefore declared to be unattached. || MandUpK 4.72 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.72
sarvaṃ grāhyagrāhakavaccittaspanditameva dvayaṃ cittaṃ paramārthata ātmaiveti nirviṣayaṃ tena nirviṣayatvena nityamasaṅgaṃ kīrtitam /
"asaṅgo hyayaṃ puruṣaḥ"(bṛ.u. 4 / 3 / 15,16) iti śruteḥ /
saviṣayasya hi viṣaye saṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who has objects has attachment to [those] objects.

children.text: nirviṣayatvāccittamasaṅgamityarthaḥ //72//
children.translated_text: Because the mind is without object, it is unattached — this is the meaning. || 72 ||

Commentary on MandUpK 4.72: All the duality appearing as the grasped and the grasper is merely the vibration of the mind; the mind is, in ultimate reality, the <s>Ātman</s> itself — hence it is without object. Because of being without object, it is eternal and unattached — so it has been declared. As scripture says: 'For this <s>Puruṣa</s> is unattached' (Bṛh. Up. 4.3.15-16).

children.text: START MandUpK 4.73
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.73

children.text: nanu nirviṣayatvena cedasaṅgatvaṃ cittasya na niḥsaṅgatā bhavati yasmācchāstā śāstraṃ śiṣyaścetyevamāderviṣayasya vidyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: if the unattachment of the mind is due to its being without object, then unattachment would not hold, since objects such as the teacher, the scripture, and the student exist.

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ ; kasmāt-
children.translated_text: This is not a fault; why?

children.text: yo 'sti kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāsty asau /
children.translated_text: What exists by imagined convention does not exist in ultimate reality;

children.text: paratantrābhisaṃvṛtyā syān nāsti paramārthataḥ // MandUpK_4.73 //
children.translated_text: what [exists] by dependent convention may be, but does not exist in ultimate reality. || MandUpK 4.73 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.73
yaḥ padārthaḥ śāstrādirvidyate sa kalpitasaṃvṛtyā; kalpitā ca sā paramārthapratipatyupāyatvena saṃvṛtiśca sā, tayā yo 'sti paramārthena nāstyasau na vidyate /
jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyata ityuktam /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.73: Whatever entity — the scripture and the like — exists, it exists by imagined convention; that [convention] is both imagined and a convention (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), serving as a means to the realization of ultimate truth. What exists by that [imagined convention] does not exist in ultimate reality. It has been said: 'When [non-duality] is known, duality does not exist.'

children.text: yaśca paratantrābhisaṃvṛtyā paraśāstravyavahāreṇa syātpadārthaḥ sa paramārthato nirūpyamāṇo nāstyeva /
children.translated_text: And whatever entity exists by dependent convention — through the transactional usage of another's scripture — that entity, when examined in ultimate reality, simply does not exist.

children.text: tena yuktamuktamasaṅgaṃ tena kīrtimiti //73//
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is rightly said that [the mind] is declared to be unattached. || 73 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.74
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.74

children.text: nanu śāstrādīnāṃ saṃvṛtitve 'ja itīyamapi kalpanāṃ saṃvṛtiḥ syāt?
children.translated_text: Objection: if the scripture and the like are conventional, then this imagination too — that [<s>Brahman</s>] is unborn — would be conventional?

children.text: satyamevam-
children.translated_text: Indeed, that is so —

children.text: ajaḥ kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāpy ajaḥ /
children.translated_text: The unborn [is called so] by imagined convention; in ultimate reality it is not even unborn;

children.text: paratantrādiniṣpattyā saṃvṛtyā jāyate tu saḥ // MandUpK_4.74 //
children.translated_text: through the dependent conventional establishment [of rival doctrines], it is [said to be] born. || MandUpK 4.74 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.74
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.74:

children.text: śāstrādikalpitasaṃvṛtyaivāja ityucyate /
children.translated_text: It is called 'unborn' only by the imagined convention of scripture and the like.

children.text: paramārthena nāpyajo yasmātparatantrābhiniṣpattyā paraśāstrasiddhimapekṣya yo 'ja ityuktaḥ sa saṃvṛtyā jāyate /
children.translated_text: In ultimate reality it is not even unborn — because that which is called 'unborn' in dependence upon the establishment of other scriptures [and their doctrines of birth] is [itself said to be] born by convention.

children.text: ato 'ja itīyamapi kalpanā paramārthaviṣaye naiva kramata ityarthaḥ //74//
children.translated_text: Therefore, this imagination of 'unborn' too does not at all apply to the domain of ultimate reality — this is the meaning. || 74 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.75
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.75

children.text: yasmādasadviṣayastasmāt-
children.translated_text: Since [the objects of attachment] are unreal, therefore —

children.text: abhūtābhiniveśo 'sti dvayaṃ tatra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is a clinging to what is unreal; duality does not exist therein;

children.text: dvayābhāvaṃ sa buddhvaiva nirnimitto na jāyate // MandUpK_4.75 //
children.translated_text: having realized the absence of duality, one who is without cause is not born. || MandUpK 4.75 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.75
asatyabhūte dvaite 'bhiniveśo 'sti kevalam /
children.translated_text: There is merely a clinging to, a fixation upon, the unreal, non-existent duality.

children.text: abhiniveśa āgrahamātram /
children.translated_text: The clinging is mere tenacious grasping.

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Duality does not exist therein.

children.text: mithyābhiniveśamātraṃ ca janmanaḥ kāraṇaṃ yasmāttasmāddvayābhāvaṃ buddhvā nirnimitto nivṛttamithyādvayābhiniveśo yaḥ sa na jāyate //75//
children.translated_text: And since the false clinging alone is the cause of birth, therefore, having realized the absence of duality, one who is without cause — whose false clinging to duality has ceased — is not born. || 75 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 4.75:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.76
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.76

children.text: yadā na labhate hetūn uttamādhamamadhyamān /
children.translated_text: When one does not find causes — superior, inferior, or middling —

children.text: tadā na jāyate cittaṃ hetvabhāve phalaṃ kutaḥ // MandUpK_4.76 //
children.translated_text: then the mind is not born; in the absence of cause, whence could an effect [arise]? || MandUpK 4.76 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.76
jātyāśramavihitā aśīrvarjitairanuṣṭhīyamānā dharmā devatvādiprāptihetava uttamāḥ kevalāśca dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> (meritorious acts) prescribed for one's caste and stage of life, performed without desire for results, which serve as causes for attaining godhood and the like, are the superior [causes]; pure <s>dharma</s> alone [is also superior].

children.text: adharmavyāmiśrā manuṣyatvādiprāptyarthā madhyamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those mixed with <s>adharma</s> (demerit), serving the purpose of attaining humanhood and the like, are the middling.

children.text: tiryagādiprāptinimittā adharmalakṣaṇāḥ pravṛttiviśeṣāścādhamāḥ /
children.translated_text: The particular activities characterized by <s>adharma</s>, serving as causes for attaining animal birth and the like, are the inferior.

children.text: tānuttamamadhyamādhamānavidyāparikalpitānyadaikamevādvitīyamātmatattvaṃ sarvakalpanāvarjitaṃ jānanna labhate na paśyati yathā bālairdṛśyamānaṃ gagane malaṃ vivekī na paśyati tadvattadā na jāyate notpadyate cittaṃ devādyākārairuttamādhamamadhyamaphalarūpeṇa na hyasati hetau phalamutpadyate bījādyabhāva iva sasyādi //76//
children.translated_text: When one who knows the one, non-dual, <s>Ātman</s>-reality, devoid of all imaginations, does not find — does not see — those superior, middling, and inferior [causes] imagined by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), just as a discriminating person does not see the impurity seen by children in the sky, then the mind is not born, does not arise in the forms of gods and the like as superior, middling, and inferior effects. For when the cause does not exist, the effect does not arise — like grain and the like [not arising] in the absence of seed and the like. || 76 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 4.76:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.77
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.77

children.text:
hetvabhāve cittaṃ notpadyata iti hyuktam /
sa punaranutpattiścittasya kīdṛśītyucyate-
children.translated_text: It has been said that in the absence of cause, the mind is not born. What kind of non-birth of the mind is this? It is said —

children.text: animittasya cittasya yānutpattiḥ samādvayā /
children.translated_text: The non-birth of the mind that is without cause is equal and non-dual;

children.text: ajātasyaiva sarvasya cittadṛśyaṃ hi tadyataḥ // MandUpK_4.77 //
children.translated_text: for the perceived [world] is [nothing but] mind, since all is unborn. || MandUpK 4.77 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.77
paramārthadarśanena nirastadharmādharmākhyotpattinimittasyānimittasya cittasyeti yā mokṣākhyānutpattiḥ sā sarvadā sarvāvasthāsu samā nirviśeṣādvayā ca /
children.translated_text: By the vision of ultimate reality, the cause of origination — namely, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — has been negated; the non-birth of this causeless mind, which is called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), is at all times, in all states, equal — without distinction — and non-dual.

children.text: pūrvamapyajātasyaivānutpannasya cittasya sarvasyādvayasyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even before, the mind was always unborn, unoriginated, and entirely non-dual — this is the meaning.

children.text: yasmātprāgapu vijñānāccittadṛśyaṃ tadadvayaṃ janma ca tasmādajātasya sarvasya sarvadā cittasya samādvayaivānutpattirna punaḥ kadācidbhavati kadācidvā na bhavati /
children.translated_text: Since, prior to cognition, the perceived [world] is [nothing but] mind — that non-dual [reality] — and birth [is also merely mind], therefore the non-birth of all, of the always-unborn mind, is equal and non-dual; it is not [the case] that sometimes it exists and sometimes it does not.

children.text: sarvadaikarūpaivetyarthaḥ //77//
children.translated_text: It is always of one nature — this is the meaning. || 77 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 4.77:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.78
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.78

children.text: yathoktena nyāyena janmanimittasya dvayasyābhāvāt-
children.translated_text: Since, by the reasoning stated, duality — the cause of birth — is absent,

children.text: buddhvā nimittatāṃ satyāṃ hetuṃ pṛthag anāpnuvan /
children.translated_text: having realized [its] true causelessness, not separately obtaining a cause,

children.text: vītaśokaṃ tathākāmam abhayaṃ padam aśnute // MandUpK_4.78 //
children.translated_text: one attains the state that is free from sorrow, free from desire, and free from fear. || MandUpK 4.78 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.78

animittatāṃ ca satyāṃ paramārtharūpāṃ buddhvā hetuṃ dharmādikāraṇaṃ devādiyoniprāptaye pṛthaganāpnuvannanupādadānastyaktabāhyaiṣaṇaḥ sankāmaśokādivarjitamavidyādirahitamabhayaṃ padamaśnute punarna jāyata ityarthaḥ //78//
children.translated_text: Having realized the true causelessness, which is of the nature of ultimate reality, and not obtaining — not taking up — a cause such as <s>dharma</s> and the like for the attainment of birth in the wombs of gods and the like, having abandoned all external desires, one attains the state free from desire, sorrow, and the like, free from <s>avidyā</s> and the rest, the fearless state — meaning one is not born again. || 78 ||
Commentary on MandUpK 4.78:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.79
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.79

children.text: abhūtābhiniveśād dhi sadṛśe tat pravartate /
children.translated_text: Due to the clinging to what is unreal, [the mind] operates upon what resembles [reality];

children.text: vastvabhāvaṃ sa budhvaiva niḥsaṅgaṃ vinivartate // MandUpK_4.79 //
children.translated_text: having realized the non-existence of [that] object, it turns away, unattached. || MandUpK 4.79 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.79
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.79:

children.text: yasmād bhūtābhiniveśādasati dvaye dvayāstitvaniścayo 'bhūtābhiniveśastasmādavidyāvyāmoharūpāddhi sadṛśe tadanurūpe taccittaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: Since due to the clinging to what is unreal — the conviction of the existence of duality, which is non-existent — a clinging to what is unreal, which is of the nature of the delusion of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the mind operates upon what resembles [that duality], i.e., in conformity with it.

children.text: tasya dvayasya vastuno 'bhāvaṃ yadā buddhavāṃstadā tasmānniḥsaṅgo nirapekṣaṃ sadvinivartate 'bhūtābhiniveśaviṣayāt //79//
children.translated_text: When one has realized the non-existence of that duality as a real thing, then one turns away from the object of that false clinging, unattached, without dependence — always. || 79 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.80
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.80

children.text: nivṛttasyāpravṛttasya niścalā hi tathā sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of [the mind] that has turned away and does not [re-]engage, the abiding is indeed stable;

children.text: viṣayaḥ sa hi buddhānāṃ tat sāmyam ajam advayam // MandUpK_4.80 //
children.translated_text: for that is the object [of realization] of the awakened ones — that equality, unborn, non-dual. || MandUpK 4.80 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.80
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.80:

children.text: nivṛtasya dvaitaviṣayādviṣayāntare cāpravṛttasyābhāvadarśanena cittasya niścalā calanavarjitā brahmasvarūpaiva tadā sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the mind that has turned away from the object of duality and does not engage in any other object — through the vision of non-existence — the abiding is stable, free from movement, of the very nature of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yaiṣā brahmasvarūpā sthitiścittasyādvayavijñānaikarasaghanalakṣaṇā, sa hi yasmādviṣayo gocaraḥ paramārthadarśināṃ buddhānāṃ tasmāttatsāmyaṃ paraṃ nirviśeṣamajamadvayaṃ ca //80//
children.translated_text: This abiding of the mind, which is of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, whose essence is the compact mass of non-dual consciousness — since that is the object, the domain of the seers of ultimate reality, the awakened ones — therefore, that equality is supreme, without distinction, unborn, and non-dual. || 80 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.81
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.81

children.text: punarapi kīdṛśaścāsau buddhānāṃ viṣaya ityāha-
children.translated_text: Again, what is the nature of that object of the awakened ones? He says —

children.text: ajam anidram asvapnaṃ prabhātaṃ bhavati svayam /
children.translated_text: Unborn, without sleep, without dream, it is self-luminous;

children.text: sakṛdvibhāto hy evaiṣa dharma dhātusvabhāvataḥ // MandUpK_4.81 //
children.translated_text: for this <s>dharma</s> (reality) is once and for all luminous, by the nature of its essence. || MandUpK 4.81 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.81
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.81:

children.text: svayameva tatprabhātaṃ bhavati, nādityapādyapekṣam; syayañjyotiḥ svabhāvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is self-luminous by itself, not dependent on the sun and the like; self-luminous by nature — this is the meaning.

children.text: sakṛdvibhātaḥ sadaiva vibhāta ityetadeṣa evaṃlakṣaṇa ātmākhyo dharmo dhātusvabhāvato vastusvabhāvata ityarthaḥ //81//
children.translated_text: 'Once and for all luminous' means always luminous — this <s>Ātman</s>-reality of such characteristics, by the nature of its essence, i.e., by the nature of the thing itself — this is the meaning. || 81 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.82
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.82

children.text: evamucyamānamapi paramārthatattvaṃ kasmāllaukikairna gṛhyata ityucyate-
children.translated_text: Even though the ultimate reality is being thus explained, why is it not grasped by worldly people? It is said —

children.text: sukham āvriyate nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vivriyate sadā /
children.translated_text: Bliss is always covered; suffering is always revealed,

children.text: yasya kasya ca dharmasya graheṇa bhagavān asau // MandUpK_4.82 //
children.translated_text: for the blessed [<s>Ātman</s>], through the grasping of any <s>dharma</s> (entity) whatsoever. || MandUpK 4.82 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.82
yasmādyasya kasyaciddvayavastuno dharmasya graheṇa grahaṇāveśena mithyābhiniviṣṭatayā sukhamāvriyate 'nāyāsenācchādyata ityarthaḥ /
dvayopalabdhinimittaṃ hi tatrāvaraṇaṃ na yatnāntaramapekṣyate /
duḥkhaṃ ca vivriyate prakaṭīkriyate, paramārthajñānasya durlabhatvāt /
bhagavānasāvātmadvayo deva ityarthaḥ, ato vedāntairācāryaiśca bahuśa ucyamāno 'pi naiva jñātuṃ śakya ityarthaḥ /
"āścaryo vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhā"(ka.u.1 / 2 / 7) iti śruteḥ //82//
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.82: Because through the grasping — the obsessive fixation upon, the false clinging to — any dual entity whatsoever, bliss is covered, meaning effortlessly obscured. For the perception of duality is itself the veiling therein — no additional effort is required. And suffering is revealed, made manifest — because of the difficulty of obtaining the knowledge of ultimate reality. The blessed, non-dual <s>Ātman</s>, the Lord — this is the meaning. Therefore, even though spoken of repeatedly by <s>Vedāntins</s> and teachers, it simply cannot be known — this is the meaning. As scripture says: 'Wonderful is the speaker, rare is the obtainer [of this knowledge]' (Kaṭha Up. 1.2.7). || 82 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.83
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.83

children.text: asti nāstītyādisūkṣmaviṣayā api paṇḍitānāṃ grahā bhagavataḥ paramātmana āvaraṇa eva kimuta mūḍhajanānāṃ buddhilakṣaṇā ityevamarthaṃ pradarśayannāha-
children.translated_text: Even the subtle views of the learned — concerning 'it exists,' 'it does not exist,' and so forth — serve only to veil the supreme <s>Ātman</s>; how much more so the notions of the deluded? Showing this meaning, he says —

children.text: asti nāsty asti nāstīti nāsti nāstīti vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It exists,' 'it does not exist,' 'it exists and does not exist,' and again 'it does not exist at all' —

children.text: calasthirobhayābhāvair āvṛṇotye va bāliśaḥ // MandUpK_4.83 //
children.translated_text: through [views characterized as] moving, stationary, both, or neither, the childish one merely veils [the <s>Ātman</s>]. || MandUpK 4.83 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.83
astyātmeti vādī kaścitpratipadyate /
nāstītyaparo vaināśiko 'sti nāstītyaparor'dhavaināśikaḥ sadasadvādī digvāsāḥ /
nāsti nāstītyatyantaśūnyavādī /
tatrāstibhāvaścalaḥ, ghaṭādyanityavilakṣaṇatvāt /
nāstibhāvaḥ sthiraḥ sadāviśeṣatvāt /
ubhayaṃ calasthiraviṣayatvātsadasadbhāvo 'bhāvo 'tyantābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on MandUpK 4.83: A certain disputant holds 'the <s>Ātman</s> exists.' Another, a nihilist (<s>vaināśika</s>), holds 'it does not exist.' Another, a semi-nihilist, a proponent of both existence and non-existence, a <s>Digambara</s> [Jain], holds 'it exists and does not exist.' An absolute nihilist holds 'it does not exist at all.' Among these, the 'existence' view is 'moving' (<s>cala</s>), because of its dissimilarity from impermanent things like pots. The 'non-existence' view is 'stationary' (<s>sthira</s>), because it is always the same. 'Both' is the view of both existence and non-existence, because of having both moving and stationary as its objects. 'Absence' is utter non-existence.

children.text: prakāracatuṣṭayasyāpi tairataiścalisthirobhayābhāvaiḥ sadasadādivādī sarvo 'pi bhagavantamāvṛṇotyeva bāliśo 'vivekī /
children.translated_text: Through any and all of these four modes — moving, stationary, both, and absence — every proponent of 'existence,' 'non-existence,' and the rest merely veils the blessed [<s>Ātman</s>], being childish, lacking discrimination.

children.text: yadyapi paṇḍito bāliśa eva paramārthatattvānavabodhāckimu svabhāvamūḍho jana ityabhiprāyaḥ //83//
children.translated_text: Even the learned person is childish through the non-realization of the ultimate truth — how much more so the person who is deluded by nature — this is the purport. || 83 ||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.84
children.translated_text: START MandUpK 4.84

children.text: kīdṛkpunaḥ paramārthatattvaṃ yadavabodhādabāliśaḥ paṇḍito bhavatītyāha-
children.translated_text: What then is the nature of the ultimate truth, the realization of which makes a person wise rather than childish? He says —

children.text: koṭhyaś catasra etās tu grahair yāsāṃ sadā vṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: These four standpoints — by which [the <s>Ātman</s>] is always veiled through grasping —

children.text: bhagavān ābhir aspṛṣṭo yena dṛṣṭaḥ sa sarvadṛk // MandUpK_4.84 //
children.translated_text: the blessed [<s>Ātman</s>], untouched by these: he by whom [it is] seen is the all-seer. || MandUpK 4.84 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.84

koṭhyaḥ prāvādukaśāstranirṇayāntā etā uktā asti nāstītyādyāścatasro yāsāṃ koṭīnāṃ grahairgrahaṇairūpalabdhiniścayaiḥ sadā sarvadāvṛta ācchāditasteṣāmeva prāvādukānāṃ yaḥ sa bhagavānābhirastināstītyādikoṭibhiścatasṛbhirapyaspṛṣṭo 'styādivikalpanāvarjita ityetadyena muninā dṛṣṭo jñāto vedānteṣvaupaniṣadaḥ puruṣaḥ sa sarvadṛksarvajñaḥ paramārthapaṇḍita ityarthaḥ //84//
children.translated_text: The positions (<s>koṭis</s>) stated — ending with the conclusions of the disputants' treatises — are the four such as 'exists,' 'does not exist,' and so on. He whose [vision] is always covered — concealed — by the apprehensions of those positions, that is, by the cognitions and convictions of those very disputants — that Blessed One is untouched by all four positions of 'exists,' 'does not exist,' and so forth, free from conceptual constructs such as 'exists' and the like. The sage by whom this Upaniṣadic <s>Puruṣa</s> — known in the <s>Vedāntas</s> (Upaniṣads) — has been seen, known, he is the all-seeing, the omniscient, the supreme knower of ultimate reality. This is the meaning. ||84||
Commentary on MandUpK 4.84:

children.text: START MandUpK 4.85
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.85

children.text: prāpya sarvajñatāṃ kṛtsnāṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ padam advayam /
children.translated_text: Having attained the complete omniscience, the non-dual state of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brāhmaṇya</s>),

children.text: anāpannādimadhyāntaṃ kim ataḥ param īhate // MandUpK_4.85 //
children.translated_text: That which has not undergone beginning, middle, or end — what more does one desire beyond this? || Kārikā 4.85 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.85
prāpyaitāṃ yathoktāṃ kṛtsnāṃ samastāṃ sarvajñatāṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ padaṃ"sa brāhmaṇaḥ"(bṛ.u.3 / 8 / 10) "eṣa nityo mahimā brāhmaṇasya" (bṛ.u.4 / 4 / 23) iti śruteḥ ; ādimadhyāntā utpattisthitilayā anāpannā aprāptā yasyādvayasya padasya na vidyante tadanāpannādimadhyāntaṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ padam, tadeva prāpya labdhvā kimataḥ paramasmādātmalābhādūrdhvamīhate ceṣṭate niṣprayojanamityarthaḥ /
"naiva tasya kṛtenārthaḥ"(gītā 3 / 18) ityādismṛteḥ //85//
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.85: Having attained this complete, total omniscience as described, the state of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brāhmaṇya</s>) — as stated in the <s>śrutis</s>: 'He is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.8.10), 'This is the eternal greatness of the knower of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.23). Beginning, middle, and end — that is, origination, subsistence, and dissolution — have not been attained, have not occurred, in this non-dual state. Having attained that state which has not undergone beginning, middle, or end — the state of <s>Brahman</s> — what more does one desire, strive for, beyond this attainment of the Self? Nothing further serves any purpose — this is the meaning. [As confirmed by] the <s>smṛti</s>: 'He has no purpose in action' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 3.18). ||85||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.86
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.86

children.text: viprāṇāṃ vinayo hy eṣa śamaḥ prākṛta ucyate /
children.translated_text: The discipline of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (knowers of <s>Brahman</s>) is this: tranquility (<s>śama</s>) is said to be natural.

children.text: damaḥ prakṛtidāntatvād evaṃ vidvāñ śamaṃ vrajet // MandUpK_4.86 //
children.translated_text: Self-control (<s>dama</s>) [arises] from the naturally tamed nature — thus the knower should abide in tranquility. || Kārikā 4.86 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.86
viprāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ vinayo vinītatvaṃ svābhāvikaṃ yadetātmasvarūpeṇāvasthānam /
children.translated_text: The discipline (<s>vinaya</s>) of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — their disciplined nature, which is natural — is this: abiding in one's own essential nature as the Self.

children.text: eṣa vinayaḥ śamo 'pyeṣa eva prākṛtaḥ svābhāviko 'kṛtaka ucyate /
children.translated_text: This discipline is also tranquility (<s>śama</s>) — this very [abiding in one's nature] is said to be natural, innate, not artificially produced.

children.text: damo 'pyeṣa eva prakṛtidāntatvātsvabhāvata eva copaśāntarūpatvādbrahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Self-control (<s>dama</s>) is also this very [abiding], because of the naturally tamed nature — because <s>Brahman</s> is by its very nature of a quiescent form.

children.text: evaṃ yathoktaṃ svabhāvopaśāntaṃ brahma vidvāñśamamupaśāntiṃ svābhāvikīṃ brahmasvarūpāṃ vrajed brahmasvarūpeṇāvatiṣṭhata ityarthaḥ //86//
children.translated_text: Thus, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, which is naturally quiescent as described, should abide in tranquility — the natural tranquility that is the very nature of <s>Brahman</s> — meaning: should remain established in the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. ||86||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.86

children.text: START MandUpK 4.87
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.87

children.text:
evamanyonyaviruddhatvātsaṃsārakāraṇāni rāgadveṣadoṣāspadāni prāvādukānāṃ darśanāni /
ato mithyādarśanāni tānīti tadyuktibhireva darśayitvā catuṣkoṭivarjitatvādrāhādidoṣānāspadaṃ svabhāvaśāntamadvaitadarśanameva samyagdarśamityupasaṃhṛtam /
athedānīṃ svaprakriyāpradarśanārtha ārambhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Since the doctrinal views of the disputants are mutually contradictory and are the locus of the defects of attachment and aversion, which are the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — therefore, having shown by their own reasoning that those are false views, it has been concluded that the vision of non-duality alone, which is free from the four-fold conceptual alternatives and not a locus for defects such as attachment and the like, naturally quiescent, is the right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>). Now, for the purpose of demonstrating his own method, the exposition begins —

children.text: savastu sopalambhaṃ ca dvayaṃ laukikam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: That which has substance (<s>savastu</s>) and has apprehension (<s>sopalambha</s>), the duality, is considered worldly (<s>laukika</s>).

children.text: avastu sopalambhaṃ ca śuddhaṃ laukikam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.87 //
children.translated_text: That which is without substance (<s>avastu</s>) yet has apprehension is considered purely worldly (<s>śuddha laukika</s>). || Kārikā 4.87 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.87
savastu saṃvṛtisatā vastunā saha vartata iti savastu, tathā copalabdhirupalambhastena saha vartata iti sopalbhaṃ ca śāstrādisarvavyavahārāspadaṃ grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇaṃ dvayaṃ laukikaṃ lokādanapetaṃ lokikaṃ jāgaritamityetat /
evaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ jāgaritamiṣyate vedānteṣu /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.87: <s>Savastu</s> — 'accompanied by substance' — means existing together with objects that have conventional reality. And <s>sopalambha</s> — 'with apprehension' — means existing together with cognition. The duality characterized by the apprehended and the apprehender, which is the basis of all conventional dealings including scriptures and the like, is <s>laukika</s> — not departed from the world — this is the waking state. Such is the character of the waking state that is accepted in the <s>Vedāntas</s>.

children.text: avastu saṃvṛterapyabhāvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Avastu</s> — because even conventional [substance] is absent.

children.text: sopalambhaṃ vastuvadupalambhanamupalambho 'satyapi vastuni tena saha vartata iti sopalambhaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Sopalambha</s> — apprehension exists as if of objects, even though objects do not exist — existing together with that [apprehension].

children.text: śuddhaṃ kevalaṃ pravibhaktaṃ jāgaritātsthūlāllaukikaṃ sarvaprāṇisādhāraṇatvādiṣyate svapna ityarthaḥ //87//
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddha</s> (pure) means separate, distinguished from the gross waking state; it is considered <s>laukika</s> (worldly) because it is common to all living beings — meaning this is the dream state. ||87||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.88
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.88

children.text: avastv anupalambhaṃ ca lokottaram iti smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Without substance (<s>avastu</s>) and without apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) is declared to be supra-mundane (<s>lokottara</s>).

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ sadā buddhaiḥ prakīrtitam // MandUpK_4.88 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge, the knowable, and the to-be-known — these are always proclaimed by the wise. || Kārikā 4.88 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.88
avastvanupalambhaṃ ca grāhyagrahaṇavarjitamityetat, lokottaram ata eva lokātītam /
grāhyagrahaṇaviṣayo hi lokastadabhāvātsarvapravṛttibījaṃ suṣuptamityetadevaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.88: Without substance and without apprehension — free from the apprehended and the act of apprehension — this is <s>lokottara</s> (supra-mundane), transcending the world for this very reason. For the world consists of the domain of the apprehended and apprehension; from its absence, this is deep sleep — the seed of all activity — thus it is declared.

children.text: sopāyaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ laukikaṃ śuddhalaukikaṃ lokottaraṃ ca krameṇa yena jñānena jñāyate tajjñānam /
jñeyametānyeva trīṇi /
children.translated_text: The 'knowable' (<s>jñeya</s>) is these very three.

children.text: etadvyatirekeṇa jñeyānupapatteḥ sarvaprāvādukakalpitavastuno 'traivāntarbhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Since there is no knowable apart from these, because all objects imagined by any disputant whatsoever are included within these.

children.text: vijñeyaṃ paramārthasatyaṃ turyākhyamadvayamajamātmatattvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The 'to-be-known' (<s>vijñeya</s>) is the ultimate truth called <s>Turīya</s> (the Fourth), the non-dual, unborn truth of the Self — this is the meaning.

children.text: sadā sarvadai9tallaukikādivijñeyāntaṃ buddhaiḥ paramārthadarśibhirbrahmavidbhiḥ prakīrtitam //88//
children.translated_text: These — from the worldly to the to-be-known — are always, at all times, proclaimed by the wise, those who see ultimate reality, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. ||88||

The knowledge by which the ultimate reality (<s>paramārthatatva</s>), together with its means, is known sequentially — the worldly, the purely worldly, and the supra-mundane — is 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>).

children.text: START MandUpK 4.89
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.89

children.text: jñāne ca trividhe jñeye krameṇa vidite svayam /
children.translated_text: When the threefold knowledge and the threefold knowable are known in sequence by oneself,

children.text: sarvajñatā hi sarvatra bhavatīha mahādhiyaḥ // MandUpK_4.89 //
children.translated_text: Then omniscience indeed arises everywhere, here, for the one of great intellect. || Kārikā 4.89 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.89

jñāne ca laukikādiviṣaye, jñeye ca laukikādau trividhe- pūrvaṃ laukikaṃ sthūlam, tadabhāvena paścācchuddhaṃ laukikam, tathābhāvena lokottaramityevaṃ krameṇa sthānatrayābhāvena paramārthasatye turye 'dvaye 'je 'bhaye vidite svayamevātmasvarūpameva sarvajñatā sarvaścāsau jñaśca sarvajñastadbhāvaḥ sarvajñatā, ihāsmiṃlloke bhavati mahādhiyo mahābuddheḥ /
children.translated_text: When the knowledge pertaining to the worldly and the rest, and the knowable — the worldly and the rest — being threefold: first the worldly (gross), then through its negation the purely worldly, then through its negation the supra-mundane — thus, through the sequential negation of the three states, when the ultimate truth, the non-dual, unborn, fearless <s>Turīya</s> is known, omniscience itself becomes the very nature of the Self. 'All' and 'knower' — the 'all-knower' — its state is 'omniscience.' It arises here in this world for the one of great intellect.

children.text: sarvalokātiśayavastuviṣayabuddhitvādevaṃvidaḥ sarvatra sarvadā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Because the knowledge of one who knows thus pertains to the object that transcends all worldly [objects], it exists everywhere and at all times.

children.text: sakṛdvidite svarūpe vyabhicārābhāvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: once the essential nature is known, there is no deviation [from it].

children.text: na hi paramārthavido jñānodbhavābhibhavau sto yathānyeṣāṃ prāvādukānām //89//
children.translated_text: For the knower of ultimate reality does not experience the arising and cessation of knowledge, as do the other disputants. ||89||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.89

children.text: START MandUpK 4.90
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.90

children.text: laukikādīnāṃ krameṇa jñeyatvena nirdeśādastitvāśaṅkā paramārthato mā bhūdityāha-
children.translated_text: Lest there be a suspicion that the worldly and the rest ultimately exist because they are indicated as knowable in sequence, he says —

children.text: heyajñeyāpyapākyāni vijñeyāny agrayāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: The to-be-abandoned, the to-be-known, the to-be-attained, and the to-be-purified — these are to be understood first.

children.text: teṣām anyatra vijñeyād upalambhas triṣu smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_4.90 //
children.translated_text: In those [three states] other than the to-be-known, apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>) is declared [to exist] in the three [states]. || Kārikā 4.90 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.90
heyāni ca laukikādīni trīṇi jāgaritasvapnasuṣuptānyātmanyasattvena rajjvāṃ sarpavaddhātavyānītyarthaḥ /
jñeyamiha catuṣkoṭivarjitaṃ paramārthatattvam /
āpyānyāptavyāni tyaktabāhyaiṣaṇātrayeṇa bhikṣuṇā pāṇḍityabālyamaunākhyāni sādhanāni /
pākyāni rāgadveṣamohādayo doṣāḥ kaṣāyākhyāni paktavyāni /
