sarvāṇyetāni heyajñeyāpyapākyāni vijñeyāni bhikṣuṇopāyatvenetyarthaḥ, agrayāṇātaḥ prathamataḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.90: The to-be-abandoned (<s>heya</s>) — the three worldly states: waking, dream, and deep sleep — are to be discarded through [the understanding of] their unreality in the Self, like a snake upon a rope. The to-be-known (<s>jñeya</s>) is here the ultimate truth free from the four-fold conceptual alternatives. The to-be-attained (<s>āpya</s>) — to be attained by the mendicant who has renounced the three types of external desires — are the means called 'learning' (<s>pāṇḍitya</s>), 'childlike simplicity' (<s>bālya</s>), and 'silence' (<s>mauna</s>). The to-be-purified (<s>pākya</s>) — the defects such as attachment, aversion, delusion, and the like, called 'impurities' (<s>kaṣāya</s>) — are to be burnt away. All these — the to-be-abandoned, the to-be-known, the to-be-attained, and the to-be-purified — are to be understood by the mendicant as means. The meaning is: first, from the very beginning.

children.text: teṣāṃ heyādīnāmanyatra vijñeyātparamārthasatyaṃ vijñeyaṃ brahmaikaṃ varjayitvā, upalbhanamupalambho 'vidyākalpanāmātram /
children.translated_text: Among those — the to-be-abandoned and the rest — apart from the to-be-known, that is, setting aside the one to-be-known, which is the single truth of <s>Brahman</s> as the ultimate reality — apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>), which is merely a fabrication of ignorance,

children.text: heyāpyāpakyeṣu triṣvapi smṛto brahmavidbhirna paramārthasatyatā trayāṇāmityarthaḥ //90//
children.translated_text: Is declared by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> to exist in the three — the to-be-abandoned, the to-be-attained, and the to-be-purified — meaning that the three do not have ultimate reality. ||90||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.91
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.91

children.text: paramārthatastu-
children.translated_text: But in ultimate reality —

children.text: prakṛtyākāśavaj jñeyāḥ sarve dharmā anādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All entities (<s>dharmas</s>) are to be known as like space by their very nature, beginningless.

children.text: vidyate na hi nānātvaṃ teṣāṃ kvacana kiñcanaḥ // MandUpK_4.91 //
children.translated_text: There is indeed no plurality whatsoever, in any way, among them. || Kārikā 4.91 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.91
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.91

children.text: prakṛtyā svabhāvata ākāśavadākāśatulyāḥ sūkṣmanirañjanasarvagatatvaiḥ sarve dharmā ātmāno jñeyāṃ mumukṣubhiranādayo nityāḥ /
children.translated_text: By their very nature, like space — comparable to space in subtlety, stainlessness, and all-pervasiveness — all entities, all selves, are to be known by seekers of liberation as beginningless, eternal.

children.text: bahuvacanakṛtabhedāśaṅkāṃ nirākurvannāha- kvacana kiñcana kindidaṇumātramapi teṣāṃ na vidyate nānātvamiti //91//
children.translated_text: Removing the suspicion of plurality created by the plural number, he says: there is not even the slightest, most minute plurality whatsoever among them. ||91||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.92
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.92

children.text: jñeyatāpi dharmāṇāṃ saṃvṛtyaiva na paramārthata ityāha-
children.translated_text: That even the 'knowability' of the entities is merely conventional and not ultimate — he says —

children.text: ādibuddhāḥ prakṛtyaiva sarve dharmāḥ suniścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All entities are awakened from the very beginning, by their very nature, well-established.

children.text: yasyaivaṃ bhavati kṣāntiḥ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate // MandUpK_4.92 //
children.translated_text: He who has such patient understanding — he is fit for immortality. || Kārikā 4.92 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.92
yasmādādau buddhā ādibuddhāḥ prakṛtyaiva svabhāvata eva yathā nityaprakāśasvarūpaḥ savitaivaṃ nityabodhasvarūpā ityarthaḥ sarve dharmāḥ sarva ātmānaḥ /
na ca teṣāṃ niścayaḥ kartavyo nityaniścitasvarūpā ityarthaḥ /
na saṃdihyamānasvarūpā evaṃ naivaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.92: Since they are awakened from the very beginning — <s>ādibuddha</s> — by their very nature, just as the sun is by nature eternally luminous, so too [all selves] are by nature eternally of the nature of awareness. This is the meaning: all entities, all selves. And their certainty need not be produced — they are by nature eternally certain. They are not of a doubtful nature, [wondering] 'thus or not thus.'

children.text: yasya mumukṣorevaṃ yathoktaprakāreṇa sarvadā bodhaniścayanirapekṣatātmārthaṃ parārthaṃ vā yathā savitā nityaṃ prakāśāntaranirapekṣaḥ svārthaṃ paramārthaṃ cetyevaṃ bhavati kṣāntirbodhakartavyatānirapekṣatā sarvadā svātmani sa amṛtatvāyāmṛtabhāvāya kalpate mokṣāya samartho bhavatītyarthaḥ //92//
children.translated_text: For the seeker of liberation who has such [understanding] — in the manner described — the state of always being independent of the need to produce awakening, whether for oneself or for others — just as the sun is eternally independent of any other light, both for its own purpose and for the ultimate purpose — when such patient understanding (<s>kṣānti</s>), the independence from the need to produce awakening, arises with respect to one's own Self at all times, he is fit for immortality — fit for the state of being immortal — meaning: he becomes capable of liberation. ||92||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.93
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.93

children.text: tathā nāpi śāntikartavyatātmanītyāha-
children.translated_text: Likewise, there is also no need to produce tranquility in oneself — he says —

children.text: ādiśāntā hy anutpannāḥ prakṛtyaiva sunirvṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Quiescent from the very beginning, unborn, by their very nature perfectly at rest,

children.text: sarve dharmāḥ samābhinnā ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam // MandUpK_4.93 //
children.translated_text: All entities are equal and undifferentiated — the unborn, the sameness, the clear [truth]. || Kārikā 4.93 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.93

yasmādādiśāntā nityameva śāntā anutpannā ajāśca prakṛtyaiva sunirvṛtāḥ suṣṭhūparatasvabhāvā ityarthaḥ, sarve dharmāḥ samāścābhinnāśca samābhinnāḥ, ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradaṃ viśuddhamātmatatvaṃ yasmāttasmācchāntirmokṣo vā nāsti kartavya ityarthaḥ, na hi nityaikasvabhāvasya kṛtaṃ kiñcidarthavatsyāt //93//
children.translated_text: Since they are quiescent from the very beginning — eternally quiescent — unborn, and by their very nature perfectly at rest, meaning their nature is well-ceased. All entities are equal and undifferentiated — <s>samābhinna</s>. Because the truth of the Self is unborn, equal, and pure (<s>viśārada</s>) — therefore, tranquility or liberation is not something to be produced. This is the meaning: for that which is of one eternal nature, nothing produced would have any purpose. ||93||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.93

children.text: START MandUpK 4.94
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.94

children.text: ye yathoktaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ pratipannāsta evākṛpaṇā loke kṛpaṇā evānya ityāha-
children.translated_text: Those who have realized the ultimate truth as described are alone the non-pitiable ones in the world; all others are pitiable — he says —

children.text: vaiśāradyaṃ tu vai nāsti bhede vicaratāṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Purity (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) does not exist for those who always move in [the realm of] difference.

children.text: bhedanimnāḥ pṛthagvādās tasmāt te kṛpaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ // MandUpK_4.94 //
children.translated_text: Those who follow difference are the proponents of plurality — therefore they are called pitiable. || Kārikā 4.94 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.94
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.94

children.text: yasmādbhedanimnā bhedānuyāyinaḥ saṃsārānugā ityarthaḥ ; ke? pṛdagvādāḥ pṛthaṅnānā vastvityevaṃ vadanaṃ yeṣāṃ te pṛthagvādā dvaitina ityarthaḥ, tasmātte kṛpaṇāḥ kṣudrāḥ smṛtāḥ; yasmādvaiśāradyaṃ viśuddhirnāsti teṣāṃ bhede vicaratāṃ dvaitamārge 'vidyākalpite sarvadā vartamānānāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since they follow difference — they are adherents of difference, followers of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning. Who? The proponents of plurality — those who speak of things as separate and diverse, meaning the dualists. Therefore they are called pitiable, mean. Since purity (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), purification, does not exist for them — for those always dwelling in the path of duality imagined by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — this is the meaning.

children.text: ato yuktameva teṣāṃ kārpaṇyamityabhiprāyaḥ //94//
children.translated_text: Therefore their pitiable condition is quite justified — this is the intention. ||94||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.95
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.95

children.text: yadidaṃ paramārthatattvamamahātmabhirapaṇḍitairvedāntabahiḥṣṭhaiḥ kṣudrairalpaprajñairanavagāhyamityāha-
children.translated_text: This ultimate truth is unfathomable by those of small spirit, the unlearned, those outside <s>Vedānta</s>, the mean, the small-minded — he says —

children.text: aje sāmye tu ye kecid bhaviṣyanti suniścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those, whoever they may be, who will be firmly established in the unborn sameness —

children.text: te hi loke mahājñānās tac ca loko na gāhate // MandUpK_4.95 //
children.translated_text: They are the ones of great knowledge in the world, and the world cannot fathom that [knowledge]. || Kārikā 4.95 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.95
aje sāmye paramārthatattva evameveti ye kecitstrāyadayo 'pi suniścitā bhaviṣyanti cetta eva hi loke mahājñānā niratiśaya tattvaviṣayajñānā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.95: In the unborn sameness, in the ultimate truth itself, those, whoever they may be — even women and others — who will be firmly established, they alone are ones of great knowledge in the world — possessing unsurpassable knowledge of ultimate truth. This is the meaning.

children.text:
tacca teṣāṃ vartma teṣāṃ viditaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ sāmānyabuddhiranyo loko na gāhate nāvatariti na viṣayīkarotītyarthaḥ /
sarvābhūtātmabhūtasya sarvabhūtahitasya ca /
devā api mārge muhyantyapadasya padaiṣiṇaḥ /
"śakunīnāmivākāśe gatirnaivopalabhyate"(mahā.śā.239 / 23,24) ityādismaraṇāt //95//
children.translated_text: And that — their path — the ultimate truth known by them — the common intellect, the ordinary world, cannot fathom, cannot enter, cannot make its object. This is the meaning. [As stated in the <s>smṛti</s>:] 'Of him who has become the Self of all beings, who works for the welfare of all beings — even the gods are confused about the path of the one who is trackless, who seeks the trackless' and 'Like the path of birds in the sky, it is never perceived' (<s>Mahābhārata</s>, Śāntiparvan 239.23-24). ||95||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.96
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.96

children.text: kathaṃ mahājñānatvamityāha-
children.translated_text: How is there great knowledge? He says —

children.text: ajeṣv ajam asaṃkrāntaṃ dharmeṣu jñānam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: In the unborn entities, the knowledge [that dwells] is [itself] unborn and non-transitive.

children.text: yato na kramate jñānam asaṅgaṃ tena kīrtitam // MandUpK_4.96 //
children.translated_text: Since knowledge does not transfer [to other objects], it is declared to be unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>). || Kārikā 4.96 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.96
children.translated_text: Commentary on Kārikā 4.96

children.text: ajeṣvanutpanneṣvacaleṣu dharmeṣvātmasvajamacalaṃ ca jñānamiṣyate savitarīvauṣṇyaṃ prakāśaśca yatastasmādasaṃkrāntamarthāntare jñānamajamiṣyate /
children.translated_text: In the unborn, unproduced, immovable entities — in the selves — the knowledge is accepted as unborn and immovable, like heat and light in the sun. Because of this, knowledge is accepted as non-transitive — not passing over to any other object — and as unborn.

children.text: yasmānna kramater'thāntare jñānaṃ tena kāraṇenāsaṅgaṃ tatkīrtitamākāśakalpamityuktam //96//
children.translated_text: Since knowledge does not transfer to any other object, for this reason it is declared to be unattached — said to be like space. ||96||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.97
children.translated_text: START Kārikā 4.97

children.text: aṇumātre 'pi vaidharmye jāyamāne 'vipaścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: If even the slightest difference is imagined to arise for the undiscriminating,

children.text: asaṅgatā sadā nāsti kimutāvaraṇacyutiḥ // MandUpK_4.97 //
children.translated_text: Non-attachment never exists [for them] — how much less the falling away of the veil [of ignorance]! || Kārikā 4.97 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.97
ito 'nyeṣāṃ vādināmaṇumātre 'pi vaidharmye vastuni bahirantarvā jāyamāna utpādyamāne 'vipaścito 'vivekino 'saṅgatā asaṅgatvaṃ sadā nāsti kimuta vaktayavyamāvaraṇacyutirbandhanāśo nāstīti //97//
children.translated_text: For the other disputants, [who maintain that] even the slightest difference in an entity exists, whether born internally or externally—[for these] undiscriminating, non-discerning ones, there is no non-attachment; non-attachment never exists [for them]. What need be said about the removal of the veil, the destruction of bondage? It does not exist [for them]. ||97||
Commentary on Kārikā 4.97

children.text: START MandUpK 4.98
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.98

children.text:
teṣāmāvaraṇacyutirnāstīti bruvatāṃ svasiddhānte 'bhyupagataṃ tarhi dharmāṇāmāvaraṇam /
netyucyate /
children.translated_text: In saying that there is no removal of the veil for them, is it then accepted in your own doctrine that there is a veil over the <s>dharmas</s> (entities)? No, it is said—

children.text: alabdhāvaraṇāḥ sarve dharmāḥ prakṛtinirmalāḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> (entities) have never obtained a veil; they are pure by nature;

children.text: ādau buddhās tathā muktā budhyanta iti nāyakāḥ // MandUpK_4.98 //
children.translated_text: They are enlightened from the very beginning, and thus liberated—the leaders (<s>nāyakāḥ</s>) are [said to] 'awaken.' || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.98 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.98
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.98:

children.text: alabdhāvaraṇāḥ- alabdhamaprāptamāvaraṇamavidyādibandhanaṃ yeṣāṃ te dharmā alabdhāvaraṇā bandhanarahitā ityarthaḥ, prakṛtinirmalāḥ svabhāvaśuddhā ādau buddhāstathā muktā yasmānnityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Have never obtained a veil' (<s>alabdhāvaraṇāḥ</s>)—those for whom no veil, no bondage of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the like, has been obtained or reached—those <s>dharmas</s> have never obtained a veil; the meaning is: they are free from bondage. 'Pure by nature' (<s>prakṛtinirmalāḥ</s>)—pure by their own essential nature. 'Enlightened from the beginning' and 'thus liberated'—because they are of the nature of eternal purity, eternal enlightenment, and eternal liberation.

children.text: yadyevaṃ kathaṃ tarhi budhyanta ityucyate?
children.translated_text: If so, how then is it said that they 'awaken' (<s>budhyante</s>)?

children.text: nāyakāḥ svāminaḥ samarthā boddhuṃ bodhaśaktimatsvabhāvā ityarthaḥ, yathā nityaprakāśasvarūpo 'pi savitā prakāśata ityucyate yathā vā nityanivṛttagatayo 'pi nityameva śailāstiṣṭhantītyucyate tadvat //98//
children.translated_text: 'Leaders' (<s>nāyakāḥ</s>) means masters, capable of knowing, having the capacity for knowledge by their very nature—that is the meaning. Just as the sun, though of eternally luminous nature, is [still] said to 'illumine'; and just as mountains, though their movement has eternally ceased, are [still] said to 'stand always'—even so [is the usage of 'awaken']. ||98||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.99
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.99

children.text: kramate na hi buddhasya jñānaṃ dharmeṣu tāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of the awakened one (<s>Buddha</s>), the protector, does not proceed toward [any] entities (<s>dharmas</s>);

children.text: sarve dharmās tathā jñānaṃ naitad buddhena bhāṣitam // MandUpK_4.99 //
children.translated_text: All entities too are like that knowledge—this was not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.99 ||

children.text:
MandUpKC_4.99
yasmānna hi kramate buddhasya paramārthadarśino jñānaṃ viṣayāntareṣu dharmeṣu dharmasaṃsthaṃ savitarīva prabhā, tāyinas tāyo 'syāstīti tāyī, saṃtānavato nirantarasyākāśakalpasyetyarthaḥ, pūjāvato vā prajñāvato vā, sarve dharmā ātmāno 'pi tathā jñānavadevākāśakalpatvānna kramante kvacidapyarthāntara ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.99: Because the knowledge of the awakened one—the seer of ultimate reality—does not proceed to entities, to objects other [than itself]; [it is] established in the entities [themselves], like the radiance in the sun. '<s>Tāyin</s>' means 'one who possesses continuity' (<s>tāyas</s>)—of unbroken continuity, like space; or alternatively, 'one worthy of reverence,' or 'one possessed of wisdom.' All <s>dharmas</s>—even the selves—are likewise, like that knowledge; being like space, they do not proceed anywhere to any other object—that is the meaning.

children.text:
yadādāvupanyastaṃ jñānenākāśakalpenetyādi tadidamākāśakalpasya tāyino buddhasya tadananyatvādākāśakalpaṃ jñānaṃ na kramaye kvacidapyarthāntare /
tathā dharmā iti /
ākāśamivācalamavikriyaṃ niravayavaṃ nityamadvitīyamasaṅgamadṛśyamagrāhyamaśanāyādyatītaṃ brahmātmatattvam /
"na hi draṣṭurdṛṣṭerviparilopo vidyate"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 23) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: What was stated at the beginning—'through knowledge that is like space' and so on—this is [restated]: the knowledge that is like space, belonging to the awakened one (<s>Buddha</s>), the protector, who is like space—because of its non-difference from him—does not proceed anywhere to any other object. Likewise [for] the entities (<s>dharmas</s>). Like space—immovable, unchanging, without parts, eternal, non-dual, unattached, invisible, ungraspable, beyond hunger and the like—such is the <s>Brahman</s>-Self-reality. As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'For the vision of the seer is never lost' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.23).

children.text: jñānajñeyajñātṛbhedarahitaṃ paramārthatattvamadvayam etanna buddhena bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: This ultimate reality, non-dual, devoid of the distinction of knower, known, and knowledge—this was not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: yadyapi bāhyārthanirākaraṇaṃ jñānamātrakalpanā cādvayavastusāmīpyamuktam /
children.translated_text: Although the negation of external objects and the postulation of consciousness-only were said [by the <s>Buddha</s>] to be close to the non-dual reality—

children.text: idaṃ tu paramārthatattvamadvaitaṃ vedānteṣveva vijñeyamityarthaḥ //99//
children.translated_text: This ultimate non-dual reality is to be known only through the <s>Vedānta</s> [scriptures]—that is the meaning. ||99||

children.text: START MandUpK 4.100
children.translated_text: START <s>Māṇḍūkya Kārikā</s> 4.100

children.text: śāstrasamāptau paramārthatattvastutyarthaṃ namaskāra ucyate-
children.translated_text: At the conclusion of the treatise, a salutation is offered for the purpose of praising the ultimate reality—

children.text: durdarśam atigambhīram ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam /
children.translated_text: Difficult to perceive, exceedingly profound, unborn, of uniform sameness, all-illumining—

children.text: buddhvā padam anānātvaṃ namaskurmo yathābalam // MandUpK_4.100 //
children.translated_text: Having realized that state of non-plurality, we bow down to it to the best of our ability. || <s>Kārikā</s> 4.100 ||

children.text: MandUpKC_4.100
children.translated_text: Commentary on <s>Kārikā</s> 4.100:

children.text: durdarśaṃ duḥkhena darśanamasyeti durdarśam, asti nāstīti catuṣkoṭivarjitatatvāddurvijñeyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Difficult to perceive' (<s>durdarśam</s>)—that whose perception is difficult; because it is beyond the fourfold logical alternatives of 'it exists,' 'it does not exist,' [both, and neither]—the meaning is: difficult to know.

children.text: ata evātigambhīraṃ duṣparveśaṃ mahāsamudravadakṛtaprajñaiḥ, ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam īdṛkpadamanānātvaṃ nānātvavarjitaṃ buddhvāvagamya tadbhūtāḥ santo namaskurmastasmai padāya, avyavahāryamapi vyavahāragocaramāpādya yathābalaṃ yathāśaktītyarthaḥ //100//
children.translated_text: For this very reason, 'exceedingly profound' (<s>atigambhīram</s>)—difficult to penetrate, like a great ocean, for those who have not cultivated wisdom. 'Unborn' (<s>ajam</s>), 'of uniform sameness' (<s>sāmyam</s>), 'all-illumining' (<s>viśāradam</s>)—having realized such a state, [which is] 'non-plurality' (<s>anānātva</s>), devoid of plurality—having understood it and become identified with it—we bow down to that state. Though it is beyond transactional usage (<s>avyavahārya</s>), bringing it within the scope of conventional expression, [we bow] to the best of our ability, to the extent of our capacity—that is the meaning. ||100||

children.text: iti śaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau gauḍapādīyāgamaśāstravivaraṇe 'lātaśāntyākhyaṃ caturthaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter called <s>Alātaśānti</s> (The Quenching of the Firebrand) in the commentary (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) on <s>Gauḍapāda's</s> <s>Āgamaśāstra</s>, composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s>. ||

children.text: oṃ śantiḥ! śāntiḥ!! śāntiḥ!!!
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Peace! Peace!! Peace!!!
